subject: Accounts
prompt: In which year was the Accounting Standards Board (ASSB) constituted by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI)?
explanation: The Accounting Standards Board (ASSB) was constituted by the ICAI on 21st April 1977. Its primary function is to formulate Accounting Standards for Indian entities.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013, who prescribes the Accounting Standards for companies in India?
optionA: The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) directly
optionB: The Central Government after considering recommendations of National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA)
optionC: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
optionD: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
answerText: The Central Government after considering recommendations of National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA)
explanation: Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 states that the Central Government (Ministry of Corporate Affairs) prescribes the Accounting Standards based on recommendations made by NFRA in consultation with ICAI.
conceptTags: Companies Act 2013 | NFRA | Standard Setting Process

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the turnover threshold above which a non-company entity is categorized as a Level I entity as per ICAI guidelines?
optionA: Exceeding ₹50 crore
optionB: Exceeding ₹100 crore
optionC: Exceeding ₹250 crore
optionD: Exceeding ₹500 crore
answerText: Exceeding ₹250 crore
explanation: As per the revised criteria issued by ICAI for classification of non-company entities, an entity whose turnover (excluding other income) exceeds ₹250 crore in the immediately preceding accounting year is categorized as Level I.
conceptTags: Level I Entity | Non-Company Criteria | Turnover Threshold

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the maximum borrowing threshold (including public deposits) allowed for a company to qualify as a Small and Medium Company (SMC) under Companies (AS) Rules, 2021?
optionA: Does not exceed ₹10 crore at any time during the preceding accounting year
optionB: Does not exceed ₹25 crore at any time during the preceding accounting year
optionC: Does not exceed ₹50 crore at any time during the preceding accounting year
optionD: Does not exceed ₹100 crore at any time during the preceding accounting year
answerText: Does not exceed ₹50 crore at any time during the preceding accounting year
explanation: Under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2021, an SMC's borrowings (including public deposits) must not exceed ₹50 crore at any time during the immediately preceding accounting year.
conceptTags: SMC Criteria | Borrowing Threshold | Companies Rules 2021

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which of the following bodies is responsible for issuing International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS)?
optionA: International Accounting Standards Committee (IASC)
optionB: International Accounting Standards Board (IASB)
optionC: Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB)
optionD: International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB)
answerText: International Accounting Standards Board (IASB)
explanation: The International Accounting Standards Board (IASB), an independent standard-setting body of the IFRS Foundation, formulates and issues IFRS.

subject: Accounts
prompt: How many levels of classification are specified by ICAI for non-company entities for the applicability of Accounting Standards?
optionA: Two levels (SMC and Non-SMC)
optionB: Three levels (Level I, Level II, Level III)
optionC: Four levels (Level I, Level II, Level III, Level IV)
optionD: Five levels (Level I to Level V)
answerText: Four levels (Level I, Level II, Level III, Level IV)
explanation: ICAI revised the classification scheme for non-company entities into four distinct levels: Level I (Large), Level II (Medium), Level III (Small), and Level IV (Micro).

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which of the following statements correctly describes Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)?
optionA: Ind AS are identical copy-paste versions of US GAAP
optionB: Ind AS are Accounting Standards issued directly by ICAI without MCA notification
optionC: Ind AS are converged versions of IFRS tailored to the Indian economic and legal environment
optionD: Ind AS apply only to sole proprietorships and partnership firms
answerText: Ind AS are converged versions of IFRS tailored to the Indian economic and legal environment
explanation: Ind AS are Accounting Standards converged with IFRS (incorporating Indian carve-outs/carve-ins) notified by the MCA under the Companies (Ind AS) Rules, 2015.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the maximum turnover ceiling for a non-company entity to be classified as Level IV (Micro Enterprise)?
optionA: Up to ₹2 crore
optionB: Up to ₹5 crore
optionC: Up to ₹10 crore
optionD: Up to ₹25 crore
answerText: Up to ₹10 crore
explanation: Level IV non-company entities are those with turnover (excluding other income) not exceeding ₹10 crore in the immediately preceding accounting year and borrowings not exceeding ₹2 crore.

subject: Accounts
prompt: A company whose equity or debt securities are listed on any recognized stock exchange in India is automatically classified as:
optionA: A Small and Medium Company (SMC)
optionB: A Non-SMC
optionC: A Level IV Entity
optionD: Exempt from Accounting Standards
answerText: A Non-SMC
explanation: Listed companies or companies in the process of listing cannot qualify as SMCs under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2021; they are categorized as Non-SMCs.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which accounting standard issued by ICAI deals with 'Cash Flow Statements'?
optionA: AS 1
optionB: AS 3
optionC: AS 7
optionD: AS 10
answerText: AS 3
explanation: AS 3 deals with Cash Flow Statements. Level II, III, and IV non-company entities as well as SMCs are granted certain relaxations/exemptions under this standard depending on statutory provisions.

subject: Accounts
prompt: When testing the borrowing condition for SMC status of a company for FY 2024-25, during what timeframe must the borrowing limit of ₹50 crore NOT be exceeded?
optionA: At the end of the current financial year (31st March 2025)
optionB: At any time during the immediately preceding financial year (FY 2023-24)
optionC: At the end of the immediately preceding financial year (31st March 2024) only
optionD: On average basis during the preceding three financial years
answerText: At any time during the immediately preceding financial year (FY 2023-24)
explanation: The condition specifies that the borrowings (including public deposits) must not exceed ₹50 crore at any time during the immediately preceding accounting year.

subject: Accounts
prompt: If an existing Non-SMC entity subsequently satisfies all criteria to become an SMC, for how many consecutive years must it satisfy those criteria before it can avail SMC exemptions?
optionA: Immediately from the current year
optionB: One reporting year
optionC: Two consecutive reporting years
optionD: Three consecutive reporting years
answerText: Two consecutive reporting years
explanation: An entity that was previously classified as a Non-SMC but subsequently meets SMC criteria must continue to meet those criteria for two consecutive years before it can claim SMC relaxations/exemptions.
conceptTags: Transitional Rules | SMC Reclassification | Two-Year Rule

subject: Accounts
prompt: Firm Alpha (a partnership firm) has turnover of ₹45 crore and borrowings of ₹12 crore during the preceding accounting year. Under which level of non-company classification does Firm Alpha fall?
optionA: Level I
optionB: Level II
optionC: Level III
optionD: Level IV
answerText: Level II
explanation: Level II criteria for non-company entities: Turnover between ₹50 crore and ₹250 crore OR borrowings between ₹10 crore and ₹50 crore. Since borrowings (₹12 crore) exceed ₹10 crore but do not exceed ₹50 crore, Firm Alpha is Level II.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Are non-company entities categorized under Level II exempt from AS 17 (Segment Reporting)?
optionA: No, AS 17 is fully mandatory for Level II entities
optionB: Yes, Level II entities are fully exempt from complying with AS 17
optionC: Exempt only if turnover is less than ₹20 crore
optionD: Exempt only if permitted by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)
answerText: Yes, Level II entities are fully exempt from complying with AS 17
explanation: AS 17 (Segment Reporting) is mandatory ONLY for Level I non-company entities. Level II, Level III, and Level IV entities are fully exempt from AS 17.

subject: Accounts
prompt: An unlisted company has a Net Worth of ₹260 crore as of 31st March 2024. Which accounting framework is mandatorily applicable to this company for FY 2024-25?
optionA: Accounting Standards (AS) under Companies (AS) Rules, 2021
optionB: Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) under Companies (Ind AS) Rules, 2015
optionC: IFRS directly as issued by IASB
optionD: US GAAP
answerText: Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) under Companies (Ind AS) Rules, 2015
explanation: Under Phase II of the Ind AS roadmap, all unlisted companies having a Net Worth of ₹250 crore or more on 31st March of any financial year are mandatorily required to adopt Ind AS from the immediate next financial year.
conceptTags: Ind AS Roadmap | Net Worth Threshold | Phase II

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which of the following statements regarding the applicability of AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures) to Non-Company Entities is CORRECT?
optionA: Exempt for Level II, Level III, and Level IV entities
optionB: Mandatory for Level I, Level II, and Level III entities, but exempt for Level IV entities
optionC: Exempt for Level III and Level IV entities only
optionD: Mandatory for Level I entities only
answerText: Mandatory for Level I, Level II, and Level III entities, but exempt for Level IV entities
explanation: AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures) is fully applicable to Level I, Level II, and Level III non-company entities. Only Level IV (Micro) non-company entities are granted full exemption from AS 18.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which body replaced the National Advisory Committee on Accounting Standards (NACAS) under the Companies Act, 2013?
optionA: Accounting Standards Board (ASSB)
optionB: National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA)
optionC: Financial Reporting Review Board (FRRB)
optionD: Quality Review Board (QRB)
answerText: National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA)
explanation: The National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) constituted under Section 132 of the Companies Act, 2013 replaced NACAS to advise the Central Government on accounting standards and oversee audit quality.
conceptTags: NFRA | NACAS | Companies Act Regulatory Setup

subject: Accounts
prompt: If a company adopting Ind AS has a non-listed subsidiary company with a Net Worth of ₹10 crore, what accounting framework must the subsidiary adopt for its standalone financial statements?
optionA: Companies (AS) Rules, 2021 as its net worth is below ₹250 crore
optionB: Ind AS mandatorily, because its holding company is covered under Ind AS
optionC: Option to choose between AS and Ind AS
optionD: Level IV Non-company framework
answerText: Ind AS mandatorily, because its holding company is covered under Ind AS
explanation: Once Ind AS becomes applicable to a parent company, it mandatorily applies to all its holding, subsidiary, joint venture, and associate companies, irrespective of their individual net worth.
conceptTags: Ind AS Holding-Subsidiary Rule | Consolidated & Standalone

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which standard setting authority was created in 2021 under the IFRS Foundation to establish comprehensive global baseline standards for ESG / sustainability disclosures?
optionA: Global Reporting Initiative (GRI)
optionB: Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB)
optionC: International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB)
optionD: Climate Disclosure Standards Board (CDSB)
answerText: International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB)
explanation: The IFRS Foundation announced the creation of the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) at COP26 in November 2021 to issue IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under Companies (AS) Rules, 2021, if an SMC incurs a total borrowing of ₹55 crore for 3 days during FY 2023-24, how does it affect its classification for FY 2024-25?
optionA: It remains an SMC as the average borrowing for the year was under ₹50 crore
optionB: It becomes a Non-SMC because borrowing exceeded ₹50 crore at any time during the preceding year
optionC: It remains an SMC if the excess borrowing was repaid within 7 days
optionD: It becomes a Level IV entity
answerText: It becomes a Non-SMC because borrowing exceeded ₹50 crore at any time during the preceding year
explanation: The criterion explicitly specifies that borrowings must not exceed ₹50 crore *at any time* during the immediately preceding accounting year. Exceeding ₹50 crore even for a single day invalidates SMC status.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which of the following accounting standards is FULLY EXEMPT for Level III non-company entities?
optionA: AS 2 (Valuation of Inventories)
optionB: AS 10 (Property, Plant and Equipment)
optionC: AS 24 (Discontinuing Operations)
optionD: AS 13 (Accounting for Investments)
answerText: AS 24 (Discontinuing Operations)
explanation: AS 24 (Discontinuing Operations) is exempt for Level III and Level IV non-company entities. AS 2, AS 10, and AS 13 are mandatory across all levels.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What happens once an entity adopts Ind AS either voluntarily or mandatorily?
optionA: It can revert back to Indian AS after 3 years
optionB: It can revert back to Indian AS if its net worth falls below ₹250 crore
optionC: It cannot revert back to Indian AS (Ind AS adoption is irrevocable)
optionD: It can switch back if approved by its shareholders in AGM
answerText: It cannot revert back to Indian AS (Ind AS adoption is irrevocable)
explanation: Under the Companies (Ind AS) Rules, 2015, once a company starts applying Ind AS (whether voluntarily or mandatorily), it must continue to comply with Ind AS for all subsequent financial statements (irrevocable rule).
conceptTags: Irrevocability of Ind AS | Ind AS Rules

subject: Accounts
prompt: Entity B (a non-company entity) has Turnover of ₹80 crore and Borrowings of ₹55 crore during the preceding accounting year. Which level of non-company classification applies to Entity B?
optionA: Level II, because turnover is less than ₹250 crore
optionB: Level I, because borrowings exceed ₹50 crore
optionC: Level III, because turnover is between ₹50 and ₹250 crore
optionD: Level IV, as it is a non-company entity
answerText: Level I, because borrowings exceed ₹50 crore
explanation: An entity is categorized as Level I if ANY of the Level I thresholds are crossed. Since borrowings (₹55 crore) exceed ₹50 crore, Entity B becomes a Level I entity regardless of its turnover.
conceptTags: Level I Criteria | Non-Company Threshold Override

subject: Accounts
prompt: If a Non-SMC company incurs a reduction in borrowings and turnover and now qualifies as an SMC, when can it start benefiting from SMC exemptions under Companies (AS) Rules, 2021?
optionA: In the current year itself if board approval is obtained
optionB: Only after meeting the SMC criteria for two consecutive accounting years
optionC: Only after getting permission from MCA and NFRA
optionD: From the immediate next accounting period following the reduction
answerText: Only after meeting the SMC criteria for two consecutive accounting years
explanation: An entity classified as Non-SMC that subsequently meets SMC criteria must satisfy those criteria for two consecutive financial years before it can claim SMC relaxations.
conceptTags: Two-Year Rule | Non-SMC to SMC Transition

subject: Accounts
prompt: A sole proprietorship trading concern has Turnover of ₹8 crore and bank borrowings of ₹1.5 crore. It holds a 75% stake in a partnership firm that is classified as a Level I non-company entity. What is the level of the sole proprietorship?
optionA: Level IV, based on its own turnover and borrowings
optionB: Level I, because it is a holding entity of a Level I entity
optionC: Level III, because holding entities are downgraded by two levels
optionD: Level II, based on consolidated figures
answerText: Level I, because it is a holding entity of a Level I entity
explanation: As per ICAI guidelines, holding entities and subsidiary entities of Level I entities are automatically classified as Level I entities, regardless of their individual standalone turnover or borrowings.
conceptTags: Holding Subsidiary Rule | Level I Extension

subject: Accounts
prompt: Regarding AS 28 (Impairment of Assets), how are Level IV non-company entities treated compared to Level I entities?
optionA: Level IV entities are completely exempt from AS 28
optionB: AS 28 applies to Level IV entities, but with relaxations in determining value in use (e.g., using reasonable estimates without detailed cash flow projections)
optionC: AS 28 applies without any relaxations or exemptions to Level IV entities
optionD: AS 28 applies to Level IV entities only if they have international borrowings
answerText: AS 28 applies to Level IV entities, but with relaxations in determining value in use (e.g., using reasonable estimates without detailed cash flow projections)
explanation: AS 28 applies to Level IV entities, but ICAI grants relaxations regarding the calculation of 'value in use'. Level IV entities can estimate value in use using reasonable surrogates/estimates rather than complex discounted cash flow modeling.
conceptTags: AS 28 Relaxations | Level IV Entities | Value in Use

subject: Accounts
prompt: Company K is an unlisted Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) with Net Worth of ₹300 crore as on 31st March 2024. Which accounting framework applies to Company K for FY 2024-25?
optionA: Companies (AS) Rules, 2021
optionB: Ind AS under Phase II of the NBFC Roadmap
optionC: RBI Core Accounting Rules exclusively
optionD: IFRS direct compliance
answerText: Ind AS under Phase II of the NBFC Roadmap
explanation: Under the NBFC Ind AS Roadmap, Phase II made Ind AS mandatory for all unlisted NBFCs having a Net Worth of ₹250 crore or more from 1st April 2019 onwards. Thus, Company K (Net Worth ₹300 cr) must follow Ind AS.
conceptTags: NBFC Roadmap | Ind AS Applicability | Phase II NBFC

subject: Accounts
prompt: How is 'Net Worth' calculated for determining Ind AS applicability for unlisted companies as per MCA guidelines?
optionA: Paid-up Equity Share Capital + Reserves out of profits - Accumulated Losses - Deferred Revenue Expenditure - Revaluation Reserves
optionB: Paid-up Capital + All Reserves + Revaluation Reserves
optionC: Total Assets minus Total External Liabilities including Preference Shares
optionD: Paid-up Equity Share Capital + Preference Share Capital + General Reserves + Revaluation Reserves
answerText: Paid-up Equity Share Capital + Reserves out of profits - Accumulated Losses - Deferred Revenue Expenditure - Revaluation Reserves
explanation: Net worth is calculated as per Section 2(57) of Companies Act 2013: aggregate value of paid-up share capital + reserves created out of profits + securities premium - accumulated losses - deferred expenditure - revaluation reserve.
conceptTags: Net Worth Definition | Section 2(57) | Ind AS Threshold

subject: Accounts
prompt: If a non-company entity moves from Level I to Level IV status due to business downsizing, when can it start availing the full exemptions available to Level IV entities?
optionA: Immediately in the year of downsizing
optionB: After remaining in Level IV for two consecutive reporting periods
optionC: After remaining in Level IV for three consecutive reporting periods
optionD: Only when certified by the ICAI ASSB
answerText: After remaining in Level IV for two consecutive reporting periods
explanation: An entity that drops from a higher level (Level I) to a lower level (Level IV) cannot claim exemptions/relaxations of the lower level until it continues to qualify for the lower level for two consecutive reporting periods.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Where there is a conflict between the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and an Accounting Standard notified under Section 133, which of the two shall prevail?
optionA: The Accounting Standard notified under Section 133
optionB: The provisions of the Companies Act, 2013
optionC: The guidance note issued by ASSB
optionD: The matter must be referred to the High Court
answerText: The provisions of the Companies Act, 2013
explanation: Accounting Standards are subservient to statutory legislation. If there is a conflict between the Companies Act, 2013 and an Accounting Standard, statutory law (the Companies Act) prevails.
conceptTags: Statutory Conflict | Hierarchy of Rules | Companies Act Supremacy

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Vibrant Threads Ltd is an unlisted public manufacturing company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013. The company is evaluating its accounting framework compliance for FY 2024-25 under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2021.

The relevant financial parameters of Vibrant Threads Ltd for the preceding three financial years are as follows:
- FY 2021-22: Turnover = ₹210 crore; Peak Borrowings = ₹35 crore.
- FY 2022-23: Turnover = ₹240 crore; Peak Borrowings = ₹48 crore.
- FY 2023-24: Turnover = ₹245 crore; Peak Borrowings = ₹54 crore (for 10 days in Nov 2023 due to temporary working capital loan).

Additionally, Vibrant Threads Ltd holds an 80% equity stake in 'WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd', an unlisted small private company with Turnover of ₹12 crore and Peak Borrowings of ₹3 crore during FY 2023-24. Neither company has listed securities or is in the process of listing.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the classification of Vibrant Threads Ltd for FY 2024-25 under the Companies (AS) Rules, 2021?
optionA: Small and Medium Company (SMC)
optionB: Non-SMC
optionC: Level IV Non-company Entity
optionD: Ind AS mandatory company
answerText: Non-SMC
explanation: For FY 2024-25, compliance is based on preceding year FY 2023-24 figures. Peak borrowings reached ₹54 crore in FY 2023-24, exceeding the ₹50 crore limit. Hence, Vibrant Threads Ltd is a Non-SMC.
conceptTags: SMC Classification | Borrowing Limit | Companies Rules 2021

subject: Accounts
prompt: How does the classification of Vibrant Threads Ltd as a Non-SMC for FY 2024-25 affect its subsidiary 'WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd'?
optionA: WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd remains an SMC because its own borrowings are only ₹3 crore
optionB: WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd becomes a Non-SMC because it is a subsidiary of a Non-SMC
optionC: WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd is reclassified as a Level IV non-company entity
optionD: WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd is exempt from all Accounting Standards
answerText: WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd becomes a Non-SMC because it is a subsidiary of a Non-SMC
explanation: Under the definition of SMC in Companies (AS) Rules, 2021, a company that is a subsidiary or holding company of a Non-SMC cannot be treated as an SMC. Thus, WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd becomes a Non-SMC.

subject: Accounts
prompt: If Vibrant Threads Ltd repays its loans so that peak borrowing in FY 2024-25 drops to ₹30 crore, in which financial year can it first claim SMC relaxations/exemptions?
optionD: Immediately in FY 2024-25
explanation: A Non-SMC that subsequently meets SMC criteria must meet those criteria for two consecutive reporting periods (FY 2024-25 and FY 2025-26) before it can claim SMC exemptions. Thus, it can claim exemptions in FY 2027-28 (based on two consecutive years of compliance).

subject: Accounts
prompt: Is Vibrant Threads Ltd required to present a Cash Flow Statement as per AS 3 for FY 2024-25?
optionA: No, because it is an unlisted company
optionB: Yes, because it is classified as a Non-SMC and does not qualify for small company exemption under Section 2(40)
optionC: No, because its turnover is less than ₹250 crore
optionD: Optional at the discretion of the Board of Directors
answerText: Yes, because it is classified as a Non-SMC and does not qualify for small company exemption under Section 2(40)
explanation: Cash Flow Statement (AS 3) is mandatory for Non-SMCs. Exemptions under Section 2(40) apply only to One Person Companies, Small Companies, Dormant Companies, and Startups; Vibrant Threads Ltd does not qualify.
conceptTags: AS 3 Applicability | Cash Flow Statement Exemptions

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Apex Consultancy Services is a partnership firm providing IT advisory services in India. The firm's partners are analyzing the applicability of Accounting Standards issued by ICAI for FY 2024-25.

Financial parameters of Apex Consultancy Services for FY 2023-24:
- Turnover (excluding other income): ₹42 crore
- Bank Borrowings (Peak balance): ₹8 crore
- Fixed Deposits accepted from partners/public: ₹3 crore

During FY 2023-24, Apex Consultancy Services acquired a 65% equity stake in 'Global Tech Solutions LLP', a non-company entity with Turnover of ₹280 crore in FY 2023-24.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the non-company classification level of 'Global Tech Solutions LLP' for FY 2024-25?
optionA: Level I
optionB: Level II
optionC: Level III
optionD: Level IV
answerText: Level I
explanation: Global Tech Solutions LLP has a turnover of ₹280 crore in FY 2023-24, which exceeds the ₹250 crore threshold. Therefore, it is a Level I non-company entity.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the non-company classification level of 'Apex Consultancy Services' for FY 2024-25?
optionA: Level III, based on its standalone turnover and borrowings
optionB: Level II, based on its total borrowings of ₹11 crore
optionC: Level I, because it is the holding entity of a Level I entity
optionD: Level IV, because it is a partnership firm
answerText: Level I, because it is the holding entity of a Level I entity
explanation: Even though Apex's standalone turnover (₹42 cr) and total borrowings (₹11 cr) place it in Level II, holding entities of Level I entities are automatically classified as Level I entities.
conceptTags: Holding Subsidiary Rule | Level I Classification

subject: Accounts
prompt: Can Apex Consultancy Services claim exemption from complying with AS 17 (Segment Reporting) for FY 2024-25?
optionA: Yes, because its turnover is below ₹50 crore
optionB: No, because AS 17 is fully mandatory for all Level I entities
optionC: Yes, because it is a partnership firm
optionD: Yes, if all partners consent unanimously
answerText: No, because AS 17 is fully mandatory for all Level I entities
explanation: AS 17 is mandatory for Level I entities. Since Apex Consultancy Services is classified as Level I (due to holding a Level I subsidiary), it cannot claim exemption from AS 17.

subject: Accounts
prompt: If Apex Consultancy Services sells its entire stake in Global Tech Solutions LLP during FY 2024-25, when can it start claiming Level III exemptions on a standalone basis (assuming its figures remain Turnover ₹42 cr, Borrowings ₹8 cr)?
optionA: Immediately in FY 2024-25
optionB: From FY 2025-26
optionC: Only after remaining in Level III criteria for two consecutive reporting periods
optionD: It can never claim Level III exemptions
answerText: Only after remaining in Level III criteria for two consecutive reporting periods
explanation: When an entity drops from Level I to a lower level (Level III), it must continue to meet the criteria of the lower level for two consecutive reporting periods before availing of exemptions.

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Nova Retail Services Pvt Ltd is an unlisted private company incorporated in 2015 operating a chain of supermarkets. The company has seen rapid expansion. Its financial position across recent years is summarised below:

- 31st March 2022: Net Worth = ₹190 crore; Turnover = ₹450 crore
- 31st March 2023: Net Worth = ₹240 crore; Turnover = ₹520 crore
- 31st March 2024: Net Worth = ₹270 crore; Turnover = ₹610 crore

Nova Retail Services Pvt Ltd has two non-listed subsidiaries: 'Tiny Express Pvt Ltd' (Net Worth ₹12 crore) and 'Fast Logistics Pvt Ltd' (Net Worth ₹8 crore). Neither parent nor subsidiaries are banks, FIs, or NBFCs.

subject: Accounts
prompt: From which financial year is Ind AS mandatorily applicable to Nova Retail Services Pvt Ltd?
explanation: Under Phase II of the Ind AS roadmap, unlisted companies with Net Worth >= ₹250 crore on 31st March of any FY must adopt Ind AS from the next FY. Net worth reached ₹270 crore on 31st March 2024; hence Ind AS applies from FY 2024-25.
conceptTags: Ind AS Roadmap | Net Worth Criteria

subject: Accounts
prompt: Is Ind AS applicable to 'Tiny Express Pvt Ltd' for FY 2024-25, despite its Net Worth being only ₹12 crore?
optionA: No, because its Net Worth is below ₹250 crore
optionB: Yes, mandatory because its parent company Nova Retail Services Pvt Ltd is adopting Ind AS from FY 2024-25
optionC: Optional at the choice of Tiny Express Pvt Ltd's Board
optionD: No, unless its turnover exceeds ₹100 crore
answerText: Yes, mandatory because its parent company Nova Retail Services Pvt Ltd is adopting Ind AS from FY 2024-25
explanation: Once Ind AS applies to a holding company, it automatically applies to all its holding, subsidiary, joint venture, and associate companies regardless of their individual net worth.

subject: Accounts
prompt: If Nova Retail Services Pvt Ltd's Net Worth falls to ₹220 crore on 31st March 2026, can it switch back from Ind AS to Companies (AS) Rules, 2021 for FY 2026-27?
optionA: Yes, because net worth fell below ₹250 crore
optionB: Yes, subject to approval from MCA
optionC: No, once Ind AS is applied, the company must continue applying Ind AS indefinitely
optionD: Yes, if shareholders pass a special resolution
answerText: No, once Ind AS is applied, the company must continue applying Ind AS indefinitely
explanation: Ind AS adoption is an irrevocable process. Once a company starts preparing statements under Ind AS, it cannot revert to Accounting Standards (AS) even if its Net Worth drops below the threshold.

subject: Accounts
prompt: When Nova Retail Services Pvt Ltd prepares its first Ind AS financial statements for FY 2024-25, what comparative information must it present?
optionA: No comparative figures are required for the first year of adoption
optionB: Comparative figures for the preceding year (FY 2023-24) converted to Ind AS
optionC: Comparative figures for the last 3 preceding years under Indian AS
optionD: Comparative figures under IFRS as issued by IASB
answerText: Comparative figures for the preceding year (FY 2023-24) converted to Ind AS
explanation: Under Ind AS 101 (First-time Adoption of Ind AS), an entity must present at least one year of comparative information under Ind AS (i.e., FY 2023-24 comparative figures translated to Ind AS).
conceptTags: Ind AS 101 | First Time Adoption | Comparatives

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: In 2024, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) and the National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) examined the standard-setting mechanism in India. A private corporate group, 'GigaTech Enterprises Group', operates multiple legal entities:

1. GigaTech Solutions Ltd (Unlisted Public Co., Turnover ₹300 crore, Net Worth ₹260 crore)
2. GigaTech Softwares Pvt Ltd (Unlisted Co., Turnover ₹40 crore, Net Worth ₹15 crore)
3. GigaTech Hardware LLP (LLP, Turnover ₹8 crore, Borrowings ₹1.2 crore)

The chief accountant is analyzing standard setting authorities, Section 133 of Companies Act 2013, NFRA jurisdiction, and standard classification.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which body formulates Accounting Standards and recommends them to NFRA for consideration before notification by MCA?
optionA: Accounting Standards Board (ASSB) of ICAI
optionB: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
optionC: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
optionD: Ministry of Finance
answerText: Accounting Standards Board (ASSB) of ICAI
explanation: The Accounting Standards Board (ASSB) set up by ICAI formulates Accounting Standards and submits them to NFRA. NFRA then examines them and makes recommendations to the Central Government (MCA).

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which set of Accounting Standards applies to 'GigaTech Hardware LLP' for FY 2024-25?
optionA: Companies (Ind AS) Rules, 2015
optionB: Companies (AS) Rules, 2021
optionC: Accounting Standards issued by ICAI for Non-Company Entities (Level IV)
optionD: IFRS direct framework
answerText: Accounting Standards issued by ICAI for Non-Company Entities (Level IV)
explanation: GigaTech Hardware LLP is an LLP (non-company entity). Statutory Companies Rules do not apply to LLPs directly. The ICAI issued scheme for Non-Company Entities applies; with Turnover ₹8 cr and Borrowings ₹1.2 cr, it is Level IV.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under Section 134(5)(a) of the Companies Act, 2013, what must Directors state in the Directors' Responsibility Statement regarding Accounting Standards?
optionA: That Accounting Standards are optional for private companies
optionB: That in preparation of annual accounts, applicable accounting standards have been followed along with proper explanation for material departures
optionC: That all accounting standards have been relaxed by the statutory auditor
optionD: That standards set by FASB US have been complied with
answerText: That in preparation of annual accounts, applicable accounting standards have been followed along with proper explanation for material departures
explanation: Section 134(5)(a) mandates that directors state in the Directors' Responsibility Statement that in the preparation of annual accounts, applicable accounting standards were followed with proper explanation for any material departures.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the relationship between Ind AS and IFRS regarding 'Carve-outs'?
optionA: Carve-outs are additions made in Ind AS that do not exist in IFRS
optionB: Carve-outs are deviations/differences in Ind AS from IFRS to suit Indian legal and economic conditions
optionC: Carve-outs represent complete rejection of IFRS principles
optionD: Carve-outs apply only to public sector undertakings
answerText: Carve-outs are deviations/differences in Ind AS from IFRS to suit Indian legal and economic conditions
explanation: Carve-outs refer to departures made in Ind AS from the corresponding IFRS standards to address specific Indian economic, legal, or regulatory circumstances.
conceptTags: Carve Outs | Ind AS vs IFRS

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Greenfield Farmers LLP is an agricultural partnership enterprise operating in Punjab. It is not listed and has no financial institutions as partners. 

Financial details for Greenfield Farmers LLP for FY 2023-24:
- Turnover (excluding government grants): ₹7.5 crore
- Bank Borrowings (Peak balance): ₹1.6 crore
- Total Assets: ₹5.0 crore

The management of Greenfield Farmers LLP wants to understand its compliance requirements for FY 2024-25 regarding AS 3 (Cash Flow Statements), AS 17 (Segment Reporting), AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures), and AS 24 (Discontinuing Operations).

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the non-company classification level of Greenfield Farmers LLP for FY 2024-25?
optionA: Level I
optionB: Level II
optionC: Level III
optionD: Level IV
answerText: Level IV
explanation: With turnover up to ₹10 crore (₹7.5 cr) and borrowings up to ₹2 crore (₹1.6 cr), Greenfield Farmers LLP falls under Level IV (Micro non-company entities).

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which of the following standards is FULLY APPLICABLE to Greenfield Farmers LLP without exemption?
optionA: AS 3 (Cash Flow Statements)
optionB: AS 17 (Segment Reporting)
optionC: AS 2 (Valuation of Inventories)
optionD: AS 24 (Discontinuing Operations)
answerText: AS 2 (Valuation of Inventories)
explanation: AS 2 (Valuation of Inventories) is mandatory for all non-company entities including Level IV. AS 3, AS 17, and AS 24 are exempt for Level IV entities.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Is Greenfield Farmers LLP required to comply with AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures) for FY 2024-25?
optionA: Yes, AS 18 is mandatory for all entities regardless of level
optionB: No, Level IV entities are fully exempt from AS 18
optionC: Yes, but with partial disclosures only
optionD: Exempt only if turnover is less than ₹1 crore
answerText: No, Level IV entities are fully exempt from AS 18
explanation: Under the revised ICAI scheme for non-company entities, AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures) is fully exempt for Level IV entities.

subject: Accounts
prompt: If Greenfield Farmers LLP takes a new business expansion loan in FY 2024-25 taking peak borrowings to ₹4.0 crore (turnover remaining ₹8.0 cr), what will be its level for FY 2025-26?
optionA: Level I
optionB: Level II
optionC: Level III
optionD: Level IV
answerText: Level III
explanation: For Level III, borrowings are between > ₹2 crore and <= ₹10 crore. Peak borrowing of ₹4.0 crore shifts the entity from Level IV to Level III for FY 2025-26.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under the ICAI Framework for the Preparation and Presentation of Financial Statements, what is the status of the Framework in the event of a conflict with a specific Accounting Standard (AS)?
optionA: The Framework overrides the Accounting Standard.
optionB: The Accounting Standard overrides the Framework.
optionC: The entity may choose whichever treatment results in a higher net profit.
optionD: The matter must be referred to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for a ruling.
answerText: The Accounting Standard overrides the Framework.
explanation: The Framework clearly states that it is not an Accounting Standard and does not override any specific Accounting Standard. In case of a conflict between the Framework and an Accounting Standard, the requirements of the specific Accounting Standard override those of the Framework.
conceptTags: Framework Status | Conflict with AS | Hierarchy of Standards

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which of the following is NOT categorized as a fundamental accounting assumption in the Framework and AS 1?
optionA: Going Concern
optionB: Accrual
optionC: Consistency
optionD: Prudence
answerText: Prudence
explanation: Going Concern, Accrual, and Consistency are the three fundamental accounting assumptions specified in AS 1 and the Framework. Prudence is a qualitative consideration used in selecting accounting policies, not a fundamental accounting assumption.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which three essential conditions must be satisfied for an item to meet the definition of an 'Asset' according to the Framework?
optionA: Legal ownership, physical existence, and past cash outflow.
optionB: Control by the enterprise, result of past events, and expected inflow of future economic benefits.
optionC: Present legal title, reliable market value, and future tax savings.
optionD: Management intention to hold long-term, historical cost measurement, and physical form.
answerText: Control by the enterprise, result of past events, and expected inflow of future economic benefits.
explanation: An asset is defined as a resource controlled by the enterprise as a result of past events and from which future economic benefits are expected to flow to the enterprise. Physical form and legal ownership are not absolute prerequisites.
conceptTags: Asset Definition | Elements of Financial Statements | Control

subject: Accounts
prompt: The Framework defines 'Income' to include both revenues and gains. Which of the following is explicitly excluded from the definition of income?
optionA: Gains on disposal of non-current assets
optionB: Unrealized appreciation on investment property
optionC: Contributions from equity participants
optionD: Reversal of excess impairment provisions
answerText: Contributions from equity participants
explanation: Income is defined as increases in economic benefits during the accounting period in the form of inflows or enhancements of assets or decreases of liabilities that result in increases in equity, other than those relating to contributions from equity participants.
conceptTags: Income Definition | Equity Contributions | Elements of Financial Statements

subject: Accounts
prompt: An entity acquires equipment under a contract where legal ownership transfers only upon payment of the final installment, but all operational risks and rewards pass to the entity on day one. How should this equipment be recognized?
optionA: Recognize as an asset and liability immediately, applying the principle of 'substance over form'.
optionB: Record as operating lease expenses as installments are paid until legal title transfers.
optionC: Disclose as a contingent asset in the notes to accounts without financial balance recognition.
optionD: Record the asset at a nominal value of Re. 1 until full legal title is acquired.
answerText: Recognize as an asset and liability immediately, applying the principle of 'substance over form'.
explanation: Under the principle of 'substance over form', transactions are accounted for in accordance with their economic reality rather than merely their legal form. Since the risk and rewards are transferred, the asset and liability are recognized immediately.
conceptTags: Substance over Form | Qualitative Characteristics | Asset Recognition

subject: Accounts
prompt: How does the Framework define the qualitative characteristic of 'Prudence'?
optionA: The deliberate understatement of assets and overstatement of liabilities to create hidden reserves.
optionB: The inclusion of a degree of caution in exercising judgments needed in making estimates under uncertainty.
optionC: The policy of recognizing revenues only when cash is fully realized in bank accounts.
optionD: The immediate write-off of all capital expenditures incurred during the financial year.
answerText: The inclusion of a degree of caution in exercising judgments needed in making estimates under uncertainty.
explanation: Prudence is the inclusion of a degree of caution in the exercise of judgments needed in making estimates required under conditions of uncertainty, such that assets or income are not overstated and liabilities or expenses are not understated. It does not permit the creation of hidden or secret reserves.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Assets are recorded at the amount of cash or cash equivalents paid or the fair value of consideration given at the time of acquisition. Which measurement basis is described?
optionA: Current Cost
optionB: Realisable Value
optionC: Historical Cost
optionD: Present Value
answerText: Historical Cost
explanation: Historical cost is the measurement basis where assets are recorded at the amount of cash or cash equivalents paid or the fair value of the consideration given to acquire them at the time of their acquisition.
conceptTags: Measurement Basis | Historical Cost | Valuation Principles

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under which measurement basis are assets carried at the amount of cash or cash equivalents that would have to be paid if the same or an equivalent asset was acquired currently?
optionA: Historical Cost
optionB: Current Cost
optionC: Settlement Value
optionD: Present Value
answerText: Current Cost
explanation: Current cost measures assets at the amount of cash or cash equivalents that would have to be paid if the same or an equivalent asset were acquired currently.
conceptTags: Current Cost | Measurement Basis | Asset Valuation

subject: Accounts
prompt: In financial statement preparation, liabilities carried at the undiscounted amount of cash expected to be paid to satisfy obligations in the normal course of business are measured at:
optionA: Realisable / Settlement Value
optionB: Present Value
optionC: Historical Cost
optionD: Fair Value through Profit and Loss
answerText: Realisable / Settlement Value
explanation: Under the realisable (settlement) value basis, liabilities are carried at their settlement values, which are the undiscounted amounts of cash or cash equivalents expected to be paid to satisfy the liabilities in the normal course of business.
conceptTags: Settlement Value | Realisable Value | Measurement Basis

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under the concept of Financial Capital Maintenance at nominal monetary units, profit is earned only if:
optionA: Physical productive capacity at the end of the period exceeds that at the beginning.
optionB: The financial amount of net assets at the end of the period exceeds that at the beginning, after excluding distributions to and contributions from owners.
optionC: Net assets at the end of the period, adjusted for inflation, exceed net assets at the beginning.
optionD: Cash balances at the end of the period exceed cash balances at the beginning.
answerText: The financial amount of net assets at the end of the period exceeds that at the beginning, after excluding distributions to and contributions from owners.
explanation: Financial capital maintenance in nominal monetary units measures profit as the increase in nominal financial capital (net assets) over the period, excluding any transactions with owners (contributions and distributions).
conceptTags: Financial Capital Maintenance | Nominal Monetary Units | Capital Maintenance

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which capital maintenance concept requires all price changes affecting assets and liabilities to be treated as capital maintenance adjustments in equity rather than profit?
optionA: Financial capital maintenance in nominal units
optionB: Financial capital maintenance in constant purchasing power
optionC: Physical capital maintenance
optionD: Realized operating cash flow maintenance
answerText: Physical capital maintenance
explanation: Under physical capital maintenance (operating capability), all price changes affecting the assets and liabilities of the enterprise are viewed as capital maintenance adjustments that form part of equity, rather than being included in profit or loss.
conceptTags: Physical Capital Maintenance | Operating Capability | Equity Adjustments

subject: Accounts
prompt: Financial information must be free from deliberate bias so that it produces neutral outcomes without influencing decisions toward a predetermined result. Which qualitative characteristic does this describe?
optionA: Neutrality
optionB: Comparability
optionC: Understandability
optionD: Timeliness
answerText: Neutrality
explanation: To be reliable, the information contained in financial statements must be neutral, meaning free from bias. Financial statements are not neutral if, by the selection or presentation of information, they influence the making of a decision or judgment in order to achieve a predetermined result or outcome.

subject: Accounts
prompt: An item meeting the definition of an element should be recognized in financial statements if and only if:
optionA: It is legally enforceable and approved by the board of directors.
optionB: It is probable that any future economic benefit will flow to/from the enterprise AND its cost or value can be measured reliably.
optionC: A completed cash flow transaction has taken place during the current financial year.
optionD: It does not result in an increased tax liability for the reporting period.
answerText: It is probable that any future economic benefit will flow to/from the enterprise AND its cost or value can be measured reliably.
explanation: The Framework mandates two cumulative criteria for recognition of an element: (1) it is probable that any future economic benefit associated with the item will flow to or from the enterprise, and (2) the item has a cost or value that can be measured with reliability.

subject: Accounts
prompt: An entity delays issuing its annual report by eight months to obtain absolute confirmation of a pending insurance claim. Which constraint trade-off is highlighted?
optionA: Timeliness versus Reliability
optionB: Relevance versus Materiality
optionC: Substance over Form versus Prudence
optionD: Understandability versus Comparability
answerText: Timeliness versus Reliability
explanation: This situation illustrates the constraint between timeliness and reliability. Delaying reporting improves the reliability of the information regarding the claim but impairs timeliness, rendering the financial statements less relevant for decision-making.
conceptTags: Timeliness vs Reliability | Constraints | Qualitative Characteristics

subject: Accounts
prompt: According to the Framework, information is considered material if its omission or misstatement could:
optionA: Lead to regulatory penalties from government authorities.
optionB: Influence the economic decisions of users taken on the basis of financial statements.
optionC: Exceed 5% of gross revenues in all circumstances.
optionD: Directly alter the credit rating assigned to the entity.
answerText: Influence the economic decisions of users taken on the basis of financial statements.
explanation: Information is material if its omission or misstatement could influence the economic decisions of users taken on the basis of the financial statements. Materiality depends on the size and nature of the item judged in the specific circumstances.

subject: Accounts
prompt: When the going concern assumption of an entity is no longer valid, how should its financial statements be prepared?
optionA: On a standard historical cost basis with explanatory note disclosure.
optionB: On a liquidation/net realisable value basis, adjusting asset carrying amounts and providing for liabilities.
optionC: On a cash basis of accounting excluding all non-cash items.
optionD: Financial statements must be withheld completely.
answerText: On a liquidation/net realisable value basis, adjusting asset carrying amounts and providing for liabilities.
explanation: If the going concern assumption is invalid, financial statements can no longer be prepared on a normal going-concern historical cost basis. They must be prepared on a net realisable / liquidation basis, remeasuring assets at realisable values and recognizing obligations arising from liquidation.
conceptTags: Going Concern | Fundamental Accounting Assumptions | Liquidation Basis

subject: Accounts
prompt: When economic benefits are expected to arise over several accounting periods and the connection with income can only be broadly or indirectly determined, expenses are recognized on the basis of:
optionA: Immediate full write-off in the year of expenditure.
optionB: Systematic and rational allocation procedures.
optionC: Cash outflows as and when disbursements occur.
optionD: Historical cost adjusted for general purchasing power.
answerText: Systematic and rational allocation procedures.
explanation: When economic benefits are expected to arise over several accounting periods and the association with income can only be broadly or indirectly determined, expenses are recognized in the income statement on the basis of systematic and rational allocation procedures (e.g., depreciation).
conceptTags: Matching Principle | Expense Recognition | Systematic Allocation

subject: Accounts
prompt: How does the Framework define 'Equity'?
optionA: Total non-current assets minus total non-current liabilities.
optionB: Residual interest in the assets of the enterprise after deducting all its liabilities.
optionC: Paid-up share capital plus statutory reserves.
optionD: Net current assets available for operational expansion.
answerText: Residual interest in the assets of the enterprise after deducting all its liabilities.
explanation: Equity is defined in the Framework as the residual interest in the assets of the enterprise after deducting all its liabilities.
conceptTags: Equity Definition | Elements of Financial Statements | Residual Interest

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which user group of financial statements is primarily concerned with the risk inherent in, and return provided by, their investments?
optionA: Lenders
optionB: Suppliers and trade creditors
optionC: Investors
optionD: Government and regulatory agencies
answerText: Investors
explanation: Investors are the providers of risk capital and are concerned with the risk inherent in, and return provided by, their investments. They need information to help them decide whether to buy, hold, or sell shares.
conceptTags: Users of Financial Statements | Investors | Information Needs

subject: Accounts
prompt: An asset is reported at the present discounted value of future net cash inflows expected to be generated in the normal course of business. Which measurement basis is used?
optionA: Historical Cost
optionB: Current Cost
optionC: Present Value
optionD: Realisable Value
answerText: Present Value
explanation: Present value is a financial measurement basis under which assets are carried at the discounted present value of the future net cash inflows that the item is expected to generate in the normal course of business.
conceptTags: Present Value | Measurement Basis | Discounted Cash Flow

subject: Accounts
prompt: Entity Delta started business with capital of ₹2,00,000 on 1st April 2024. During FY 2024-25, the general price index increased by 15%. At year-end (31st March 2025), closing net assets were ₹2,50,000. Under Financial Capital Maintenance in Constant Purchasing Power units, what is Delta's profit?
optionD: Nil
explanation: Capital required to maintain constant purchasing power = ₹2,00,000 * 1.15 = ₹2,30,000. Profit = Closing Net Assets (₹2,50,000) - Adjusted Capital (₹2,30,000) = ₹20,00,000.
conceptTags: Constant Purchasing Power | Financial Capital Maintenance | Profit Determination

subject: Accounts
prompt: To be reliable, financial statement information must be complete within the bounds of:
optionA: Legal permissibility and taxation provisions.
optionB: Materiality and cost.
optionC: Statutory audit deadlines.
optionD: Management's discretionary judgment.
answerText: Materiality and cost.
explanation: To be reliable, the information in financial statements must be complete within the bounds of materiality and cost. An omission can cause information to be false or misleading and thus unreliable.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Entity Omega enters into a construction contract expected to generate losses of ₹8,00,000 due to severe structural modifications required mid-project. How should this loss be recognized under the Framework?
optionA: Deferred and written off upon final contract handover.
optionB: Recognized immediately as a provision/expense, as a present obligation with a probable economic outflow exists.
optionC: Disclosed solely as a note to the financial statements.
optionD: Capitalized as part of contract work-in-progress assets.
answerText: Recognized immediately as a provision/expense, as a present obligation with a probable economic outflow exists.
explanation: Under the Framework's liability and expense recognition principles, an onerous obligation where future costs exceed economic benefits represents a present liability and an immediate expense that must be recognized when probable and measurable.
conceptTags: Liability Recognition | Onerous Contracts | Expense Recognition

subject: Accounts
prompt: The consistency assumption requires that accounting policies are:
optionA: Never altered under any circumstances.
optionB: Applied consistently from one period to another, unless a change is required by law/AS or yields better presentation.
optionC: Identical to those followed by competitors in the same industry.
optionD: Updated annually to match changing tax regulations.
answerText: Applied consistently from one period to another, unless a change is required by law/AS or yields better presentation.
explanation: Consistency assumes that accounting policies are followed consistently from one period to another. Changes are permitted only if required by statute, for compliance with an accounting standard, or if it results in a more appropriate presentation.
conceptTags: Consistency | Fundamental Accounting Assumptions | Accounting Policy Changes

subject: Accounts
prompt: According to the Framework, financial statements present a 'true and fair view' when:
optionA: An unqualified audit report is issued by a Chartered Accountant.
optionB: Qualitative characteristics and applicable Accounting Standards are appropriately applied.
optionC: Zero tax disputes are pending with revenue authorities.
optionD: Positive net profits are recorded consistently every year.
answerText: Qualitative characteristics and applicable Accounting Standards are appropriately applied.
explanation: Financial statements are described as showing a true and fair view, or presenting fairly, if the principal qualitative characteristics are present and appropriate accounting standards are applied.
conceptTags: True and Fair View | Financial Statement Objective | Application of Standards

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under the Physical Capital Maintenance concept, price increases in held assets are accounted for as:
optionA: Realized operational gains in the Income Statement.
optionB: Extraordinary items in Profit and Loss.
optionC: Capital maintenance adjustments included directly in Equity.
optionD: Deferred revenue credits in liabilities.
answerText: Capital maintenance adjustments included directly in Equity.
explanation: Under physical capital maintenance, price increases on assets retained by the enterprise are treated as capital maintenance adjustments forming part of equity, rather than operational profit.
conceptTags: Physical Capital Maintenance | Holding Gains | Equity Adjustments

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which user group requires financial statement information to regulate enterprise activities, determine taxation policies, and compile national income statistics?
optionA: Public at large
optionB: Government and its agencies
optionC: Lenders and financial institutions
optionD: Employees and trade unions
answerText: Government and its agencies
explanation: Government and its agencies are interested in the allocation of resources and the activities of enterprises. They require information to regulate activities, establish taxation policies, and serve as the basis for national income and similar statistics.
conceptTags: Users of Financial Statements | Government and Agencies | Information Needs

subject: Accounts
prompt: When an item has strong relevance to decision-making but cannot be measured with acceptable reliability, the Framework dictates that the item should be:
optionA: Recognized in the balance sheet at a token value of Re. 1.
optionB: Excluded from financial balance recognition, but disclosed in explanatory notes if material.
optionC: Included in the Income Statement as an extraordinary expense.
optionD: Recognized using the highest possible subjective estimate.
answerText: Excluded from financial balance recognition, but disclosed in explanatory notes if material.
explanation: If an item meets the relevance test but fails the reliable measurement criterion, it cannot be recognized in the body of financial statements. However, disclosure in notes is appropriate when the item is relevant to user evaluation.
conceptTags: Reliability vs Relevance | Recognition Criteria | Note Disclosure

subject: Accounts
prompt: A trading firm holds inventory acquired for ₹1,00,000. Due to market decline, expected net realisable value drops to ₹70,000. At what amount should inventory be reported under the Framework?
explanation: Assets should not be carried at amounts exceeding expected economic benefits. Inventory measurement follows lower of cost and net realisable value, so it must be reported at ₹70,000, recognizing a ₹30,000 write-down.
conceptTags: Inventory Valuation | Realisable Value | Asset Recognition

subject: Accounts
prompt: Entity Gamma sells machinery carrying a book value of ₹5,00,000 for ₹3,80,000. The resulting ₹1,20,000 difference meets the Framework's definition of:
optionA: A capital deficit contribution by owners.
optionB: An expense, specifically a loss.
optionC: A long-term deferred liability.
optionD: A capital reserve charge.
answerText: An expense, specifically a loss.
explanation: Expenses encompass losses as well as expenses arising in the ordinary course of activity. A loss on disposal of non-current assets represents a decrease in economic benefits (and reduction in equity) not relating to distributions to owners.
conceptTags: Expense Definition | Losses | Elements of Financial Statements

subject: Accounts
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Enterprises began operations on 1st April 2024 with a financial capital of ₹20,00,000, represented by 2,000 units of Product A at ₹1,000 per unit. During FY 2024-25, Zenith sold all 2,000 units for ₹32,00,000 cash. During the year, the general price index rose from 100 to 125 (a 25% inflation rate). At the end of the year on 31st March 2025, the replacement cost of Product A rose to ₹1,400 per unit. Zenith made no equity contributions or withdrawals during the financial year.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the net profit earned by Zenith Enterprises under the Financial Capital Maintenance concept in nominal monetary units?
explanation: Under nominal monetary units, profit = Closing Net Assets (₹32,00,000) - Opening Capital (₹20,00,000) = ₹12,00,000.
conceptTags: Nominal Capital Maintenance | Profit Determination | Capital Maintenance

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the net profit earned by Zenith Enterprises under the Financial Capital Maintenance concept in Constant Purchasing Power units?
explanation: Inflation-adjusted opening capital = ₹20,00,000 * (125 / 100) = ₹25,00,000. Profit under constant purchasing power = Closing Net Assets (₹32,00,000) - Adjusted Capital (₹25,00,000) = ₹7,00,000.
conceptTags: Constant Purchasing Power | Financial Capital Maintenance | Inflation Accounting

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the net profit earned by Zenith Enterprises under the Physical Capital Maintenance concept?
explanation: Capital required to maintain physical productive capacity (2,000 units at ₹1,400 replacement cost) = ₹28,00,000. Profit = Closing Cash (₹32,00,000) - Physical Capital needed (₹28,00,000) = ₹4,00,000.
conceptTags: Physical Capital Maintenance | Operating Capability | Profit Determination

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under the Physical Capital Maintenance concept, how is the ₹8,00,000 price increase (from ₹20,00,000 opening cost to ₹28,00,000 replacement cost) recognized?
optionA: Credited to Profit and Loss as realized operating revenue.
optionB: Credited directly to Equity as a capital maintenance adjustment.
optionC: Debited to Profit and Loss as an extraordinary operating expense.
optionD: Recognized as a long-term deferred liability in the Balance Sheet.
answerText: Credited directly to Equity as a capital maintenance adjustment.
explanation: Under physical capital maintenance, holding gains resulting from price changes on assets are not treated as profit. Instead, they are recognized directly in equity as capital maintenance adjustments required to preserve productive capacity.
conceptTags: Physical Capital Maintenance | Equity Adjustments | Holding Gains

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Nova Technologies Ltd. is finalizing its financial statements for the year ended 31st March 2025. Management faces four distinct accounting dilemmas:
1. Nova spent ₹40,00,000 on preliminary research for a novel battery technology. Commercial viability is unproven.
2. Nova acquired high-end servers under a 5-year non-cancellable lease matching the total economic life of the servers. Nova incurs maintenance and risk, but legal title remains with the lessor until the final token payment in Year 5.
3. A former employee filed a legal suit claiming ₹60,00,000 for wrongful termination. Legal counsel estimates only a 15% probability that Nova will lose.
4. Nova spent ₹15,00,000 on general brand-building advertisements. While management expects long-term brand equity, future economic inflows cannot be isolated or measured reliably.

subject: Accounts
prompt: How should the research expenditure of ₹40,00,000 be treated under the Framework's asset recognition criteria?
optionA: Capitalized as an Intangible Asset in the Balance Sheet.
optionB: Expensed immediately in Profit and Loss.
optionC: Deferred and amortized over a 5-year period.
optionD: Deducted directly from Shareholder Equity reserves.
answerText: Expensed immediately in Profit and Loss.
explanation: Because commercial viability is unproven, future economic benefit flow is not probable. Under the Framework, if probability of economic inflow is absent, expenditure must be expensed immediately in Profit and Loss.
conceptTags: Asset Recognition Criteria | Research Expenditure | Probability Criterion

subject: Accounts
prompt: The server acquisition should be capitalized as an asset by Nova based on which key qualitative characteristic/principle?
optionA: Prudence
optionB: Substance over Form
optionC: Materiality
optionD: Timeliness
answerText: Substance over Form
explanation: Under 'substance over form', economic reality prevails over legal form. Since Nova assumes all economic risks and rewards for the full economic life, the servers are recognized as assets despite legal title remaining with the lessor.
conceptTags: Substance over Form | Qualitative Characteristics | Asset Recognition

subject: Accounts
prompt: How should the legal lawsuit of ₹60,00,000 (15% loss probability) be treated in Nova's financial statements?
optionA: Recognized as a Provision liability in the Balance Sheet.
optionB: Written off as an extraordinary loss in Profit and Loss.
optionC: Disclosed as a Contingent Liability in notes without balance sheet liability recognition.
optionD: Ignored entirely with no disclosure required.
answerText: Disclosed as a Contingent Liability in notes without balance sheet liability recognition.
explanation: A liability recognition requires a probable outflow of resources (greater than 50%). Since the loss probability is only 15% (not probable), it fails balance sheet liability recognition criteria and must be disclosed as a contingent liability in the notes.
conceptTags: Liability Recognition | Contingent Liability | Probability Assessment

subject: Accounts
prompt: Why are the ₹15,00,000 brand-building advertisement costs excluded from asset recognition?
optionA: Because advertisement cost is not physical property.
optionB: Because future economic benefits cannot be measured with reasonable reliability.
optionC: Because advertising violates the fundamental going concern assumption.
optionD: Because advertising is regulated under tax laws only.
answerText: Because future economic benefits cannot be measured with reasonable reliability.
explanation: An asset requires both probable future economic benefits and a cost/value that can be measured with reliability. General brand expenditure cannot be separately identified or measured reliably, failing the reliable measurement recognition criterion.

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Valence Manufacturing Ltd. holds four assets/liabilities at year-end (31st March 2025) and requires valuation guidance under the Framework:
- Asset 1: Raw Material 'M' purchased for ₹6,00,000. Replacement cost today is ₹5,10,000. Finished product made from 'M' will be sold at a price above cost.
- Asset 2: Finished Goods 'G' produced at cost of ₹10,00,000. Current market selling price is ₹9,20,000, with estimated selling costs of ₹50,000.
- Asset 3: Heavy Machinery purchased 4 years ago for ₹25,00,000 (carrying value ₹16,00,000). Current replacement cost of equivalent new machine is ₹20,00,000. Present value of expected future cash flows from continuing usage is ₹14,50,000.
- Obligation 4: Foreign supplier debt of $20,000 initially recorded at $1 = ₹75 (₹15,00,000). Closing exchange rate on 31st March 2025 is $1 = ₹83.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under the Framework and applicable valuation rules, at what value should Raw Material 'M' be reported?
explanation: Raw materials held for use in production are not written down below cost if the finished products in which they will be incorporated are expected to be sold at or above cost. Hence, Raw Material 'M' remains valued at historical cost ₹6,00,000.
conceptTags: Raw Material Valuation | Lower of Cost and NRV | Asset Measurement

subject: Accounts
prompt: At what value should Finished Goods 'G' be carried in the Balance Sheet?
explanation: Inventories are measured at lower of cost and net realisable value (NRV). NRV = Selling Price (₹9,20,000) - Selling Costs (₹50,000) = ₹8,70,000. Since NRV (₹8,70,000) is lower than cost (₹10,00,000), it is valued at ₹8,70,000.
conceptTags: Inventory NRV | Lower of Cost and NRV | Measurement Basis

subject: Accounts
prompt: What figure represents the Present Value measurement basis for Heavy Machinery (Asset 3)?
explanation: Present value is defined as the discounted present value of the future net cash inflows expected from the item in the normal course of business, which is explicitly given as ₹14,50,000.
conceptTags: Present Value | Measurement Basis | Asset Valuation

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under which measurement basis principle is Foreign Obligation 4 adjusted to ₹16,60,000 ($20,000 × ₹83) at year-end?
optionA: Historical Cost
optionB: Current Settlement Value at balance sheet date rates
optionC: Physical Capital Maintenance
optionD: Discounted Future Cash Flows
answerText: Current Settlement Value at balance sheet date rates
explanation: Settlement value reflects the undiscounted amount of cash required to discharge obligations at the reporting date. Adjusting foreign currency debt to closing spot rates measures the obligation at its current settlement value.
conceptTags: Settlement Value | Foreign Currency Obligation | Measurement Basis

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Aura Retail Ltd., a chain store, faces four accounting evaluation issues in preparing financial reports:
Issue A: Aura owns 5,00,000 low-value shopping baskets costing ₹10 each. Tracking individual depreciation across 500 stores would cost ₹12,00,000 in administrative systems. Aura proposes expensing them immediately.
Issue B: To beat competitors, management wants to publish financial results 5 days after year-end using unverified sales estimates rather than waiting 25 days for fully audited sales numbers.
Issue C: Aura changed its depreciation policy from Straight Line Method to Written Down Value Method purely to reduce reported profits and save manager bonuses, without any change in asset usage pattern or AS compliance.
Issue D: Management created a 'General Contingency Reserve' of ₹30,00,000 against vague future business risks, claiming compliance with 'prudence'.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Regarding Issue A (shopping baskets), which constraint justifies expensing these items immediately rather than tracking detailed depreciation?
optionA: Timeliness versus Reliability
optionB: Balance between Benefit and Cost
optionC: Substance over Form
optionD: Prudence versus Neutrality
answerText: Balance between Benefit and Cost
explanation: The balance between benefit and cost is a pervasive constraint. The benefits derived from tracking low-value items individually should exceed the cost of providing that detailed accounting info.
conceptTags: Benefit and Cost Constraint | Materiality | Qualitative Constraints

subject: Accounts
prompt: Issue B (early reporting using estimated figures) highlights a direct trade-off between which two qualitative attributes/constraints?
optionA: Timeliness and Reliability
optionB: Materiality and Relevance
optionC: Substance over Form and Prudence
optionD: Neutrality and Comparability
answerText: Timeliness and Reliability
explanation: Releasing results quickly enhances timeliness, but relying on unverified estimates compromises reliability. Management must balance timeliness with reliability to best satisfy economic decision-making needs.
conceptTags: Timeliness vs Reliability | Constraints | Reporting Trade-offs

subject: Accounts
prompt: Issue C (changing accounting policy to manipulate bonuses) violates which fundamental principle/assumption?
optionA: Going Concern
optionB: Consistency / Comparability
optionC: Accrual
optionD: Materiality
answerText: Consistency / Comparability
explanation: Consistency requires accounting policies to be applied uniformly over time. Arbitrary changes without justification (like better presentation or statutory requirement) violate consistency and comparability.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Does Issue D (vague contingency reserve) comply with the Framework's concept of 'Prudence'?
optionA: Yes, because prudence encourages anticipating all imaginable future operational risks.
optionB: No, because prudence does not permit the creation of hidden reserves or deliberate overstatement of liabilities/expenses.
optionC: Yes, provided it is authorized by the board of directors.
optionD: No, because prudence applies exclusively to assets, not provisions or liabilities.
answerText: No, because prudence does not permit the creation of hidden reserves or deliberate overstatement of liabilities/expenses.
explanation: Prudence does not permit the creation of hidden reserves or excessive provisions, as deliberate understatement of assets/income or overstatement of liabilities/expenses makes financial statements non-neutral and unreliable.

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Kestrel Logistics Ltd. suffered severe operational disruption in FY 2024-25. On 20th March 2025, its primary banking facility was withdrawn, and major clients terminated service contracts. On 31st March 2025, management determined that the entity has no realistic alternative but to cease operations and liquidate within 60 days.
Financial records at 31st March 2025 show:
- Transport Trucks: Original Historical Cost ₹1,00,000,000; Accumulated Depreciation ₹40,00,000; Realisable Value in forced liquidation ₹25,00,000.
- Warehouse Lease Agreement: Early termination penalty payable upon breach in April 2025 is ₹10,00,000.
- Outstanding Driver Salaries: ₹6,00,000 incurred for services rendered in March 2025.
- Spares Inventory: Cost ₹15,00,000; Realizable liquidation value ₹4,00,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which fundamental accounting assumption is invalidated for Kestrel Logistics Ltd. as of 31st March 2025?
optionA: Accrual
optionB: Consistency
optionC: Going Concern
optionD: Materiality
answerText: Going Concern
explanation: Since the entity is forced to liquidate within 60 days, it cannot continue operations for the foreseeable future. Thus, the Going Concern assumption is no longer valid.
conceptTags: Going Concern | Fundamental Accounting Assumptions | Liquidation Impact

subject: Accounts
prompt: At what amount should the Transport Trucks be carried on the Balance Sheet as of 31st March 2025?
optionA: ₹60,00,000 (Book Value)
optionB: ₹25,00,000 (Liquidation Value)
optionC: ₹100,00,000 (Historical Cost)
optionD: Nil
answerText: ₹25,00,000 (Liquidation Value)
explanation: When going concern is invalidated, assets cannot be carried at book values under normal historical cost assumptions. They must be written down to their net realisable / forced liquidation values (₹25,00,000).
conceptTags: Net Realisable Value | Liquidation Measurement Basis | Asset Valuation

subject: Accounts
prompt: How should the Warehouse Lease termination penalty of ₹10,00,000 be treated on 31st March 2025?
optionA: Ignored because the breach technically occurs in April 2025.
optionB: Recognized as a present liability/provision because liquidation is imminent.
optionC: Disclosed only as a non-quantifiable footnote.
optionD: Deferred and amortized over the original lease duration.
answerText: Recognized as a present liability/provision because liquidation is imminent.
explanation: Because liquidation is imminent, the termination of the lease becomes an unavoidable present obligation arising from current events, requiring immediate liability recognition on the liquidation basis.
conceptTags: Liability Recognition | Present Obligation | Liquidation Adjustments

subject: Accounts
prompt: At what value should Spares Inventory be reported in Kestrel's financial statements?
explanation: Under the net realisable / liquidation framework, inventories are written down to their immediate net liquidation value of ₹4,00,000.
conceptTags: Inventory Valuation | Realisable Value | Going Concern Invalidation

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the turnover threshold (excluding other income) for a non-corporate entity to be classified as a Level I entity as per ICAI guidelines?
optionA: Exceeds ₹50 crore
optionB: Exceeds ₹100 crore
optionC: Exceeds ₹250 crore
optionD: Exceeds ₹500 crore
answerText: Exceeds ₹250 crore
explanation: As per ICAI guidelines for applicability of Accounting Standards to non-corporate entities, Level I entities are large-sized entities. One of the criteria is that turnover (excluding other income) exceeds ₹250 crore in the immediately preceding accounting year.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, a company is NOT classified as a Small and Medium-Sized Company (SMC) if its borrowings (including public deposits) at any time during the immediately preceding accounting year exceed:
optionA: ₹10 crore
optionB: ₹25 crore
optionC: ₹50 crore
optionD: ₹100 crore
answerText: ₹50 crore
explanation: Under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, one of the essential conditions for an unlisted company to be an SMC is that its borrowings (including public deposits) do not exceed ₹50 crore at any time during the immediately preceding accounting year. If borrowings exceed ₹50 crore, the company is classified as a Non-SMC.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which standard-setting body was constituted by the ICAI in 1977 to formulate Accounting Standards in India?
optionA: National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA)
optionB: Accounting Standards Board (ASB)
optionC: Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA)
optionD: Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (AASB)
answerText: Accounting Standards Board (ASB)
explanation: The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) constituted the Accounting Standards Board (ASB) in 1977. ASB is responsible for formulating Accounting Standards to establish uniform accounting policies and practices in India.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under Section 2(40) of the Companies Act, 2013, which of the following corporate entities is explicitly exempted from preparing a Cash Flow Statement (AS 3)?
optionA: Any unlisted public company
optionB: One Person Company (OPC)
optionC: Listed company with turnover below ₹250 crore
optionD: Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC)
answerText: One Person Company (OPC)
explanation: Section 2(40) of the Companies Act, 2013 provides that the financial statements of a One Person Company (OPC), Small Company, Dormant Company, and recognized Startup private company need not include a Cash Flow Statement. Thus, OPC is statutorily exempted from preparing AS 3 Cash Flow Statement.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Non-corporate entities are categorized into how many levels by the ICAI for the purpose of applicability of Accounting Standards?
optionA: Two levels
optionB: Three levels
optionC: Four levels
optionD: Five levels
answerText: Four levels
explanation: ICAI revised the scheme for classification of non-corporate entities into four distinct levels: Level I (Large size), Level II (Medium size), Level III (Small size), and Level IV (Micro size). Differential relaxations and exemptions are prescribed based on these levels.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under which section of the Companies Act, 2013 does the Central Government prescribe Accounting Standards as recommended by ICAI and NFRA?
optionA: Section 129
optionB: Section 133
optionC: Section 134
optionD: Section 143
answerText: Section 133
