explanation: Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 empowers the Central Government to prescribe the standards of accounting or any addendum thereto, as recommended by ICAI and examined/recommended by NFRA.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the net worth threshold at or above which unlisted Indian companies are required to mandatorily comply with Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)?
optionA: ₹100 crore
optionB: ₹250 crore
optionC: ₹500 crore
optionD: ₹1,000 crore
answerText: ₹250 crore
explanation: Under the Ind AS roadmap issued by the MCA, all unlisted companies having a net worth of ₹250 crore or more are required to apply Ind AS. Unlisted companies below ₹250 crore net worth continue to apply Accounting Standards (AS).
conceptTags: Ind AS Applicability | Net Worth Threshold

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which of the following is NOT one of the three fundamental accounting assumptions specified in AS 1 'Disclosure of Accounting Policies'?
optionA: Going Concern
optionB: Consistency
optionC: Accrual
optionD: Prudence
answerText: Prudence
explanation: AS 1 specifies three fundamental accounting assumptions: Going Concern, Consistency, and Accrual. Prudence is a major consideration in selecting accounting policies, not a fundamental accounting assumption.

subject: Accounts
prompt: When a non-corporate entity moves from a higher level (Level I) to a lower level (Level II), for how many consecutive years must it satisfy the lower level criteria before it can claim relaxations of that lower level?
optionA: 1 year
optionB: 2 consecutive years
optionC: 3 consecutive years
optionD: No waiting period required
answerText: 2 consecutive years
explanation: An entity that drops from a higher level to a lower level must remain in the lower level for two consecutive years before it can avail the exemptions or relaxations available to that lower level. This prevents frequent status switching due to temporary operational fluctuations.

subject: Accounts
prompt: When a Level IV non-corporate entity migrates to Level I during a financial year because its borrowings cross ₹50 crore, when do its exemptions cease to apply?
optionA: Immediately in the current accounting year
optionB: After 2 consecutive years
optionC: From the next financial year only
optionD: At the discretion of management
answerText: Immediately in the current accounting year
explanation: If an entity moves from a lower level to a higher level, exemptions and relaxations previously enjoyed cease to apply immediately from the current accounting period in which the event causing reclassification occurs.

subject: Accounts
prompt: M/s Alpha Traders is a partnership firm. To be classified as a Level III non-corporate entity, its borrowings (including public deposits) during the immediately preceding accounting year must be:
optionA: Up to ₹2 crore
optionB: Exceeding ₹2 crore but not exceeding ₹10 crore
optionC: Exceeding ₹10 crore but not exceeding ₹50 crore
optionD: Exceeding ₹50 crore
answerText: Exceeding ₹2 crore but not exceeding ₹10 crore
explanation: Level III (Small size) non-corporate entities are those whose borrowings (including public deposits) exceed ₹2 crore but do not exceed ₹10 crore at any time during the immediately preceding accounting year (and turnover is > ₹10 crore up to ₹50 crore).

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the turnover limit range (excluding other income) for a non-corporate entity to be categorized as a Level II (Medium size) entity?
optionA: Exceeds ₹10 crore but does not exceed ₹50 crore
optionB: Exceeds ₹50 crore but does not exceed ₹250 crore
optionC: Exceeds ₹250 crore
optionD: Up to ₹10 crore
answerText: Exceeds ₹50 crore but does not exceed ₹250 crore
explanation: For Level II (Medium size) non-corporate entities, turnover (excluding other income) must exceed ₹50 crore but not exceed ₹250 crore in the immediately preceding accounting year.

subject: Accounts
prompt: How does AS 17 'Segment Reporting' apply to Level II non-corporate entities under ICAI guidelines?
optionA: Fully applicable without any exemption or relaxation
optionB: Completely exempted
optionC: Applicable only if listed on stock exchanges
optionD: Applicable with disclosure relaxations
answerText: Fully applicable without any exemption or relaxation
explanation: AS 17 Segment Reporting is fully applicable to Level I and Level II non-corporate entities without exemptions. Complete exemption from AS 17 is available only to Level III and Level IV non-corporate entities.

subject: Accounts
prompt: If a Small and Medium-Sized Company (SMC) opts to avail exemptions/relaxations available to it under Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, what specific disclosure must it make in its financial statements?
optionA: No special disclosure is needed
optionB: It must disclose by way of a note that it is an SMC and has complied with AS applicable to SMCs
optionC: It must present full reconciliations as if exemptions were not taken
optionD: It must obtain prior written approval from MCA and disclose the approval number
answerText: It must disclose by way of a note that it is an SMC and has complied with AS applicable to SMCs
explanation: An SMC that avails exemptions/relaxations must explicitly state in the notes to financial statements that it is an SMC and has complied with Accounting Standards applicable to Small and Medium-Sized Companies.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Zeta Ltd is an unlisted company with turnover of ₹15 crore and zero borrowings. However, it is a subsidiary of Omega Ltd, which is a Non-SMC. Can Zeta Ltd qualify as an SMC?
optionA: Yes, because its individual turnover is well within SMC limits
optionB: Yes, provided its shareholders pass a special resolution
optionC: No, because a subsidiary of a Non-SMC cannot be classified as an SMC
optionD: No, unless MCA grants a specific exemption
answerText: No, because a subsidiary of a Non-SMC cannot be classified as an SMC
explanation: Under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, a company that is a holding or subsidiary company of a Non-SMC entity cannot be classified as an SMC, regardless of its individual size or turnover.

subject: Accounts
prompt: According to the Framework for Preparation and Presentation of Financial Statements, under which measurement basis are assets recorded at the discounted present value of future net cash inflows?
optionA: Historical Cost
optionB: Current Cost
optionC: Realizable Value
optionD: Present Value
answerText: Present Value
explanation: Under the Present Value measurement basis, assets are carried at the discounted present value of the future net cash inflows that the item is expected to generate in the normal course of business.

subject: Accounts
prompt: With respect to AS 28 'Impairment of Assets', which specific relaxation is available to Level IV non-corporate entities?
optionA: Fully exempt from the entire standard AS 28
optionB: Exempt from calculating Value in Use using discounted cash flow models if reasonable estimate of net selling price is available
optionC: Allowed to ignore impairment losses completely
optionD: Exempt from recording impairment loss in profit or loss
answerText: Exempt from calculating Value in Use using discounted cash flow models if reasonable estimate of net selling price is available
explanation: Level IV non-corporate entities are granted relaxation in AS 28 whereby Value in Use can be estimated based on reasonable indications rather than complex discounted cash flow calculations if net selling price cannot be determined.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the maximum borrowing limit (including public deposits) at any time during the immediately preceding accounting year for an entity to qualify as a Level IV non-corporate entity?
optionA: Does not exceed ₹2 crore
optionB: Does not exceed ₹5 crore
optionC: Does not exceed ₹10 crore
optionD: Does not exceed ₹50 crore
answerText: Does not exceed ₹2 crore
explanation: Level IV (Micro size) non-corporate entities are entities whose turnover does not exceed ₹10 crore and borrowings (including public deposits) do not exceed ₹2 crore at any time during the immediately preceding accounting year.

subject: Accounts
prompt: When an SMC loses its SMC status and becomes a Non-SMC in the current year, how should it handle the financial figures of the comparative previous accounting period?
optionA: It must restate previous year figures fully as if it was a Non-SMC
optionB: Comparative figures need not be revised for exemptions enjoyed in previous year unless required by specific AS
optionC: It must re-audit previous year financial statements under Non-SMC rules
optionD: Comparative figures must be completely omitted from financial statements
answerText: Comparative figures need not be revised for exemptions enjoyed in previous year unless required by specific AS
explanation: When an SMC becomes a Non-SMC, comparative figures for the previous year need not be revised for exemptions enjoyed in the previous year, unless specific transitional provisions of individual Accounting Standards state otherwise.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Can a small private sector bank with turnover of ₹100 crore and borrowings of ₹20 crore qualify as an SMC under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules?
optionA: Yes, because turnover is below ₹250 crore
optionB: Yes, because borrowings are below ₹50 crore
optionC: No, because banks, financial institutions, and insurance companies are excluded from SMC definition regardless of size
optionD: Yes, if approved by the Reserve Bank of India
answerText: No, because banks, financial institutions, and insurance companies are excluded from SMC definition regardless of size
explanation: The definition of SMC explicitly excludes banks, financial institutions, and insurance companies regardless of their turnover or borrowing limits. Therefore, a bank can never qualify as an SMC.
conceptTags: SMC Criteria | Banks and Financial Institutions

subject: Accounts
prompt: According to the Framework, to be reliable, information in financial statements must be neutral, free from material error, complete, and:
optionA: Prepared strictly under historical cost
optionB: Represent faithfully the transactions and events it purports to represent
optionC: Audited by an independent chartered accountant
optionD: Approved by the Board of Directors
answerText: Represent faithfully the transactions and events it purports to represent
explanation: Under the Framework, information possesses the quality of reliability when it is free from material error and bias, and can be depended upon by users to represent faithfully that which it either purports to represent or could reasonably be expected to represent.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Level IV non-corporate entities enjoy which relaxation regarding defined benefit plans under AS 15 'Employee Benefits'?
optionA: Full exemption from recognizing liability for short-term benefits
optionB: Exemption from actuarial valuation for defined benefit plan liability using projected unit credit method, allowing simplified methods
optionC: Allowed to classify all employee costs as deferred revenue expenditure
optionD: Exempt from paying statutory provident fund
answerText: Exemption from actuarial valuation for defined benefit plan liability using projected unit credit method, allowing simplified methods
explanation: For defined benefit plans, Level IV non-corporate entities are exempt from using the Projected Unit Credit Method and actuarial valuation; they are allowed to measure liabilities using simplified methods (e.g., accrued liability without discounting).

subject: Accounts
prompt: Firm X (a partnership firm) has turnover of ₹5 crore and borrowings of ₹50 lakh. However, 80% of its equity interest is held by ABC Ltd, a listed corporate entity. What is the non-corporate entity level classification of Firm X?
optionA: Level IV
optionB: Level III
optionC: Level II
optionD: Level I
answerText: Level I
explanation: If a non-corporate entity is a holding or subsidiary entity of a Level I / Non-SMC entity (such as a listed company), it automatically gets classified as a Level I non-corporate entity, irrespective of its individual turnover and borrowing numbers.

subject: Accounts
prompt: For determining Level classification for FY 2025-26, an entity checks its figures of FY 2024-25. Turnover was ₹40 crore throughout. Borrowings were zero except for 2 days in Nov 2024 when a temporary bank overdraft reached ₹52 crore. The entity's classification for FY 2025-26 is:
optionA: Level IV, because overdraft was temporary
optionB: Level III, because average borrowings were below ₹10 crore
optionC: Level II, based on turnover criteria
optionD: Level I, because borrowings exceeded ₹50 crore 'at any time' during the preceding year
answerText: Level I, because borrowings exceeded ₹50 crore 'at any time' during the preceding year
explanation: The borrowing criterion test for entity classification requires checking if borrowings exceed the threshold (₹50 crore for Level I) 'at any time during the immediately preceding accounting year'. Since borrowings hit ₹52 crore for 2 days, it qualifies as Level I.
conceptTags: Borrowing Limit Test | Level I Criteria

subject: Accounts
prompt: A non-corporate entity was Level I in FY 2022-23. In FY 2023-24, its turnover dropped to ₹30 crore and borrowings to ₹1 crore (qualifying for Level III). In FY 2024-25, figures remained in Level III. Can it claim Level III relaxations for FY 2025-26?
optionA: No, it must wait 3 consecutive years
optionB: Yes, because it maintained Level III criteria for 2 consecutive years (FY 2023-24 & 2024-25)
optionC: No, because once Level I, exemptions are lost permanently
optionD: Yes, instantly from FY 2023-24 without waiting
answerText: Yes, because it maintained Level III criteria for 2 consecutive years (FY 2023-24 & 2024-25)
explanation: Under ICAI guidelines, when an entity drops from Level I to a lower level (Level III), it must maintain the criteria of the lower level for 2 consecutive accounting years (FY 23-24 and FY 24-25). Once satisfied, it can avail Level III relaxations in FY 2025-26.

subject: Accounts
prompt: M/s Green Enterprises is a Level IV non-corporate entity holding a 30% investment in an associate partnership firm. Is M/s Green Enterprises required to mandatorily prepare Consolidated Financial Statements under AS 23?
optionA: Yes, AS 23 is mandatory for all entities having associates
optionB: No, AS 23 applies only if the entity is required or elects to prepare Consolidated Financial Statements
optionC: Yes, but with disclosure relaxations
optionD: No, Level IV entities are banned from investing in associates
answerText: No, AS 23 applies only if the entity is required or elects to prepare Consolidated Financial Statements
explanation: AS 23 (Accounting for Investments in Associates in Consolidated Financial Statements) does not mandate preparation of Consolidated Financial Statements by itself. It applies only if the entity is required by statute/contract or voluntarily elects to prepare Consolidated Financial Statements.

subject: Accounts
prompt: An item that meets the definition of an 'Asset' under the Framework should be recognized in the financial statements if and only if:
optionA: It is owned legally by the enterprise and has historical cost
optionB: It is probable that future economic benefits will flow to the entity and the item has a cost or value that can be measured with reliability
optionC: Its fair value is greater than its book value
optionD: Management intends to hold it for more than 12 months
answerText: It is probable that future economic benefits will flow to the entity and the item has a cost or value that can be measured with reliability
explanation: Under the Framework, an item meeting the definition of an element (asset) should be recognized if: (a) it is probable that any future economic benefit associated with the item will flow to or from the entity; and (b) the item has a cost or value that can be measured with reliability.

subject: Accounts
prompt: An enterprise holds machinery. The amount of cash or cash equivalents that could currently be obtained by selling the asset in an orderly disposal is known as its:
optionA: Historical Cost
optionB: Current Cost
optionC: Realizable (Settlement) Value
optionD: Present Value
answerText: Realizable (Settlement) Value
explanation: Realizable value is defined in the Framework as the amount of cash or cash equivalents that could currently be obtained by selling an asset in an orderly disposal.

subject: Accounts
prompt: M/s Apex Traders is a Level II non-corporate sole proprietorship firm. Does AS 20 'Earnings Per Share' apply to it?
optionA: Yes, fully applicable including diluted EPS
optionB: Applicable with disclosure relaxations for Diluted EPS
optionC: Exempted entirely, as AS 20 applies only to corporate entities having share capital
optionD: Mandatory only if turnover exceeds ₹100 crore
answerText: Exempted entirely, as AS 20 applies only to corporate entities having share capital
explanation: AS 20 Earnings Per Share applies only to entities whose equity shares or potential equity shares are listed or in process of listing, and to corporate entities. Non-corporate entities do not have share capital, so AS 20 is completely non-applicable to them.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under Section 2(40) of the Companies Act, 2013, a private company recognized as a 'startup' by DPIIT is exempt from preparing which component of financial statements?
optionA: Balance Sheet
optionB: Profit and Loss Account
optionC: Cash Flow Statement
optionD: Notes to Accounts
answerText: Cash Flow Statement
explanation: The proviso to Section 2(40) of Companies Act, 2013 explicitly grants exemption from preparing Cash Flow Statement to One Person Companies, Small Companies, Dormant Companies, and recognized Private Startup companies.

subject: Accounts
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Vidyut Tech Ltd is an unlisted public company incorporated in India. For FY 2024-25, its turnover was ₹220 crore, and it maintained a short-term working capital loan from a bank of ₹42 crore throughout the year. On 15th March 2025, it temporarily took a bridge loan of ₹10 crore, taking total borrowings to ₹52 crore for 5 days before repaying it on 20th March 2025. Vidyut Tech Ltd holds a 100% subsidiary company, Spark Cables Pvt Ltd, which has a turnover of ₹12 crore and borrowings of ₹1 crore. Neither company is in the process of listing. Management is evaluating SMC status for both companies for FY 2025-26 and assessing compliance requirements under AS 3 and AS 17.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the classification status of Vidyut Tech Ltd for FY 2025-26 under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules?
optionA: SMC, because average borrowings were below ₹50 crore
optionB: Non-SMC, because total borrowings exceeded ₹50 crore at a point in FY 2024-25
optionC: SMC, because turnover was below ₹250 crore
optionD: Non-SMC, solely because it is a public company
answerText: Non-SMC, because total borrowings exceeded ₹50 crore at a point in FY 2024-25
explanation: Borrowings crossed ₹50 crore (reaching ₹52 crore) during FY 2024-25 'at any time'. Therefore, Vidyut Tech Ltd fails the borrowing limit criterion of SMC (<= ₹50 crore) and is classified as a Non-SMC for FY 2025-26.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Can Spark Cables Pvt Ltd be classified as an SMC for FY 2025-26?
optionA: Yes, because its individual turnover and borrowings are within SMC limits
optionB: No, because its holding company (Vidyut Tech Ltd) is a Non-SMC
optionC: Yes, if its Board passes a resolution
optionD: No, because all subsidiaries of public companies are Non-SMCs
answerText: No, because its holding company (Vidyut Tech Ltd) is a Non-SMC
explanation: Under Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, an entity cannot be classified as an SMC if it is a holding or subsidiary company of a Non-SMC entity. Since holding company Vidyut Tech Ltd is a Non-SMC, Spark Cables Pvt Ltd becomes a Non-SMC.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Is Vidyut Tech Ltd required to present Segment Reporting under AS 17 for FY 2025-26?
optionA: No, AS 17 applies only to listed companies
optionB: Yes, AS 17 is fully applicable to Non-SMCs
optionC: No, because turnover is less than ₹250 crore
optionD: Yes, but with disclosure relaxations
answerText: Yes, AS 17 is fully applicable to Non-SMCs
explanation: AS 17 Segment Reporting is fully applicable to all Non-SMC companies (both listed and unlisted) without any exemption.

subject: Accounts
prompt: If Spark Cables Pvt Ltd qualifies as a 'Small Company' under Section 2(85) of Companies Act 2013, is it required to prepare a Cash Flow Statement for statutory compliance under the Act?
optionA: Yes, because it is a Non-SMC under AS Rules
optionB: No, Small Companies are exempted from Cash Flow Statement under Section 2(40) of Companies Act 2013
optionC: Yes, because AS 3 overrides Companies Act provisions
optionD: No, only if turnover is below ₹2 crore
answerText: No, Small Companies are exempted from Cash Flow Statement under Section 2(40) of Companies Act 2013
explanation: Under Section 2(40) of the Companies Act, 2013, financial statements of a 'Small Company' need not include a Cash Flow Statement. The statutory exemption under the Act prevails for filing requirements.

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: M/s Apex & Co. is a partnership firm engaged in wholesale trading. Its financial indicators over recent years are as follows:
- FY 2022-23: Turnover ₹260 crore, Borrowings ₹60 crore (Classified as Level I for FY 2023-24).
- FY 2023-24: Turnover ₹180 crore, Borrowings ₹35 crore (Meets Level II criteria).
- FY 2024-25: Turnover ₹160 crore, Borrowings ₹30 crore (Meets Level II criteria).
- FY 2025-26: Turnover ₹40 crore, Borrowings ₹8 crore (Meets Level III criteria).
The firm wants to determine its Level classification for FY 2024-25, FY 2025-26, and FY 2026-27, and understand when it can avail relaxations/exemptions available to lower levels.

subject: Accounts
prompt: For FY 2024-25, can M/s Apex & Co. avail exemptions/relaxations available to Level II non-corporate entities?
optionA: Yes, immediately in FY 2024-25
optionB: No, because FY 2023-24 was the 1st year of meeting Level II criteria, and 2 consecutive years are required
optionC: Yes, because turnover fell below ₹250 crore
optionD: No, partnership firms cannot claim Level II exemptions
answerText: No, because FY 2023-24 was the 1st year of meeting Level II criteria, and 2 consecutive years are required
explanation: When an entity drops from a higher level (Level I) to a lower level (Level II), it must satisfy the lower level criteria for two consecutive accounting years before claiming lower level relaxations. FY 2024-25 is only the 1st year after dropping, so relaxations cannot be availed in FY 2024-25.

subject: Accounts
prompt: For FY 2025-26, which Level status relaxations can M/s Apex & Co. claim, given it met Level II criteria in both FY 2023-24 and FY 2024-25?
optionA: Level I rules apply with no relaxations
optionB: Level II relaxations, as it completed 2 consecutive years meeting Level II criteria
optionC: Level III relaxations, instantly
optionD: Level IV relaxations
answerText: Level II relaxations, as it completed 2 consecutive years meeting Level II criteria
explanation: Having satisfied Level II criteria for two consecutive years (FY 2023-24 and FY 2024-25), M/s Apex & Co. can claim Level II exemptions/relaxations in FY 2025-26.

subject: Accounts
prompt: In FY 2026-27, what is the level criteria evaluation of M/s Apex & Co. based on FY 2025-26 figures (Turnover ₹40 cr, Borrowings ₹8 cr)?
optionA: It meets Level III criteria
optionB: It meets Level I criteria
optionC: It meets Level IV criteria
optionD: It meets Level II criteria
answerText: It meets Level III criteria
explanation: For Level III classification, turnover is between ₹10 cr and ₹50 cr, and borrowings are between ₹2 cr and ₹10 cr. FY 2025-26 figures (Turnover ₹40 cr, Borrowings ₹8 cr) meet Level III criteria.

subject: Accounts
prompt: If M/s Apex & Co. takes fresh bank loans in October 2026 raising total borrowings to ₹55 crore during FY 2026-27, how does its status change for FY 2026-27?
optionA: It becomes Level I immediately for FY 2026-27 and loses all exemptions
optionB: It remains Level II till the end of the year
optionC: It must wait 2 years before becoming Level I
optionD: No effect until next financial year
answerText: It becomes Level I immediately for FY 2026-27 and loses all exemptions
explanation: When an entity migrates from a lower level to a higher level (Level I), exemptions and relaxations cease to apply immediately from the current financial year in which the threshold is exceeded.

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Reliable Goods Ltd is evaluating several accounting treatments under the ICAI 'Framework for the Preparation and Presentation of Financial Statements':
1. Item A: Machinery purchased 3 years ago for ₹50 lakh. Current replacement cost is ₹70 lakh; cash realizable on immediate sale is ₹40 lakh; present value of net future cash flows is ₹45 lakh.
2. Item B: Internal R&D expenditure of ₹15 lakh incurred in developing a new software process. Ultimate economic benefits are uncertain.
3. Item C: A legal claim against the company of ₹20 lakh where loss is probable and can be measured reliably.
The CFO wants to know the appropriate measurement bases and recognition criteria applicable under the Framework.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under the Framework, if Item A (Machinery) is measured at ₹70 lakh (the amount of cash required to purchase the same asset currently), which measurement basis is being applied?
optionA: Historical Cost
optionB: Current Cost
optionC: Realizable Value
optionD: Present Value
answerText: Current Cost
explanation: Current Cost is defined as the amount of cash or cash equivalents that would have to be paid if the same or an equivalent asset were acquired currently.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under the Framework, why should Item B (Internal R&D expenditure with uncertain benefits) NOT be recognized as an asset in the Balance Sheet?
optionA: Because it has no historical cost
optionB: Because it fails the recognition criterion of probable future economic benefits
optionC: Because intangible assets are strictly banned under Framework
optionD: Because cash has already been paid
answerText: Because it fails the recognition criterion of probable future economic benefits
explanation: An asset is recognized in the balance sheet when it is probable that future economic benefits will flow to the entity and the asset has a cost or value that can be measured reliably. Uncertainty of benefits fails the probability test.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under the Framework, Item C (probable legal claim of ₹20 lakh) satisfies the definition of a liability. Which qualitative characteristic ensures liabilities are recognized without understating them?
optionA: Prudence as part of Reliability
optionB: Timeliness
optionC: Materiality
optionD: Understandability
answerText: Prudence as part of Reliability
explanation: Prudence is the inclusion of a degree of caution in the exercise of judgments, ensuring assets/income are not overstated and liabilities/expenses are not understated, maintaining reliability.

subject: Accounts
prompt: If Item A (Machinery) is shown at ₹40 lakh (cash obtainable by selling in an orderly disposal), which measurement basis is being used?
optionA: Historical Cost
optionB: Present Value
optionC: Realizable (Settlement) Value
optionD: Current Cost
answerText: Realizable (Settlement) Value
explanation: Realizable value is the amount of cash or cash equivalents that could currently be obtained by selling an asset in an orderly disposal.

subject: Accounts
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s Precision Engineering is a sole proprietorship non-corporate entity engaged in small-scale machining. For FY 2024-25, its turnover was ₹4 crore and bank borrowings were ₹50 lakh. It has zero listed securities and no group entities. The proprietor is reviewing compliance for Accounting Standards and seeks advice on exemptions available for Level IV entities regarding AS 3 (Cash Flow Statement), AS 17 (Segment Reporting), AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures), and AS 28 (Impairment of Assets).

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the classification level of M/s Precision Engineering for FY 2025-26 under ICAI non-corporate entity guidelines?
optionA: Level I
optionB: Level II
optionC: Level III
optionD: Level IV
answerText: Level IV
explanation: Turnover <= ₹10 crore (actual ₹4 cr) and Borrowings <= ₹2 crore (actual ₹50 lakh) classify M/s Precision Engineering as a Level IV (Micro size) non-corporate entity.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Is M/s Precision Engineering required to comply with AS 3 (Cash Flow Statement) and AS 17 (Segment Reporting)?
optionA: Fully required for both AS 3 and AS 17
optionB: Exempt from AS 17, but mandatory for AS 3
optionC: Exempt from AS 3, but mandatory for AS 17
optionD: Exempt from both AS 3 and AS 17
answerText: Exempt from both AS 3 and AS 17
explanation: Level IV non-corporate entities are completely exempt from both AS 3 (Cash Flow Statement) and AS 17 (Segment Reporting).

subject: Accounts
prompt: Regarding AS 18 'Related Party Disclosures', what exemption is available to Level IV non-corporate entities?
optionA: Fully exempt from AS 18
optionB: Must comply with full disclosures without relaxation
optionC: Exempt from AS 18 only if turnover is below ₹1 crore
optionD: Exempt from disclosing key management personnel remuneration only
answerText: Fully exempt from AS 18
explanation: Level IV non-corporate entities are fully exempt from AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures).

subject: Accounts
prompt: Regarding AS 28 'Impairment of Assets', what relaxation is granted to Level IV non-corporate entities regarding 'Value in Use'?
optionA: They are completely exempt from AS 28
optionB: They can estimate Value in Use based on reasonable indication without using present value discount techniques
optionC: They are not allowed to recognize impairment losses
optionD: They must use a mandatory 15% discount rate
answerText: They can estimate Value in Use based on reasonable indication without using present value discount techniques
explanation: Level IV non-corporate entities are granted relaxation in AS 28 whereby Value in Use can be estimated based on reasonable indications rather than complex discounted cash flow calculations.

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Global Spectrum Group consists of multiple corporate and non-corporate entities in India:
1. Spectrum India Ltd: Unlisted public company with Net Worth of ₹320 crore as on 31st March 2025.
2. Spectrum Infra Pvt Ltd: Unlisted subsidiary of Spectrum India Ltd, Net Worth ₹40 crore.
3. Spectrum Retail LLP: Non-corporate partnership entity with turnover ₹600 crore, borrowings ₹80 crore.
4. Spectrum Finance Ltd: Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC), unlisted, Net Worth ₹180 crore.
The board is determining whether Accounting Standards (AS) or Ind AS applies to each group entity for FY 2025-26.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which accounting standard framework applies to Spectrum India Ltd for FY 2025-26?
optionA: Accounting Standards (AS)
optionB: Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)
optionC: IFRS directly
optionD: US GAAP
answerText: Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)
explanation: Unlisted companies having a Net Worth of ₹250 crore or more are mandatorily required to follow Ind AS. Since Spectrum India Ltd has a Net Worth of ₹320 crore, Ind AS applies.
conceptTags: Ind AS Roadmap | Net Worth Criteria

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which accounting framework applies to Spectrum Infra Pvt Ltd (unlisted subsidiary of Spectrum India Ltd)?
optionA: Accounting Standards (AS) because its individual Net Worth is below ₹250 crore
optionB: Ind AS, because holding company Spectrum India Ltd is covered under Ind AS
optionC: SMC Accounting Standards
optionD: Level II Non-corporate standards
answerText: Ind AS, because holding company Spectrum India Ltd is covered under Ind AS
explanation: Under the Ind AS roadmap, holding, subsidiary, joint venture, or associate companies of an entity covered under Ind AS must also adopt Ind AS, regardless of their individual net worth.
conceptTags: Ind AS Subsidiary Propagation | Ind AS Roadmap

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which accounting standards framework applies to Spectrum Retail LLP (non-corporate LLP)?
optionA: Ind AS, because turnover exceeds ₹500 crore
optionB: Accounting Standards (AS) issued by ICAI (as a Level I non-corporate entity)
optionC: Ind AS, because it belongs to a group following Ind AS
optionD: No accounting standards apply to LLPs
answerText: Accounting Standards (AS) issued by ICAI (as a Level I non-corporate entity)
explanation: Ind AS roadmap applies exclusively to corporate entities (companies, NBFCs, Banks, Insurance). Non-corporate entities (LLPs/firms) follow Accounting Standards (AS) issued by ICAI, categorized here as Level I due to turnover > ₹250 crore.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which framework applies to Spectrum Finance Ltd (unlisted NBFC with Net Worth ₹180 crore)?
optionA: Ind AS
optionB: Accounting Standards (AS) prescribed under Companies (AS) Rules
optionC: Ind AS mandatorily regardless of net worth
optionD: Direct IFRS compliance
answerText: Accounting Standards (AS) prescribed under Companies (AS) Rules
explanation: Unlisted NBFCs with Net Worth below ₹250 crore are not covered under mandatory Ind AS phase and must follow Accounting Standards (AS) prescribed under Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules.
conceptTags: NBFC Ind AS Roadmap | Accounting Standards

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which of the following is NOT recognized as a Fundamental Accounting Assumption under AS 1 (Disclosure of Accounting Policies)?
optionA: Going Concern
optionB: Consistency
optionC: Prudence
optionD: Accrual
answerText: Prudence
explanation: AS 1 explicitly identifies Going Concern, Consistency, and Accrual as the three Fundamental Accounting Assumptions. Prudence is a major consideration in selecting and applying accounting policies, not a fundamental accounting assumption. Therefore, Prudence is the correct answer.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 1, if all fundamental accounting assumptions are followed in the preparation of financial statements, what disclosure is required?
optionA: A specific disclosure is required in the notes to accounts stating that all fundamental assumptions were followed.
optionB: No specific disclosure is required.
optionC: Disclosure is required only in the Director's Report.
optionD: Disclosure is required only if the enterprise is a listed entity.
answerText: No specific disclosure is required.
explanation: According to AS 1, fundamental accounting assumptions are presumed to have been followed in financial statements. Specific disclosure is required only if a fundamental accounting assumption is NOT followed. Hence, no specific disclosure is needed when they are followed.

subject: Accounts
prompt: According to AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures), which of the following relationships automatically constitutes a related party relationship?
optionA: A single major customer who accounts for 85% of total sales
optionB: Key Management Personnel (KMP) of the enterprise
optionC: A provider of finance who exercises normal restrictive covenants
optionD: A trade union representing 90% of the workforce
answerText: Key Management Personnel (KMP) of the enterprise
explanation: AS 18 explicitly covers Key Management Personnel (KMP) and their relatives as related parties. Major customers, providers of finance, and trade unions are explicitly excluded from being considered related parties merely by virtue of their normal dealings.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which of the following persons is EXCLUDED from the definition of 'relative' of an individual under AS 18?
optionA: Spouse
optionB: Brother or Sister
optionC: Grandparent
optionD: Son or Daughter
answerText: Grandparent
explanation: Under AS 18, 'relative' in relation to an individual means the spouse, son, daughter, brother, sister, father, and mother who are expected to influence, or be influenced by, that individual in dealings with the enterprise. Grandparents are not included in this definition.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 20 (Earnings Per Share), how should bonus shares issued during the financial year be treated in the calculation of Weighted Average Number of Equity Shares (WANES)?
optionA: Weighted from the actual date of issue of the bonus shares
optionB: Treated as if they were issued at the beginning of the earliest period reported
optionC: Weighted for 6 months irrespective of the date of issue
optionD: Ignored for Basic EPS and included only for Diluted EPS
answerText: Treated as if they were issued at the beginning of the earliest period reported
explanation: AS 20 specifies that in case of a bonus issue, equity shares are issued without additional consideration. Therefore, they are treated as if they had been issued at the beginning of the earliest period reported, adjusting WANES retrospectively.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the basic formula for calculating Basic Earnings Per Share under AS 20?
optionA: Net Profit before Tax / Total Number of Equity Shares issued
optionB: Net Profit or Loss for the period attributable to Equity Shareholders / Weighted Average Number of Equity Shares outstanding during the period
optionC: (Net Profit after Tax + Non-controlling Interest) / Weighted Average Number of Equity Shares
optionD: Operating Profit / Total Paid-up Equity Share Capital
answerText: Net Profit or Loss for the period attributable to Equity Shareholders / Weighted Average Number of Equity Shares outstanding during the period
explanation: AS 20 defines Basic EPS as Net Profit or Loss for the period attributable to equity shareholders divided by the Weighted Average Number of Equity Shares outstanding during the period. Numerator must be after deducting preference dividends and tax.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which of the following events triggers the 'Initial Disclosure Event' for a discontinuing operation under AS 24?
optionA: When the enterprise decides in an informal meeting to shut down a segment
optionB: Whichever occurs EARLIER: entering into a binding sale agreement OR board approval of a detailed formal plan and making a public announcement
optionC: Whichever occurs LATER: entering into a binding sale agreement OR board approval of a detailed formal plan and making a public announcement
optionD: When the actual transfer of all assets of the discontinuing segment is completed
answerText: Whichever occurs EARLIER: entering into a binding sale agreement OR board approval of a detailed formal plan and making a public announcement
explanation: AS 24 defines the Initial Disclosure Event as the earlier of two events: (a) the enterprise entering into a binding sale agreement for substantially all assets of the discontinuing operation, or (b) approval by the board of a detailed formal plan and making a public announcement.
conceptTags: AS 24 | Initial Disclosure Event | Discontinuing Operations

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 24, a discontinuing operation is a component of an enterprise that represents:
optionA: Any small product line that is being phased out
optionB: A separate major line of business or geographical area of operations
optionC: A temporary suspension of factory operations due to strike
optionD: Sale of individual obsolete machinery in the ordinary course of business
answerText: A separate major line of business or geographical area of operations
explanation: AS 24 requires that a discontinuing operation must represent a separate major line of business or geographical area of operations that can be distinguished operationally and for financial reporting purposes pursuant to a single plan.

subject: Accounts
prompt: According to AS 18, transactions with which of the following entities are exempt from disclosure requirements in the financial statements of state-controlled enterprises?
optionA: Key Management Personnel of the state-controlled enterprise
optionB: Other state-controlled enterprises
optionC: Private limited subsidiaries of the state-controlled enterprise
optionD: Foreign joint ventures of the state-controlled enterprise
answerText: Other state-controlled enterprises
explanation: AS 18 explicitly provides an exemption to state-controlled enterprises from disclosing related party transactions with other state-controlled enterprises. However, disclosures of transactions with KMP or non-state-controlled entities remain applicable.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Potential equity shares are considered 'anti-dilutive' under AS 20 when their conversion into equity shares would:
optionA: Decrease Earnings Per Share from continuing ordinary operations
optionB: Increase Earnings Per Share from continuing ordinary operations
optionC: Have zero effect on Earnings Per Share
optionD: Reduce Loss Per Share from continuing ordinary operations
answerText: Increase Earnings Per Share from continuing ordinary operations
explanation: Under AS 20, potential equity shares are anti-dilutive when their conversion would result in an increase in earnings per share (or a decrease in loss per share) from continuing ordinary operations. Anti-dilutive potential shares are excluded from Diluted EPS.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Alpha Ltd changes its method of charging depreciation from Straight Line Method (SLM) to Written Down Value (WDV) method for all plant items to better reflect the pattern of economic benefits. Under AS 1, how should this change be disclosed?
optionA: No disclosure is required as depreciation is an accounting estimate, not a policy.
optionB: The change, reason for change, and its financial effect on current period profit must be disclosed.
optionC: It must be disclosed retrospectively by adjusting opening retained earnings without disclosure in notes.
optionD: Only the total accumulated depreciation amount needs to be disclosed.
answerText: The change, reason for change, and its financial effect on current period profit must be disclosed.
explanation: A change in accounting policy or accounting treatment (such as method of depreciation reflecting economic benefit consumption) requires disclosure of the change, reasons for the change, and the financial impact on current period financial statements under AS 1.

subject: Accounts
prompt: An enterprise presents financial statements where 'Substance over Form' was prioritized over technical legal form in recording a lease transaction. Which Accounting Standard governs this overarching principle of policy selection?
optionA: AS 1 (Disclosure of Accounting Policies)
optionB: AS 19 (Leases)
optionC: AS 5 (Net Profit or Loss for the Period)
optionD: AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures)
answerText: AS 1 (Disclosure of Accounting Policies)
explanation: AS 1 lays down the primary considerations for selection and application of accounting policies, which are Prudence, Substance over Form, and Materiality.
conceptTags: AS 1 | Substance over Form | Policy Considerations

subject: Accounts
prompt: Company A holds 22% of the voting power in Company B. During the year ended 31st March 2025, Company B sold goods to Company A worth ₹15 Lakhs. No transactions occurred between them in the prior year. Under AS 18, how should Company B disclose this in its financial statements?
optionA: No disclosure required as 22% voting power only represents significant influence and not control.
optionB: Disclosure of related party relationship name, nature of relationship, and details of transaction (amount & outstanding balance) is mandatory.
optionC: Only the name of Company A needs to be disclosed without transaction amounts.
optionD: Disclosure is required only in Consolidated Financial Statements, not Standalone Financial Statements.
answerText: Disclosure of related party relationship name, nature of relationship, and details of transaction (amount & outstanding balance) is mandatory.
explanation: Holding 20% or more voting power creates significant influence under AS 18. When related party transactions take place during the period, disclosure of the relationship, description of transaction, volume/amount, and outstanding balances is mandatory in standalone FS.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Director X is a Director in both Company P and Company Q. Director X holds 1% equity shares in Company P and 2% equity shares in Company Q, and cannot direct the policies of either enterprise. Are Company P and Company Q related parties under AS 18?
optionA: Yes, because they have a common director.
optionB: No, mere common directorship without ability to affect transactions does not make enterprises related parties.
optionC: Yes, because Director X holds equity shares in both companies.
optionD: Yes, provided transactions exceed ₹10 Lakhs.
answerText: No, mere common directorship without ability to affect transactions does not make enterprises related parties.
explanation: AS 18 specifically states that two enterprises are not related parties simply because they have a director in common, unless the director is able to affect the policies of both enterprises in their mutual dealings.
conceptTags: AS 18 | Common Directorship | Related Party Exclusions

subject: Accounts
prompt: If a control relationship exists between Holding Co and Subsidiary Co, but NO transactions took place between them during the financial year, what is the requirement under AS 18?
optionA: No disclosure is required because no transactions took place.
optionB: The reporting enterprise must disclose the name of the related party and the nature of the related party relationship.
optionC: Disclosure is required only if requested by auditors.
optionD: Disclosure is required only if the holding company is a foreign entity.
answerText: The reporting enterprise must disclose the name of the related party and the nature of the related party relationship.
explanation: Under AS 18, where CONTROL exists between parties, disclosure of the related party relationship (name and nature) is mandatory irrespective of whether any transactions took place between them during the year.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Beta Ltd had 100,000 equity shares outstanding on 1st April 2024. It issued 20,000 equity shares for cash on 1st October 2024. Net profit after tax for the year ended 31st March 2025 is ₹11,000,000. Calculate Basic EPS under AS 20.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Gamma Ltd had 200,000 equity shares outstanding on 1st April 2024. On 1st January 2025, the company executed a share split, dividing each existing equity share of ₹10 into 2 equity shares of ₹5 each. What is the WANES for calculating Basic EPS for the year ended 31st March 2025?
optionA: 250,000 shares
optionB: 400,000 shares
optionC: 200,000 shares
optionD: 300,000 shares
answerText: 400,000 shares
explanation: A share split increases the number of equity shares without additional consideration. Under AS 20, a share split is treated as if it occurred at the beginning of the earliest period reported. Thus, total shares = 200,000 * 2 = 400,000 shares for the entire year.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 20, when calculating Diluted EPS, what adjustment is required in the numerator (Net Profit attributable to equity shareholders) for convertible debentures?
optionA: Deduct interest on debentures net of tax effect
optionB: Add back interest on debentures net of tax effect
optionC: Add back interest on debentures without adjusting tax effect
optionD: No adjustment to numerator, only denominator is adjusted
answerText: Add back interest on debentures net of tax effect
explanation: If convertible debentures are converted into equity shares, the company saves interest expense on those debentures. Hence, for Diluted EPS, the interest expense saved (net of attributable tax effect) is added back to the net profit attributable to equity shareholders.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Delta Ltd reported Basic EPS of ₹15.00 for FY 2023-24 (WANES was 1,000,000 shares). On 1st July 2024, Delta Ltd issued 1 bonus share for every 1 existing share held (1:1 bonus issue). What is the restated Basic EPS for FY 2023-24 to be presented in the comparative column of FY 2024-25 financial statements?
explanation: Under AS 20, if bonus shares are issued, the Basic EPS for all prior periods presented must be restated. Restated WANES for FY 2023-24 = 1,000,000 * 2 = 2,000,000 shares. Restated EPS = Original EPS / 2 = ₹15.00 / 2 = ₹7.50.
conceptTags: AS 20 | Restatement of EPS | Comparative Figures

subject: Accounts
prompt: On 15th December 2024, the Board of Directors of Apex Ltd approved a detailed formal plan to dispose of its Fertilizer Division. On 20th January 2025, a formal public announcement of the plan was made. On 10th February 2025, a binding sale agreement was signed. What is the date of the Initial Disclosure Event under AS 24?
optionA: 15th December 2024
optionB: 20th January 2025
optionC: 10th February 2025
optionD: 31st March 2025
answerText: 20th January 2025
explanation: Initial Disclosure Event is the EARLIER of (a) entering into a binding sale agreement (10th Feb 2025) or (b) board approval of detailed formal plan AND making a public announcement (20th Jan 2025). Approval plus announcement occurred on 20th January 2025, which is earlier than 10th February 2025.

subject: Accounts
prompt: How should cash flows attributable to operating, investing, and financing activities of a discontinuing operation be presented under AS 24?
optionA: They should be combined with continuing operations without separate disclosure.
optionB: Net cash flows attributable to operating, investing, and financing activities of the discontinuing operation must be disclosed separately on the face of cash flow statement or in notes.
optionC: Only operating cash flows of discontinuing operations need disclosure.
optionD: Cash flow disclosure is optional under AS 24.
answerText: Net cash flows attributable to operating, investing, and financing activities of the discontinuing operation must be disclosed separately on the face of cash flow statement or in notes.
explanation: AS 24 requires disclosure of the net cash flows attributable to the operating, investing, and financing activities of the discontinuing operation either on the face of the cash flow statement or in the notes to financial statements.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Company ABC changed its valuation of inventory from FIFO to Weighted Average Cost method. The change resulted in a decrease in current year profit by ₹8 Lakhs, but the effect on future years is not determinable. What is the appropriate disclosure requirement under AS 1?
optionA: Disclose only the change in policy without any monetary quantification.
optionB: Disclose the change in policy, reasons for change, current year impact of ₹8 Lakhs reduction in profit, and state that future impact is not determinable.
optionC: No disclosure is needed since future impact is unknown.
optionD: Restate prior year financial statements to show Weighted Average Cost.
answerText: Disclose the change in policy, reasons for change, current year impact of ₹8 Lakhs reduction in profit, and state that future impact is not determinable.
explanation: Under AS 1, any change in accounting policy having a material effect must be disclosed along with monetary impact. If the effect on future periods is not ascertainable, that fact must be explicitly stated in the financial statements.
conceptTags: AS 1 | Accounting Policy Change | Unascertainable Future Impact

subject: Accounts
prompt: Holding Ltd owns 60% of Sub Ltd. Sub Ltd owns 40% of Assoc Ltd. Holding Ltd directly holds 10% of Assoc Ltd. How is Assoc Ltd related to Holding Ltd under AS 18?
optionA: Assoc Ltd is a Subsidiary of Holding Ltd.
optionB: Assoc Ltd is an Associate of Holding Ltd because Holding Ltd directly and indirectly controls/exercises significant influence over 50% voting power.
optionC: Assoc Ltd is not a related party of Holding Ltd.
optionD: Assoc Ltd is a Joint Venture of Holding Ltd.
answerText: Assoc Ltd is an Associate of Holding Ltd because Holding Ltd directly and indirectly controls/exercises significant influence over 50% voting power.
explanation: Holding Ltd controls Sub Ltd (60%). Sub Ltd holds 40% in Assoc Ltd, so Sub Ltd has significant influence. Directly Holding Ltd has 10%. Combined effective voting influence/control over Assoc Ltd exceeds 20% (direct 10% + indirect 40% held via subsidiary = 50% voting power influence). Thus, Assoc Ltd is an associate/related party of Holding Ltd.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Alpha Ltd pays ₹60 Lakhs as KMP remuneration to its Managing Director Mr. R. During the year, Mr. R's spouse, Mrs. R, provides legal consultancy services to Alpha Ltd worth ₹6 Lakhs. Mrs. R is an independent professional. How should this be disclosed under AS 18 in Alpha Ltd's financial statements?
optionA: No disclosure required for Mrs. R because legal services were provided on arm's length basis.
optionB: Both KMP remuneration of Mr. R and the transaction with Mrs. R (relative of KMP) must be disclosed as related party transactions.
optionC: Only Mr. R's remuneration needs disclosure; transactions with relatives are exempt if under ₹10 Lakhs.
optionD: Aggregate disclosure of ₹66 Lakhs as KMP remuneration without splitting.
answerText: Both KMP remuneration of Mr. R and the transaction with Mrs. R (relative of KMP) must be disclosed as related party transactions.
explanation: Under AS 18, KMP and their relatives are related parties. Both remuneration paid to KMP and commercial transactions with relatives of KMP must be disclosed, regardless of whether they are at arm's length.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Zeta Ltd had 1,000,000 equity shares outstanding on 1st April 2024. On 1st July 2024, it made a Rights Issue in the ratio of 1:4 (1 new share for every 4 shares held) at an issue price of ₹20 per share. The fair value of one equity share immediately prior to the exercise of rights was ₹30. What is the Theoretical Ex-Rights Price (TERP) per share under AS 20?
explanation: TERP = [(Fair value of shares prior to rights * No. of shares prior) + (Rights issue price * No. of rights shares)] / Total shares after rights issue. TERP = [(4 * ₹30) + (1 * ₹20)] / (4 + 1) = (120 + 20) / 5 = ₹140 / 5 = ₹28.00.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Omega Ltd reported Net Profit after tax of ₹50,000,000 for FY 2024-25 and has 5,000,000 equity shares of ₹10 each. It has 100,000 10% Convertible Debentures of ₹100 each outstanding, each debenture convertible into 2 equity shares. Tax rate is 30%. What is the Diluted EPS under AS 20?

subject: Accounts
prompt: A company has 100,000 stock options outstanding exercisable at ₹40 per share. The average fair value of one equity share during the year was ₹50. Under AS 20, what is the incremental number of dilutive potential equity shares to be added to WANES for calculating Diluted EPS?
optionA: 100,000 shares
optionB: 80,000 shares
optionC: 20,000 shares
optionD: 50,000 shares
answerText: 20,000 shares
explanation: Number of shares issued for full consideration = (100,000 * ₹40) / ₹50 = 80,000 shares. Incremental free/dilutive shares = Total options - Shares for consideration = 100,000 - 80,000 = 20,000 shares [or 100,000 * (1 - 40/50) = 20,000 shares].

subject: Accounts
prompt: An enterprise sells its idle manufacturing equipment representing 15% of total plant assets from its ongoing main operating unit. The equipment sale is completed in a single deal. Does this transaction qualify as a Discontinuing Operation under AS 24?
optionA: Yes, because it represents a disposal of a significant portion of assets pursuant to a single plan.
optionB: No, because selling individual assets without disposing of a major line of business or geographical segment does not satisfy AS 24 definition.
optionC: Yes, provided the revenue from the equipment is disclosed separately.
optionD: No, because AS 24 applies only to statutory mergers and amalgamations.
answerText: No, because selling individual assets without disposing of a major line of business or geographical segment does not satisfy AS 24 definition.
explanation: AS 24 explicitly clarifies that disposal of individual assets or routine phasing out of products/machinery within an ongoing major line of business does not constitute a discontinuing operation unless it represents a separate major line of business or geographical area.
conceptTags: AS 24 | Discontinuing Operation Scope | Asset Disposal

subject: Accounts
prompt: If a discontinuing operation continues operations into the next financial year before final completion, what disclosure is required under AS 24 in subsequent period financial statements?
optionA: No further disclosures required once initial disclosure event occurred in prior year.
optionB: Disclosures must be updated in subsequent periods including description of significant changes in the plan, cash flows, and pre-tax profit/loss until completion.
optionC: The entire operation must be reclassified back to continuing operations.
optionD: Only the total realized cash consideration needs disclosure.
answerText: Disclosures must be updated in subsequent periods including description of significant changes in the plan, cash flows, and pre-tax profit/loss until completion.
explanation: AS 24 mandates that for a discontinuing operation, disclosures must continue in financial statements for subsequent periods until the completion of the disposal plan, including updates on any significant changes in the amounts or timing of cash flows/proceeds.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Company X has Net Profit of ₹1,000,000 and 100,000 equity shares (Basic EPS = ₹10). It has 10,000 12% Convertible Debentures of ₹100 each (each convertible into 1 share; interest net of tax = ₹8,400) and 5,000 15% Convertible Preference Shares of ₹100 each (dividend = ₹75,000, each convertible into 10 shares). Which potential equity shares are dilutive?
optionA: Both Convertible Debentures and Convertible Preference Shares are dilutive.
optionB: Only Convertible Debentures are dilutive (incremental EPS = ₹0.84), while Convertible Preference Shares are anti-dilutive (incremental EPS = ₹1.50). Both are dilutive relative to Basic EPS ₹10, but tested in sequence.
optionC: Convertible Debentures (incremental EPS ₹0.84) and Convertible Preference Shares (incremental EPS ₹1.50) are both dilutive since their incremental EPS is below basic EPS of ₹10.
optionD: Neither is dilutive.
answerText: Convertible Debentures (incremental EPS ₹0.84) and Convertible Preference Shares (incremental EPS ₹1.50) are both dilutive since their incremental EPS is below basic EPS of ₹10.
explanation: Incremental EPS of Convertible Debentures = ₹8,400 / 10,000 = ₹0.84. Incremental EPS of Convertible Preference Shares = ₹75,000 / 50,000 = ₹1.50. Since both incremental EPS values (₹0.84 and ₹1.50) are lower than Basic EPS (₹10), both are dilutive potential equity shares when tested individually and sequentially.
conceptTags: AS 20 | Diluted EPS | Sequential Dilution Test

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Apex Ltd is preparing its financial statements for the year ended 31st March 2025. On 1st April 2024, the company had 1,000,000 equity shares of ₹10 each outstanding. Net profit attributable to equity shareholders for FY 2024-25 is ₹60,000,000.
During the year, the following corporate transactions occurred:
1. On 1st July 2024, Apex Ltd issued rights shares to existing shareholders in the ratio of 1:4 (1 new share for every 4 held) at an issue price of ₹40 per share. The fair value of one equity share immediately prior to the exercise of rights on 1st July 2024 was ₹50.
2. Apex Ltd had 100,000 stock options outstanding throughout the year, exercisable at ₹30 per share. The average fair value per equity share during FY 2024-25 was ₹50.
3. On 1st October 2024, the company issued 50,000 10% Convertible Debentures of ₹100 each. Each debenture is convertible into 2 equity shares. Applicable tax rate is 30%.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the Theoretical Ex-Rights Price (TERP) per share and the rights adjustment factor for Apex Ltd under AS 20?
optionA: TERP = ₹48.00; Adjustment Factor = 1.0417 (or 25/24)
optionB: TERP = ₹45.00; Adjustment Factor = 1.1111
optionC: TERP = ₹40.00; Adjustment Factor = 1.2500
optionD: TERP = ₹50.00; Adjustment Factor = 1.0000
answerText: TERP = ₹48.00; Adjustment Factor = 1.0417 (or 25/24)
explanation: TERP = [(4 * ₹50) + (1 * ₹40)] / 5 = (200 + 40) / 5 = ₹48.00. Rights Adjustment Factor = Fair Value prior to rights / TERP = 50 / 48 = 1.041667 (or 25/24).

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the Weighted Average Number of Equity Shares (WANES) for calculating Basic EPS for FY 2024-25 under AS 20?
optionA: 1,197,917 shares
optionB: 1,250,000 shares
optionC: 1,187,500 shares
optionD: 1,000,000 shares
answerText: 1,197,917 shares

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the number of incremental dilutive potential equity shares arising from the stock options to be included in Diluted EPS calculation under AS 20?
optionA: 40,000 shares
optionB: 100,000 shares
optionC: 60,000 shares
optionD: 20,000 shares
answerText: 40,000 shares
explanation: Options dilutive shares = Total options * (1 - Exercise Price / Fair Value) = 100,000 * (1 - 30/50) = 100,000 * 0.40 = 40,000 shares.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the Diluted Earnings Per Share (DEPS) of Apex Ltd for FY 2024-25 under AS 20?
explanation: Basic EPS = ₹60,000,000 / 1,197,917 = ₹50.09. Convertible Debentures interest saved net of tax (for 6 months from 1st Oct) = 50,000 * 100 * 10% * 6/12 * (1 - 0.30) = ₹175,000. Incremental shares from debentures weighted for 6 months = (50,000 * 2) * 6/12 = 50,000 shares. Total Diluted WANES = 1,197,917 (Basic) + 40,000 (Options) + 50,000 (Debentures) = 1,287,917 shares. Adjusted Profit = 60,000,000 + 175,000 = ₹60,175,000. Diluted EPS = 60,175,000 / 1,287,917 = ₹46.72.

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Vibrant Infra Ltd (VIL) is an unlisted public company. For the financial year ended 31st March 2025, the accountant is reviewing the following relationships and transactions for compliance with AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures):
1. Mr. Vijay is the Managing Director of VIL. VIL paid him a salary of ₹1.2 Crores. Mr. Vijay's brother, Mr. Ajay, supplied raw materials worth ₹40 Lakhs to VIL at prevailing market rates.
2. VIL holds 25% voting power in Solar Tech Ltd (STL). VIL had no commercial transactions with STL during FY 2024-25.
3. VIL holds 60% equity shares in Metro Projects Ltd (MPL). VIL had zero business transactions with MPL during FY 2024-25.
4. State Bank of India (SBI) provided a term loan of ₹50 Crores to VIL with standard financial covenants. VIL also purchased machinery worth ₹2 Crores from Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd (BHEL), a state-controlled enterprise.

subject: Accounts
prompt: How should the raw material supply transaction with Mr. Ajay (brother of Managing Director Mr. Vijay) be disclosed in VIL's financial statements under AS 18?
optionA: Exempt from disclosure because the transaction was conducted at prevailing market rates (arm's length).
optionB: Must be disclosed as a related party transaction including the nature of relationship, description, and amount of ₹40 Lakhs.
optionC: Disclosed only if the amount exceeds ₹1 Crore.
optionD: Merged with KMP remuneration of Mr. Vijay without separate disclosure.
answerText: Must be disclosed as a related party transaction including the nature of relationship, description, and amount of ₹40 Lakhs.
explanation: Under AS 18, relatives of Key Management Personnel are related parties. Transactions with related parties must be disclosed regardless of whether they are on an arm's length basis.
conceptTags: AS 18 | KMP Relatives | Arm's Length Exemption

subject: Accounts
prompt: Is VIL required to disclose its relationship with Solar Tech Ltd (STL) for FY 2024-25 under AS 18?
optionA: Yes, because holding 25% voting power creates significant influence.
optionB: No, because no transactions took place during the year and the relationship is only 'significant influence' (not control).
optionC: Yes, disclosure of relationship name is mandatory even for significant influence without transactions.
optionD: No, because STL is an unlisted company.
answerText: No, because no transactions took place during the year and the relationship is only 'significant influence' (not control).
explanation: Under AS 18, when NO transactions take place during the financial year, disclosures are required ONLY for relationships where CONTROL exists. Since VIL exercises significant influence (not control) over STL and no transactions took place, no disclosure is required.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Is VIL required to disclose its relationship with Metro Projects Ltd (MPL) for FY 2024-25 under AS 18?
optionA: No, because no business transactions took place between VIL and MPL during the year.
optionB: Yes, because VIL exercises CONTROL (60% holding) over MPL, requiring disclosure of relationship name and nature even without transactions.
optionC: Disclosure is optional at management's discretion.
optionD: Disclose only in the Director's Report, not in financial statements.
answerText: Yes, because VIL exercises CONTROL (60% holding) over MPL, requiring disclosure of relationship name and nature even without transactions.
explanation: AS 18 mandates that where CONTROL exists, disclosure of the related party relationship (name and nature) is mandatory irrespective of whether any transactions took place between the related parties during the year.
conceptTags: AS 18 | Control Relationship | Nil Transaction Requirement

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which of the following entities is EXEMPT from being considered a related party of VIL under AS 18 based on the facts provided?
optionA: Mr. Vijay (Managing Director)
optionB: Metro Projects Ltd (Subsidiary)
optionC: State Bank of India (Provider of Finance)
optionD: Mr. Ajay (Brother of KMP)
answerText: State Bank of India (Provider of Finance)
explanation: AS 18 explicitly excludes providers of finance (such as banks) from being considered related parties merely by virtue of their normal dealings with an enterprise.

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Consumer Products Ltd has two distinct operating divisions: Division A (Electronics) and Division B (Home Appliances). Both represent major lines of business and are operationally and financially distinguishable.
During FY 2024-25, Zenith's management initiated a process regarding Division B:
- On 15th September 2024, the Board of Directors approved a detailed formal plan to discontinue Division B by selling its assets piecemeal.
- On 1st November 2024, Zenith issued a press release and formally notified stock exchanges about the board's decision to discontinue Division B.
- On 15th January 2025, Zenith signed a binding sale agreement to dispose of 60% of Division B's assets to a buyer.
- The remaining assets were sold in March 2025.
For FY 2024-25, Division B reported revenue of ₹20 Crores, pre-tax operating loss of ₹3 Crores, and income tax benefit of ₹0.9 Crores.

subject: Accounts
prompt: On which date did the 'Initial Disclosure Event' (IDE) occur for Division B under AS 24?
optionA: 15th September 2024
optionB: 1st November 2024
optionC: 15th January 2025
optionD: 31st March 2025
answerText: 1st November 2024
explanation: Initial Disclosure Event is the EARLIER of (a) entering into binding sale agreement (15th Jan 2025) or (b) approval of detailed formal plan AND making a public announcement (1st Nov 2024). Hence, IDE occurred on 1st November 2024.

subject: Accounts
prompt: How should the pre-tax loss and tax benefit of Division B be presented in Zenith's financial statements for FY 2024-25 under AS 24?
optionA: Pre-tax loss of ₹3 Crores and tax benefit of ₹0.9 Crores attributable to the discontinuing operation must be disclosed on the face of profit & loss or in notes.
optionB: Net loss of ₹2.1 Crores must be credited directly to General Reserve.
optionC: No disclosure is required until all assets are completely transferred.
optionD: Include Division B's results under Continuing Operations without separate breakdown.
answerText: Pre-tax loss of ₹3 Crores and tax benefit of ₹0.9 Crores attributable to the discontinuing operation must be disclosed on the face of profit & loss or in notes.
explanation: AS 24 mandates disclosure of the amount of pre-tax gain/loss recognized on the disposal of assets or settlement of liabilities attributable to discontinuing operation, and the related income tax expense/benefit.

subject: Accounts
prompt: How should cash flows attributable to Division B be presented in the Cash Flow Statement of Zenith Ltd under AS 24?
optionA: Net cash flows from operating, investing, and financing activities of Division B must be disclosed separately on the face of Cash Flow Statement or in notes.
optionB: Cash flows must be omitted from Cash Flow Statement since it is a discontinuing operation.
optionC: Only financing cash flows of Division B require disclosure.
optionD: Cash flows should be adjusted against capital reserves.
answerText: Net cash flows from operating, investing, and financing activities of Division B must be disclosed separately on the face of Cash Flow Statement or in notes.
explanation: AS 24 requires separate disclosure of net cash flows attributable to operating, investing, and financing activities of the discontinuing operation.

subject: Accounts
prompt: If Zenith Ltd had sold only one idle manufacturing unit of Division B (which did not constitute a separate major line of business or geographical area), how would AS 24 apply?
optionA: AS 24 would fully apply because it is a disposal of plant assets.
optionB: AS 24 would NOT apply because disposal of an individual unit within an operating segment does not satisfy the definition of a discontinuing operation.
optionC: AS 24 would apply only if the sale generated a capital loss.
optionD: AS 24 applies at management's discretion.
answerText: AS 24 would NOT apply because disposal of an individual unit within an operating segment does not satisfy the definition of a discontinuing operation.
explanation: AS 24 explicitly excludes from its scope the disposal of individual assets or components that do not represent a separate major line of business or geographical area of operations.
conceptTags: AS 24 | Scope Exclusion | Major Line of Business

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Nova Retail Ltd operates a chain of supermarkets. For the financial year ended 31st March 2025, the auditor identified the following matters regarding accounting policies:
1. Nova Retail changed its method of valuation of inventory from Weighted Average Cost method to FIFO method to achieve uniformity with its parent company. This change resulted in an increase in closing inventory and current period profit by ₹45 Lakhs. The financial impact on prior periods cannot be reasonably determined.
2. The company capitalized administrative overheads of ₹12 Lakhs into the cost of store fixtures, arguing that corporate management spent time supervising store setup.
3. Due to intense competition, Nova Retail's accumulated losses eroded its net worth by 80%. However, management secured a binding line of credit from promoters for 3 years and restructured store operations, expecting cash inflows.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 1, is the change in inventory valuation method permissible, and how should it be disclosed?
optionA: Impermissible; inventory valuation methods can never be changed once chosen.
optionB: Permissible if it complies with AS 2 / AS 1 or statute; the change, reasons, and ₹45 Lakhs current period profit impact must be disclosed along with a note that prior period impact is undeterminable.
optionC: Permissible only with prior approval from ICAI.
optionD: Permissible without disclosure if profit increases.
answerText: Permissible if it complies with AS 2 / AS 1 or statute; the change, reasons, and ₹45 Lakhs current period profit impact must be disclosed along with a note that prior period impact is undeterminable.
explanation: A change in accounting policy is permissible if required by statute, for AS compliance, or for more appropriate presentation. Under AS 1, the impact (₹45 Lakhs profit increase) and reasons must be disclosed, and if past impacts are undeterminable, that fact must be stated.
conceptTags: AS 1 | Change in Accounting Policy | Disclosure

subject: Accounts
prompt: Regarding the capitalization of administrative overheads into store fixtures, which principle under AS 1 and general AS principles is violated?
optionA: Prudence and Substance over Form, as general administrative overheads do not directly add to the location/condition of assets.
optionB: Consistency Assumption.
optionC: Going Concern Assumption.
optionD: Accrual Assumption.
answerText: Prudence and Substance over Form, as general administrative overheads do not directly add to the location/condition of assets.
explanation: Under AS 1 and asset valuation standards, administrative overheads that do not directly contribute to bringing assets to their present location and condition should be expensed. Capitalizing them distorts true financial position, violating Prudence and Substance over Form.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Regarding the fundamental accounting assumption of 'Going Concern' for Nova Retail Ltd, what is the reporting requirement under AS 1?
optionA: Going concern assumption must be treated as failed and liquidation basis must be adopted mandatory.
optionB: If management reasonably assesses that going concern is valid (supported by promoter credit line), no disclosure of non-going concern is required, but disclosure of material uncertainties in notes may be necessary.
optionC: Specific disclosure is mandatory stating that Going Concern IS followed.
optionD: The company must cease financial reporting.
answerText: If management reasonably assesses that going concern is valid (supported by promoter credit line), no disclosure of non-going concern is required, but disclosure of material uncertainties in notes may be necessary.
explanation: Under AS 1, fundamental accounting assumptions are assumed to be followed. If management concludes going concern remains valid despite distress (due to credit support), specific disclosure that fundamental assumption is NOT followed is not required, though material uncertainty disclosures may be made.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What are the three primary considerations prescribed by AS 1 for the selection and application of accounting policies?
optionA: Prudence, Substance over Form, and Materiality
optionB: Relevance, Reliability, and Comparability
optionC: Going Concern, Consistency, and Accrual
optionD: Historical Cost, Fair Value, and Liquidation Value
answerText: Prudence, Substance over Form, and Materiality
explanation: AS 1 explicitly states that the major considerations governing the selection and application of accounting policies are: (a) Prudence, (b) Substance over Form, and (c) Materiality.
conceptTags: AS 1 | Policy Selection Criteria | Core Principles

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Orion Enterprises Ltd had 200,000 equity shares of ₹10 each outstanding on 1st April 2024. Profit after tax attributable to equity shareholders for FY 2024-25 is ₹40,000,000.
During FY 2024-25, Orion engaged in the following events:
1. On 1st October 2024, Orion issued 100,000 equity shares for cash at market price.
2. On 1st January 2025, Orion declared a bonus issue of 1 equity share for every 3 equity shares held as on that date.
3. Mr. K is the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of Orion. During the year, Orion paid ₹30 Lakhs as CFO salary to Mr. K. Orion also paid ₹15 Lakhs as professional fee to a legal firm in which Mr. K's son holds a 50% partnership interest.
Comparative financial figures for FY 2023-24 showed Net Profit of ₹30,000,000 and 200,000 equity shares.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the Weighted Average Number of Equity Shares (WANES) for FY 2024-25 for calculating Basic EPS under AS 20?
optionA: 333,333 shares
optionB: 400,000 shares
optionC: 250,000 shares
optionD: 300,000 shares
answerText: 333,333 shares
explanation: Original 200k + Bonus 1:3 on 200k (66.667k) = 266,667 shares for 12 months = 266,667. Issued on 1st Oct 100k + Bonus 1:3 on 100k (33.333k) = 133,333 shares for 6 months = 66,667. Total WANES = 266,667 + 66,667 = 333,334 (or 333,333) shares.
conceptTags: AS 20 | WANES Calculation | Bonus & Cash Issue

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the restated Basic EPS for the comparative year FY 2023-24 under AS 20?
explanation: Original WANES FY 23-24 = 200,000 shares. Bonus issue ratio 1:3 adds 66,667 bonus shares retrospectively. Restated WANES = 266,667 shares. Restated EPS = ₹30,000,000 / 266,667 = ₹112.50.
conceptTags: AS 20 | Comparative EPS Restatement | Bonus Issue

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the Basic EPS of Orion Enterprises Ltd for FY 2024-25 under AS 20?
explanation: Basic EPS FY 2024-25 = Net Profit / WANES = ₹40,000,000 / 333,333 shares = ₹120.00.

subject: Accounts
prompt: How should the payment of ₹15 Lakhs to the legal firm (where CFO Mr. K's son is a partner) be disclosed under AS 18?
optionA: No disclosure required as it was paid to a partnership firm, not directly to Mr. K.
optionB: Must be disclosed as a related party transaction with a relative of KMP/enterprise influenced by relative of KMP.
optionC: Exempt from disclosure because it is a professional fee.
optionD: Aggregate with CFO salary and disclose total as ₹45 Lakhs without breakup.
answerText: Must be disclosed as a related party transaction with a relative of KMP/enterprise influenced by relative of KMP.
explanation: Under AS 18, KMP and their relatives are related parties. An enterprise over which a KMP or their relative exercises significant influence (e.g., 50% partner) is a related party. Hence, transaction details of ₹15 Lakhs must be disclosed.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 2 'Valuation of Inventories', raw materials and other supplies held for use in the production of inventories are NOT written down below cost if:
optionA: The finished products in which they will be incorporated are expected to be sold at or above cost.
optionB: The net realizable value of raw materials is greater than their replacement cost.
optionC: The fair value of the finished product is less than its cost of production.
optionD: The raw materials have been held in stock for less than six months.
answerText: The finished products in which they will be incorporated are expected to be sold at or above cost.
explanation: As per AS 2, materials and other supplies held for use in the production of inventories are not written down below cost if the finished products in which they will be incorporated are expected to be sold at or above cost. Raw materials are written down to replacement cost only when there has been a decline in the price of materials and it is estimated that the cost of finished products will exceed net realizable value.

subject: Accounts
prompt: A company holds 1,000 units of raw material purchased at ₹ 200 per unit. The replacement cost of raw material is ₹ 150 per unit. The finished product requires 1 unit of raw material with an additional conversion cost of ₹ 100 per unit. The estimated selling price of the finished product is ₹ 280 per unit, and selling expenses are ₹ 10 per unit. At what total value should the raw material inventory be carried?
