explanation: The Net Realizable Value (NRV) of the finished product is ₹ 270 (₹ 280 - ₹ 10). The total cost to produce the finished product is ₹ 300 (₹ 200 raw material + ₹ 100 conversion). Since the finished product is expected to be sold below cost (NRV ₹ 270 < Cost ₹ 300), the raw material must be written down to its replacement cost of ₹ 150 per unit. Total raw material valuation = 1,000 units × ₹ 150 = ₹ 1,50,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which of the following cost formulas is explicitly NOT permitted under AS 2 'Valuation of Inventories' for determining the cost of inventories?
optionA: Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) formula
optionB: First-In, First-Out (FIFO) formula
optionC: Weighted Average Cost formula
optionD: Specific Identification Method
answerText: Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) formula
explanation: AS 2 explicitly prohibits the use of the LIFO (Last-In, First-Out) formula because it often results in inventories being recognized in the balance sheet at amounts far removed from recent cost levels. Permitted cost formulas under AS 2 include FIFO, Weighted Average, and Specific Identification Method.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 10 'Property, Plant and Equipment', when an item of PPE is revalued upwards for the first time, how should the increase in carrying amount be recognized?
optionA: Credited directly to Revaluation Surplus under Reserve and Surplus
optionB: Credited to the Profit and Loss Account as Extraordinary Income
optionC: Credited to General Reserve
optionD: Deducted from the accumulated depreciation account
answerText: Credited directly to Revaluation Surplus under Reserve and Surplus
explanation: Under AS 10, when an asset's carrying amount is increased as a result of a revaluation for the first time, the increase should be credited directly to owners' interests under the heading of Revaluation Surplus. If it reverses a revaluation decrease of the same asset previously recognized in profit or loss, it is recognized in profit or loss to that extent.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which of the following costs should be EXCLUDED from the initial cost of an item of Property, Plant and Equipment under AS 10?
optionA: Initial operating losses incurred before the asset achieves planned performance
optionB: Costs of site preparation
optionC: Initial delivery and handling costs
optionD: Professional fees arising directly from bringing the asset to its working condition
answerText: Initial operating losses incurred before the asset achieves planned performance
explanation: AS 10 specifically requires initial operating losses, such as those incurred while demand for the asset's output builds up, to be excluded from the carrying amount of an item of PPE. Site preparation, initial delivery, and direct professional fees are directly attributable costs and must be capitalized.

subject: Accounts
prompt: An entity purchases a chemical plant for ₹ 50,00,000. Under AS 10, the cost includes a major overhauling component required every 3 years costing ₹ 6,00,000. After 3 years, the overhaul is performed at a cost of ₹ 7,50,000. How should this new overhaul cost be accounted for?
optionA: Capitalized as a replacement component in PPE, derecognizing the remaining carrying amount of the old overhaul component
optionB: Charged entirely as a routine repair and maintenance expense in Profit and Loss
optionC: Adjusted against the Revaluation Surplus balance
optionD: Deferred and amortized over the remaining life of the main chemical plant
answerText: Capitalized as a replacement component in PPE, derecognizing the remaining carrying amount of the old overhaul component
explanation: AS 10 requires component accounting for major inspections or overhauls. When each major inspection/overhaul is performed, its cost is recognized in the carrying amount of the item of PPE as a replacement if recognition criteria are satisfied, and any remaining carrying amount of the cost of the previous overhaul is derecognized.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 10, an entity measures an asset using the Revaluation Model. If a change in the estimated decommissioning liability reduces the liability, how is this reduction treated?
optionA: Added to/credited to Revaluation Surplus, except that it is recognized in Profit and Loss to the extent it reverses a revaluation deficit previously recognized in P&L.
optionB: Recognized immediately in Profit and Loss as an exceptional gain in all circumstances.
optionC: Credited to a deferred revenue account and recognized over the remaining asset life.
optionD: Deducted directly from the opening Retained Earnings balance.
answerText: Added to/credited to Revaluation Surplus, except that it is recognized in Profit and Loss to the extent it reverses a revaluation deficit previously recognized in P&L.
explanation: Under AS 10 (Appendix I principles), for assets measured under the revaluation model, a reduction in the decommissioning liability is credited to Revaluation Surplus, except that it shall be recognized in profit or loss to the extent that it reverses a revaluation deficit on the asset that was previously recognized in profit or loss.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 13 'Accounting for Investments', a 'Current Investment' is defined as an investment that by its nature is readily realizable and is intended to be held for:
optionA: Not more than one year from the date on which such investment is made.
optionB: Not more than six months from the date of the balance sheet.
optionC: Not more than two years from the date on which such investment is made.
optionD: Indefinite period depending on market fluctuations.
answerText: Not more than one year from the date on which such investment is made.
explanation: As per AS 13, a current investment is an investment that is by its nature readily realizable and is intended to be held for not more than one year from the date on which such investment is made.

subject: Accounts
prompt: How are Current Investments valued at the Balance Sheet date as per AS 13?
optionA: Lower of cost and fair value / net realizable value determined on an individual investment basis or category basis
optionB: At cost less permanent diminution only
optionC: Always at fair value with gains taken to profit and loss
optionD: At lower of cost and net realizable value determined strictly on aggregate portfolio basis only
answerText: Lower of cost and fair value / net realizable value determined on an individual investment basis or category basis
explanation: Under AS 13, current investments are carried in the financial statements at lower of cost and fair value (or net realizable value). The valuation is determined either on an individual investment basis or by category of investment, but not on an overall aggregate basis.

subject: Accounts
prompt: When an investment is reclassified from Long-Term Investments to Current Investments under AS 13, the transfer should be made at:
optionA: Lower of cost and carrying amount at the date of transfer
optionB: Fair value at the date of transfer with difference credited to capital reserve
optionC: Cost irrespective of market value
optionD: Higher of cost and net realizable value
answerText: Lower of cost and carrying amount at the date of transfer
explanation: AS 13 prescribes that where long-term investments are reclassified as current investments, transfers are made at the lower of cost and carrying amount at the date of transfer. If written down previously for permanent decline, that written-down carrying amount is compared with cost.

subject: Accounts
prompt: An investor purchases 1,000 equity shares of X Ltd. cum-right at ₹ 150 per share. Later, the company announces 1 right share for every 2 shares held at ₹ 80 per share. The investor sells all right entitlements in the market for ₹ 30 per right. If the ex-rights market price of the original shares does not fall below the cost, how should the ₹ 15,000 proceeds from sale of rights be treated under AS 13?
optionA: Credited to the Profit and Loss Statement
optionB: Deducted from the cost of original investment in the Balance Sheet
optionC: Credited to Capital Reserve
optionD: Deferred as Unearned Income until original shares are sold
answerText: Credited to the Profit and Loss Statement
explanation: As per AS 13, rights offer proceeds from the sale of right entitlements are generally credited to the Profit and Loss Statement. They are applied to reduce the carrying amount of investment only when the shares were purchased cum-right and the market value of shares after ex-rights falls below the purchase cost.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 16 'Borrowing Costs', what is a 'qualifying asset'?
optionA: An asset that necessarily takes a substantial period of time to get ready for its intended use or sale
optionB: Any fixed asset purchased on credit terms exceeding 30 days
optionC: An asset that is funded 100% by specific bank loans
optionD: An asset whose useful life exceeds 10 accounting periods
answerText: An asset that necessarily takes a substantial period of time to get ready for its intended use or sale
explanation: AS 16 defines a qualifying asset as an asset that necessarily takes a substantial period of time to get ready for its intended use or sale. What constitutes a substantial period depends on the facts and circumstances (ordinarily 12 months unless a shorter duration can be justified).

subject: Accounts
prompt: Entity A has general borrowings of ₹ 10,00,000 at 10% p.a. and ₹ 20,00,000 at 13% p.a. during the year. It uses ₹ 6,00,000 out of general borrowings for the construction of a qualifying asset. What is the weighted average capitalization rate for borrowing costs?

subject: Accounts
prompt: According to AS 16, capitalization of borrowing costs should be suspended during:
optionA: Extended periods in which active development of the qualifying asset is interrupted
optionB: Brief periods when substantial technical and administrative work is taking place
optionC: Temporary delays that are a necessary part of the process of getting an asset ready for use
optionD: The entire construction period if general interest rates increase
answerText: Extended periods in which active development of the qualifying asset is interrupted
explanation: Under AS 16, capitalization of borrowing costs should be suspended during extended periods in which active development is interrupted. However, capitalization is not suspended during a period when substantial technical and administrative work is being carried out or when a temporary delay is a necessary part of the process.
conceptTags: AS 16 | Borrowing Costs | Suspension of Capitalization

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 16, any income earned on the temporary investment of specific borrowings raised for a qualifying asset prior to its expenditure should be:
optionA: Deducted from the borrowing costs eligible for capitalization
optionB: Recognized as income in the Profit and Loss Statement
optionC: Credited directly to Capital Reserve
optionD: Ignored for accounting purposes
answerText: Deducted from the borrowing costs eligible for capitalization
explanation: AS 16 states that to the extent funds are borrowed specifically for the purpose of obtaining a qualifying asset, the amount of borrowing costs eligible for capitalization should be determined as actual borrowing costs incurred on that borrowing during the period less any income on temporary investment of those borrowings.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 19 'Leases', which of the following scenarios indicates that a lease is classified as a Finance Lease?
optionA: At the inception of the lease, the present value of minimum lease payments substantially covers the initial fair value of the leased asset.
optionB: The lease term is for 10% of the economic life of the asset.
optionC: The lessee can cancel the lease at any time without paying any penalty.
optionD: Gains or losses from the fluctuation in the fair value of the residual fall to the lessor.
answerText: At the inception of the lease, the present value of minimum lease payments substantially covers the initial fair value of the leased asset.
explanation: AS 19 provides indicators of a finance lease, one of which is that at the inception of the lease, the present value of the minimum lease payments amounts to at least substantially all of the fair value of the leased asset.

subject: Accounts
prompt: In a finance lease transaction, the lessor defines 'Unearned Finance Income' as the difference between:
optionA: Gross investment in the lease and the net investment in the lease
optionB: Present value of minimum lease payments and fair value of the asset
optionC: Minimum lease payments and residual value
optionD: Lease receipts and initial direct costs incurred by lessor
answerText: Gross investment in the lease and the net investment in the lease
explanation: Under AS 19, Unearned Finance Income is defined as the difference between the gross investment in the lease and the net investment in the lease. Gross investment is aggregate of minimum lease payments from lessor perspective plus unguaranteed residual value.

subject: Accounts
prompt: How should initial direct costs incurred by a lessee in respect of an operating lease be treated under AS 19?
optionA: Recognized as an expense in the Profit and Loss Statement in the period in which they are incurred
optionB: Capitalized as part of the carrying amount of the leased asset
optionC: Amortized strictly over the economic life of the asset
optionD: Deducted from the liability for lease payments
answerText: Recognized as an expense in the Profit and Loss Statement in the period in which they are incurred
explanation: In an operating lease, initial direct costs incurred by the lessee (such as legal fees, negotiation costs) are recognized as an immediate expense in the Profit and Loss Statement in the period in which they are incurred.

subject: Accounts
prompt: If a sale and leaseback transaction results in a Finance Lease, any excess of sale proceeds over the carrying amount of the asset should be:
optionA: Deferred and amortized by the seller-lessee over the lease term in proportion to the depreciation of the leased asset
optionB: Recognized immediately as profit in the Profit and Loss Account in the year of sale
optionC: Credited to General Reserve immediately
optionD: Adjusted against the fair value of the asset in the books of the lessor
answerText: Deferred and amortized by the seller-lessee over the lease term in proportion to the depreciation of the leased asset
explanation: Under AS 19, if a sale and leaseback transaction results in a finance lease, any excess or deficiency of sales proceeds over the carrying amount should not be immediately recognized as income or loss. Instead, it should be deferred and amortized over the lease term in proportion to the depreciation of the leased asset.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 26 'Intangible Assets', expenditure incurred on the 'Research Phase' of an internal project must be:
optionA: Recognized as an expense when it is incurred
optionB: Capitalized as an intangible asset if future economic benefits are probable
optionC: Deferred and written off over a period of 5 years
optionD: Included in the cost of inventory as work-in-progress
answerText: Recognized as an expense when it is incurred
explanation: Under AS 26, no intangible asset arising from research (or from the research phase of an internal project) should be recognized. Expenditure on research should be recognized as an expense when it is incurred because an entity cannot demonstrate that an intangible asset exists that will generate future economic benefits.

subject: Accounts
prompt: As per AS 26, there is a rebuttable presumption that the useful life of an intangible asset will NOT exceed how many years from the date when the asset is available for use?
optionA: 10 years
optionB: 5 years
optionC: 20 years
optionD: 15 years
answerText: 10 years
explanation: AS 26 includes a rebuttable presumption that the useful life of an intangible asset will not exceed 10 years from the date when the asset is available for use.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which of the following internally generated items CANNOT be recognized as an Intangible Asset under AS 26?
optionA: Internally generated brands, mastheads, publishing titles, and customer lists
optionB: Purchased software licenses for internal accounting system
optionC: Patents acquired through business combinations
optionD: Copyrights acquired from a third party
answerText: Internally generated brands, mastheads, publishing titles, and customer lists
explanation: AS 26 explicitly states that internally generated brands, mastheads, publishing titles, customer lists, and items similar in substance should not be recognized as intangible assets because expenditures on them cannot be distinguished from the cost of developing the business as a whole.
conceptTags: AS 26 | Intangible Assets | Internally Generated Assets

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 28 'Impairment of Assets', the 'Recoverable Amount' of an asset is defined as the HIGHER of:
optionA: Net Selling Price and its Value in Use
optionB: Carrying Amount and Replacement Cost
optionC: Historical Cost and Net Realizable Value
optionD: Fair Value and Salvage Value
answerText: Net Selling Price and its Value in Use
explanation: AS 28 defines Recoverable Amount as the higher of an asset's net selling price and its value in use. If either of these amounts exceeds the carrying amount, the asset is not impaired.

subject: Accounts
prompt: 'Value in Use' of an asset under AS 28 represents:
optionA: The present value of estimated future cash flows expected to arise from the continuing use of an asset and from its disposal at the end of its useful life
optionB: The net amount obtainable from the sale of an asset in an arm's length transaction between knowledgeable, willing parties
optionC: The current replacement cost minus cumulative depreciation
optionD: The liquidation value of the asset in an forced transaction
answerText: The present value of estimated future cash flows expected to arise from the continuing use of an asset and from its disposal at the end of its useful life
explanation: AS 28 defines Value in Use as the present value of estimated future cash flows expected to arise from the continuing use of an asset and from its disposal at the end of its useful life.

subject: Accounts
prompt: When an impairment loss is recognized for a Cash-Generating Unit (CGU) under AS 28, how is the impairment loss allocated?
optionA: First, to reduce the carrying amount of any goodwill allocated to the CGU, and then to other assets of the CGU pro-rata based on carrying amount.
optionB: Equally across all assets of the CGU regardless of carrying amount.
optionC: First to non-current tangible assets, then to goodwill, and finally to current assets.
optionD: Pro-rata to all assets based on their original historical cost.
answerText: First, to reduce the carrying amount of any goodwill allocated to the CGU, and then to other assets of the CGU pro-rata based on carrying amount.
explanation: AS 28 requires that an impairment loss for a CGU be allocated first to reduce the carrying amount of any goodwill allocated to the CGU, and then to the other assets of the unit pro-rata on the basis of the carrying amount of each asset in the unit.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 28, can an impairment loss recognized for Goodwill be reversed in a subsequent period?
optionA: No, an impairment loss recognized for Goodwill should NEVER be reversed in a subsequent period.
optionB: Yes, if the economic indicators show a significant recovery in market value.
optionC: Yes, provided the reversal is approved by the Board of Directors.
optionD: Yes, up to the maximum of 50% of the original impairment loss.
answerText: No, an impairment loss recognized for Goodwill should NEVER be reversed in a subsequent period.
explanation: AS 28 strictly states that an impairment loss recognized for goodwill should not be reversed in a subsequent period unless the impairment loss was caused by a specific external event of an exceptional nature that is not expected to recur and subsequent external events have occurred that reverse the effect of that event (in practice, ICAI syllabus standard rule is strictly prohibited/non-reversible).

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 10, how should net proceeds from selling items produced while bringing an item of PPE to its location and condition (such as samples produced when testing machinery) be treated?
optionA: Deducted from the directly attributable costs of PPE before capitalization
optionB: Recognized as revenue in the Profit and Loss Account
optionC: Credited to Revaluation Reserve
optionD: Deducted from administrative overheads
answerText: Deducted from the directly attributable costs of PPE before capitalization
explanation: Under AS 10, testing costs are directly attributable costs. Any net proceeds from selling items produced while bringing the asset to its location and condition (such as test samples) are deducted from the cost of the asset.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 16, exchange differences arising from foreign currency borrowings used for acquiring a qualifying asset are treated as borrowing costs to the extent that:
optionA: They are regarded as an adjustment to interest costs (limit being the difference between foreign interest and domestic interest cost).
optionB: 100% of the total exchange loss is always capitalized.
optionC: They exceed the principal amount borrowed.
optionD: They are recognized in the Foreign Currency Monetary Item Translation Difference Account (FCMITDA).
answerText: They are regarded as an adjustment to interest costs (limit being the difference between foreign interest and domestic interest cost).
explanation: Under AS 16, exchange differences arising from foreign currency borrowings are treated as borrowing costs to the extent that they are regarded as an adjustment to interest costs (calculated as the difference between interest on local borrowings vs foreign borrowings). Any excess exchange loss is expensed in Profit & Loss.
conceptTags: AS 16 | Borrowing Costs | Foreign Currency Borrowings

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 19, when a lease includes both land and building elements, how should an entity classify the lease of each element?
optionA: Land and building elements must be considered separately for lease classification unless title passes to lessee for land.
optionB: The entire lease is always classified as finance lease because land has indefinite economic life.
optionC: The entire lease is always classified as operating lease because land cannot be depreciated.
optionD: The classification depends solely on the value of the building regardless of the land value.
answerText: Land and building elements must be considered separately for lease classification unless title passes to lessee for land.
explanation: Under AS 19, land and building elements of a lease are considered separately for the purpose of lease classification. Since land normally has an indefinite economic life, a land lease is usually an operating lease unless title is expected to pass to the lessee.
conceptTags: AS 19 | Leases | Land and Building Split

subject: Accounts
prompt: An entity spends ₹ 15,00,000 on developing an internal website purely for promoting and advertising its own products. How should this cost be treated as per the principles of AS 26?
optionA: Expensed immediately in Profit and Loss as advertising expenditure when incurred
optionB: Capitalized as an Intangible Asset and amortized over 5 years
optionC: Capitalized under PPE as office equipment
optionD: Deferred and shown under Other Non-Current Assets
answerText: Expensed immediately in Profit and Loss as advertising expenditure when incurred
explanation: Under AS 26 guidance, expenditure on an internal website developed solely or primarily for promoting and advertising an entity's own products and services cannot demonstrate that future economic benefits will flow directly. Hence, all such costs must be recognized as an expense in Profit & Loss when incurred.
conceptTags: AS 26 | Intangible Assets | Website Development Costs

subject: Accounts
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Vedic Texfab Ltd. purchased a specialized textile processing plant on 1st April 2024. The invoice price was ₹ 80,00,000 (excluding trade discount of ₹ 2,00,000). Statutory import duties paid were ₹ 5,00,000 (non-refundable). Freight and handling charges amounted to ₹ 3,00,000. Site preparation costs incurred were ₹ 2,00,000. Architect design fees directly related to installation were ₹ 1,00,000. Initial operating losses incurred during the first month before reaching commercial capacity were ₹ 4,00,000. Trial run costs were ₹ 1,50,000 and net proceeds from sale of trial run sample output were ₹ 50,000. Present value of estimated decommissioning cost at the end of its 10-year useful life is ₹ 5,00,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the initial cost at which the plant should be capitalized in the books on 1st April 2024 under AS 10?
explanation: Cost = Net Invoice (80,00,000 - 2,00,000 = 78,00,000) + Import duties (5,00,000) + Freight (3,00,000) + Site prep (2,00,000) + Architect fees (1,00,000) + Net trial run cost (1,50,000 - 50,000 = 1,00,000) + Decommissioning PV (5,00,000) = ₹ 95,00,000. Initial operating losses (4,00,000) are excluded under AS 10.

subject: Accounts
prompt: The company uses straight-line depreciation over 10 years with zero residual value. On 31st March 2026 (after 2 years), the revaluation model is adopted and market value is determined as ₹ 88,00,000. What amount should be credited to Revaluation Surplus on 31st March 2026?

subject: Accounts
prompt: On 1st April 2026 (beginning of Year 3), due to changes in discount rates, the present value of the estimated decommissioning liability is revised downwards by ₹ 1,60,000. Under AS 10 (Revaluation Model), how should this reduction be accounted for?
optionA: Credited to Revaluation Surplus, increasing it from ₹ 12,00,000 to ₹ 13,60,000
optionB: Credited to Profit and Loss Account as an exceptional income
optionC: Deducted from the carrying amount of the asset
optionD: Credited to General Reserve
answerText: Credited to Revaluation Surplus, increasing it from ₹ 12,00,000 to ₹ 13,60,000
explanation: Under the revaluation model, changes in decommissioning liabilities are added to or deducted from the revaluation surplus. A reduction in liability increases the revaluation surplus from ₹ 12,00,000 to ₹ 13,60,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What will be the revised annual depreciation expense for Year 3 (FY 2026-27) after accounting for the revaluation on 31st March 2026?
explanation: Carrying amount on 31st March 2026 is ₹ 88,00,000. Remaining useful life is 8 years (10 - 2). Revised Depreciation = ₹ 88,00,000 / 8 years = ₹ 11,00,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Prism Infra Project Ltd. commenced the construction of a commercial shopping complex (a qualifying asset) on 1st April 2024. The project was completed on 31st March 2025.
The details of borrowings during FY 2024-25 are:
1. Specific Bank Loan: ₹ 20,00,000 at 12% p.a. taken on 1st April 2024. Funds temporarily invested earned interest income of ₹ 30,000.
2. General Borrowings:
- Loan A: ₹ 15,00,000 at 10% p.a.
- Loan B: ₹ 25,00,000 at 14% p.a.
Expenditures incurred on construction out of general borrowings were:
- 1st October 2024: ₹ 12,00,000
- 1st January 2025: ₹ 8,00,000
Active construction was halted for 2 months (October and November 2024) due to an extended labor strike (non-routine interruption).

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the net interest cost eligible for capitalization from the Specific Borrowing for FY 2024-25?
explanation: Gross Interest on specific borrowing = ₹ 20,00,000 × 12% = ₹ 2,40,000. Net interest eligible = ₹ 2,40,000 - ₹ 30,00,000 interest income = ₹ 2,10,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the weighted average capitalization rate for General Borrowings of Prism Infra Project Ltd. for FY 2024-25?
explanation: Total interest on general borrowings = (15,00,000 × 10%) + (25,00,000 × 14%) = 1,50,000 + 3,50,000 = ₹ 5,00,000. Total general borrowings = ₹ 40,00,000. Weighted Average Rate = 5,00,000 / 40,00,000 = 12.50%.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Considering that active construction was suspended for 2 months due to an unexpected labor strike, how should borrowing costs for those 2 months be treated under AS 16?
optionA: Capitalization of borrowing costs must be suspended during those 2 months and interest expensed to Profit and Loss.
optionB: Capitalization of borrowing costs continues without interruption because strikes are common.
optionC: Capitalization is permanently discontinued for the remaining project.
optionD: Interest for 2 months is added to General Reserve.
answerText: Capitalization of borrowing costs must be suspended during those 2 months and interest expensed to Profit and Loss.
explanation: AS 16 mandates that capitalization of borrowing costs should be suspended during extended periods in which active development is interrupted by non-routine delays such as labor strikes.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the total borrowing cost from general borrowings to be capitalized for FY 2024-25 taking into account the suspension period?
explanation: For ₹ 12,00,000 incurred on 1st Oct: Oct & Nov suspended. Active period = Dec to Mar (4 months). Interest = 12,00,000 × 12.5% × 4/12 = ₹ 50,000. For ₹ 8,00,000 incurred on 1st Jan: Active period = Jan to Mar (3 months). Interest = 8,00,000 × 12.5% × 3/12 = ₹ 25,000. Total general borrowing interest capitalized = 50,000 + 25,000 = ₹ 75,000.
conceptTags: AS 16 | Borrowing Costs | General Borrowings Capitalization

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Nivaan Investments Ltd. engaged in the following transactions regarding equity shares of Beta Ltd. during FY 2024-25:
- 15th May 2024: Purchased 5,000 equity shares of Beta Ltd. (face value ₹ 10) cum-dividend at ₹ 120 per share.
- 20th June 2024: Beta Ltd. declared and paid a dividend of ₹ 4 per share for FY 2023-24 (pre-acquisition period).
- 10th August 2024: Beta Ltd. issued bonus shares in the ratio of 1:5 (1 bonus share for every 5 shares held).
- 15th November 2024: Beta Ltd. issued rights shares in the ratio of 1:3 at ₹ 50 per share. Nivaan Ltd. subscribed to 50% of its rights entitlement and sold the remaining 50% rights entitlement in the market at ₹ 15 per right.
- 31st March 2025: Nivaan Ltd. reclassified these shares from Long-Term Investments to Current Investments. Market price on 31st March 2025 was ₹ 80 per share.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the total carrying cost of the original 5,000 shares immediately after receiving the pre-acquisition dividend on 20th June 2024?
explanation: Initial cost = 5,000 × ₹ 120 = ₹ 6,00,000. Pre-acquisition dividend received = 5,000 × ₹ 4 = ₹ 20,000. Under AS 13, pre-acquisition dividend is deducted from the cost of investment. Carrying cost = 6,00,000 - 20,000 = ₹ 5,80,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt: How many total shares are held by Nivaan Ltd. after receiving bonus shares and subscribing to 50% of the rights shares?
optionA: 7,000 shares
optionB: 6,000 shares
optionC: 8,000 shares
optionD: 6,500 shares
answerText: 7,000 shares
explanation: Original = 5,000. Bonus (1:5) = 1,000. Total before rights = 6,000 shares. Rights entitlement (1:3) = 2,000 rights. Subscribed 50% = 1,000 shares. Total shares held = 6,000 + 1,000 = 7,000 shares.
conceptTags: AS 13 | Investments | Bonus and Rights Shares

subject: Accounts
prompt: How should the sale of remaining 1,000 rights entitlements at ₹ 15 per right (total ₹ 15,000) be treated under AS 13?
optionA: Credited to the Profit and Loss Statement as income
optionB: Deducted from the carrying cost of the investment
optionC: Credited to Capital Reserve Account
optionD: Added to the cost of rights shares subscribed
answerText: Credited to the Profit and Loss Statement as income
explanation: Under AS 13, proceeds from the sale of right entitlements are credited to the Profit and Loss Statement unless the market value of original shares falls below cost ex-rights.
conceptTags: AS 13 | Investments | Sale of Rights Entitlement

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the carrying amount at which the investment in Beta Ltd. should be reclassified and shown as Current Investment on 31st March 2025?
explanation: Total Cost of 7,000 shares = ₹ 5,80,000 + (1,000 rights × ₹ 50) = ₹ 6,30,000. Cost per share = 6,30,000 / 7,000 = ₹ 90. Market value = ₹ 80 per share. Reclassification is at lower of cost (₹ 90) and fair value (₹ 80). Valuation = 7,000 × ₹ 80 = ₹ 5,60,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: On 1st April 2024, Aksat Leasing Ltd. (Lessor) leased equipment to Starline Services Ltd. (Lessee) for a period of 4 years.
Key details of the lease agreement:
- Fair value of equipment at inception: ₹ 20,00,000.
- Annual lease payment payable at the end of each year: ₹ 6,50,000.
- Guaranteed Residual Value (GRV) by Lessee: ₹ 1,00,000.
- Unguaranteed Residual Value (URV): ₹ 50,000.
- Implicit interest rate (IRR): 12% p.a.
- PV Factors at 12%: Year 1 = 0.8929, Year 2 = 0.7972, Year 3 = 0.7118, Year 4 = 0.6355.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the Gross Investment in the lease for Aksat Leasing Ltd. (Lessor)?
explanation: Gross Investment in Lease = Total Lease Payments (4 × 6,50,000 = 26,00,000) + Guaranteed Residual Value (1,00,000) + Unguaranteed Residual Value (50,000) = ₹ 27,50,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the 'Unearned Finance Income' for Aksat Leasing Ltd. (Lessor) at inception of the lease?
explanation: Unearned Finance Income = Gross Investment (₹ 27,50,000) - Net Investment (Fair Value ₹ 20,00,000) = ₹ 7,50,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the Finance Income to be recognized by Aksat Leasing Ltd. in its Profit and Loss Account for Year 1 (FY 2024-25)?
explanation: Finance Income Year 1 = Net Investment at beginning (₹ 20,00,000) × IRR (12%) = ₹ 2,40,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Starline Services Ltd. (Lessee) depreciates the asset on a straight-line basis over 4 years to its GRV of ₹ 1,00,000. At what initial carrying amount is the leased asset recorded by the lessee, and what is the depreciation for Year 1?
optionA: Asset recorded at ₹ 20,00,000 and Year 1 depreciation is ₹ 4,75,000
optionB: Asset recorded at ₹ 27,50,000 and Year 1 depreciation is ₹ 6,62,500
optionC: Asset recorded at ₹ 20,00,000 and Year 1 depreciation is ₹ 5,00,000
optionD: Asset recorded at ₹ 20,37,829 and Year 1 depreciation is ₹ 4,84,457
answerText: Asset recorded at ₹ 20,00,000 and Year 1 depreciation is ₹ 4,75,000
explanation: Asset recorded at lower of PV of MLP and Fair Value = ₹ 20,00,000. Annual Depreciation = (₹ 20,00,000 - ₹ 1,00,000 GRV) / 4 years = ₹ 4,75,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Kuber Chemical Ltd. has a distinct Cash-Generating Unit (CGU) producing industrial solvents. On 31st March 2025, due to adverse regulatory changes, the company tests the CGU for impairment.
The carrying amounts of the assets of the CGU before impairment testing are:
- Goodwill: ₹ 10,00,000
- Factory Building: ₹ 30,00,000
- Plant & Machinery: ₹ 40,00,000
- Intangible Asset (Technical Know-how): ₹ 20,00,000
Total Carrying Amount of CGU = ₹ 1,00,00,000 (₹ 100 Lakhs).

Additional Information:
- Net Selling Price of the CGU as a whole is estimated at ₹ 65,00,000.
- Value in Use of the CGU is calculated as ₹ 70,00,000.
- The Net Selling Price of Technical Know-how individually is known to be ₹ 17,00,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the Recoverable Amount of the Cash-Generating Unit (CGU) on 31st March 2025?
explanation: Recoverable Amount = Higher of Net Selling Price (₹ 65,00,000) and Value in Use (₹ 70,00,000) = ₹ 70,00,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the total Impairment Loss to be recognized for the CGU on 31st March 2025?
explanation: Impairment Loss = Carrying Amount (₹ 1,00,00,000) - Recoverable Amount (₹ 70,00,000) = ₹ 30,00,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the maximum impairment loss that can be allocated to the Intangible Asset (Technical Know-how) under AS 28?
explanation: Under AS 28, the carrying amount of an individual asset shall not be reduced below the highest of its net selling price (₹ 17,00,000), value in use, and zero. Since carrying amount is ₹ 20,00,000 and net selling price is ₹ 17,00,000, maximum impairment loss allocated to Technical Know-how is ₹ 3,00,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the revised carrying amount of Plant & Machinery after the complete allocation of the CGU impairment loss on 31st March 2025?
explanation: Total Loss = 30,00,000. Goodwill = 10,00,000. Remaining = 20,00,000. Initial pro-rata share for Plant = 20,00,000 × (40/90) = 8,88,889. Initial share for Technical Know-how = 20,00,000 × (20/90) = 4,44,444 (capped at 3,00,000). Excess loss of 1,44,444 is reallocated to Building and Plant in ratio 30:40. Plant share of excess = 1,44,444 × 4/7 = 82,539. Total Plant impairment = 8,88,889 + 82,539 = 9,71,428. Revised Carrying Amount = 40,00,000 - 9,71,428 = ₹ 30,28,572.
conceptTags: AS 28 | Impairment | Asset Carrying Value Allocation

subject: Accounts
prompt: According to AS 29 'Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets', how should a provision be measured in the balance sheet?
optionA: At the present value of the expected expenditure discounted at the risk-free rate
optionB: At the best estimate of the expenditure required to settle the present obligation at the balance sheet date without discounting
optionC: At the maximum potential loss that could arise from the obligation
optionD: At the average of the minimum and maximum possible outcome amounts
answerText: At the best estimate of the expenditure required to settle the present obligation at the balance sheet date without discounting
explanation: Under AS 29, provisions are measured at the best estimate of the expenditure required to settle the present obligation at the balance sheet date. Unlike Ind AS 37, standard provisions under AS 29 are generally not discounted to present value unless specifically required by another standard.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 15 'Employee Benefits', short-term employee benefits are defined as benefits expected to be settled wholly before how many months after the end of the period in which employees render the related service?
optionA: 6 months
optionB: 12 months
optionC: 24 months
optionD: 36 months
answerText: 12 months
explanation: AS 15 defines short-term employee benefits as employee benefits (other than termination benefits) that fall due wholly within twelve months after the end of the period in which the employees render the related service.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which of the following events triggers the 'Initial Disclosure Event' for a discontinuing operation under AS 24?
optionA: The Board of Directors considers a preliminary feasibility report to sell an operating component
optionB: The enterprise enters into a binding sale agreement for substantially all assets attributable to the discontinuing operation
optionC: The firm negotiations with potential buyers begin without any formal board decision
optionD: The competitor announces a market takeover of the firm's business sector
answerText: The enterprise enters into a binding sale agreement for substantially all assets attributable to the discontinuing operation
explanation: Under AS 24, the Initial Disclosure Event occurs on the earlier of: (a) the enterprise entering into a binding sale agreement for substantially all of the assets attributable to the discontinuing operation, or (b) the board of directors approving a detailed formal plan and making an announcement of the plan.
conceptTags: AS 24 | Initial Disclosure Event | Discontinuing Operations

subject: Accounts
prompt: How should a contingent asset be treated in the financial statements under AS 29?
optionA: Recognized in the Balance Sheet when economic inflow is probable
optionB: Disclosed in the Notes to Accounts when economic inflow is remote
optionC: Neither recognized nor disclosed in the financial statements, but disclosed in the Report of the Board of Directors if inflow is probable
optionD: Recognized directly in the Statement of Profit and Loss as accrued revenue
answerText: Neither recognized nor disclosed in the financial statements, but disclosed in the Report of the Board of Directors if inflow is probable
explanation: AS 29 prohibits the recognition of contingent assets in financial statements. Where an inflow of economic benefits is probable, the contingent asset is disclosed in the Report of the Board of Directors, not in the financial statements.

subject: Accounts
prompt: In a defined contribution plan under AS 15, who bears the actuarial risk and investment risk?
optionA: The enterprise (employer)
optionB: The employee
optionC: The trustee of the fund jointly with the employer
optionD: The Government pension authority
answerText: The employee
explanation: In a defined contribution plan, the enterprise's obligation is limited to the contribution agreed to be paid into the fund. Consequently, actuarial risk and investment risk fall on the employee.
conceptTags: AS 15 | Defined Contribution Plan | Actuarial Risk

subject: Accounts
prompt: A company has a present obligation arising from a past event, but it is NOT probable that an outflow of resources embodying economic benefits will be required to settle it. How should this item be treated under AS 29?
optionA: Recognize a Provision
optionB: Disclose as a Contingent Liability, unless the possibility of outflow is remote
optionC: Do not disclose or recognize anything
optionD: Recognize as a Contingent Asset
answerText: Disclose as a Contingent Liability, unless the possibility of outflow is remote
explanation: Under AS 29, a present obligation where an outflow of resources embodying economic benefits is not probable (i.e. possible or less than 50% likely) is disclosed as a contingent liability, unless the possibility of outflow is remote.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Does the piecemeal disposal of individual assets of a business line without a detailed formal plan constitute a discontinuing operation under AS 24?
optionA: Yes, if the aggregate sale value of assets exceeds 10% of total assets
optionB: Yes, provided all assets are sold within one financial year
optionC: No, individual asset disposals without a single coordinated plan do not constitute a discontinuing operation
optionD: Yes, always
answerText: No, individual asset disposals without a single coordinated plan do not constitute a discontinuing operation
explanation: Under AS 24, a discontinuing operation must be pursuant to a single overall plan to dispose of, abandon, or terminate a major line of business or geographical area. Gradual piecemeal disposals without such a plan do not meet the definition.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 15, how should an enterprise account for non-vesting accumulating compensated absences?
optionA: No liability is recognized until employees actually take the leave
optionB: Recognize an expense and liability for the expected cost of the accumulated unutilized leave expected to be used as a result of the unused entitlement
optionC: Recognize a provision for the total accumulated unutilized leave balance for all employees at gross pay rates
optionD: Charge the entire accumulated amount directly to reserves
answerText: Recognize an expense and liability for the expected cost of the accumulated unutilized leave expected to be used as a result of the unused entitlement
explanation: For accumulating non-vesting paid absences, AS 15 requires an enterprise to measure the expected cost as the additional amount that it expects to pay as a result of the unused entitlement that has accumulated at the balance sheet date.

subject: Accounts
prompt: When the possibility of an outflow of economic resources to settle an obligation is remote, how is it treated under AS 29?
optionA: Recognized as a provision
optionB: Disclosed in the Notes to Accounts
optionC: No provision and no disclosure required in financial statements
optionD: Disclosed only in the Directors' Report
answerText: No provision and no disclosure required in financial statements
explanation: Under AS 29, if the possibility of any outflow of resources in settlement of an obligation is remote, neither recognition of a provision nor disclosure as a contingent liability is required.

subject: Accounts
prompt: When should an enterprise recognize an expense and liability for termination benefits under AS 15?
optionA: Over the remaining service life of the retrenched employees
optionB: Immediately when the enterprise is demonstrably committed to terminate the employment
optionC: In equal installments over 5 years starting from the date of payment
optionD: Only when actual cash payment is disbursed to employees
answerText: Immediately when the enterprise is demonstrably committed to terminate the employment
explanation: Under AS 15, an enterprise should recognize termination benefits as an expense immediately when the enterprise is demonstrably committed to either terminate employment before normal retirement or provide termination benefits as a result of an offer made to encourage voluntary redundancy.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 15, how is unvested past service cost recognized in the Statement of Profit and Loss?
optionA: Recognized immediately as an expense in the year of amendment
optionB: Recognized as an expense on a straight-line basis over the average period until the benefits become vested
optionC: Capitalized as an intangible asset and amortized over 10 years
optionD: Deducted directly from General Reserves without routing through P&L
answerText: Recognized as an expense on a straight-line basis over the average period until the benefits become vested
explanation: Under AS 15, past service cost for unvested benefits is recognized as an expense on a straight-line basis over the average period until the benefits become vested. Vested past service cost is recognized immediately.
conceptTags: AS 15 | Past Service Cost | Defined Benefit Plans

subject: Accounts
prompt: Apex Ltd. enters into an onerous operating lease contract for an empty warehouse. The remaining non-cancellable lease payment is ₹600,000 per annum for 2 years. The cancellation penalty is ₹900,000. Sub-leasing is permitted and estimated to yield ₹400,000 per annum. What is the provision amount under AS 29?
explanation: An onerous contract provision is measured at the unavoidable costs of meeting obligations, which is the lower of net cost of fulfilling the contract and penalty for non-fulfillment. Fulfilling net cost = (₹600,000 - ₹400,000) × 2 years = ₹400,000. Cancellation penalty = ₹900,000. Provision required = Lower of ₹400,000 and ₹900,000 = ₹400,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 15, which rate should be used to discount post-employment benefit obligations (both funded and unfunded)?
optionA: The enterprise's weighted average cost of capital (WACC)
optionB: The prime lending rate of State Bank of India
optionC: Market yields at the balance sheet date on government bonds
optionD: The expected rate of return on plan assets
answerText: Market yields at the balance sheet date on government bonds
explanation: Under AS 15, the rate used to discount post-employment benefit obligations should be determined by reference to market yields at the balance sheet date on government bonds.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Gamma Ltd. sells goods with a 1-year product warranty. Historical data shows that 80% goods have no defects, 15% have minor defects costing ₹200 to repair per unit, and 5% have major defects costing ₹800 to repair per unit. If 1,000 units were sold during the year, what provision for warranty should be recognized under AS 29?

subject: Accounts
prompt: When an enterprise expects to be reimbursed by a third party (e.g., an insurer) for expenditure required to settle a provision, how should this reimbursement be accounted for under AS 29?
optionA: Recognized as a net deduction from the provision liability in the Balance Sheet
optionB: Recognized as a separate asset when it is virtually certain that reimbursement will be received, with the asset not exceeding the provision amount
optionC: Recognized as income immediately in Statement of Profit and Loss before the provision is settled
optionD: Disclosed only as a contingent asset in the Directors' Report
answerText: Recognized as a separate asset when it is virtually certain that reimbursement will be received, with the asset not exceeding the provision amount
explanation: AS 29 mandates that reimbursement is recognized as a separate asset in the Balance Sheet when it is virtually certain that reimbursement will be received if the obligation is settled. The asset recognized cannot exceed the provision amount.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 24, which of the following is NOT a mandatory disclosure requirement in the financial statements for a discontinuing operation?
optionA: A description of the discontinuing operation
optionB: The business segment or geographical segment in which it is reported under AS 17
optionC: The exact name and postal address of prospective buyers of the assets
optionD: The date and nature of the Initial Disclosure Event
answerText: The exact name and postal address of prospective buyers of the assets
explanation: AS 24 mandates disclosure of the operation's description, segment details, and date/nature of the initial disclosure event, but does not require disclosing the exact identity or postal address of prospective buyers.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 15, actuarial gains and losses on defined benefit obligations and plan assets should be:
optionA: Recognized immediately in the Statement of Profit and Loss as income or expense
optionB: Deferred and amortized over the expected average remaining working lives of employees
optionC: Recognized directly in Capital Reserve
optionD: Carried forward in a special buffer reserve until retirement of employees
answerText: Recognized immediately in the Statement of Profit and Loss as income or expense
explanation: Under AS 15 (revised), actuarial gains and losses must be recognized immediately in the Statement of Profit and Loss in the period in which they arise.
conceptTags: AS 15 | Actuarial Gains and Losses | P&L Treatment

subject: Accounts
prompt: A restructuring provision under AS 29 can include which of the following expenditures?
optionA: Retraining or relocating continuing staff
optionB: Marketing and advertising expenditure for new products
optionC: Direct costs strictly arising from restructuring such as employee severance pay
optionD: Investment in new systems and distribution networks for continuing operations
answerText: Direct costs strictly arising from restructuring such as employee severance pay
explanation: A restructuring provision includes only direct expenditures arising from restructuring, which are necessarily entailed by restructuring and not associated with ongoing activities. Costs like retraining staff, marketing, or investment in new systems relate to ongoing future operations and cannot be included.
conceptTags: AS 29 | Restructuring Provision | Scope of Provision

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 15, profit-sharing and bonus plans require recognition as a liability and expense when the enterprise has a present legal or constructive obligation AND:
optionA: The bonus has already been physically distributed to employees
optionB: A reliable estimate of the obligation can be made
optionC: The profit after tax exceeds 20% of net worth
optionD: The Board of Directors passes a final resolution after the AGM
answerText: A reliable estimate of the obligation can be made
explanation: Under AS 15, an enterprise recognizes the expected cost of profit-sharing and bonus payments when it has a present legal or constructive obligation to make such payments as a result of past events, AND a reliable estimate of the obligation can be made.
conceptTags: AS 15 | Profit-Sharing and Bonus Plans | Recognition Criteria

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which actuarial valuation method is mandated by AS 15 for determining the present value of defined benefit obligations and related current service cost?
optionA: Pay-as-you-go method
optionB: Projected Unit Credit Method
optionC: Entry Age Normal Method without projection
optionD: Aggregate Cost Method
answerText: Projected Unit Credit Method
explanation: AS 15 explicitly mandates the use of the Projected Unit Credit Method (also known as the accrued benefit method prorated on service) to determine the present value of defined benefit obligations and current service cost.
conceptTags: AS 15 | Projected Unit Credit Method | Actuarial Valuation

subject: Accounts
prompt: Delta Ltd. has an ongoing business unit. On 10th March 2026, management decides to close the unit but takes no formal action, makes no announcement, and enters no binding contracts before 31st March 2026. Can a restructuring provision be recognized as of 31st March 2026 under AS 29?
optionA: Yes, because management intent creates a constructive obligation
optionB: No, because management decision alone does not raise a valid expectation in those affected before the balance sheet date
optionC: Yes, provided the closure occurs before financial statements are approved
optionD: Yes, but only as a contingent liability
answerText: No, because management decision alone does not raise a valid expectation in those affected before the balance sheet date
explanation: Under AS 29, a management decision alone does not give rise to a constructive obligation at the balance sheet date unless a detailed formal plan has been approved and implementation started or main features announced to affected parties on or before the balance sheet date.

subject: Accounts
prompt: When an operation meets the definition of a discontinuing operation under AS 24, from which period's financial statements should the initial disclosures begin?
optionA: From the prospective financial year following the physical closure of operations
optionB: In the financial statements for the period in which the Initial Disclosure Event occurs
optionC: Only in the year when all assets of the component are fully liquidated
optionD: Retrospectively for the past 5 financial years as prior period adjustments
answerText: In the financial statements for the period in which the Initial Disclosure Event occurs
explanation: AS 24 requires an enterprise to apply the disclosure requirements for a discontinuing operation starting with the financial statements for the period in which the Initial Disclosure Event occurs.
conceptTags: AS 24 | Initial Disclosure Event | Timing of Disclosure

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 29, can an enterprise create a provision for future operating losses of a business segment?
optionA: Yes, if expected operating losses are reliably estimated
optionB: Yes, provided the segment is classified as a discontinuing operation under AS 24
optionC: No, provisions shall not be recognized for future operating losses because they do not meet the definition of a present obligation arising from past events
optionD: Yes, but limited to 50% of projected losses
answerText: No, provisions shall not be recognized for future operating losses because they do not meet the definition of a present obligation arising from past events
explanation: AS 29 explicitly states that provisions shall not be recognized for future operating losses because future operating losses do not meet the definition of a liability/present obligation arising from a past event.
conceptTags: AS 29 | Future Operating Losses | Provisions Prohibition

subject: Accounts
prompt: If the Initial Disclosure Event for a discontinuing operation occurs AFTER the balance sheet date but BEFORE the financial statements are approved by the Board of Directors, what is the accounting treatment under AS 24 and AS 4?
optionA: It is an adjusting event; full AS 24 disclosures must be incorporated in the balance sheet and P&L of the current reporting period
optionB: It is a non-adjusting event; no disclosure is required anywhere
optionC: It is a non-adjusting event under AS 4, but disclosure of the discontinuing operation is made in the Report of the Board of Directors
optionD: The financial statements must be delayed until the disposal process is complete
answerText: It is a non-adjusting event under AS 4, but disclosure of the discontinuing operation is made in the Report of the Board of Directors
explanation: If the IDE occurs after the balance sheet date but before approval of financial statements, it does not represent a condition existing at the balance sheet date (non-adjusting event under AS 4). However, disclosure is made in the Board's Report as per AS 24 / AS 4 guidance.
conceptTags: AS 24 | AS 4 | Post Balance Sheet Events

subject: Accounts
prompt: In a defined benefit plan under AS 15, if the net actuarial calculation results in an asset (surplus), how is the maximum asset to be recognized in the Balance Sheet capped?
optionA: At 100% of the total annual service cost
optionB: At the lower of the net surplus and the present value of any economic benefits available in the form of refunds from the plan or reductions in future contributions
optionC: At the total fair value of plan assets
optionD: Surpluses can never be recognized under AS 15
answerText: At the lower of the net surplus and the present value of any economic benefits available in the form of refunds from the plan or reductions in future contributions
explanation: Under AS 15, the asset recognized in the balance sheet is limited to the lower of the net defined benefit asset (surplus) and the present value of economic benefits available in the form of refunds from the plan or reductions in future contributions to the plan.
conceptTags: AS 15 | Defined Benefit Asset Ceiling | Surplus Cap

subject: Accounts
prompt: When an enterprise is jointly and severally liable for an obligation with other parties, how should the portion expected to be met by other parties be treated under AS 29?
optionA: Recognized as a provision for the total 100% liability
optionB: Treated as a contingent liability for the portion expected to be met by other parties
optionC: Ignored completely from both Balance Sheet and Notes
optionD: Recognized as an asset under Reimbursements
answerText: Treated as a contingent liability for the portion expected to be met by other parties
explanation: Under AS 29, that part of the joint and several obligation that is expected to be met by other parties is treated as a contingent liability (and disclosed), while the portion for which an outflow is probable is recognized as a provision.
conceptTags: AS 29 | Joint and Several Liability | Contingent Liabilities

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 24, when an enterprise presents financial statements after the Initial Disclosure Event, how are comparative figures for prior periods presented?
optionA: Prior period statements are fully restated by removing discontinuing operations from previous revenues
optionB: Comparative information for prior periods presented in financial statements is reclassified to segregate continuing and discontinuing assets, liabilities, revenues, and expenses
optionC: Prior period figures are left untouched and no reclassification or disclosure is permitted
optionD: Prior period financial statements are restated as a cumulative effect adjustment in opening retained earnings
answerText: Comparative information for prior periods presented in financial statements is reclassified to segregate continuing and discontinuing assets, liabilities, revenues, and expenses
explanation: AS 24 requires comparative information for prior periods presented in the financial statements to be reclassified to segregate continuing and discontinuing assets, liabilities, revenues, expenses, and cash flows to enable meaningful comparison.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 15, expected return on plan assets is based on market expectations at the beginning of the period for returns over the entire life of the related obligation. How is the difference between expected return and actual return on plan assets accounted for?
optionA: Amortized over 5 years on a straight-line basis
optionB: Recognized immediately as an actuarial gain or loss in the Statement of Profit and Loss
optionC: Adjusted against opening General Reserve
optionD: Transferred to a separate Asset Equalization Reserve
answerText: Recognized immediately as an actuarial gain or loss in the Statement of Profit and Loss
explanation: The difference between the actual return on plan assets and the expected return on plan assets constitutes an actuarial gain or loss on plan assets, which is recognized immediately in the Statement of Profit and Loss under AS 15.
conceptTags: AS 15 | Return on Plan Assets | Actuarial Gain/Loss

subject: Accounts
prompt: A company is defending a lawsuit. Management's legal counsel advises that there is a 60% probability that the company will lose the case and have to pay ₹5,000,000, and a 40% probability that it will win and pay ₹0. How should this be accounted for under AS 29?
optionA: Recognize a provision of ₹3,000,000 (weighted average outcome)
optionB: Recognize a provision of ₹5,000,000
optionC: Disclose a contingent liability of ₹5,000,000 with zero provision
optionD: Recognize a provision of ₹2,500,000
answerText: Recognize a provision of ₹5,000,000
explanation: Where a single obligation is being measured, the most likely outcome generally represents the best estimate under AS 29. Since there is a 60% (probable) chance of losing ₹5,000,000, the provision should be recognized at ₹5,000,000 rather than expected value.
conceptTags: AS 29 | Single Obligation Measurement | Best Estimate

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 29, if a provision is reviewed at each balance sheet date and it is clear that an outflow of resources is no longer probable, what action must be taken?
optionA: The provision should be retained in the balance sheet indefinitely until the legal limitation period expires
optionB: The provision should be written back and reversed to the Statement of Profit and Loss
optionC: The provision should be transferred directly to Capital Reserve
optionD: The provision should be reclassified as a deferred liability
answerText: The provision should be written back and reversed to the Statement of Profit and Loss
explanation: AS 29 requires provisions to be reviewed at each balance sheet date and adjusted to reflect the current best estimate. If it is no longer probable that an outflow of resources embodying economic benefits will be required to settle the obligation, the provision should be reversed to P&L.

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Kaveri Chemicals Ltd. operates two separate business lines: a Bulk Chemical Plant and a Speciality Solvents division. For the financial year ended 31st March 2026, the following situations arise:

1. In March 2026, the State Environmental Control Board passed a mandatory directive requiring Kaveri Chemicals to decontaminate soil at its Bulk Chemical Plant before April 2028. The estimated cost of decontamination is ₹15,000,000. Under AS 29, the management is evaluating whether to discount this provision.

2. The Speciality Solvents division sold 2,000 chemical containers during 2025-26 under a standard 1-year leakage warranty. Historical performance indicates that 90% of containers experience no leakage, 7% suffer minor leakage (repair cost ₹2,000 per container), and 3% suffer major leakage (replacement cost ₹10,000 per container).

3. An employee filed a damages suit of ₹8,000,000 against the company for workplace injury. Legal experts advise that there is a 30% chance the company will be held liable.

4. For warranty claims exceeding ₹500,000 in total, Kaveri Chemicals holds an indemnity insurance contract with an insurer. The insurer has confirmed in writing that it will reimburse 80% of warranty costs incurred above ₹500,000 once claims are paid.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Regarding the decontamination liability of ₹15,000,000 for the Bulk Chemical Plant, how should it be recognized in the financial statements for FY 2025-26 under AS 29?
optionA: Recognize a provision at the present value of ₹15,000,000 using a 10% discount rate
optionB: Recognize a provision at the undiscounted amount of ₹15,000,000 as a present obligation
optionC: Disclose as a contingent liability because actual payment is due in 2028
optionD: Do not recognize or disclose until the decontamination work commences in 2028
answerText: Recognize a provision at the undiscounted amount of ₹15,000,000 as a present obligation
explanation: A mandatory directive creates a present obligation from a past event with a probable outflow. Under AS 29, provisions are measured at best estimate and are generally not discounted to present value. Hence, an undiscounted provision of ₹15,000,000 is recognized.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the warranty provision required for the Speciality Solvents division as of 31st March 2026 under AS 29?
explanation: Expected cost per container = (90% × ₹0) + (7% × ₹2,000) + (3% × ₹10,000) = ₹0 + ₹140 + ₹300 = ₹440 per container. Total provision for 2,000 containers = 2,000 × ₹440 = ₹880,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt: How should the insurance reimbursement for warranty claims be presented in the Balance Sheet as of 31st March 2026?
optionA: Deduct ₹304,000 directly from the Warranty Provision liability in the Balance Sheet
optionB: Recognize a separate Reimbursement Asset of ₹304,000 in the Balance Sheet, as reimbursement is virtually certain
optionC: Recognize a Reimbursement Asset of ₹704,000
optionD: Disclose as a Contingent Asset in the Board's Report only
answerText: Recognize a separate Reimbursement Asset of ₹304,000 in the Balance Sheet, as reimbursement is virtually certain
explanation: Total warranty provision = ₹880,000. Reimbursement applies to excess over ₹500,000 = ₹880,000 - ₹500,000 = ₹380,000. Insurer covers 80% of excess = 80% × ₹380,000 = ₹304,000. Under AS 29, reimbursement is recognized as a separate asset (not netted against liability in Balance Sheet) when virtually certain.

subject: Accounts
prompt: How should the pending damages lawsuit of ₹8,000,000 be treated in the financial statements for FY 2025-26 under AS 29?
optionA: Recognize a provision of ₹2,400,000 (30% of ₹8,000,000)
optionB: Recognize a provision of ₹8,000,000
optionC: Disclose as a Contingent Liability in the Notes to Accounts, since the outflow is possible (30%) but not probable
optionD: Ignore completely without any disclosure since probability is less than 50%
answerText: Disclose as a Contingent Liability in the Notes to Accounts, since the outflow is possible (30%) but not probable
explanation: A 30% chance represents a possible obligation (not probable, as probability < 50%). Under AS 29, a possible obligation that is not remote must be disclosed as a Contingent Liability in the Notes to Accounts.

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Engineering Ltd. maintains a funded Defined Benefit Gratuity Scheme for its employees. Actuarial valuation and scheme data for the financial year ended 31st March 2026 reveal the following:

• Opening Present Value of Defined Benefit Obligation (DBO) as on 1st April 2025: ₹5,000,000
• Opening Fair Value of Plan Assets as on 1st April 2025: ₹4,000,000
• Discount Rate (based on Government Securities): 10% per annum
• Expected Rate of Return on Plan Assets: 10% per annum
• Current Service Cost for FY 2025-26: ₹800,000
• Plan amendment on 1st July 2025 granted past service benefits of ₹1,000,000, of which ₹400,000 vested immediately and ₹600,000 vests over 3 remaining years of service.
• Benefits paid to retired employees during FY 2025-26: ₹500,000
• Contributions paid by Zenith Engineering into the plan during FY 2025-26: ₹800,000
• Closing DBO as per Actuarial Valuation on 31st March 2026: ₹7,200,000
• Closing Fair Value of Plan Assets as on 31st March 2026: ₹4,900,000

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the amount of Actuarial Gain or Loss on the Defined Benefit Obligation (DBO) for FY 2025-26?
optionA: Actuarial Loss of ₹400,000
optionB: Actuarial Gain of ₹400,000
optionC: Actuarial Loss of ₹200,000
optionD: Actuarial Loss of ₹600,000
answerText: Actuarial Loss of ₹400,000
explanation: Expected DBO at year end = Opening DBO (₹5,000,000) + Interest Cost (10% of ₹5,000,000 = ₹500,000) + Current Service Cost (₹800,000) + Total Past Service Cost (₹1,000,000) - Benefits Paid (₹500,000) = ₹6,800,000. Actual Closing DBO = ₹7,200,000. Actuarial Loss on DBO = ₹7,200,000 - ₹6,800,000 = ₹400,000.
conceptTags: AS 15 | Actuarial Loss | Defined Benefit Obligation

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the Actuarial Gain or Loss on Plan Assets for FY 2025-26?
optionA: Actuarial Loss of ₹200,000
optionB: Actuarial Gain of ₹200,000
optionC: Actuarial Gain of ₹400,000
optionD: Actuarial Loss of ₹100,000
answerText: Actuarial Gain of ₹200,000
explanation: Expected Plan Assets at year end = Opening Plan Assets (₹4,000,000) + Expected Return (10% of ₹4,000,000 = ₹400,000) + Contributions (₹800,000) - Benefits Paid (₹500,000) = ₹4,700,000. Actual Closing Plan Assets = ₹4,900,000. Actuarial Gain on Plan Assets = ₹4,900,000 - ₹4,700,000 = ₹200,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What total net expense should Zenith Engineering Ltd. recognize in the Statement of Profit and Loss for FY 2025-26 under AS 15?
explanation: Net Expense in P&L = Current Service Cost (₹800,000) + Interest Cost (₹500,000) - Expected Return on Plan Assets (₹400,000) + Recognized Past Service Cost [₹400,000 vested + (₹600,000 / 3 yrs unvested) = ₹600,000] + Actuarial Loss on DBO (₹400,000) - Actuarial Gain on Plan Assets (₹200,000) = 800,000 + 500,000 - 400,000 + 600,000 + 400,000 - 200,000 = ₹2,100,000.
conceptTags: AS 15 | Net Gratuity Expense | P&L Calculation

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the Net Defined Benefit Liability to be reported in the Balance Sheet of Zenith Engineering Ltd. as of 31st March 2026?
explanation: Net Liability in Balance Sheet = Closing Present Value of DBO (₹7,200,000) - Unrecognized Past Service Cost (₹600,000 total - ₹200,000 recognized = ₹400,000 remaining) - Closing Fair Value of Plan Assets (₹4,900,000) = 7,200,000 - 400,000 - 4,900,000 = ₹1,900,000. (Check: Opening Net Liability ₹1,000,000 + P&L Expense ₹2,100,000 - Contributions ₹800,000 = ₹1,900,000).
conceptTags: AS 15 | Net Defined Benefit Liability | Balance Sheet

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Crimson Consumer Goods Ltd. manufactures textiles and healthcare products. Due to sustained losses in its Textile Division, the Board of Directors took the following actions during FY 2025-26:

• On 15th December 2025, the Board approved a detailed formal plan to discontinue the entire Textile Division (which constitutes a separate major line of business and segment).
• On 20th January 2026, the company entered into a legally binding agreement to sell the spinning equipment of Unit A of the Textile Division for ₹12,000,000.
• On 10th February 2026, Crimson Consumer Goods Ltd. made a formal public announcement of its plan to discontinue the Textile Division.
• The financial year ended on 31st March 2026. Financial statements were approved by the Board on 25th May 2026.
• Carrying value of total assets of Textile Division as of 31st March 2026 was ₹50,000,000, while their net realizable value was estimated at ₹42,000,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the date of the 'Initial Disclosure Event' (IDE) for the discontinuing operation under AS 24?
optionA: 15th December 2025
optionB: 20th January 2026
optionC: 10th February 2026
optionD: 31st March 2026
answerText: 20th January 2026
explanation: Under AS 24, the Initial Disclosure Event occurs on the EARLIER of: (a) binding sale agreement date (20th January 2026), or (b) board approval of detailed plan AND public announcement (10th February 2026). Thus, the binding agreement date (20th January 2026) is the IDE date.
conceptTags: AS 24 | Initial Disclosure Event | Discontinuing Operations

subject: Accounts
prompt: How should the impairment loss on the assets of the Textile Division be recognized in the financial statements for FY 2025-26?
optionA: Recognize an impairment loss of ₹8,000,000 in the Statement of Profit and Loss for FY 2025-26
optionB: Defer the impairment loss until all assets of the division are physically handed over
optionC: Charge ₹8,000,000 directly to Revaluation Reserve
optionD: Disclose ₹8,000,000 as a contingent loss without reducing asset carrying values
answerText: Recognize an impairment loss of ₹8,000,000 in the Statement of Profit and Loss for FY 2025-26
explanation: Under AS 24 and AS 28, when an initial disclosure event occurs or assets are held for disposal, their recoverable/net realizable value is assessed. An impairment loss equal to Carrying Value (₹50,000,000) - Net Realizable Value (₹42,000,000) = ₹8,000,000 must be recognized immediately in P&L.

subject: Accounts
prompt: In the financial statements for FY 2025-26, which of the following details regarding the Textile Division MUST be disclosed on the face of or in the notes to the financial statements under AS 24?
optionA: Pre-tax profit/loss of the discontinuing operation and income tax expense related thereto
optionB: Names of all individual machine operators who will be laid off
optionC: Estimated market share of competitors after Crimson's exit
optionD: Board minutes of all internal strategy meetings held prior to 15th December 2025
answerText: Pre-tax profit/loss of the discontinuing operation and income tax expense related thereto
explanation: AS 24 mandates disclosure of the amounts of revenue, expenses, pre-tax profit or loss of the discontinuing operation, and the related income tax expense.

subject: Accounts
prompt: How should cash flow disclosures for the Textile Division be presented in the Cash Flow Statement for FY 2025-26 under AS 24?
optionA: Cash flows of discontinuing operations should be completely omitted from the Cash Flow Statement
optionB: Net cash flows attributable to operating, investing, and financing activities of the discontinuing operation must be disclosed on the face or in notes
optionC: All cash flows of the discontinuing operation must be merged into operating activities only
optionD: Cash flows should only be disclosed for future prospective years
answerText: Net cash flows attributable to operating, investing, and financing activities of the discontinuing operation must be disclosed on the face or in notes
explanation: AS 24 mandates disclosure of the net cash flows attributable to the operating, investing, and financing activities of the discontinuing operation either on the face of the cash flow statement or in the notes.
conceptTags: AS 24 | Cash Flow Statement | Discontinuing Operations

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Apex Retailers Ltd. is preparing its financial statements for the year ended 31st March 2026. The controller faces the following independent issues:

Issue 1: Apex entered into a non-cancellable 5-year commercial lease for an outlet at ₹1,200,000/year. 2 years remain. Apex vacated the premises to relocate. The landlord demands a cancellation fee of ₹1,800,000. Apex can sublet the outlet for the remaining 2 years at ₹800,000/year.

Issue 2: Division B is incurring losses. The budget for FY 2026-27 projects an operating loss of ₹3,000,000 for Division B. Management wants to create a provision for this projected operating loss as of 31st March 2026.

Issue 3: On 25th March 2026, the Board approved a detailed restructuring plan to close Branch X. The plan entails severance payments of ₹1,500,000. However, the plan was communicated to affected employees and public announcement was made on 5th April 2026 (before audit completion).

subject: Accounts
prompt: For Issue 1 (Onerous Lease), what provision should Apex Retailers Ltd. recognize as of 31st March 2026 under AS 29?
explanation: Onerous contract provision is the lower of net fulfillment cost and cancellation penalty. Net fulfillment cost = (₹1,200,000 rent - ₹800,000 sublet) × 2 years = ₹800,000. Cancellation penalty = ₹1,800,000. Provision required = Lower of ₹800,000 and ₹1,800,000 = ₹800,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt: For Issue 2 (Projected Operating Loss), how should the ₹3,000,000 projected loss of Division B be accounted for as of 31st March 2026 under AS 29?
optionA: Recognize a provision of ₹3,000,000 as a current liability
optionB: Recognize a provision of ₹1,500,000 (50% prudential provision)
optionC: No provision should be recognized because future operating losses do not meet the definition of a present obligation arising from past events
optionD: Disclose as a Contingent Asset in the Directors' Report
answerText: No provision should be recognized because future operating losses do not meet the definition of a present obligation arising from past events
explanation: AS 29 explicitly prohibits provisions for future operating losses because they do not arise from past events and do not meet the definition of a present obligation.

subject: Accounts
prompt: For Issue 3 (Restructuring Plan), can Apex Retailers Ltd. recognize a restructuring provision of ₹1,500,000 for Branch X in the balance sheet as of 31st March 2026?
optionA: Yes, because the Board approved the detailed plan before 31st March 2026
optionB: No, because a constructive obligation arises only when implementation starts or main features are announced to affected parties ON OR BEFORE 31st March 2026
optionC: Yes, because public announcement occurred before audit completion date
optionD: Yes, provided approval is disclosed in the Directors' Report
answerText: No, because a constructive obligation arises only when implementation starts or main features are announced to affected parties ON OR BEFORE 31st March 2026
explanation: Under AS 29, a management/board decision taken before the balance sheet date does not create a constructive obligation as of the balance sheet date unless the plan was announced to affected parties or implementation commenced ON OR BEFORE the balance sheet date (31st March 2026). Communication on 5th April 2026 is a post-balance sheet non-adjusting event.
conceptTags: AS 29 | Restructuring Provision | Constructive Obligation Timing

subject: Accounts
prompt: If in FY 2026-27, Apex Retailers Ltd. sub-leases the outlet in Issue 1 for ₹1,300,000/year (which exceeds the lease rent of ₹1,200,000/year), what should happen to the onerous lease provision of ₹800,000?
optionA: Retain ₹800,000 in Capital Reserve
optionB: Reverse the ₹800,000 provision to the Statement of Profit and Loss as it is no longer required
optionC: Amortize the provision over the remaining lease term
optionD: Transfer ₹800,000 to General Reserve
answerText: Reverse the ₹800,000 provision to the Statement of Profit and Loss as it is no longer required
explanation: Under AS 29, provisions must be reviewed at each balance sheet date. If an obligation is no longer onerous (sub-lease covers lease liability), an outflow is no longer probable, so the provision must be reversed to Profit and Loss.

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Beta Services Ltd. employs 100 individuals and has the following employee benefit policies for FY 2025-26:
