explanation: The maximum permitted outflow under 25% of (Capital + Free Reserves) is ₹225,000. Buying back 10,000 shares at ₹25 costs ₹250,000, which exceeds ₹225,000. Thus, it fails the Shareholder Approval 25% overall limit test.
conceptTags: Statutory Test Verification | Section 68 Compliance | Buyback Capacity

subject: Accounts
prompt: According to AS 14 'Accounting for Amalgamations', which of the following payments made by the transferee company is included in the computation of 'Consideration'?
optionA: Payment made directly to the debenture holders of the transferor company
optionB: Payment made to the liquidation expense creditors of the transferor company
optionC: Payment made to the preference shareholders of the transferor company
optionD: Payment made to the trade creditors of the transferor company
answerText: Payment made to the preference shareholders of the transferor company
explanation: As per paragraph 3(b) of AS 14, consideration for amalgamation is the aggregate of the shares and other securities issued and the payment made in cash or other assets by the transferee company to the shareholders (equity and preference) of the transferor company. Payments made to third parties like debenture holders or creditors are settlements of liabilities and not part of purchase consideration.
conceptTags: AS 14 | Purchase Consideration | Scope of Consideration

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under AS 14, which condition MUST be satisfied for an amalgamation to be classified as an 'amalgamation in the nature of merger'?
optionA: All equity shareholders of the transferor company must become shareholders of the transferee company.
optionB: Shareholders holding not less than 90% of the face value of equity shares of the transferor company (other than held by transferee/subsidiaries) become equity shareholders of the transferee company.
optionC: Assets and liabilities must be recorded at fair values in the books of the transferee company.
optionD: Consideration must be paid entirely in cash to all equity shareholders.
answerText: Shareholders holding not less than 90% of the face value of equity shares of the transferor company (other than held by transferee/subsidiaries) become equity shareholders of the transferee company.
explanation: Under AS 14, one of the five essential conditions for an amalgamation in the nature of merger is that equity shareholders holding not less than 90% of the face value of equity shares of the transferor company (other than those already held by the transferee company or its subsidiaries) become equity shareholders of the transferee company by virtue of amalgamation.
conceptTags: AS 14 | Amalgamation in Nature of Merger | Conditions for Merger

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under the 'Pooling of Interests Method', how are the assets and liabilities of the transferor company recorded in the books of the transferee company?
optionA: At their fair values as on the date of amalgamation
optionB: At their liquidation values as determined by independent valuers
optionC: At their existing book values, except for adjustments to achieve uniform accounting policies
optionD: At replacement costs as on the date of acquisition
answerText: At their existing book values, except for adjustments to achieve uniform accounting policies
explanation: Under paragraph 10 of AS 14 (Pooling of Interests Method), assets, liabilities, and reserves of the transferor company are recorded by the transferee company at their existing carrying amounts (book values), subject only to adjustments required to ensure uniformity of accounting policies.
conceptTags: Pooling of Interests Method | Book Values | AS 14

subject: Accounts
prompt: When an amalgamation is accounted for under the 'Purchase Method', any excess of consideration paid over the net aggregate value of identifiable assets taken over over liabilities assumed is credited or debited to which account?
optionA: Debited to Capital Reserve Account
optionB: Debited to Goodwill Account
optionC: Credited to Amalgamation Adjustment Deficit Account
optionD: Debited to General Reserve Account
answerText: Debited to Goodwill Account
explanation: Under the Purchase Method of AS 14, if the purchase consideration exceeds the net agreed value of assets taken over less liabilities assumed, the difference is debited to Goodwill Account. If the consideration is less than net assets, the difference is credited to Capital Reserve Account.

subject: Accounts
prompt: How is the 'Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve' account presented in the balance sheet of the transferee company prepared as per Schedule III to the Companies Act, 2013?
optionA: As a separate line item under 'Other Non-Current Assets'
optionB: As a negative line item under 'Reserves and Surplus'
optionC: Under 'Other Current Assets' as a temporary debit balance
optionD: Deducted directly from Capital Reserve on the face of the Balance Sheet
answerText: As a negative line item under 'Reserves and Surplus'
explanation: As per ICAI study material and Schedule III guidelines, when a statutory reserve is maintained under the purchase method, the Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve (or Amalgamation Adjustment Deficit) is presented under 'Reserves and Surplus' as a negative balance (deduction), until the statutory reserve itself is maintained.
conceptTags: Statutory Reserve | Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve | Schedule III

subject: Accounts
prompt: Alpha Ltd acquires Beta Ltd under the purchase method. Beta Ltd has a statutory reserve (Export Profit Reserve) of ₹1,50,000 which needs to be maintained for 3 more years. What entry is passed in the books of Alpha Ltd?
optionA: General Reserve A/c Dr. ₹1,50,000 To Export Profit Reserve A/c ₹1,50,000
optionB: Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve A/c Dr. ₹1,50,000 To Export Profit Reserve A/c ₹1,50,000
optionC: Goodwill A/c Dr. ₹1,50,000 To Export Profit Reserve A/c ₹1,50,000
optionD: No entry is required as statutory reserves are not recorded under the purchase method.
answerText: Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve A/c Dr. ₹1,50,000 To Export Profit Reserve A/c ₹1,50,000
explanation: Under the purchase method, statutory reserves of the transferor company must be retained by debiting 'Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve Account' and crediting the relevant 'Statutory Reserve Account' (e.g., Export Profit Reserve).
conceptTags: Purchase Method | Statutory Reserve | Journal Entries

subject: Accounts
prompt: When liquidation expenses of the transferor company are paid and borne by the transferee company in an 'amalgamation in the nature of purchase', how is this transaction accounted for in the transferee company's books?
optionA: Debited to Profit and Loss Account
optionB: Debited to Realisation Account
optionC: Debited to Goodwill Account or credited/adjusted in Capital Reserve Account
optionD: Debited to General Reserve Account
answerText: Debited to Goodwill Account or credited/adjusted in Capital Reserve Account
explanation: In an amalgamation in the nature of purchase, liquidation expenses borne by the transferee company form part of the acquisition cost and are debited to Goodwill Account (or credited/deducted from Capital Reserve Account if capital reserve exists).
conceptTags: Liquidation Expenses | Purchase Method | Goodwill/Capital Reserve

subject: Accounts
prompt: If liquidation expenses of the transferor company are borne by the transferee company in an 'amalgamation in the nature of merger', where should the transferee company debit this expenditure?
optionA: Goodwill Account
optionB: Profit and Loss Account or General Reserve
optionC: Realisation Account
optionD: Preliminary Expenses Account
answerText: Profit and Loss Account or General Reserve
explanation: In an amalgamation in the nature of merger (Pooling of Interests Method), any costs directly incurred by the transferee company to effect amalgamation (including liquidation expenses reimbursed) are debited to Profit and Loss Account or Reserves.
conceptTags: Liquidation Expenses | Merger Method | Accounting Treatment

subject: Accounts
prompt: X Ltd agreed to acquire Y Ltd. X Ltd agreed to issue 3 equity shares of ₹10 each (market price ₹15) for every 5 equity shares in Y Ltd. Y Ltd has 1,00,000 equity shares of ₹10 each. Calculate the total Purchase Consideration under AS 14 using the Net Payment Method.
explanation: Number of shares to be issued = (1,00,000 / 5) * 3 = 60,000 equity shares. Value of shares issued for consideration = 60,000 shares * ₹15 (issue price/agreed value) = ₹9,00,000. Purchase consideration is evaluated based on agreed issue price/value of securities offered.
conceptTags: Purchase Consideration | Net Payment Method | Valuation

subject: Accounts
prompt: P Ltd takes over Q Ltd. P Ltd agrees to issue 2 equity shares of ₹10 each at a premium of ₹5 per share for every 4 equity shares in Q Ltd, and pay ₹2 cash per equity share held in Q Ltd. Q Ltd has 50,000 equity shares of ₹10 each fully paid. Compute the Purchase Consideration.
explanation: Equity shares issued = (50,000 / 4) * 2 = 25,000 shares. Value of shares issued = 25,000 * ₹15 = ₹3,75,000. Cash paid = 50,000 * ₹2 = ₹1,00,000. Total Purchase Consideration = ₹3,75,000 + ₹1,00,000 = ₹4,75,000.
conceptTags: Purchase Consideration | Net Payment Method | Cash and Share Component

subject: Accounts
prompt: In the books of the Transferor Company, where is the carrying value of assets transferred to the transferee company transferred upon liquidation?
optionA: Debit of Transferee Company's Account
optionB: Debit of Realisation Account
optionC: Credit of Realisation Account
optionD: Debit of Equity Shareholders' Account
answerText: Debit of Realisation Account
explanation: When closing the books of the transferor company, all asset accounts taken over (or to be realised) are closed by transferring their book values to the debit side of the Realisation Account.
conceptTags: Transferor Company Books | Realisation Account | Closure of Books

subject: Accounts
prompt: How is preference share capital settled in the books of the Transferor Company if preference shareholders are paid more than their book value?
optionA: The excess amount is debited to General Reserve Account.
optionB: The excess amount is debited to Realisation Account.
optionC: The excess amount is credited to Profit and Loss Account.
optionD: The excess amount is debited to Goodwill Account.
answerText: The excess amount is debited to Realisation Account.
explanation: Any excess paid to preference shareholders over their carrying value represents a loss on settlement, which is debited to Realisation Account in the books of the transferor company.
conceptTags: Transferor Company Books | Realisation Account | Preference Shareholders

subject: Accounts
prompt: Sun Ltd acquires Moon Ltd under the purchase method. Net Agreed Assets taken over are ₹12,00,000 and total liabilities assumed are ₹3,00,000. Purchase consideration payable is ₹10,00,000. What is the amount of Goodwill or Capital Reserve resulting from this transaction?
optionA: Goodwill of ₹1,00,000
optionB: Capital Reserve of ₹1,00,000
optionC: Goodwill of ₹2,00,000
optionD: Capital Reserve of ₹2,00,000
answerText: Goodwill of ₹1,00,000
explanation: Net Assets taken over = Agreed Assets (₹12,00,000) - Liabilities assumed (₹3,00,000) = ₹9,00,000. Purchase Consideration = ₹10,00,000. Since PC (₹10,00,000) > Net Assets (₹9,00,000), Goodwill = ₹10,00,000 - ₹9,00,000 = ₹1,00,000.
conceptTags: Purchase Method | Goodwill Calculation | Net Agreed Assets

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under the Pooling of Interests Method, if the Purchase Consideration paid exceeds the paid-up share capital of the Transferor Company, how is the difference adjusted in the transferee company's books?
optionA: Debited to Goodwill Account
optionB: Debited to Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve Account
optionC: Deducted from Reserves (General Reserve/Capital Reserve/P&L) of the Transferee Company
optionD: Credited to Capital Reserve Account
answerText: Deducted from Reserves (General Reserve/Capital Reserve/P&L) of the Transferee Company
explanation: Under the Pooling of Interests Method, any difference between the amount recorded as share capital issued plus any additional consideration in other forms and the amount of share capital of the transferor company should be adjusted in Reserves (General Reserve or other revenue/capital reserves).
conceptTags: Pooling of Interests Method | Reserve Adjustment | AS 14

subject: Accounts
prompt: Prior to amalgamation, Transferee Ltd sold goods costing ₹80,000 to Transferor Ltd for ₹1,00,000. Half of these goods remain unsold in the inventory of Transferor Ltd on the date of amalgamation. If amalgamation is under the purchase method, what adjustment entry is made in Transferee Ltd's books post-amalgamation for unrealized profit?
optionA: Goodwill / Capital Reserve A/c Dr. ₹10,000 To Inventory A/c ₹10,000
optionB: Profit and Loss A/c Dr. ₹20,000 To Inventory A/c ₹20,000
optionC: Inventory A/c Dr. ₹10,000 To Goodwill A/c ₹10,000
optionD: Realisation A/c Dr. ₹10,000 To Profit and Loss A/c ₹10,000
answerText: Goodwill / Capital Reserve A/c Dr. ₹10,000 To Inventory A/c ₹10,000
explanation: Unrealized profit in stock = (₹1,00,000 - ₹80,000) * 50% = ₹10,000. Under the purchase method, post-amalgamation adjustment for unrealized profit on stock included in transferee's inventory is debited to Goodwill / Capital Reserve (or Profit & Loss/General Reserve) and credited to Inventory.
conceptTags: Unrealized Profit | Inter-company Inventory | Purchase Method

subject: Accounts
prompt: Company A absorbs Company B. Company A holds 20% equity shares of Company B prior to amalgamation. How is this existing holding treated when calculating Purchase Consideration under Net Payment Method?
optionA: Consideration is calculated for 100% shares and 20% is paid to Company A itself.
optionB: Consideration is calculated only for the 80% shares held by outside shareholders.
optionC: Consideration is calculated for 100% shares and then 20% is credited to Realisation Account.
optionD: Consideration is ignored and Net Asset method must be mandatorily applied.
answerText: Consideration is calculated only for the 80% shares held by outside shareholders.
explanation: When the transferee company already holds shares in the transferor company, no payment (shares/cash) is made to itself. Thus, purchase consideration under Net Payment method is computed only for the shares held by outside shareholders (80%).
conceptTags: Inter-company Holding | Purchase Consideration | Net Payment Method

subject: Accounts
prompt: In an amalgamation in the nature of merger, Transferor Ltd has General Reserve of ₹2,00,000, Profit & Loss A/c (Cr.) of ₹1,00,000, and Statutory Reserve of ₹50,000. Which of these reserves are incorporated in the transferee company's books?
optionA: Only Statutory Reserve of ₹50,000
optionB: Only General Reserve and Profit & Loss A/c totaling ₹3,00,000
optionC: All reserves (General Reserve, Profit & Loss A/c, and Statutory Reserve) amounting to ₹3,50,000
optionD: None of the reserves are incorporated; all are credited to Capital Reserve.
answerText: All reserves (General Reserve, Profit & Loss A/c, and Statutory Reserve) amounting to ₹3,50,000
explanation: Under the Pooling of Interests method (merger), all reserves (whether capital reserves, revenue reserves, or statutory reserves) of the transferor company are preserved and recorded in the books of the transferee company at their book values.
conceptTags: Pooling of Interests Method | Preservation of Reserves | Merger

subject: Accounts
prompt: When debentures of the transferor company are taken over and settled by the transferee company by issuing its own 12% Debentures at a 10% premium, how is this handled in computing Purchase Consideration under AS 14?
optionA: The value of debentures issued is added to Purchase Consideration.
optionB: The premium on debentures is added to Purchase Consideration.
optionC: Debentures issued are ignored in Purchase Consideration as it is a settlement of liability.
optionD: Only the nominal value of debentures is included in Purchase Consideration.
answerText: Debentures issued are ignored in Purchase Consideration as it is a settlement of liability.
explanation: Under AS 14, consideration is payment made to SHAREHOLDERS only. Discharge of debenture holders is a settlement of a liability assumed, not part of purchase consideration.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What happens to 'Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve' when the statutory requirement to maintain the statutory reserve of the transferor company expires?
optionA: It is transferred to General Reserve.
optionB: It is transferred to Capital Reserve.
optionC: It is reversed by crediting Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve and debiting Statutory Reserve.
optionD: It is written off to Profit and Loss Account as an exceptional item.
answerText: It is reversed by crediting Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve and debiting Statutory Reserve.
explanation: When the statutory reserve is no longer required to be maintained by law, both the Statutory Reserve Account and the Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve Account are closed by passing a reversal entry: Statutory Reserve A/c Dr. To Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve A/c.
conceptTags: Statutory Reserve | Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve | Reversal Entry

subject: Accounts
prompt: Star Ltd acquired Moon Ltd. Equity share capital of Moon Ltd consists of 1,00,000 shares of ₹10 each. Star Ltd issues 1 share of ₹10 (market value ₹20) for every 2 shares of Moon Ltd. Equity shareholders of Moon Ltd also receive cash of ₹3 per share. Preference shareholders (10,00,000 10% Preference shares of ₹10 each) receive 11% Preference shares of Star Ltd of equal value. What is the total Purchase Consideration?
explanation: Equity Shareholders receive: Shares = (1,00,000 / 2) * 1 = 50,000 shares * ₹20 = ₹10,00,000. Cash = 1,00,000 * ₹3 = ₹3,00,000. Preference Shareholders receive: Preference shares = ₹10,00,000. Total PC = ₹10,00,000 + ₹3,00,000 + ₹10,00,000 = ₹23,00,000.
conceptTags: Purchase Consideration | Net Payment Method | Equity and Preference

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under the Net Asset Method of computing purchase consideration, which of the following assets of the transferor company should NOT be included in total agreed assets taken over?
optionA: Unrecorded Patent Rights having commercial value
optionB: Prepaid Expenses
optionC: Fictitious Assets like preliminary expenses and debit balance of P&L account
optionD: Trade Receivables at net realisable value
answerText: Fictitious Assets like preliminary expenses and debit balance of P&L account
explanation: Fictitious assets (such as unamortized preliminary expenses, underwriting commission, or debit balance of P&L account) have no realisable value and are not assets taken over by the transferee company. They are transferred to Equity Shareholders' Account in transferor's books.
conceptTags: Net Asset Method | Fictitious Assets | Purchase Consideration

subject: Accounts
prompt: In the books of the Transferor Company, if Realisation Account shows a debit balance (loss on realisation), how is this loss closed?
optionA: Credited to Realisation A/c and debited to Equity Shareholders' A/c
optionB: Debited to Realisation A/c and credited to Capital Reserve A/c
optionC: Debited to Transferee Company A/c and credited to Realisation A/c
optionD: Debited to Profit and Loss A/c and credited to Realisation A/c
answerText: Credited to Realisation A/c and debited to Equity Shareholders' A/c
explanation: Any profit or loss on realisation belongs to the ultimate owners, i.e., equity shareholders. A realisation loss (debit balance) is closed by crediting Realisation Account and debiting Equity Shareholders' Account.
conceptTags: Transferor Company Books | Realisation Loss | Equity Shareholders

subject: Accounts
prompt: A Ltd acquired B Ltd. Equity intrinsic value per share of A Ltd is ₹50 and B Ltd is ₹25. B Ltd has 40,000 equity shares. Based on intrinsic values, what is the exchange ratio and total number of A Ltd shares to be issued to B Ltd shareholders?
optionA: Ratio 2:1; 80,000 shares issued
optionB: Ratio 1:2; 20,000 shares issued
optionC: Ratio 1:1; 40,000 shares issued
optionD: Ratio 1:4; 10,000 shares issued
answerText: Ratio 1:2; 20,000 shares issued
explanation: Exchange ratio = Intrinsic value of B Ltd / Intrinsic value of A Ltd = ₹25 / ₹50 = 0.5 (i.e., 1 share of A Ltd for every 2 shares of B Ltd). Number of shares issued = 40,000 * (1/2) = 20,000 shares of A Ltd.
conceptTags: Intrinsic Value Method | Share Exchange Ratio | Purchase Consideration

subject: Accounts
prompt: If there is a mutual debt (inter-company debtor/creditor balance of ₹50,000) between Transferor Ltd and Transferee Ltd, how is it eliminated in the books of Transferee Ltd after amalgamation?
optionA: Debtors A/c Dr. ₹50,000 To Creditors A/c ₹50,000
optionB: Sundry Creditors A/c Dr. ₹50,000 To Sundry Debtors A/c ₹50,000
optionC: Realisation A/c Dr. ₹50,000 To Sundry Debtors A/c ₹50,000
optionD: General Reserve A/c Dr. ₹50,000 To Sundry Debtors A/c ₹50,000
answerText: Sundry Creditors A/c Dr. ₹50,000 To Sundry Debtors A/c ₹50,000
explanation: Mutual debts are eliminated in the transferee company's books after recording assets and liabilities by debiting Sundry Creditors and crediting Sundry Debtors with the common/mutual amount.

subject: Accounts
prompt: In an amalgamation in the nature of purchase, existing Goodwill standing in the balance sheet of the Transferor Company is ₹1,00,000. It is taken over at agreed value of ₹80,000. How is this ₹80,000 treated while computing Net Assets taken over by the transferee?
optionA: Included as an asset at ₹80,000 in computing Net Agreed Assets
optionB: Ignored completely while calculating Net Agreed Assets
optionC: Deducted from Capital Reserve
optionD: Transferred directly to Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve
answerText: Included as an asset at ₹80,000 in computing Net Agreed Assets
explanation: If existing goodwill is taken over at an agreed valuation (₹80,000), it is treated as an identifiable asset taken over at that agreed value while calculating Net Agreed Assets for goodwill/capital reserve determination.
conceptTags: Net Asset Method | Existing Goodwill | Agreed Value

subject: Accounts
prompt: When fractional shares arise in calculating share entitlement on amalgamation, how are they typically settled by the transferee company?
optionA: By issuing bonus equity shares
optionB: In cash based on the market/agreed value of shares
optionC: By ignoring the fractional entitlement completely
optionD: By issuing preference shares of equal nominal value
answerText: In cash based on the market/agreed value of shares
explanation: As per AS 14, consideration includes cash paid for fractional shares. Fractional entitlements are settled in cash based on the issue/market price of the transferee company's shares.

subject: Accounts
prompt: X Ltd acquires Y Ltd. The trade bills accepted by Y Ltd include ₹30,000 drawn by X Ltd. Prior to amalgamation, X Ltd had discounted ₹10,000 of these bills with its bank. What amount of Bills Payable and Bills Receivable should be cancelled upon amalgamation in X Ltd's books?
optionD: Nil
explanation: Out of ₹30,000 bills, ₹10,000 was discounted with the bank (so X Ltd no longer holds the Bills Receivable for that ₹10,000). The mutual B/R and B/P held internally between X Ltd and Y Ltd is only ₹20,000. Therefore, only ₹20,000 is cancelled.
conceptTags: Mutual Owings | Discounted Bills | Inter-company Cancellation

subject: Accounts
prompt: If the business of the transferor company is NOT intended to be carried on by the transferee company post-amalgamation, the amalgamation MUST be accounted for as:
optionA: Amalgamation in the nature of Merger
optionB: Amalgamation in the nature of Purchase
optionC: Pooling of Interests Method
optionD: Reconstruction in the nature of Merger
answerText: Amalgamation in the nature of Purchase
explanation: One of the 5 essential conditions for an amalgamation in the nature of merger under AS 14 is that the business of the transferor company is intended to be carried on by the transferee company. If this condition is violated, it is classified as an amalgamation in the nature of purchase.
conceptTags: AS 14 | Conditions for Merger | Purchase Method Classification

subject: Accounts
prompt: In the books of the Transferor Company, how are preference shareholders' claims settled when shares of the Transferee Company are received specifically for them as part of Purchase Consideration?
optionA: Debited to Realisation A/c and Credited to Transferee Co. Shares A/c
optionB: Debited to Preference Shareholders A/c and Credited to Shares in Transferee Co. A/c
optionC: Debited to Equity Shareholders A/c and Credited to Preference Shareholders A/c
optionD: Debited to Bank A/c and Credited to Preference Share Capital A/c
answerText: Debited to Preference Shareholders A/c and Credited to Shares in Transferee Co. A/c
explanation: When shares in transferee company received for preference shareholders are distributed to them, the entry in the transferor company's books is: Preference Shareholders A/c Dr. To Shares in Transferee Company A/c.
conceptTags: Transferor Company Books | Settlement of Preference Shareholders | Journal Entries

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which of the following statements is CORRECT regarding the treatment of statutory reserves under AS 14?
optionA: Statutory reserves are preserved only under the Pooling of Interests Method.
optionB: Statutory reserves are preserved under both Merger and Purchase methods, but under the Purchase method, an Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve account is used.
optionC: Statutory reserves are written off to Profit and Loss Account upon amalgamation.
optionD: Statutory reserves under Purchase method are directly credited to Capital Reserve.
answerText: Statutory reserves are preserved under both Merger and Purchase methods, but under the Purchase method, an Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve account is used.
explanation: Statutory reserves must be maintained by the transferee company as required by law. In merger (pooling of interests), all reserves are taken over naturally. In purchase method, statutory reserves are incorporated by debiting 'Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve Account' and crediting the relevant statutory reserve.

subject: Accounts
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Vanguard Ltd acquires the entire business of Zenith Ltd on 1st April 2026. The Balance Sheet of Zenith Ltd as on 31st March 2026 shows: Equity Share Capital (1,00,000 shares of ₹10 each) ₹10,00,000; 12% Preference Share Capital (4,000 shares of ₹100 each) ₹4,00,000; General Reserve ₹3,00,000; Export Profit Reserve (Statutory Reserve) ₹1,00,000; Profit & Loss A/c (Cr.) ₹2,00,000; 10% Debentures ₹5,00,000; Trade Payables ₹2,00,000. Assets consist of: Property, Plant & Equipment ₹18,00,000; Inventory ₹4,00,000; Trade Receivables ₹3,50,000; Cash at Bank ₹1,50,000. Vanguard Ltd agreed to: (1) Issue 3 Equity Shares of ₹10 each (agreed value ₹15 per share) for every 2 Equity Shares in Zenith Ltd. (2) Issue 11% Preference Shares of ₹100 each at par to redeem the 12% Preference Shareholders of Zenith Ltd at a premium of 10%. (3) Discharge 10% Debentures of Zenith Ltd at a 5% premium by issuing 12% Debentures of Vanguard Ltd at par. (4) Expenses of liquidation of ₹30,000 were paid by Vanguard Ltd. The amalgamation is in the nature of purchase. Export Profit Reserve is to be maintained for 2 more years.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Calculate the total Purchase Consideration for Zenith Ltd as per AS 14.
explanation: Purchase consideration is aggregate payment to shareholders. (1) Equity Shareholders: (1,00,000 / 2) * 3 = 1,50,000 shares * ₹15 = ₹22,50,000. (2) Preference Shareholders: ₹4,00,000 + 10% premium = ₹4,40,000. Total PC = ₹22,50,000 + ₹4,40,000 = ₹26,40,000. (Debenture discharge is not part of PC).
conceptTags: Purchase Consideration | Net Payment Method | AS 14

subject: Accounts
prompt: Compute the Net Agreed Assets taken over by Vanguard Ltd (excluding goodwill/capital reserve calculation).
explanation: Total Assets taken over = PPE (₹18,00,000) + Inventory (₹4,00,000) + Debtors (₹3,50,000) + Bank (₹1,50,000) = ₹27,00,000. Liabilities assumed = Trade Payables (₹2,00,000) + 10% Debentures discharge value (₹5,00,000 * 1.05 = ₹5,25,000) = ₹7,25,000. Net Assets taken over = ₹27,00,000 - ₹7,25,000 = ₹19,75,000.
conceptTags: Net Assets Taken Over | Liabilities Assumed | Debenture Settlement

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the amount of Goodwill / Capital Reserve arising on acquisition (after considering liquidation expenses paid by Vanguard Ltd)?
optionA: Goodwill of ₹6,95,000
optionB: Capital Reserve of ₹6,65,000
optionC: Goodwill of ₹6,65,000
optionD: Goodwill of ₹6,35,000
answerText: Goodwill of ₹6,95,000
explanation: Excess of PC over Net Assets = ₹26,40,000 - ₹19,75,000 = ₹6,65,000 (Goodwill). Liquidation expenses of ₹30,000 paid by transferee under purchase method are debited to Goodwill Account. Total Goodwill = ₹6,65,000 + ₹30,000 = ₹6,95,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt: How is Export Profit Reserve recorded in Vanguard Ltd's books?
optionA: Debited to General Reserve A/c ₹1,00,000 and Credited to Export Profit Reserve A/c ₹1,00,000
optionB: Debited to Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve A/c ₹1,00,000 and Credited to Export Profit Reserve A/c ₹1,00,000
optionC: Debited to Goodwill A/c ₹1,00,000 and Credited to Export Profit Reserve A/c ₹1,00,000
optionD: No entry is made because it is a statutory reserve under purchase method.
answerText: Debited to Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve A/c ₹1,00,000 and Credited to Export Profit Reserve A/c ₹1,00,000
explanation: Under the purchase method, to maintain statutory reserve, Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve Account is debited and Export Profit Reserve Account is credited with ₹1,00,000.
conceptTags: Statutory Reserve | Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve | Purchase Method

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Titan Ltd and Orion Ltd decide to amalgamate to form a new company, Nova Ltd, on 1st April 2026. The amalgamation satisfies all 5 conditions of an 'amalgamation in the nature of merger' under AS 14. 

Balance Sheet summaries as on 31st March 2026:
- Titan Ltd: Equity Share Capital (₹10 each) ₹20,00,000; General Reserve ₹5,00,000; Profit & Loss A/c ₹3,00,000; Liabilities ₹4,00,000. Total Assets ₹32,00,000.
- Orion Ltd: Equity Share Capital (₹10 each) ₹10,00,000; General Reserve ₹2,00,000; Investment Allowance Reserve (Statutory) ₹1,00,000; Profit & Loss A/c ₹1,00,000; Liabilities ₹2,00,000. Total Assets ₹16,00,000.

Nova Ltd issues equity shares of ₹10 each fully paid to the equity shareholders of both companies to satisfy the purchase consideration. Total PC paid: To Titan Ltd = ₹22,00,000 in shares; To Orion Ltd = ₹11,00,000 in shares.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under the Pooling of Interests Method, what is the balance of General Reserve of Nova Ltd immediately after amalgamation (before any other adjustments)?
optionD: Nil
explanation: Combined General Reserves of transferors = ₹5,00,000 + ₹2,00,000 = ₹7,00,000. Adjustment for excess PC over face value of share capital: Titan Ltd PC excess = ₹22,00,000 - ₹20,00,000 = ₹2,00,000. Orion Ltd PC excess = ₹11,00,000 - ₹10,00,000 = ₹1,00,000. Total excess PC = ₹3,00,000. Net General Reserve = ₹7,00,000 - ₹3,00,000 = ₹4,00,000.
conceptTags: Pooling of Interests Method | General Reserve Adjustment | Merger

subject: Accounts
prompt: How is the Investment Allowance Reserve of Orion Ltd incorporated in Nova Ltd's books?
optionA: Debited to Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve A/c and credited to Investment Allowance Reserve A/c
optionB: Incorporated directly as Investment Allowance Reserve A/c ₹1,00,000 without using Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve
optionC: Transferred to Capital Reserve A/c
optionD: Ignored since it belongs to the transferor company
answerText: Incorporated directly as Investment Allowance Reserve A/c ₹1,00,000 without using Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve
explanation: Under the Pooling of Interests Method (merger), all reserves (including statutory reserves) are taken over directly at book values into the respective reserve accounts. Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve account is NOT used in merger accounting.
conceptTags: Pooling of Interests Method | Statutory Reserves | Direct Incorporation

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the total Profit & Loss Account balance appearing in the balance sheet of Nova Ltd post-amalgamation?
optionD: Nil
explanation: Under the pooling of interests method, the profit and loss account balances of transferor companies are preserved and combined: ₹3,00,000 (Titan) + ₹1,00,000 (Orion) = ₹4,00,000.
conceptTags: Pooling of Interests Method | Profit and Loss Preservation | Merger

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the total Paid-up Equity Share Capital of Nova Ltd after issuing shares for amalgamation?
explanation: Nova Ltd issued shares of face value ₹10 each for total purchase consideration: ₹22,00,000 (for Titan Ltd) + ₹11,00,000 (for Orion Ltd) = ₹33,00,000.
conceptTags: Share Capital Issued | Purchase Consideration | Nova Ltd

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Kavya Ltd and Navya Ltd operate in the same industry. Kavya Ltd agrees to absorb Navya Ltd on 31st March 2026. The intrinsic value per share of Kavya Ltd is ₹40 (face value ₹10) and Navya Ltd is ₹20 (face value ₹10).

Navya Ltd's Share Capital consists of 80,000 equity shares of ₹10 each fully paid.
Additional Facts:
1. Consideration is to be discharged on the basis of Intrinsic Value ratio by issuing fully paid Equity Shares of Kavya Ltd.
2. Cash is to be paid for any fractional share entitlements.
3. Navya Ltd has 1,00,000 trade payables, including ₹20,00,000 due to Kavya Ltd.
4. Unsold inventory of Kavya Ltd includes goods purchased from Navya Ltd for ₹6,00,000 on which Navya Ltd made a profit of 20% on cost.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Calculate the share exchange ratio and total number of full equity shares to be issued by Kavya Ltd to Navya Ltd shareholders.
optionA: 1 share of Kavya for every 2 shares of Navya; 40,000 shares
optionB: 2 shares of Kavya for every 1 share of Navya; 1,60,000 shares
optionC: 1 share of Kavya for every 4 shares of Navya; 20,000 shares
optionD: 3 shares of Kavya for every 4 shares of Navya; 60,000 shares
answerText: 1 share of Kavya for every 2 shares of Navya; 40,000 shares
explanation: Exchange ratio = Intrinsic Value of Navya / Intrinsic Value of Kavya = ₹20 / ₹40 = 0.5 (1 share of Kavya for every 2 shares of Navya). Total shares to be issued = 80,000 * 0.5 = 40,000 equity shares.
conceptTags: Intrinsic Value Method | Exchange Ratio | Share Computation

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the total Purchase Consideration under AS 14 (assuming no fractional shares)?
explanation: Total PC = Number of shares issued (40,000) * Agreed Intrinsic Value / Issue Price per share of Kavya Ltd (₹40) = 40,000 * ₹40 = ₹16,00,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the amount of unrealized profit included in inventory to be adjusted post-absorption?
explanation: Profit element on cost = 20%. Selling price = Cost + 20% = 120%. Profit included in invoice value of ₹6,00,000 = ₹6,00,000 * (20 / 120) = ₹1,00,000.
conceptTags: Unrealized Profit | Inter-company Stock | Inventory Adjustment

subject: Accounts
prompt: What entry is passed in Kavya Ltd's books to eliminate mutual owing/trade payables post-amalgamation?
optionA: Trade Payables A/c Dr. ₹20,00,000 To Trade Receivables A/c ₹20,00,000
optionB: Trade Receivables A/c Dr. ₹20,00,000 To Trade Payables A/c ₹20,00,000
optionC: Trade Payables A/c Dr. ₹1,00,000 To Trade Receivables A/c ₹1,00,000
optionD: Goodwill A/c Dr. ₹20,00,000 To Trade Receivables A/c ₹20,00,000
answerText: Trade Payables A/c Dr. ₹20,00,000 To Trade Receivables A/c ₹20,00,000
explanation: To eliminate the mutual balance between Kavya Ltd and Navya Ltd of ₹20,00,000, Trade Payables Account is debited and Trade Receivables Account is credited with ₹20,00,000.

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Apex Ltd absorbs Zenith Ltd on 1st April 2026 under the purchase method. 

Balance Sheet details of Zenith Ltd on 31st March 2026:
- Equity Share Capital (50,00,000 shares of ₹10 each) = ₹500 lakhs
- 10% Preference Share Capital = ₹100 lakhs
- General Reserve = ₹200 lakhs
- Statutory Reserve = ₹50 lakhs
- Profit & Loss A/c (Dr. balance) = ₹(40) lakhs
- Non-Current Liabilities = ₹300 lakhs
- Current Liabilities = ₹140 lakhs
- Total Assets (Book Value) = ₹1,210 lakhs

Agreed Valuation Terms:
1. Non-Current Assets (book value ₹800 lakhs) valued at ₹900 lakhs.
2. Current Assets (book value ₹410 lakhs) valued at ₹380 lakhs.
3. Apex Ltd issues 4 equity shares of ₹10 each (market price ₹25) for every 5 equity shares of Zenith Ltd.
4. Preference shareholders are paid at 10% premium in cash.
5. Non-current liabilities are taken over at book value.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the Purchase Consideration payable by Apex Ltd under AS 14?
optionA: ₹1,000 lakhs
optionB: ₹1,110 lakhs
optionC: ₹1,010 lakhs
optionD: ₹1,210 lakhs
answerText: ₹1,110 lakhs
explanation: To Equity Shareholders: Shares issued = (50 lakhs / 5) * 4 = 40 lakh shares * ₹25 = ₹1,000 lakhs. To Preference Shareholders: Cash = ₹100 lakhs + 10% premium = ₹110 lakhs. Total PC = ₹1,000 lakhs + ₹110 lakhs = ₹1,110 lakhs.
conceptTags: Purchase Consideration | Net Payment Method | Calculation

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the value of Net Agreed Assets taken over by Apex Ltd?
optionA: ₹840 lakhs
optionB: ₹800 lakhs
optionC: ₹1,280 lakhs
optionD: ₹760 lakhs
answerText: ₹840 lakhs
explanation: Total Agreed Assets = Non-Current Assets (₹900 lakhs) + Current Assets (₹380 lakhs) = ₹1,280 lakhs. Total Liabilities assumed = Non-Current Liabilities (₹300 lakhs) + Current Liabilities (₹140 lakhs) = ₹440 lakhs. Net Agreed Assets = ₹1,280 lakhs - ₹440 lakhs = ₹840 lakhs. (P&L debit balance is fictitious asset, excluded).
conceptTags: Net Agreed Assets | Purchase Method | Valuation

subject: Accounts
prompt: Calculate Goodwill or Capital Reserve resulting from the transaction.
optionA: Capital Reserve of ₹270 lakhs
optionB: Goodwill of ₹270 lakhs
optionC: Goodwill of ₹170 lakhs
optionD: Capital Reserve of ₹170 lakhs
answerText: Goodwill of ₹270 lakhs
explanation: Purchase Consideration = ₹1,110 lakhs. Net Agreed Assets = ₹840 lakhs. Goodwill = PC - Net Agreed Assets = ₹1,110 lakhs - ₹840 lakhs = ₹270 lakhs.

subject: Accounts
prompt: How should the debit balance of Profit & Loss Account of ₹40 lakhs in Zenith Ltd be dealt with in Zenith Ltd's books upon liquidation?
optionA: Transferred to Realisation Account Debit
optionB: Transferred to Equity Shareholders' Account Debit
optionC: Transferred to Goodwill Account Debit
optionD: Taken over by Apex Ltd under Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve
answerText: Transferred to Equity Shareholders' Account Debit
explanation: Fictitious assets and accumulated losses like debit balance of Profit & Loss Account are not taken over by transferee company and are transferred directly to the debit of Equity Shareholders' Account in transferor's books.
conceptTags: Transferor Company Books | Accumulated Losses | Equity Shareholders

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Target Ltd goes into voluntary liquidation to amalgamate with Acquirer Ltd on 31st March 2026. 
Target Ltd's balance sheet summarized:
- Equity Share Capital (1,00,000 shares of ₹10 each) = ₹10,00,000
- Reserves & Surplus = ₹4,00,000
- 10% Debentures = ₹3,00,000
- Creditors = ₹2,00,000
- PPE (Net) = ₹12,00,000
- Current Assets = ₹7,00,000

Terms of Amalgamation:
1. Acquirer Ltd takes over all assets and liabilities.
2. Acquirer Ltd pays Purchase Consideration of ₹15,00,000 by issuing 1,00,000 equity shares of ₹10 each at a premium of ₹5 per share.
3. Realisation expenses incurred by Target Ltd amounted to ₹20,000 which were paid by Target Ltd itself prior to completion of transfer.
4. Realisation of assets and discharge of liabilities was executed via Realisation Account in Target Ltd's books.

subject: Accounts
prompt: In the books of Target Ltd, what is the profit or loss on Realisation Account?
optionA: Profit of ₹80,000
optionB: Profit of ₹1,00,000
optionC: Loss of ₹20,000
optionD: Profit of ₹78,000
answerText: Profit of ₹80,000
explanation: Debit side of Realisation A/c: PPE (₹12,00,000) + Current Assets (₹7,00,000) + Realisation Exp (₹20,00) = ₹19,20,000. Credit side of Realisation A/c: 10% Debentures (₹3,00,000) + Creditors (₹2,00,000) + PC (₹15,00,000) = ₹20,00,000. Realisation Profit = Credit (₹20,00,000) - Debit (₹19,20,000) = ₹80,000.
conceptTags: Realisation Profit | Transferor Company Books | Accounting Ledger

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the final amount payable/distributable to Equity Shareholders of Target Ltd upon closing their account?
explanation: Equity Shareholders' A/c credit side: Equity Share Capital (₹10,00,000) + Reserves & Surplus (₹4,00,000) + Profit on Realisation (₹80,000) = ₹14,80,000. Wait! Cash in bank was part of Current Assets (₹7,00,000) transferred to transferee, but Target Ltd paid ₹20,000 expenses out of its bank/cash before transfer, or from PC cash. Since PC was paid fully in shares worth ₹15,00,000, those shares worth ₹15,00,000 are distributed to Equity Shareholders to close Equity Shareholders' A/c at ₹14,80,000 + adjustment. Specifically, net equity entitlement equals PC of ₹15,00,000 (which matches total assets realized less liabilities discharged).
conceptTags: Equity Shareholders Account | Transferor Company | Final Distribution

subject: Accounts
prompt: How are realization expenses of ₹20,000 paid by Target Ltd recorded in Target Ltd's books?
optionA: Debited to Profit and Loss Account and Credited to Bank
optionB: Debited to Realisation Account and Credited to Bank Account
optionC: Debited to Acquirer Ltd Account and Credited to Bank Account
optionD: Debited to Equity Shareholders Account and Credited to Bank
answerText: Debited to Realisation Account and Credited to Bank Account
explanation: When liquidation/realisation expenses are paid and borne by the transferor company itself, the journal entry in the transferor company's books is: Realisation Account Dr. ₹20,000 To Bank Account ₹20,000.
conceptTags: Liquidation Expenses | Transferor Company Books | Realisation Entry

subject: Accounts
prompt: What entry is passed in Target Ltd's books to record the Purchase Consideration due from Acquirer Ltd?
optionA: Acquirer Ltd A/c Dr. ₹15,00,000 To Realisation A/c ₹15,00,000
optionB: Realisation A/c Dr. ₹15,00,000 To Acquirer Ltd A/c ₹15,00,000
optionC: Bank A/c Dr. ₹15,00,000 To Purchase Consideration A/c ₹15,00,000
optionD: Equity Shareholders A/c Dr. ₹15,00,000 To Acquirer Ltd A/c ₹15,00,000
answerText: Acquirer Ltd A/c Dr. ₹15,00,000 To Realisation A/c ₹15,00,000
explanation: To record PC due from transferee company in the transferor company's books, the journal entry is: Transferee Company A/c (Acquirer Ltd) Dr. To Realisation Account.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which of the following internal reconstruction schemes under the Companies Act, 2013 does NOT require confirmation or sanction from the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)?
optionA: Reduction of paid-up share capital under Section 66
optionB: Sub-division of fully paid equity shares into shares of smaller face value under Section 61
optionC: Extinguishing the liability on unpaid share capital under Section 66
optionD: Paying off any paid-up share capital which is in excess of the wants of the company under Section 66
answerText: Sub-division of fully paid equity shares into shares of smaller face value under Section 61
explanation: Under Section 61 of the Companies Act, 2013, alteration of share capital such as sub-division or consolidation of shares requires only an ordinary resolution in the general meeting if authorized by articles. Confirmation from the NCLT is compulsory for reduction of share capital governed under Section 66. Hence, sub-division does not require NCLT sanction.
conceptTags: Section 61 | Section 66 | NCLT Approval | Alteration of Capital

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under Section 66 of the Companies Act, 2013, a company can reduce its share capital only after obtaining approval from which authority?
optionA: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
optionB: Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA)
optionC: National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
optionD: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
answerText: National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
explanation: Section 66 of the Companies Act, 2013 mandates that a company may reduce its share capital by passing a special resolution subject to confirmation by the NCLT. The NCLT satisfies itself that interests of creditors and stakeholders are protected before issuing an order confirming the reduction. Other regulatory bodies do not issue the formal confirmation order under Section 66.
conceptTags: Section 66 | NCLT | Capital Reduction | Legal Framework

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the underlying financial nature of the Reconstruction Account or Capital Reduction Account prepared during an internal reconstruction scheme?
optionA: Real Account
optionB: Personal Account
optionC: Nominal Account
optionD: Representative Personal Account
answerText: Nominal Account
explanation: The Capital Reduction Account or Reconstruction Account is a temporary Nominal Account created to accumulate sacrifices made by shareholders, creditors, and debenture holders. All gains and sacrifices are credited to this account, while losses written off and asset reductions are debited to it. Once the reconstruction scheme is fully executed, the balance in this account is closed by transferring it to Capital Reserve.
conceptTags: Capital Reduction Account | Account Nature | Accounting Entries

subject: Accounts
prompt: When a company sub-divides its 10,000 equity shares of Rs. 100 each into 1,00,000 equity shares of Rs. 10 each, what is the net accounting entry required in the main ledger?
optionA: Debit Equity Share Capital A/c (Rs. 100) and Credit Equity Share Capital A/c (Rs. 10) for Rs. 10,00,000
optionB: Debit Capital Reduction A/c and Credit Equity Share Capital A/c for Rs. 10,00,000
optionC: Debit Equity Share Capital A/c and Credit Capital Reduction A/c for Rs. 9,00,000
optionD: No entry is required in the general ledger as total capital remains unchanged
answerText: Debit Equity Share Capital A/c (Rs. 100) and Credit Equity Share Capital A/c (Rs. 10) for Rs. 10,00,000
explanation: Sub-division of shares under Section 61 changes the denomination and total number of shares, but total paid-up share capital remains unchanged at Rs. 10,00,000. An entry is passed debiting the old Equity Share Capital Account (Rs. 100 face value) and crediting the new Equity Share Capital Account (Rs. 10 face value) for Rs. 10,00,000. This maintains correct capital representation in the ledger.

subject: Accounts
prompt: After meeting all specified write-offs of accumulated losses and asset overvaluations, any surplus remaining in the Capital Reduction Account is transferred to which head?
optionA: General Reserve Account
optionB: Capital Reserve Account
optionC: Securities Premium Account
optionD: Profit & Loss Account
answerText: Capital Reserve Account
explanation: Any credit balance remaining in the Capital Reduction Account after absorbing all accumulated P&L losses, fictitious assets, and overvalued fixed assets represents a capital profit. In accordance with standard accounting procedures for internal reconstruction, this credit balance is transferred to the Capital Reserve Account. It cannot be distributed as dividend or credited to General Reserve.
conceptTags: Capital Reserve | Capital Reduction Account | Final Transfer

subject: Accounts
prompt: As per Schedule III to the Companies Act, 2013, under which head should the Capital Reserve created through internal reconstruction be presented in the Balance Sheet?
optionA: Share Capital
optionB: Reserves and Surplus under Other Equity
optionC: Long-term Provisions
optionD: Other Current Liabilities
answerText: Reserves and Surplus under Other Equity
explanation: Under Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013, Capital Reserve is categorized under 'Reserves and Surplus', which forms part of 'Other Equity' in the Statement of Assets and Liabilities. It represents non-distributable capital profits generated through internal financial reorganisation. Thus, it is presented under Other Equity.
conceptTags: Schedule III | Capital Reserve | Financial Statements

subject: Accounts
prompt: What journal entry is passed in the financial books of account when a company cancels its unissued share capital under Section 61 of the Companies Act, 2013?
optionA: Debit Unissued Share Capital A/c and Credit Capital Reduction A/c
optionB: Debit Share Capital A/c and Credit Capital Reduction A/c
optionC: Debit Capital Reduction A/c and Credit Unissued Share Capital A/c
optionD: No journal entry is required in the financial books
answerText: No journal entry is required in the financial books
explanation: Unissued share capital is not part of the paid-up or issued share capital brought into financial books of account. Section 61(1)(e) permits cancellation of unissued capital, which merely reduces authorized capital. Since authorized capital is shown by way of a note and not as a ledger balance, no formal financial journal entry is recorded.

subject: Accounts
prompt: How should the payment of professional expenses directly incurred for executing an internal reconstruction scheme be treated in the books?
optionA: Debited to Profit & Loss Account
optionB: Debited to Capital Reduction Account
optionC: Debited to Miscellaneous Expenditure Account
optionD: Debited to General Reserve Account
answerText: Debited to Capital Reduction Account
explanation: Expenses incurred in carrying out an internal reconstruction scheme (such as court fees, legal charges, and professional fees) are part of the reconstruction process itself. They are debited directly to the Capital Reduction / Reconstruction Account and credited to Bank Account. This ensures all costs associated with capital reduction are absorbed by the capital reduction scheme balance.
conceptTags: Reconstruction Expenses | Capital Reduction Account | Journal Entry

subject: Accounts
prompt: What resolution is required to be passed by a company in its General Meeting to convert fully paid equity shares into stock under Section 61?
optionA: Special Resolution
optionB: Ordinary Resolution
optionC: Board Resolution only
optionD: Unanimous Consent of Creditors
answerText: Ordinary Resolution
explanation: Under Section 61(1)(c) of the Companies Act, 2013, conversion of all or any fully paid-up shares into stock (and reconversion of stock into fully paid-up shares) requires an Ordinary Resolution passed in a general meeting, provided such alteration is authorized by the Articles of Association. A Special Resolution is required for capital reduction under Section 66, not Section 61.
conceptTags: Conversion into Stock | Section 61 | Company Law

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under which financial accounting standard framework is the internal reconstruction balance sheet prepared after capital reduction?
optionA: AS 14 / Ind AS 103 on Business Combinations
optionB: Schedule III to the Companies Act, 2013 along with applicable Accounting Standards
optionC: AS 24 on Discontinuing Operations
optionD: AS 13 on Accounting for Investments
answerText: Schedule III to the Companies Act, 2013 along with applicable Accounting Standards
explanation: Internal reconstruction does not involve an acquisition or amalgamation of legal entities, so AS 14 / Ind AS 103 does not govern its financial statement presentation. The balance sheet post-reconstruction is prepared in accordance with Schedule III to the Companies Act, 2013 and applicable Accounting Standards. If instructed by the NCLT order, the words 'And Reduced' are appended to the company name for a specified period.
conceptTags: Balance Sheet Presentation | Schedule III | Accounting Framework

subject: Accounts
prompt: If preference shareholders agree to waive Rs. 1,20,000 of preference dividend arrears that were never recognized in the financial statements, what is the journal entry?
optionA: Debit Capital Reduction A/c Rs. 1,20,000 and Credit Cash A/c Rs. 1,20,000
optionB: Debit Preference Dividend Arrears A/c Rs. 1,20,000 and Credit Capital Reduction A/c Rs. 1,20,000
optionC: Debit Capital Reduction A/c Rs. 1,20,000 and Credit Preference Share Capital A/c Rs. 1,20,000
optionD: No journal entry is required in the books of account
answerText: No journal entry is required in the books of account
explanation: Unrecorded arrears of cumulative preference dividend are contingent liabilities not shown as actual liabilities in the balance sheet. When preference shareholders agree to forego/waive such unrecorded arrears, no claim or liability is extinguished from the books. Therefore, no formal journal entry is passed for the waived portion.
conceptTags: Dividend Arrears | Unrecorded Liability | Waiver Entry

subject: Accounts
prompt: A company pays 30% of unrecorded preference dividend arrears of Rs. 2,00,000 in cash as part of an NCLT approved scheme. What is the journal entry impact on Capital Reduction Account?
optionA: Debited by Rs. 60,000
optionB: Credited by Rs. 1,40,000
optionC: Debited by Rs. 2,00,000
optionD: Credited by Rs. 60,000
answerText: Debited by Rs. 60,000
explanation: Since the dividend arrears were unrecorded, any actual cash outlay to settle a portion of these arrears creates a financial obligation not previously debited to accounts. The cash payment of 30% on Rs. 2,00,000 equals Rs. 60,000, which is debited to the Capital Reduction Account and credited to Bank Account. The remaining waived 70% requires no accounting entry.
conceptTags: Dividend Settlement | Capital Reduction Account | Cash Payment

subject: Accounts
prompt: Unsecured creditors of Rs. 8,00,000 agree to accept 75% of their claims in Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each at par and waive the rest. What amount is credited to Capital Reduction Account?
optionD: Nil
explanation: Total unsecured creditors liability eliminated is Rs. 8,00,000. In exchange, equity share capital of Rs. 6,00,000 (75% of Rs. 8,00,000) is issued. The sacrifice made by creditors is 25% of Rs. 8,00,000 = Rs. 2,00,000, which represents a gain to the company and is credited to the Capital Reduction Account.
conceptTags: Creditors Compromise | Capital Reduction Account | Sacrifice Calculation

subject: Accounts
prompt: A company has 20,000 Equity Shares of Rs. 100 each, Rs. 70 paid up. It reduces the paid-up value to Rs. 40 per share fully paid up. What amount is credited to Capital Reduction A/c?
explanation: The existing paid-up capital per share is Rs. 70. The new paid-up capital per share is Rs. 40 fully paid up. The reduction per share is Rs. 70 - Rs. 40 = Rs. 30 per share. Total amount credited to Capital Reduction Account = 20,000 shares × Rs. 30 = Rs. 6,00,000.
conceptTags: Paid-up Reduction | Capital Reduction Account | Share Reduction Entry

subject: Accounts
prompt: An unrecorded contingent liability of Rs. 60,000 crystallizes during reconstruction and is settled at Rs. 45,000 in cash. What is the entry in Capital Reduction Account?
optionA: Debited by Rs. 45,000
optionB: Credited by Rs. 15,00,000
optionC: Debited by Rs. 60,000
optionD: Credited by Rs. 45,000
answerText: Debited by Rs. 45,000
explanation: When an unrecorded contingent liability crystallizes and is paid under a reconstruction scheme, the actual payment made to settle the liability (Rs. 45,000) is a loss/cost to the scheme. Hence, Capital Reduction Account is debited by Rs. 45,000 and Bank Account is credited by Rs. 45,000.
conceptTags: Contingent Liability | Capital Reduction Account | Settlement Entry

subject: Accounts
prompt: 10% Debentures of Rs. 6,00,000 are replaced by 12% Debentures of Rs. 5,00,000 in full and final settlement. What amount is credited to Capital Reduction Account?
optionD: Nil
explanation: Old 10% Debentures Account is debited by Rs. 6,00,000. New 12% Debentures Account is credited by Rs. 5,00,000. The gain arising from debenture holders surrendering Rs. 1,00,000 of principal claim is credited to Capital Reduction Account (Rs. 6,00,000 - Rs. 5,00,000 = Rs. 1,00,000).
conceptTags: Debenture Sacrifice | Capital Reduction Account | Debenture Conversion

subject: Accounts
prompt: When equity shareholders surrender their shares under an internal reconstruction scheme, which account is credited initially?
optionA: Capital Reduction Account
optionB: Share Surrender Account
optionC: Capital Reserve Account
optionD: Profit & Loss Account
answerText: Share Surrender Account
explanation: When shares are surrendered by shareholders, Equity Share Capital Account is debited and 'Share Surrender Account' is credited as a temporary holding account. The surrendered shares are subsequently either re-issued to creditors/debenture holders or cancelled. Upon cancellation, the balance in Share Surrender Account is transferred to Capital Reduction Account.
conceptTags: Share Surrender | Temporary Account | Accounting Procedure

subject: Accounts
prompt: Shares surrendered by equity shareholders are reissued to trade creditors to discharge claims of Rs. 1,50,000. What entry is passed on reissue?
optionA: Debit Trade Creditors A/c Rs. 1,50,000 and Credit Share Surrender A/c Rs. 1,50,000
optionB: Debit Trade Creditors A/c Rs. 1,50,000 and Credit Capital Reduction A/c Rs. 1,50,000
optionC: Debit Share Surrender A/c Rs. 1,50,000 and Credit Capital Reduction A/c Rs. 1,50,000
optionD: Debit Capital Reduction A/c Rs. 1,50,000 and Credit Equity Share Capital A/c Rs. 1,50,000
answerText: Debit Trade Creditors A/c Rs. 1,50,000 and Credit Share Surrender A/c Rs. 1,50,000
explanation: When surrendered shares are reissued to discharge liability of creditors, Trade Creditors Account is debited by Rs. 1,50,000 and Share Surrender Account is credited by Rs. 1,50,000. This cancels out the creditor liability against the surrendered shares held in trust without affecting Capital Reduction Account at this intermediate stage.
conceptTags: Share Surrender Reissue | Creditor Settlement | Journal Entry

subject: Accounts
prompt: Which of the following transactions is classified under Section 61 (Alteration of Share Capital) rather than Section 66 (Reduction of Share Capital)?
optionA: Extinguishing unpaid liability on existing equity shares
optionB: Consolidation of shares of smaller denomination into shares of larger denomination
optionC: Writing off lost paid-up capital not represented by available assets
optionD: Refunding excess paid-up share capital to equity shareholders
answerText: Consolidation of shares of smaller denomination into shares of larger denomination
explanation: Consolidation of shares into larger face value without altering total paid-up capital or voting rights proportion is an alteration of share capital governed by Section 61. In contrast, extinguishing unpaid liability, writing off lost capital, and returning excess capital involve reduction of capital governed by Section 66.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Plant and Machinery with a book value of Rs. 20,00,000 is written down to its recoverable value of Rs. 14,00,000 under a scheme. What amount is debited to Capital Reduction A/c?
explanation: The overvaluation/write-down required for Plant and Machinery is Rs. 20,00,000 - Rs. 14,00,000 = Rs. 6,00,000. Capital Reduction Account is debited by Rs. 6,00,000 and Plant and Machinery Account is credited by Rs. 6,00,000 to bring the asset to its true recoverable value of Rs. 14,00,000.
conceptTags: Asset Revaluation | Write-down | Capital Reduction Account

subject: Accounts
prompt: Creditors amounting to Rs. 4,00,000 agree to a 20% haircut provided the balance is paid immediately in cash. What is the credit to Capital Reduction Account?
optionD: Nil
explanation: A haircut of 20% on Rs. 4,00,000 equals Rs. 80,000 (0.20 × 4,00,000). The creditors surrender Rs. 80,000 of their claims, which is a sacrifice and gain to the company credited to Capital Reduction Account. The balance Rs. 3,20,000 paid in cash reduces Bank Account.
conceptTags: Creditors Haircut | Sacrifice | Capital Reduction Account

subject: Accounts
prompt: While executing an internal reconstruction scheme, which of the following accounts MUST be completely written off first before transferring any surplus to Capital Reserve?
optionA: General Reserve
optionB: Profit & Loss Debit Balance and Fictitious Assets
optionC: Capital Redemption Reserve
optionD: Securities Premium Account
answerText: Profit & Loss Debit Balance and Fictitious Assets
explanation: The primary goal of internal reconstruction is to clean the balance sheet by writing off accumulated losses (Profit & Loss debit balance), intangible assets (Goodwill, Patents), and fictitious assets (preliminary expenses, discount on issue of debentures). Surplus in Capital Reduction Account can only be transferred to Capital Reserve after all losses and fictitious assets are fully eliminated.
conceptTags: Write-off Order | Accumulated Losses | Capital Reduction Rules

subject: Accounts
prompt: A company reduces 40,000 equity shares of Rs. 10 each fully paid to Rs. 2 each fully paid, and then consolidates every 5 reduced shares into 1 new share of Rs. 10 each. What is the final number of equity shares?
optionA: 40,000 shares
optionB: 8,000 shares
optionC: 20,000 shares
optionD: 16,000 shares
answerText: 8,000 shares
explanation: First, 40,000 shares are reduced to face value of Rs. 2 each ( total paid-up capital = Rs. 80,000). Next, 5 shares of Rs. 2 each are consolidated into 1 share of Rs. 10 each. Total number of new shares = 40,000 ÷ 5 = 8,000 shares of Rs. 10 each fully paid ( total capital = 8,000 × 10 = Rs. 80,000).

subject: Accounts
prompt: Capital Reduction Account has a credit balance of Rs. 5,00,000. Accumulated P&L loss is Rs. 3,20,000 and Patents are overstated by Rs. 2,00,000. To what extent can Patents be written down?
explanation: Total credit available in Capital Reduction Account = Rs. 5,00,000. P&L debit balance of Rs. 3,20,000 must be written off completely first. Remaining balance in Capital Reduction Account = Rs. 5,00,000 - Rs. 3,20,000 = Rs. 1,80,000. Therefore, Patents can only be written down to the extent of the available balance, which is Rs. 1,80,000.
conceptTags: Write-off Priority | Partial Write-down | Capital Reduction Account

subject: Accounts
prompt: An unrecorded claim for damages of Rs. 1,00,000 is settled during reconstruction by issuing 6,000 Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each as fully paid. What amount is debited to Capital Reduction Account?
optionD: Nil
explanation: The claim was unrecorded in the financial books. Settling this unrecorded liability by issuing equity shares of face value Rs. 60,000 (6,000 shares × Rs. 10) creates a new equity liability. Capital Reduction Account is debited by the fair value of consideration given (Rs. 60,000) and Equity Share Capital Account is credited by Rs. 60,000. The claim sacrifice of Rs. 40,000 requires no entry as original claim was unrecorded.
conceptTags: Unrecorded Claim Settlement | Capital Reduction Account | Share Issue

subject: Accounts
prompt: Shareholders surrender 30% of 2,00,000 equity shares of Rs. 10 each. Out of these, 40,000 surrendered shares are reissued to debenture holders and remaining are cancelled. What amount is credited to Capital Reduction Account upon cancellation?
explanation: Total shares surrendered = 30% of 2,00,000 = 60,000 shares of Rs. 10 each (total face value Rs. 6,00,000) credited to Share Surrender A/c. Reissued shares = 40,000 shares (face value Rs. 4,00,000). Remaining surrendered shares to be cancelled = 60,000 - 40,000 = 20,000 shares. Value of cancelled shares transferred from Share Surrender A/c to Capital Reduction A/c = 20,000 shares × Rs. 10 = Rs. 2,00,000.
conceptTags: Share Surrender Cancellation | Capital Reduction Account | Surrender Computation

subject: Accounts
prompt: 10% Preference Shares of Rs. 1,00,000 (face value Rs. 100) are converted into 600 12% Preference Shares of Rs. 100 each and 4,000 Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each. What is the credit to Capital Reduction Account?
optionC: Nil
answerText: Nil
explanation: Old 10% Preference Share Capital debited = Rs. 1,00,000. Consideration given: New 12% Preference Share Capital = 600 × Rs. 100 = Rs. 60,000, plus Equity Share Capital = 4,00,000 (4,000 × Rs. 10) = Rs. 40,000. Total value of new securities issued = Rs. 60,000 + Rs. 40,000 = Rs. 1,00,000. Since total value issued equals total face value surrendered, there is no sacrifice or gain, so credit to Capital Reduction Account is Nil.
conceptTags: Preference Capital Conversion | No Sacrifice | Capital Reduction Account

subject: Accounts
prompt: A company has a P&L debit balance of Rs. 10,00,000 and Securities Premium Account balance of Rs. 3,00,000. Under NCLT scheme, Securities Premium is fully utilized. How much reduction from share capital is needed to eliminate the loss?
explanation: Securities Premium can be utilized under Section 52 read with Section 66 for capital reduction schemes approved by court/NCLT. Total accumulated loss to write off = Rs. 10,00,000. Less: Securities Premium utilized = Rs. 3,00,000. Net loss remaining to be absorbed by Capital Reduction Account (via share capital reduction) = Rs. 7,00,000.
conceptTags: Securities Premium Utilization | Section 52 | Net Capital Reduction

subject: Accounts
prompt: Bank Loan of Rs. 3,00,000 is secured against Land of book value Rs. 2,50,000. Bank takes over the Land at Rs. 3,20,000 in full settlement and pays Rs. 20,00,00 cash back to the company. What is the net credit to Capital Reduction Account?
explanation: Land (Book value Rs. 2,50,000) was taken over at agreed value of Rs. 3,20,000. Profit on revaluation/transfer of Land = Rs. 3,20,000 - Rs. 2,50,000 = Rs. 70,00,00 credited to Capital Reduction Account. Bank Loan of Rs. 3,00,000 is settled against Rs. 3,00,000 of asset value, and Bank refunds remaining Rs. 20,000 cash to the company. The net credit to Capital Reduction Account is the profit on asset revaluation, which is Rs. 70,000.
conceptTags: Asset Takeover | Loan Settlement | Capital Reduction Credit

subject: Accounts
prompt: 15,00,000 Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each (Rs. 8 paid up) are reduced to equity shares of Rs. 5 each fully paid up. What is the total reduction in share capital credited to Capital Reduction Account?
explanation: Existing paid-up capital = 15,00,000 shares × Rs. 8 = Rs. 1,20,00,000. New paid-up capital = 15,00,000 shares × Rs. 5 = Rs. 75,00,000. Reduction in paid-up share capital = Rs. 1,20,00,000 - Rs. 75,00,000 = Rs. 45,00,000 (which is 15,00,000 shares × Rs. 3 reduction per share). This amount is credited to Capital Reduction Account.
conceptTags: Partly Paid Shares | Paid-up Reduction | Capital Reduction Calculation

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Delta Ltd. has an existing capital structure of 50,000 Equity Shares of Rs. 100 each, Rs. 70 paid up. The balance sheet shows a Profit & Loss debit balance of Rs. 22,00,000, Plant & Machinery book value of Rs. 18,00,000, and Trade Creditors of Rs. 6,00,000.
An NCLT approved internal reconstruction scheme is implemented as under:
1. A final call of Rs. 30 per share is made and fully collected in cash from shareholders.
2. Paid-up share capital is then reduced from Rs. 100 per share to Rs. 40 per share fully paid up.
3. Trade Creditors agree to forego 25% of their total claim. The balance claim is settled by issuing 9% Debentures for Rs. 3,00,000 and paying the remaining amount in cash.
4. Capital Reduction Account is utilized to completely write off the Profit & Loss debit balance, and the remaining credit balance in Capital Reduction Account is used to write down Plant & Machinery.

subject: Accounts
prompt: Under Delta Ltd.'s scheme, what is the net total credit generated in the Capital Reduction Account from capital reduction and creditors' sacrifice?
explanation: Call money creates paid-up capital of Rs. 100 per share (50,000 × Rs. 100 = Rs. 50,00,000). Reduction to Rs. 40 fully paid generates capital reduction credit = 50,000 × Rs. 60 = Rs. 30,00,000. Creditors' sacrifice = 25% of Rs. 6,00,000 = Rs. 1,50,000. Total credit generated in Capital Reduction Account = Rs. 30,00,000 + Rs. 1,50,000 = Rs. 31,50,000.
conceptTags: Capital Reduction Credit | Creditors Sacrifice | Call Money

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the net cash balance available with Delta Ltd. after receiving call money and paying the cash portion to creditors?
explanation: Cash received from final call = 50,000 × Rs. 30 = Rs. 15,00,000. Creditors remaining after 25% waiver = Rs. 6,00,000 - Rs. 1,50,000 = Rs. 4,50,000. Out of Rs. 4,50,000, Rs. 3,00,000 is settled in debentures and balance Rs. 1,50,000 is paid in cash. Net cash remaining = Rs. 15,00,000 - Rs. 1,50,000 = Rs. 13,50,000.
conceptTags: Cash Balance | Creditors Settlement | Call Proceeds

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the revised book value of Plant & Machinery in Delta Ltd.'s balance sheet after fully utilizing the remaining Capital Reduction Account?
explanation: Total credit in Capital Reduction Account = Rs. 31,50,000. Less P&L debit balance written off = Rs. 22,00,000. Remaining balance available in Capital Reduction Account = Rs. 31,50,000 - Rs. 22,00,000 = Rs. 9,50,000. Plant & Machinery is written down by Rs. 9,50,000. Revised book value = Rs. 18,00,000 - Rs. 9,50,000 = Rs. 8,50,000.
conceptTags: Asset Write-down | Revised Book Value | Capital Reduction Application

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the balance transferred to Capital Reserve Account upon completing Delta Ltd.'s internal reconstruction?
optionC: Nil (Rs. 0)
answerText: Nil (Rs. 0)
explanation: The entire remaining balance of Rs. 9,50,000 in Capital Reduction Account after writing off P&L loss was fully absorbed to reduce Plant & Machinery. Since no credit balance remains in the Capital Reduction Account, the amount transferred to Capital Reserve is Nil (Rs. 0).
conceptTags: Capital Reserve | Zero Balance | Final Transfer

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Ltd. underwent internal reconstruction. Its pre-reconstruction books show:
- 10,000 10% Cumulative Preference Shares of Rs. 100 each fully paid: Rs. 10,00,000
- 50,000 Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each fully paid: Rs. 5,00,000
- 12% Debentures: Rs. 4,00,000
- Arrears of preference dividend for 2 years (unrecorded): Rs. 2,00,000
- Land & Building (Book Value): Rs. 3,00,000

Scheme of Reconstruction:
1. 10% Preference shares are reduced to Rs. 60 per share fully paid up. Preference shareholders waive 50% of dividend arrears. For the remaining 50% arrears, Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each fully paid are issued to them.
2. Equity shares are reduced to Rs. 3 per share fully paid up.
3. 12% Debenture holders accept Land & Building (Book value Rs. 3,00,000) at an agreed valuation of Rs. 3,50,000 in part satisfaction of Rs. 3,50,000 of their claims, and the balance debentures of Rs. 50,00,00 are paid off in cash.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the total amount debited to Capital Reduction Account on account of issuing equity shares for preference dividend arrears settlement in Zenith Ltd.?
optionD: Nil
explanation: Total unrecorded arrears = Rs. 2,00,000. 50% is waived (no entry). 50% (Rs. 1,00,000) is paid by issuing Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each. Since this was an unrecorded obligation, issuing equity shares of Rs. 1,00,000 requires debiting Capital Reduction Account by Rs. 1,00,000 and crediting Equity Share Capital Account by Rs. 1,00,000.
conceptTags: Preference Dividend Arrears | Equity Share Issue | Capital Reduction Debit

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the total credit balance in Capital Reduction Account of Zenith Ltd. before writing off any losses or asset overvaluations?
explanation: Credits generated: Preference capital reduction = 10,000 × Rs. 40 = Rs. 4,00,000. Equity capital reduction = 50,000 × Rs. 7 = Rs. 3,50,000. Profit on transfer of Land & Building = Agreed value Rs. 3,50,000 - Book value Rs. 3,00,000 = Rs. 50,000. Total gross credit generated = Rs. 4,00,000 + Rs. 3,50,000 + Rs. 50,000 = Rs. 8,00,000.
conceptTags: Gross Capital Reduction | Revaluation Gain | Capital Reduction Credit

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the total number of Equity Shares of Zenith Ltd. after executing all steps of the reconstruction scheme?
optionA: 50,000 shares
optionB: 60,000 shares
optionC: 10,000 shares
optionD: 1,00,000 shares
answerText: 60,000 shares
explanation: Existing equity shares reduced in value = 50,00,00 shares (now Rs. 3 each). New equity shares issued to preference shareholders for dividend arrears = Rs. 1,00,000 ÷ Rs. 10 per share = 10,000 shares of Rs. 10 each. Total equity shares post reconstruction = 50,000 + 10,000 = 60,000 shares.
conceptTags: Total Equity Shares | Share Count | Post-reconstruction

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the net financial impact (gain/loss) credited or debited to Zenith Ltd.'s Capital Reduction Account on the takeover of Land & Building by debenture holders?
optionA: Gain of Rs. 50,000 credited
optionB: Loss of Rs. 50,000 debited
optionC: No gain or loss
optionD: Gain of Rs. 3,50,000 credited
answerText: Gain of Rs. 50,000 credited
explanation: Land & Building having a book value of Rs. 3,00,000 was accepted at Rs. 3,50,000 to settle Rs. 3,50,000 of debentures. Transferring an asset at Rs. 50,000 above book value generates a revaluation gain of Rs. 50,000, which is credited to the Capital Reduction Account.
conceptTags: Asset Takeover Gain | Debenture Settlement | Capital Reduction Credit

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Apex Manufacturing Ltd. has an existing capital of 1,00,000 Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each fully paid. The financial statements show a Profit & Loss debit balance of Rs. 4,50,000, Patents of Rs. 1,50,000, and 14% Debentures of Rs. 3,00,000.
Under an approved scheme of internal reconstruction:
1. Shareholders agree to surrender 80% of their equity shares.
2. Out of the surrendered shares, 20,000 shares are reissued to 14% Debenture holders of Rs. 3,00,000 in full and final settlement of their claims.
3. The remaining surrendered shares are cancelled.
4. Capital Reduction Account is utilized to completely write off the Profit & Loss debit balance and Patents, and any surplus is transferred to Capital Reserve.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What amount is initially credited to the Share Surrender Account of Apex Manufacturing Ltd. upon surrender of 80% shares?
explanation: Total equity shares = 1,00,000 of Rs. 10 each = Rs. 10,00,000. 80% surrendered = 80,000 shares of Rs. 10 each = Rs. 8,00,000. The entry is Equity Share Capital A/c Dr. Rs. 8,00,000 to Share Surrender A/c Rs. 8,00,000.
conceptTags: Share Surrender | Surrender Amount | Initial Entry

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the amount transferred from Share Surrender Account to Capital Reduction Account upon cancellation of unutilized surrendered shares in Apex Manufacturing Ltd.?
explanation: Total surrendered shares = 80,000 shares (Rs. 8,00,000). Shares reissued to debenture holders = 20,000 shares (Rs. 2,00,000). Remaining surrendered shares cancelled = 80,000 - 20,000 = 60,000 shares of Rs. 10 each = Rs. 6,00,000. Upon cancellation, Share Surrender Account is debited and Capital Reduction Account is credited by Rs. 6,00,000.
conceptTags: Surrender Cancellation | Capital Reduction Credit | Surrender Account

subject: Accounts
prompt: What amount is credited to Capital Reduction Account directly from the settlement of 14% Debenture holders in Apex Manufacturing Ltd.?
optionD: Nil
explanation: Debenture holders had a claim of Rs. 3,00,000. They accepted 20,000 surrendered shares of face value Rs. 2,00,000 in full settlement. The entry is 14% Debentures A/c Dr. Rs. 3,00,000 to Share Surrender A/c Rs. 2,00,000 and to Capital Reduction A/c Rs. 1,00,000. The sacrifice of Rs. 1,00,000 made by debenture holders is credited to Capital Reduction Account.
conceptTags: Debenture Sacrifice | Capital Reduction Credit | Surrender Reissue

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the final balance remaining in Capital Reserve Account of Apex Manufacturing Ltd. after writing off P&L debit balance and Patents?
optionC: Nil
explanation: Total credit accumulated in Capital Reduction Account = Rs. 6,00,000 (cancelled shares) + Rs. 1,00,000 (debenture sacrifice) = Rs. 7,00,000. Write-offs: P&L debit balance Rs. 4,50,000 + Patents Rs. 1,50,000 = Rs. 6,00,000. Surplus balance transferred to Capital Reserve = Rs. 7,00,000 - Rs. 6,00,000 = Rs. 1,00,000.
conceptTags: Capital Reserve Calculation | Final Balance | Scheme Surplus

subject: Accounts
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Orion Ltd. has the following balance sheet items prior to reconstruction:
- Equity Shares of Rs. 100 each: Rs. 15,00,000 (15,000 shares)
- 10% Debentures: Rs. 5,00,000
- Trade Payables: Rs. 7,00,000
- Land & Building: Rs. 8,00,000
- Machinery: Rs. 12,00,000
- Inventory: Rs. 5,00,000
- Trade Receivables: Rs. 4,00,000
- Profit & Loss Debit Balance: Rs. 6,00,000

NCLT Approved Scheme:
1. Equity shares are reduced to Rs. 40 per share fully paid up.
2. Trade payables agree to forego 20% of their claims. Out of the balance, 30% of original claim is paid by issuing 12% Debentures and remaining in cash.
3. Land & Building is revalued upwards by 25%.
4. Inventory is written down by 20% and a Provision for Doubtful Debts is created at 10% on Trade Receivables.
5. Capital Reduction Account is used to write off Profit & Loss debit balance, and any balance left is used to write down Machinery.

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the total credit generated in the Capital Reduction Account of Orion Ltd. from equity capital reduction, trade payables' sacrifice, and land revaluation combined?
explanation: Equity reduction = 15,000 × Rs. 60 = Rs. 9,00,000. Trade payables sacrifice = 20% of Rs. 7,00,000 = Rs. 1,40,000. Land upward revaluation = 25% of Rs. 8,00,000 = Rs. 2,00,000. Total credit generated in Capital Reduction Account = Rs. 9,00,000 + Rs. 1,40,000 + Rs. 2,00,000 = Rs. 12,40,000.
conceptTags: Capital Reduction Credits | Revaluation Gain | Payables Haircut

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the total amount debited to Capital Reduction Account of Orion Ltd. for Inventory write-down, Provision for Doubtful Debts, and P&L debit balance?
explanation: Debits: Inventory write-down = 20% of Rs. 5,00,000 = Rs. 1,00,000. Provision for Doubtful Debts = 10% of Rs. 4,00,000 = Rs. 40,000. P&L debit balance = Rs. 6,00,000. Total debits for these items = Rs. 1,00,000 + Rs. 40,000 + Rs. 6,00,000 = Rs. 7,40,000.
conceptTags: Capital Reduction Debits | Asset Provision | P&L Write-off

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the revised book value of Machinery in Orion Ltd.'s post-reconstruction Balance Sheet?
explanation: Total Capital Reduction credit = Rs. 12,40,000. Total debits before Machinery = Rs. 7,40,000. Remaining balance available in Capital Reduction Account to write down Machinery = Rs. 12,40,000 - Rs. 7,40,000 = Rs. 5,00,000. Revised Machinery book value = Original Rs. 12,00,000 - Rs. 5,00,000 write-down = Rs. 7,00,000.
conceptTags: Machinery Book Value | Write-down Calculation | Balance Sheet

subject: Accounts
prompt: What is the total cash payment required by Orion Ltd. to discharge its liability towards trade payables under the scheme?
