The Board also decides to transfer 15% of its current profits to general reserves voluntarily before recommending the dividend. On the 32nd day after the declaration of dividend at the Annual General Meeting, an amount of Rs. 4 Lakhs meant for certain shareholders remains unpaid due to incorrect bank account details provided by those shareholders.

subject: Law
prompt: Is the voluntary transfer of 15% of profits to general reserves by Aura Pharmaceuticals Limited legally valid under Section 123?
optionA: Yes, a company may voluntarily transfer such percentage of its profits to reserves as it thinks fit before declaring a dividend.
optionB: No, voluntary transfer to reserves has been abolished under the Companies Act, 2013.
optionC: No, the maximum voluntary transfer allowed is 10%.
optionD: Yes, but it requires prior approval of the Central Government.
answerText: Yes, a company may voluntarily transfer such percentage of its profits to reserves as it thinks fit before declaring a dividend.
explanation: The proviso to Section 123(1) allows a company to voluntarily transfer any percentage of its profits to reserves before the declaration of any dividend.

subject: Law
prompt: What action must Aura Pharmaceuticals Limited take regarding the unpaid dividend of Rs. 4 Lakhs after the expiry of 30 days from the date of declaration?
optionA: Transfer the unpaid amount to an Unpaid Dividend Account in a scheduled bank within 7 days from the expiry of the 30 days.
optionB: Retain the amount in the company's regular operational bank account until shareholders correct their details.
optionC: Transfer the amount immediately to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF).
optionD: Write off the amount as miscellaneous company income.
answerText: Transfer the unpaid amount to an Unpaid Dividend Account in a scheduled bank within 7 days from the expiry of the 30 days.
explanation: Section 124(1) mandates that unpaid or unclaimed dividend must be transferred to an Unpaid Dividend Account in a scheduled bank within 7 days from the expiry of the 30 days of declaration.

subject: Law
prompt: Will the company or its directors attract penal consequences under Section 127 for the unpaid dividend of Rs. 4 Lakhs on the 32nd day?
optionA: No, because the failure to pay was due to incorrect bank details provided by shareholders, which falls under statutory exceptions.
optionB: Yes, penalties under Section 127 apply automatically if any amount remains unpaid past 30 days.
optionC: Yes, directors are liable for imprisonment up to 6 months.
optionD: No, because dividends under 5% of total turnover are exempt from Section 127.
answerText: No, because the failure to pay was due to incorrect bank details provided by shareholders, which falls under statutory exceptions.
explanation: Section 127 explicitly provides that failure to pay dividend within 30 days is not an offense if the dividend could not be paid due to valid reasons such as incorrect details or directions given by the shareholder which could not be complied with.

subject: Law
prompt: Within what period must Aura Pharmaceuticals Limited prepare a statement containing details of the unpaid dividend and place it on its website?
optionA: Within 90 days of making transfer to the Unpaid Dividend Account
optionB: Within 30 days of declaration
optionC: Within 7 days of declaration
optionD: Within 1 year of transfer
answerText: Within 90 days of making transfer to the Unpaid Dividend Account
explanation: Section 124(2) requires the company to prepare a statement of unpaid dividend and place it on its website within a period of 90 days of making any transfer to the Unpaid Dividend Account.

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Retail Limited incurred a net loss during the financial year 2025-26. However, the company has accumulated profits (free reserves) from past years. The Board of Directors intends to declare a dividend out of these accumulated profits to maintain investor sentiment. The company's paid-up share capital is Rs. 5 Crores and its free reserves stand at Rs. 3 Crores. The average dividend declared by Zenith Retail Limited for the immediately preceding three financial years is 10%. The Board is considering declaring a dividend of 14% for the current year by drawing from accumulated reserves.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the maximum rate of dividend that Zenith Retail Limited can declare out of accumulated reserves when current profits are inadequate, as per Rule 3?
explanation: Rule 3 of the Dividend Rules prescribes that the rate of dividend declared out of accumulated profits shall not exceed the average of the rates at which dividend was declared in the 3 immediately preceding years, which is 10% in this case.
conceptTags: Rule 3 | Inadequate Profits | Average Rate Limit

subject: Law
prompt: What is the maximum amount that can be drawn from the accumulated profits by Zenith Retail Limited under Rule 3?
optionA: 10% of the sum of its paid-up share capital and free reserves
optionB: 14% of the paid-up share capital
optionC: 50% of the accumulated reserves
optionD: Rs. 50 Lakhs fixed ceiling
answerText: 10% of the sum of its paid-up share capital and free reserves
explanation: Rule 3(1)(iv) restricts the total amount to be drawn from accumulated profits to a maximum of 10% of the sum of its paid-up share capital and free reserves as appearing in the latest audited financial statement.
conceptTags: Rule 3 | Drawal Limit | Paid-up Capital and Reserves

subject: Law
prompt: Before drawing from accumulated reserves for declaring the dividend, what must Zenith Retail Limited do with regard to any loss incurred in the current financial year?
optionA: First utilize the profit or set off the loss of the current financial year against past profits/losses before drawing from reserves.
optionB: Write off all intangible assets first.
optionC: Obtain approval from the stock exchange.
optionD: Transfer 50% of reserves to capital redemption reserve.
answerText: First utilize the profit or set off the loss of the current financial year against past profits/losses before drawing from reserves.
explanation: Rule 3 requires that the company shall first utilize the profit/set off the loss of the current financial year before drawing from accumulated profits to declare a dividend.
conceptTags: Rule 3 | Set-off of Current Loss | Accumulated Reserves

subject: Law
prompt: Can Zenith Retail Limited declare the dividend at 14% by passing a special resolution at the general meeting?
optionA: No, the 3-year average rate restriction under Rule 3 is mandatory and cannot be overridden by shareholder resolution.
optionB: Yes, a special resolution overrides all rules under the Companies Act, 2013.
optionC: Yes, provided 75% of institutional shareholders agree.
optionD: No, but an ordinary resolution would suffice.
answerText: No, the 3-year average rate restriction under Rule 3 is mandatory and cannot be overridden by shareholder resolution.
explanation: The conditions specified in Rule 3 regarding the maximum rate (3-year average) are statutory prescriptions for drawing from reserves when profits are inadequate and cannot be breached by shareholder resolution.

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Beta Engineering Works declared an interim dividend of Rs. 2 per share on 10th August 2026. The total interim dividend amounted to Rs. 60 Lakhs. Due to an administrative oversight by the finance team, the amount was not deposited in a scheduled bank in a separate account within the stipulated statutory timeline. Instead, the company disbursed the dividend directly from its regular operational cash flow account on the 28th day following the declaration. A shareholder holding 10,000 shares filed a complaint regarding the delay and procedural lapse.

subject: Law
prompt: Within how many days from the date of declaration was Beta Engineering Works required to deposit the interim dividend in a separate bank account under Section 123(4)?
optionA: Within 5 days
optionB: Within 7 days
optionC: Within 15 days
optionD: Within 30 days
answerText: Within 5 days
explanation: Section 123(4) mandates that the amount of dividend, including interim dividend, shall be deposited in a scheduled bank in a separate account within 5 days from the date of declaration.
conceptTags: Section 123 | Interim Dividend | Separate Account Timeline

subject: Law
prompt: Did Beta Engineering Works violate Section 127 by disbursing the dividend on the 28th day?
optionA: No, because the dividend was paid within 30 days of declaration, which is within the permitted payment window.
optionB: Yes, because interim dividends must be paid within 10 days of declaration.
optionC: Yes, because failing to deposit in a separate bank account makes payment illegal even if done within 30 days.
optionD: No, but the company is liable for compounding.
answerText: No, because the dividend was paid within 30 days of declaration, which is within the permitted payment window.
explanation: Section 127 penalizes failure to pay dividend within 30 days from the date of declaration. Since payment was made on the 28th day, the payment window of 30 days was met, though there was a separate violation under Section 123(4) for not depositing in a separate bank account within 5 days.

subject: Law
prompt: What penalty or consequence does Beta Engineering Works face for failing to deposit the interim dividend in a separate bank account within 5 days under Section 123(4)?
optionA: Penalties as applicable under general provisions of the Act for non-compliance where no specific penalty is provided.
optionB: Automatic winding up of the company.
optionC: Imprisonment of all employees for 1 year.
optionD: Forfeiture of all company assets to the Central Government.
answerText: Penalties as applicable under general provisions of the Act for non-compliance where no specific penalty is provided.
explanation: Section 123(4) non-compliance attracts general penalties under Section 450 since a specific penalty is not detailed directly under Section 123(4) apart from the separate account mandate.

subject: Law
prompt: Who authorized the declaration of the interim dividend in Beta Engineering Works?
optionA: The Board of Directors of the company
optionB: The shareholders in the Annual General Meeting
optionC: The Managing Director solely
optionD: The Debenture Trustees
answerText: The Board of Directors of the company
explanation: Section 123(3) empowers the Board of Directors of a company to declare interim dividend during any financial year.
conceptTags: Section 123 | Interim Dividend Authority | Board of Directors

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Gamma Technologies Limited had declared dividends in past years, but certain dividends declared in 2018 remained unclaimed by several shareholders. The total unclaimed dividend amount transferred to the Unpaid Dividend Account in 2018 was Rs. 15 Lakhs. As of October 2025, this amount has remained completely unclaimed in the Unpaid Dividend Account for a period of 7 years. Additionally, 25,000 equity shares of the company on which dividends had not been claimed for 7 consecutive years or more are identified by the company secretary.

subject: Law
prompt: Where must Gamma Technologies Limited transfer the Rs. 15 Lakhs unclaimed dividend after the completion of 7 years from the date of transfer to the Unpaid Dividend Account?
optionA: To the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF)
optionB: To the company's general reserve account as retained earnings
optionC: To the Central Government's Consolidated Fund directly
optionD: To the corporate social responsibility (CSR) corpus
answerText: To the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF)
explanation: Section 124(5) mandates transferring any money remaining unpaid or unclaimed in the Unpaid Dividend Account for 7 years to the IEPF along with interest accrued.

subject: Law
prompt: What action must Gamma Technologies Limited take regarding the 25,000 equity shares whose dividends were unclaimed for 7 consecutive years or more under Section 124(6)?
optionA: Transfer the shares in the name of the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF) Authority.
optionB: Cancel the shares and reduce the paid-up share capital of the company.
optionC: Auction the shares in the open market and credit proceeds to the company's P&L.
optionD: Transfer the shares to the promoters of the company.
answerText: Transfer the shares in the name of the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF) Authority.
explanation: Section 124(6) requires all shares in respect of which dividend has not been paid or claimed for 7 consecutive years or more to be transferred in the name of the IEPF Authority.
conceptTags: Section 124 | Transfer of Shares | IEPF Authority

subject: Law
prompt: Can a shareholder whose shares were transferred to the IEPF Authority subsequently claim them back?
optionA: Yes, by making an application to the IEPF Authority in the prescribed manner.
optionB: No, the transfer is permanent and irreversible under all circumstances.
optionC: Yes, but only after filing a suit in the High Court.
optionD: No, equity rights extinguish permanently upon transfer to IEPF.
answerText: Yes, by making an application to the IEPF Authority in the prescribed manner.
explanation: Under the proviso to Section 124(6), any person claiming to be entitled to any shares transferred to the IEPF may apply to the IEPF Authority for claiming the same.

subject: Law
prompt: Who administers the fund to which the unclaimed dividend and shares are transferred under Section 125?
optionA: The IEPF Authority constituted by the Central Government
optionB: The Reserve Bank of India
optionC: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
optionD: The Ministry of Corporate Affairs Secretariat directly without an authority
answerText: The IEPF Authority constituted by the Central Government
explanation: Section 125(1) specifies that the IEPF shall be administered by an authority specified by the Central Government.

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Delta Agro Industries Limited declared a dividend of Rs. 1.50 per share at its Annual General Meeting held on 15th September 2026. Mr. Roy, a registered shareholder holding 50,000 shares, did not receive his dividend warrant even after 35 days from the date of declaration. Upon inquiry, Mr. Roy discovered that the company willfully withheld his dividend because the company alleged Mr. Roy owed them a minor contractual debt arising from a separate commercial supply contract. There was no court injunction or dispute regarding the ownership of the shares themselves.

subject: Law
prompt: Has Delta Agro Industries Limited committed an offense under Section 127 for failing to pay Mr. Roy's dividend within 30 days?
optionA: Yes, because withholding dividend against a separate commercial trade debt without lawful adjustment provisions under the Act violates Section 127.
optionB: No, companies can adjust any pending dues of any nature against dividends.
optionC: No, because trade debts automatically act as legal stay on dividends.
optionD: Yes, but only the company is penalized; directors have absolute immunity.
answerText: Yes, because withholding dividend against a separate commercial trade debt without lawful adjustment provisions under the Act violates Section 127.
explanation: Section 127 permits lawful adjustment against sums due from the shareholder to the company in relation to shares (such as calls in arrears). Withholding dividend for a separate commercial trade debt outside share-related sums is illegal and attracts Section 127 penalties.

subject: Law
prompt: What rate of interest is the company liable to pay to Mr. Roy under Section 127 during the period the default continues?
optionA: Simple interest at the rate of 18% per annum
optionB: Compound interest at 12% per annum
optionC: Bank rate plus 2%
optionD: Fixed statutory interest of 6% per annum
answerText: Simple interest at the rate of 18% per annum
explanation: Section 127 explicitly mandates that in case of default in paying declared dividend within 30 days, the company shall be liable to pay simple interest at the rate of 18% per annum during the period such default continues.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the penal liability of the directors of Delta Agro Industries Limited who knowingly were party to this default under Section 127?
optionA: Punishable with imprisonment up to 2 years and with fine not less than Rs. 1,000 for every day during which default continues.
optionB: Punishable with community service only.
optionC: Fine of flat Rs. 5,000 with no imprisonment risk.
optionD: Disqualification from directorship for life without court review.
answerText: Punishable with imprisonment up to 2 years and with fine not less than Rs. 1,000 for every day during which default continues.
explanation: Section 127 prescribes imprisonment up to 2 years and a fine of not less than Rs. 1,000 per day of default for every director knowingly a party to the default.
conceptTags: Section 127 | Director Penalties | Imprisonment and Fine

subject: Law
prompt: Can Delta Agro Industries Limited legally adjust the dividend against calls in arrears due on shares held by a shareholder?
optionA: Yes, lawful adjustment against sums due from the shareholder in respect of shares is an explicit exception under Section 127.
optionB: No, dividend must be paid in cash regardless of calls in arrears.
optionC: Yes, but only with prior written permission of SEBI.
optionD: No, calls in arrears can only be recovered through liquidation.
answerText: Yes, lawful adjustment against sums due from the shareholder in respect of shares is an explicit exception under Section 127.
explanation: Section 127 provides an exception where failure to pay is not an offense if the dividend has been lawfully adjusted by the company against any sum due from the shareholder in respect of shares.
conceptTags: Section 127 | Calls in Arrears | Lawful Adjustment

subject: Law
prompt: Which of the following books of account must be kept by every company at its registered office as per Section 128 of the Companies Act, 2013?
optionA: Books of account showing only cash receipts and disbursements
optionB: Books of account and other relevant books and papers and financial statement giving true and fair view of the state of the company's affairs
optionC: Detailed minutes of all general meetings and board meetings only
optionD: Register of members and debenture holders only
answerText: Books of account and other relevant books and papers and financial statement giving true and fair view of the state of the company's affairs
explanation: Section 128(1) mandates that every company shall prepare and keep at its registered office books of account and other relevant books and papers and financial statements reflecting a true and fair view of the state of the affairs of the company.
conceptTags: Books of Account | Registered Office | Section 128

subject: Law
prompt: For how many preceding financial years must a company maintain its books of account in good order under Section 128 of the Companies Act, 2013?
optionA: 5 financial years
optionB: 7 financial years
optionC: 8 financial years
optionD: 10 financial years
answerText: 7 financial years
explanation: Section 128(1) requires a company to keep proper books of account and other relevant books and papers for a period of not less than eight financial years immediately preceding a financial year, or where the company has been in existence for less than eight years, for all such preceding years.
conceptTags: Preservation of Books | Section 128 | Financial Years

subject: Law
prompt: Where a company maintains its books of account in electronic mode, what is the mandatory requirement regarding the location of the server?
optionA: The server must be hosted exclusively within the territorial limits of India at all times.
optionB: The server may be located anywhere globally provided the backup is kept in India.
optionC: The server for hosting the backed-up books of account must be physically located in India.
optionD: There is no restriction on server location if the company is an unlisted private entity.
answerText: The server for hosting the backed-up books of account must be physically located in India.
explanation: Rule 3 of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014 states that where books of account are maintained in electronic mode, the periodic backup of the books of account accessible in India must be kept on servers physically located in India at all times.
conceptTags: Electronic Mode | Server Location | Rule 3 Accounts Rules

subject: Law
prompt: Who among the following has the statutory right to inspect the books of account of a company kept at its registered office during business hours?
optionA: Any equity shareholder of the company
optionB: Any unsecured creditor of the company
optionC: Any director of the company
optionD: The statutory registrar of employees
answerText: Any director of the company
explanation: As per Section 128(3), the books of account and other books and papers of the company shall be open for inspection by any director during business hours.

subject: Law
prompt: Within what period must a financial statement be placed before the Annual General Meeting (AGM) of a company under Section 134?
optionA: At every annual general meeting of the company
optionB: Once in every three calendar years
optionC: Within 6 months from the end of every financial year
optionD: Within 90 days from the close of the financial year
answerText: At every annual general meeting of the company
explanation: Section 134(1) read with Section 96 mandates that financial statements must be laid before every annual general meeting of the company.

subject: Law
prompt: Which of the following is NOT a component of 'Financial Statement' for a company under Section 2(40)?
optionA: Balance sheet as at the end of the financial year
optionB: Profit and loss account or income and expenditure account
optionC: Cash flow statement for the financial year
optionD: Internal auditor's comprehensive report
answerText: Internal auditor's comprehensive report
explanation: Section 2(40) defines financial statement as including a balance sheet, profit and loss account (or income and expenditure account), cash flow statement, statement of changes in equity (if applicable), and any explanatory note. Internal auditor's report is not part of the statutory financial statement definition.

subject: Law
prompt: Which class of companies is specifically exempted from preparing a Cash Flow Statement as part of its financial statements?
optionA: All listed companies
optionB: One Person Company (OPC), small company, dormant company, and private company (start-up)
optionC: Government companies engaged in defense production
optionD: Foreign companies operating a branch office in India
answerText: One Person Company (OPC), small company, dormant company, and private company (start-up)
explanation: The proviso to Section 2(40) states that the financial statement may not include the cash flow statement in case of a One Person Company, small company, dormant company, and private company (if it is a start-up as per DPIIT notification).

subject: Law
prompt: Who is required to sign the financial statements of a company under Section 134(1)?
optionA: Only the Managing Director and the Company Secretary
optionB: The chairperson of the company if authorized by the Board, or two directors out of which one shall be Managing Director and the Chief Executive Officer, CFO, and Company Secretary, wherever they are appointed.
optionC: Any single independent director and the statutory auditor
optionD: All the shareholders present at the AGM
answerText: The chairperson of the company if authorized by the Board, or two directors out of which one shall be Managing Director and the Chief Executive Officer, CFO, and Company Secretary, wherever they are appointed.
explanation: Section 134(1) prescribes that financial statements shall be signed by the chairperson of the company where he is authorized by the Board or by two directors out of which one shall be managing director and the Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Company Secretary, wherever they are appointed.
conceptTags: Signing of Financial Statements | Section 134 | Key Managerial Personnel

subject: Law
prompt: What is the penalty for the Managing Director or CFO (or other officer in charge) in case of contravention of provisions relating to books of account under Section 128?
optionA: Imprisonment for a term up to 1 year only
optionB: A monetary penalty of not less than fifty thousand rupees which may extend to five lakh rupees
optionC: Mandatory disqualification from directorship for 5 years without monetary fine
optionD: Fine of exactly one lakh rupees
answerText: A monetary penalty of not less than fifty thousand rupees which may extend to five lakh rupees
explanation: Section 128(6) states that if the managing director, whole-time director in charge of finance, Chief Financial Officer or any other person of a company charged by the Board fail to take reasonable steps to secure compliance, they shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to 1 year or with fine between fifty thousand and five lakh rupees, or both.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the primary condition for a company to voluntarily revise its financial statements or Board's report under Section 130 and 131?
optionA: Prior approval of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
optionB: Approval of the Central Government (MCA)
optionC: Simple majority vote of retail shareholders
optionD: Recommendation of the statutory auditors alone
answerText: Approval of the Central Government (MCA)
explanation: Section 131 permits voluntary revision of financial statements or Board's report with the approval of the Central Government (delegated to Regional Director) if they do not comply with Section 129 or 134.
conceptTags: Voluntary Revision | Section 131 | Central Government Approval

subject: Law
prompt: Under Section 130, who has the authority to order the re-opening and revision of accounts on the grounds of fraud or mismanagement?
optionA: The Registrar of Companies (ROC)
optionB: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
optionC: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
optionD: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)
answerText: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
explanation: Section 130 empowers the NCLT to order a company to re-open its books of account and revise its financial statements if it is of the opinion that the relevant accounts were prepared in a fraudulent manner or the affairs of the company were mismanaged.

subject: Law
prompt: Which bodies or authorities can apply to the NCLT for re-opening of accounts under Section 130?
optionA: Central Government, Income Tax authorities, SEBI, or any other statutory body/person concerned
optionB: Only the minority shareholders holding at least 10% voting power
optionC: Only the statutory auditor of the company
optionD: Any trade union operating within the company
answerText: Central Government, Income Tax authorities, SEBI, or any other statutory body/person concerned
explanation: Section 130(1) allows application to NCLT by the Central Government, Income-tax authorities, SEBI, Reserve Bank of India, Registrar, or any other statutory regulatory body or person.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the mandatory period up to which a notice of application for re-opening of accounts under Section 130 must be given by NCLT to the concerned authorities?
optionA: 7 days
optionB: 15 days
optionC: 30 days
optionD: 60 days
answerText: 15 days
explanation: Section 130(2) requires the NCLT to give notice to the Central Government, Income-tax authorities, and SEBI/regulatory body and take into consideration their representations before passing any order under Section 130.

subject: Law
prompt: Can accounts re-opened or revised under Section 130 or 131 be subsequently prepared for a period prior to the preceding how many financial years?
optionA: 3 financial years
optionB: 5 financial years
optionC: 8 financial years
optionD: 10 financial years
answerText: 8 financial years
explanation: Section 130(3) and Section 131(1) proviso specify that accounts shall not be re-opened or revised for more than eight financial years immediately preceding the current financial year.

subject: Law
prompt: Which type of companies are required to prepare Consolidated Financial Statements (CFS) in addition to standalone financial statements?
optionA: Every company without exception
optionB: Companies having one or more subsidiaries, associate companies, or joint ventures
optionC: Only listed public companies
optionD: Only government companies with paid-up capital exceeding 100 crores
answerText: Companies having one or more subsidiaries, associate companies, or joint ventures
explanation: Section 129(3) mandates that where a company has one or more subsidiaries, it shall, in addition to standalone statements, prepare a consolidated financial statement of the company and of all the subsidiaries in the same form and manner as its own.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the penalty prescribed under Section 129(7) for a company officer in default for contravening the provisions relating to financial statements?
optionA: Imprisonment up to 1 year or fine between Rs. 50,000 and Rs. 5,00,000, or both
optionB: Only a fixed penalty of Rs. 10,000
optionC: Fine of Rs. 5,00,000 without any option of imprisonment
optionD: Cancellation of company registration immediately
answerText: Imprisonment up to 1 year or fine between Rs. 50,000 and Rs. 5,00,000, or both
explanation: Section 129(7) prescribes punishment for the officer in default as imprisonment for a term up to 1 year or with fine not less than Rs. 50,000 which may extend to Rs. 5,00,000, or both.

subject: Law
prompt: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) reporting forms an integral part of which document under the Companies Act, 2013?
optionA: Auditor's Report
optionB: Board's Report
optionC: Prospectus
optionD: Annual Return (MGT-7)
answerText: Board's Report
explanation: Section 134(3)(o) requires the Board's report to include details about the policy developed and implemented by the company on Corporate Social Responsibility initiatives.

subject: Law
prompt: Which companies are required to constitute a Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Committee under Section 135?
optionA: Every company registered under the Act
optionB: Companies satisfying net worth of Rs. 500 cr+, turnover of Rs. 1000 cr+, or net profit of Rs. 5 cr+ during the immediately preceding financial year
optionC: Only companies listed on recognized stock exchanges
optionD: All banking companies irrespective of their turnover
answerText: Companies satisfying net worth of Rs. 500 cr+, turnover of Rs. 1000 cr+, or net profit of Rs. 5 cr+ during the immediately preceding financial year
explanation: Section 135(1) applies to every company having net worth of Rs. 500 crore or more, turnover of Rs. 1000 crore or more, or a net profit of Rs. 5 crore or more during the immediately preceding financial year.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the minimum percentage of average net profits of the preceding three financial years that a qualifying company must spend on CSR activities?
explanation: Section 135(5) requires the Board of every qualifying company to ensure that the company spends, in every financial year, at least 2% of the average net profits of the company made during the three immediately preceding financial years.
conceptTags: CSR Spend | Section 135 | Average Net Profits

subject: Law
prompt: If a company fails to spend the mandatory CSR amount in a financial year, and such unspent amount does NOT relate to any ongoing project, what must the company do with the unspent amount?
optionA: Transfer it to the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund within 30 days
optionB: Transfer it to a Fund specified in Schedule VII within a period of 6 months of the expiry of the financial year
optionC: Retain it in the profit and loss account as general reserve
optionD: Distribute it as special dividend to shareholders
answerText: Transfer it to a Fund specified in Schedule VII within a period of 6 months of the expiry of the financial year
explanation: Section 135(5) read with rules specifies that any unspent CSR amount, other than relating to an ongoing project, shall be transferred to a Fund specified in Schedule VII within 6 months of the expiry of the financial year.

subject: Law
prompt: Where the unspent CSR amount relates to an 'ongoing project', within what timeframe must the company transfer such amount to a special unspent CSR account?
optionA: Within 30 days from the end of the financial year
optionB: Within 6 months from the end of the financial year
optionC: Within 3 years from the date of transfer
optionD: Within 90 days from the end of the financial year
answerText: Within 30 days from the end of the financial year
explanation: Section 135(6) requires that any unspent amount pertaining to an ongoing project shall be transferred by the company within a period of 30 days from the end of the financial year to a special account to be opened by the company in any scheduled bank called the 'Unspent Corporate Social Responsibility Account'.
conceptTags: Ongoing Project | Unspent CSR Account | Section 135

subject: Law
prompt: Within how many years must the amount transferred to the 'Unspent Corporate Social Responsibility Account' for an ongoing project be utilized by the company?
optionA: 1 financial year
optionB: 2 financial years from the date of such transfer
optionC: 3 financial years from the date of such transfer
optionD: 5 financial years
answerText: 3 financial years from the date of such transfer
explanation: Section 135(6) provides that such amount transferred to the Unspent CSR Account must be spent by the company in pursuance of its obligation toward the CSR policy within a period of 3 financial years from the date of such transfer.
conceptTags: Unspent CSR Account | Time Limit | Section 135

subject: Law
prompt: What is the penalty for default in complying with CSR spend or transfer provisions under Section 135(7)?
optionA: Company is liable to penalty of twice the amount required to be transferred to the Fund/Unspent CSR Account or Rs. 1 crore, whichever is less, and every officer in default is liable to 1/10th of the amount or Rs. 2 lakh, whichever is less
optionB: Mandatory winding up of the company and imprisonment of directors
optionC: Fixed penalty of Rs. 10 lakh on the company only
optionD: No monetary penalty, only warning notice from ROC
answerText: Company is liable to penalty of twice the amount required to be transferred to the Fund/Unspent CSR Account or Rs. 1 crore, whichever is less, and every officer in default is liable to 1/10th of the amount or Rs. 2 lakh, whichever is less
explanation: Section 135(7) prescribes that the company shall be liable to a penalty of twice the amount required to be transferred to the Fund/Unspent CSR Account, or Rs. 1 crore, whichever is less, and every officer in default shall be liable to 1/10th of the amount or Rs. 2 lakh, whichever is less.

subject: Law
prompt: Which committee is responsible for formulating and recommending the CSR policy to the Board in qualifying companies?
optionA: Audit Committee
optionB: Nomination and Remuneration Committee
optionC: Corporate Social Responsibility Committee
optionD: Stakeholders Relationship Committee
answerText: Corporate Social Responsibility Committee
explanation: Section 135(2) mandates that the CSR Committee shall formulate and recommend to the Board, a Corporate Social Responsibility Policy indicating activities to be undertaken.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the composition requirement of the CSR Committee for an unlisted public company or private company that has only two directors on its Board?
optionA: The committee must be formed with minimum three directors including one independent director
optionB: The committee shall consist of two directors
optionC: Exemption from forming CSR committee is granted if there are less than three directors
optionD: The Board itself functions as the CSR Committee without restriction
answerText: The committee shall consist of two directors
explanation: Proviso to Section 135(1) states that where a company is not required to appoint an independent director under Section 149(4), it shall have its CSR Committee with two or more directors.
conceptTags: CSR Committee Composition | Private Company | Section 135

subject: Law
prompt: Who is required to file a copy of the financial statements, along with all required documents, with the Registrar of Companies (ROC) under Section 137?
optionA: Every company
optionB: Only listed companies
optionC: Only companies having paid-up capital above Rs. 10 crore
optionD: Government companies audited by Comptroller and Auditor General
answerText: Every company
explanation: Section 137(1) applies to every company, requiring it to file with the Registrar the financial statements including consolidated financial statements along with all documents required to be attached.
conceptTags: Filing of Financial Statements | Section 137 | ROC

subject: Law
prompt: Within what period from the date of the Annual General Meeting must the financial statements be filed with the ROC under Section 137(1)?
optionA: 30 days
optionB: 60 days
optionC: 90 days
optionD: 6 months
answerText: 30 days
explanation: Section 137(1) stipulates that a copy of the financial statements, including consolidated financial statement, adopted at the AGM shall be filed with the Registrar within 30 days of the date of AGM.

subject: Law
prompt: If the Annual General Meeting of a company is NOT held or cannot be held, within what period from the close of the financial year must the financial statements still be filed with the ROC?
optionA: Within 30 days from the last date on which the AGM ought to have been held
optionB: Within 6 months from the close of the financial year
optionC: Within 90 days from the close of the financial year
optionD: No filing is required if AGM is not held
answerText: Within 30 days from the last date on which the AGM ought to have been held
explanation: First proviso to Section 137(1) specifies that where the financial statements are not adopted at the AGM or AGM is not held, they shall be filed with the Registrar within 30 days of the last date on which the AGM ought to have been held, along with the reasons.
conceptTags: AGM Not Held | Filing of Accounts | Section 137

subject: Law
prompt: What is the statutory penalty for a company upon default in filing financial statements under Section 137?
optionA: Penalty of Rs. 1,000 for every day during which the failure continues subject to a maximum of Rs. 10,00,000
optionB: Fixed penalty of Rs. 50,000 only
optionC: Imprisonment of all shareholders
optionD: Strike off of company name immediately without notice
answerText: Penalty of Rs. 1,000 for every day during which the failure continues subject to a maximum of Rs. 10,00,000
explanation: Section 137(3) provides that if a company fails to file financial statements, the company shall be liable to a penalty of Rs. 1,000 for each day during which such failure continues, subject to a maximum of Rs. 10,00,000.

subject: Law
prompt: Which of the following persons is specifically punishable under Section 137(3) in case of failure to file financial statements?
optionA: The managing director and the Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
optionB: The company secretary and every director of the company who is in default
optionC: Only the external statutory auditor
optionD: All registered shareholders holding more than 5% shares
answerText: The company secretary and every director of the company who is in default
explanation: Section 137(3) prescribes penalty for the managing director and Chief Financial Officer, if any, and, if not, then to every director who is in default, along with the company secretary, with penalty and imprisonment terms specified.
conceptTags: Officer in Default | Section 137 | Filing Penalty

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Pharma Limited is a listed public company having a paid-up share capital of Rs. 40 crores and a turnover of Rs. 250 crores during the financial year 2024-25. The company maintains its primary books of account in electronic mode on a cloud server located in Frankfurt, Germany, with a real-time backup server maintained in Mumbai, India. During an internal audit, it is discovered that the financial statements for the year 2022-23 contained erroneous accounting entries due to inadvertent misclassification of capital expenditure as revenue expenditure. The Board wishes to rectify these accounts voluntarily.

subject: Law
prompt: Is the maintenance of books of account in electronic mode by Zenith Pharma Limited compliant with the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014?
optionA: No, because the primary books cannot be stored on a cloud server outside India.
optionB: Yes, because the periodic backup of the books of account is kept on a server physically located in India.
optionC: No, because listed companies are strictly prohibited from maintaining electronic books.
optionD: Yes, provided the German server is owned by the Government of India.
answerText: Yes, because the periodic backup of the books of account is kept on a server physically located in India.
explanation: Rule 3 of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014 permits electronic maintenance of books provided that the servers for hosting the backed-up books of account are physically located in India at all times.

subject: Law
prompt: What legal procedure must Zenith Pharma Limited follow if it intends to voluntarily revise its financial statements for the year 2022-23?
optionA: Pass an ordinary resolution at a general meeting without any government approval
optionB: Apply to the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) under Section 130
optionC: Obtain approval from the Central Government (Regional Director) under Section 131
optionD: File revised statements directly with ROC without prior permissions
answerText: Obtain approval from the Central Government (Regional Director) under Section 131
explanation: Section 131 allows a company to voluntarily revise its financial statements by obtaining the prior approval of the Central Government (powers delegated to Regional Director), when they do not comply with Section 129.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the maximum number of preceding financial years for which Zenith Pharma Limited can revise its accounts under Section 131?
optionA: 2 financial years
optionB: 3 financial years
optionC: 5 financial years
optionD: 8 financial years
answerText: 8 financial years
explanation: The proviso to Section 131(1) stipulates that voluntary revision shall not be made in respect of more than eight financial years immediately preceding the current financial year.
conceptTags: Voluntary Revision | Limit of Years | Section 131

subject: Law
prompt: If Zenith Pharma Limited fails to keep proper books of account at its registered office as required by Section 128, what penalty is attracted by the Managing Director in charge?
optionA: Imprisonment up to 1 year or fine between Rs. 50,000 and Rs. 5,00,000, or both
optionB: A fixed penalty of Rs. 10,00,000
optionC: Only disqualification from directorship for 2 years
optionD: Fine equal to 50% of the company's turnover
answerText: Imprisonment up to 1 year or fine between Rs. 50,000 and Rs. 5,00,000, or both
explanation: Section 128(6) penalizes the managing director or CFO for failure to take reasonable steps with imprisonment up to 1 year or fine ranging from Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 5,00,000, or both.

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: GreenEarth Agro Industries Private Limited is a profitable company. For the financial year 2024-25, its financial parameters are as follows: Net Worth is Rs. 550 crores, Turnover is Rs. 1,100 crores, and Net Profit is Rs. 6 crores. The company constitutes a CSR Committee and resolves to spend its CSR budget. However, at the close of the financial year, out of the total mandatory CSR obligation of Rs. 1.20 crores, the company spent only Rs. 80 lakhs on regular community welfare projects. The remaining Rs. 40 lakhs was unspent, out of which Rs. 25 lakhs relates to an ongoing school building project initiated last year, and Rs. 15 lakhs relates to a completed tree plantation drive.

subject: Law
prompt: Is GreenEarth Agro Industries Private Limited statutorily required to constitute a CSR Committee under Section 135?
optionA: No, because it is a private limited company.
optionB: Yes, because its turnover exceeds Rs. 1,000 crores and net profit exceeds Rs. 5 crores.
optionC: No, because its net worth is below Rs. 1,000 crores.
optionD: Yes, only if ordered by the Registrar of Companies.
answerText: Yes, because its turnover exceeds Rs. 1,000 crores and net profit exceeds Rs. 5 crores.
explanation: Section 135(1) applies if any of the three thresholds (Net Worth Rs. 500 cr+, Turnover Rs. 1000 cr+, Net Profit Rs. 5 cr+) is met. Here, turnover (Rs. 1,100 cr) and net profit (Rs. 6 cr) exceed the thresholds.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the legal requirement for GreenEarth Agro Industries Private Limited regarding the unspent CSR amount of Rs. 15 lakhs relating to the completed tree plantation drive?
optionA: It must be transferred to the Unspent CSR Account within 30 days.
optionB: It must be transferred to a Fund specified in Schedule VII within 6 months of the expiry of the financial year.
optionC: It can be carried forward as a reserve for future tree plantation.
optionD: It is waived off since the company spent majority of its budget.
answerText: It must be transferred to a Fund specified in Schedule VII within 6 months of the expiry of the financial year.
explanation: Section 135(5) mandates that unspent amount other than relating to an ongoing project must be transferred to a Fund specified in Schedule VII within 6 months of the expiry of the financial year.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the requirement for the unspent CSR amount of Rs. 25 lakhs relating to the ongoing school building project?
optionA: Transfer it to an 'Unspent CSR Account' in a scheduled bank within 30 days of the end of the financial year.
optionB: Transfer it to the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund within 7 days.
optionC: Spend it within 30 days from the end of the financial year.
optionD: Surrender it to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs immediately.
answerText: Transfer it to an 'Unspent CSR Account' in a scheduled bank within 30 days of the end of the financial year.
explanation: Section 135(6) requires that unspent amount pertaining to an ongoing project be transferred within 30 days of the end of the financial year to a special account called 'Unspent Corporate Social Responsibility Account'.
conceptTags: Ongoing Project | Unspent CSR Account | Section 135

subject: Law
prompt: Within what maximum period must the Rs. 25 lakhs transferred to the Unspent CSR Account be utilized by the company?
optionA: 1 financial year
optionB: 2 financial years
optionC: 3 financial years from the date of such transfer
optionD: 5 financial years
answerText: 3 financial years from the date of such transfer
explanation: Section 135(6) specifies that the amount transferred to the Unspent CSR Account must be spent by the company within a period of 3 financial years from the date of such transfer.
conceptTags: Unspent CSR Account | Time Limit | Section 135

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Apex Global Limited, a listed company, held its Annual General Meeting (AGM) for the financial year 2024-25 on September 28, 2025. Due to administrative delays and a change in statutory auditors, the adoption of financial statements was postponed, and consequently, the financial statements were not adopted at the said AGM. The company finally filed its financial statements with the Registrar of Companies (ROC) on November 25, 2025.

subject: Law
prompt: By what date ought Apex Global Limited to have held its AGM for the financial year 2024-25 under general provisions?
optionA: August 31, 2025
optionB: September 30, 2025
optionC: October 31, 2025
optionD: December 31, 2025
answerText: September 30, 2025
explanation: Section 96 requires an AGM to be held within 6 months from the close of the financial year (i.e., by September 30 for a financial year ending on March 31). Apex held it on September 28, 2025, which was within time.
conceptTags: AGM Timing | Section 96 | Financial Year Close

subject: Law
prompt: What is the statutory due date for filing financial statements with the ROC under Section 137(1) when financial statements are not adopted at the AGM?
optionA: Within 30 days from the date of the AGM
optionB: Within 30 days from the last date on which the AGM ought to have been held
optionC: Within 60 days from the close of the financial year
optionD: Within 90 days from the date of the AGM
answerText: Within 30 days from the last date on which the AGM ought to have been held
explanation: First proviso to Section 137(1) states that where financial statements are not adopted at the AGM, they shall be filed with the Registrar within 30 days of the last date on which the AGM ought to have been held.

subject: Law
prompt: Considering the facts, what was the last date by which Apex Global Limited should have filed its unadopted financial statements with the ROC?
optionA: October 28, 2025
optionB: October 30, 2025
optionC: November 28, 2025
optionD: December 30, 2025
answerText: October 30, 2025
explanation: Since the AGM ought to have been held by September 30, 2025, filing must be done within 30 days thereof, making the due date October 30, 2025.

subject: Law
prompt: Given that Apex Global Limited filed its financial statements on November 25, 2025, which is past the due date, what penalty is the company liable to under Section 137(3)?
optionA: A penalty of Rs. 1,000 for every day during which failure continues, subject to a maximum of Rs. 10,00,000
optionB: A fixed penalty of Rs. 50,000 without daily accumulation
optionC: Imprisonment of all directors for 6 months
optionD: Fine of Rs. 1 crore flat
answerText: A penalty of Rs. 1,000 for every day during which failure continues, subject to a maximum of Rs. 10,00,000
explanation: Section 137(3) prescribes a penalty of Rs. 1,000 for each day during which the failure to file financial statements continues, subject to a maximum ceiling of Rs. 10,00,000 for the company.
conceptTags: Penalty for Non-Filing | Section 137 | Daily Fine

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Vanguard Technologies Private Limited is a wholly owned subsidiary of Vanguard Inc., USA. The company closes its financial year on March 31, 2025. The Board of Directors prepared the financial statements for the year 2024-25. The company's board consists of two directors, Mr. A and Mr. B. The company has appointed a Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and a Company Secretary (CS). When preparing the financial statements, the Board wonders who is legally mandated to sign these financial statements under Section 134(1).

subject: Law
prompt: Who among the following must sign the financial statements of Vanguard Technologies Private Limited as per Section 134(1)?
optionA: Only Mr. A as the sole authorized director
optionB: The chairperson authorized by the Board or two directors (including Managing Director if any), along with CFO and CS (where appointed)
optionC: Only the Chief Financial Officer and statutory auditor
optionD: The holding company's directors in the USA
answerText: The chairperson authorized by the Board or two directors (including Managing Director if any), along with CFO and CS (where appointed)
explanation: Section 134(1) mandates that financial statements be signed by the chairperson authorized by the Board or two directors (one being MD if appointed), and the CEO, CFO, and CS, wherever they are appointed.

subject: Law
prompt: Is Vanguard Technologies Private Limited required to include a Cash Flow Statement in its financial statements under Section 2(40)?
optionA: Yes, all companies without exception must file a cash flow statement.
optionB: No, because it is a private company and a subsidiary of a foreign corporate body.
optionC: No, because OPC, small companies, dormant companies, and private company start-ups are exempted, but being a subsidiary of a foreign corporate body, it does not automatically enjoy the start-up private company exemption unless it qualifies under specific rules.
optionD: Yes, since it is a subsidiary of a foreign company, cash flow is mandatory.
answerText: Yes, since it is a subsidiary of a foreign company, cash flow is mandatory.
explanation: The exemption from cash flow statement under Section 2(40) is available to OPC, small companies, dormant companies, and private company start-ups. Since Vanguard is a subsidiary of a foreign body corporate (not an Indian start-up private company), cash flow statement is required.
conceptTags: Cash Flow Statement | Subsidiary | Section 2(40) Exemption

subject: Law
prompt: Under Section 129(3), what additional financial statement must Vanguard Technologies Private Limited prepare if it has its own subsidiary company in India?
optionA: Consolidated Financial Statement (CFS) along with standalone statement
optionB: Only segment reporting statements
optionC: Tax audit report in Form 3CD
optionD: Quarterly un-audited results
answerText: Consolidated Financial Statement (CFS) along with standalone statement
explanation: Section 129(3) mandates that where a company has one or more subsidiaries, it shall prepare a Consolidated Financial Statement of the company and all subsidiaries in the same form and manner as its own.

subject: Law
prompt: Where must Vanguard Technologies Private Limited keep its books of account as per Section 128?
optionA: At its registered office in India
optionB: At the holding company's headquarters in USA
optionC: At the statutory auditor's office in India
optionD: At any place in India decided by the CFO
answerText: At its registered office in India
explanation: Section 128(1) requires every company to prepare and keep books of account and other relevant papers at its registered office in India.
conceptTags: Registered Office | Books of Account | Section 128

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: A serious financial scam comes to light in Stellar Infrastructure Limited. The Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) and Income Tax authorities suspect that the financial statements of the company for the past 5 financial years were manipulated and prepared in a fraudulent manner to inflate profits and secure bank loans. The regulatory authorities decide to approach the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) for re-opening the company's books of account.

subject: Law
prompt: Which section of the Companies Act, 2013 governs the re-opening of accounts on Court or Tribunal orders based on fraud or mismanagement?
optionA: Section 128
optionB: Section 129
optionC: Section 130
optionD: Section 131
answerText: Section 130
explanation: Section 130 deals specifically with the re-opening of accounts on Tribunal's or Court's orders where accounts were prepared in a fraudulent manner or due to mismanagement.

subject: Law
prompt: Which authorities are specifically empowered under Section 130(1) to apply to the NCLT for re-opening of accounts?
optionA: Central Government, Income-tax authorities, SEBI, RBI, or any other statutory regulatory body
optionB: Any retail shareholder holding a single share
optionC: Only the statutory auditors of the company
optionD: Any commercial bank that has granted a loan
answerText: Central Government, Income-tax authorities, SEBI, RBI, or any other statutory regulatory body
explanation: Section 130(1) lists Central Government, Income-tax authorities, SEBI, RBI, Registrar, or any other statutory regulatory body as authorized applicants to NCLT.

subject: Law
prompt: Before passing an order under Section 130, what procedural step must the NCLT mandatorily undertake with respect to notices?
optionA: Give notice to Central Government, Income-tax authorities, and SEBI/regulatory body and consider their representations
optionB: Publish a public advertisement in international newspapers and wait for 90 days
optionC: Obtain unanimous consent of all equity shareholders
optionD: Direct the police commissioner to arrest the Board of Directors
answerText: Give notice to Central Government, Income-tax authorities, and SEBI/regulatory body and consider their representations
explanation: Section 130(2) requires the NCLT to give notice to the Central Government, Income-tax authorities, and SEBI or any other statutory body and take into consideration their representations before passing any order.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the maximum retrospective timeframe limitation up to which accounts can be re-opened under Section 130?
optionA: 3 financial years
optionB: 5 financial years
optionC: 8 financial years immediately preceding the current financial year
optionD: No time limit whatsoever
answerText: 8 financial years immediately preceding the current financial year
explanation: Section 130(3) restricts re-opening of accounts to not more than eight financial years immediately preceding the current financial year.

subject: Law
prompt: Who holds the primary responsibility for appointing the first auditor of a company other than a Government company under Section 139(6) of the Companies Act, 2013?
optionA: The Board of Directors
optionB: The members in a general meeting
optionC: The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
optionD: The Regional Director
answerText: The Board of Directors
explanation: According to Section 139(6) of the Companies Act, 2013, the first auditor of a company, other than a Government company, shall be appointed by the Board of Directors within 30 days of the date of registration of the company. If the Board fails, it informs the members to appoint the auditor.

subject: Law
prompt: Within what period from the date of registration must the Board of Directors appoint the first auditor of a non-Government company?
optionA: 15 days
optionB: 30 days
optionC: 60 days
optionD: 90 days
answerText: 30 days
explanation: Section 139(6) mandates that the Board of Directors of a non-Government company must appoint the first auditor within 30 days from the date of registration of the company.

subject: Law
prompt: What happens if the Board of Directors of a non-Government company fails to appoint the first auditor within the stipulated 30-day period?
optionA: The office of the auditor remains vacant permanently for that year.
optionB: The Central Government directly makes the appointment.
optionC: The company shall inform the members, who shall appoint the auditor within 90 days at an extraordinary general meeting.
optionD: The Registrar of Companies automatically assumes the role of the auditor.
answerText: The company shall inform the members, who shall appoint the auditor within 90 days at an extraordinary general meeting.
explanation: Under Section 139(6), if the Board fails to appoint the first auditor within 30 days, it shall inform the members of the company, who shall within 90 days at an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) appoint such auditor.
conceptTags: First Auditor | Default by Board | Member Appointment

subject: Law
prompt: For a Government company or any other company owned or controlled, directly or indirectly, by the Central Government, who appoints the first auditor under Section 139(7)?
optionA: The Board of Directors within 30 days
optionB: The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India (CAG) within 60 days from registration
optionC: The members in the first Annual General Meeting
optionD: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
answerText: The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India (CAG) within 60 days from registration
explanation: Section 139(7) states that in the case of a Government company, the first auditor shall be appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India within 60 days from the date of registration of the company.
conceptTags: Government Company | CAG Appointment | First Auditor

subject: Law
prompt: What is the maximum tenure for which an individual can be appointed as an auditor in a listed company before mandatory rotation applies under Section 139(2)?
optionA: One term of 3 consecutive years
optionB: One term of 5 consecutive years
optionC: Two terms of 5 consecutive years each
optionD: Maximum of 10 consecutive years without limit
answerText: Two terms of 5 consecutive years each
explanation: Section 139(2) provides that an individual can be appointed as an auditor for not more than one term of 5 consecutive years. However, they can be re-appointed for another term of 5 consecutive years after a cooling period, making a maximum of two terms of 5 years each.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the mandatory cooling period required for an individual auditor after completing their maximum tenure in a company where rotation of auditors applies?
optionA: 2 consecutive years
optionB: 3 consecutive years
optionC: 5 consecutive years
optionD: 10 consecutive years
answerText: 5 consecutive years
explanation: According to Section 139(2), an individual who has completed their term of 5 consecutive years (or two terms totaling 10 years, depending on the rule applicability) cannot be re-appointed as auditor of the same company for a period of 5 years from the completion of their term.

subject: Law
prompt: Under Section 139(2), what is the maximum continuous tenure permitted for an audit firm in a listed company?
optionA: One term of 5 years
optionB: Two terms of 5 consecutive years each
optionC: Three terms of 5 consecutive years each
optionD: Five consecutive years with no renewal
answerText: Two terms of 5 consecutive years each
explanation: Section 139(2) specifies that an audit firm can be appointed for not more than two terms of 5 consecutive years each, followed by a mandatory cooling period of 5 years.

subject: Law
prompt: Which of the following classes of companies, other than listed companies, are specifically required to comply with the mandatory rotation of auditors provisions under Rule 5 of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014?
optionA: All private limited companies regardless of paid-up share capital
optionB: Unlisted public companies having paid-up share capital of rupees 10 crore or more
optionC: All dormant companies
optionD: All Nidhi companies with any deposit size
answerText: Unlisted public companies having paid-up share capital of rupees 10 crore or more
explanation: Rule 5 of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014 requires unlisted public companies having paid-up share capital of Rs. 10 crore or more, and private limited companies having paid-up share capital of Rs. 50 crore or more, to rotate their auditors.

subject: Law
prompt: Can a retiring auditor be re-appointed at an Annual General Meeting (AGM) if they have become disqualified under Section 141(3)?
optionA: Yes, if the Board unanimously recommends them.
optionB: Yes, with the prior approval of the Registrar of Companies.
optionC: No, a disqualified person cannot be appointed or re-appointed as an auditor.
optionD: Yes, provided 75% of members vote in favor.
answerText: No, a disqualified person cannot be appointed or re-appointed as an auditor.
explanation: Section 141(3) outlines disqualifications for appointment as an auditor. A person who incurs a disqualification cannot be appointed or re-appointed, and any ongoing appointment ceases immediately upon disqualification.

subject: Law
prompt: Which of the following persons is NOT disqualified from being appointed as an auditor of a company under Section 141(3)?
optionA: A body corporate other than a Limited Liability Partnership
optionB: An officer or employee of the company
optionC: A person who, or whose relative or partner, holds any security of or interest in the company of face value rupees 500
optionD: A chartered accountant in practice who is holding a valid Certificate of Practice
answerText: A chartered accountant in practice who is holding a valid Certificate of Practice
explanation: A practicing Chartered Accountant with a valid COP is eligible for appointment, provided they do not suffer from any specific disqualifications listed in Section 141(3) such as being an officer/employee, holding securities above the permitted limit, or being a corporate body.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the maximum face value limit of securities that a relative of an auditor can hold in the company, subsidiary, holding, or associate company without disqualifying the auditor under Section 141(3)(d)(i)?
optionA: Rupees 1,000
optionB: Rupees 50,000
optionC: Rupees 1,00,000
optionD: Rupees 5,00,000
answerText: Rupees 1,00,000
explanation: Under Section 141(3)(d)(i), a person is disqualified if they, their relative, or partner holds any security of or interest in the company, its subsidiary, holding, or associate company of face value exceeding Rs. 1,00,000 (as amended by the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2017).

subject: Law
prompt: If a relative of an auditor acquires securities exceeding the permitted threshold of rupees 1,00,000 post-appointment, what corrective action must be taken and within what timeframe?
optionA: The auditor must resign within 60 days.
optionB: The corrective action to divest or rectify must be taken within 60 days.
optionC: The company must redeem the shares within 30 days.
optionD: No action is required if the holding was unintentional.
answerText: The corrective action to divest or rectify must be taken within 60 days.
explanation: As per the proviso to Section 141(3)(d), where a person acquires securities or interest exceeding the threshold after appointment, the corrective action to maintain the limits must be taken by the person concerned within 60 days of such acquisition.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the maximum indebtedness limit to the company, its holding, subsidiary, or associate company that will disqualify a person from being appointed as an auditor under Section 141(3)(d)(ii)?
optionA: Rupees 1,00,000
optionB: Rupees 5,00,000
optionC: Rupees 10,00,000
optionD: Any amount exceeding rupees 5,00,000
answerText: Rupees 5,00,000
explanation: Under Section 141(3)(d)(ii), a person is disqualified if they or their relative or partner is indebted to the company, its subsidiary, holding, or associate company, or a subsidiary of such holding company, in excess of Rs. 5,00,000.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the maximum guarantee or security limit provided by a person in connection with any third party to the company, its holding, subsidiary, or associate company that disqualifies an auditor under Section 141(3)(d)(iii)?
optionA: Rupees 50,000
optionB: Rupees 1,00,000
optionC: Rupees 5,00,000
optionD: Rupees 10,00,000
answerText: Rupees 1,00,000
explanation: Section 141(3)(d)(iii) states that a person is disqualified if they or their relative or partner has given a guarantee or provided any security in connection with the indebtedness of any third person to the company, its subsidiary, holding, or associate company, in excess of Rs. 1,00,000.

subject: Law
prompt: Under Section 141(3)(f), what is the maximum number of companies (excluding dormant companies, one person companies, small companies, and private companies having paid-up share capital of less than Rs. 100 crore) in respect of which an auditor can hold office at a given time?
optionA: 10 companies
optionB: 20 companies
optionC: 30 companies
optionD: 50 companies
answerText: 20 companies
explanation: Section 141(3)(f) specifies the ceiling limit on audit assignments. A person cannot hold office as an auditor in more than 20 companies at the same time, subject to exclusions for certain categories of companies.

subject: Law
prompt: How is a casual vacancy in the office of an auditor filled in the case of a company other than a Government company under Section 139(8)?
optionA: Filled by the Comptroller and Auditor-General within 30 days.
optionB: Filled by the Board of Directors within 30 days, but if due to resignation, it must also be approved by the company at a general meeting within 3 months.
optionC: Filled exclusively by the members at an extraordinary general meeting called within 7 days.
optionD: Filled by the Registrar of Companies directly.
answerText: Filled by the Board of Directors within 30 days, but if due to resignation, it must also be approved by the company at a general meeting within 3 months.
explanation: Section 139(8)(i) provides that casual vacancies other than due to resignation are filled by the Board within 30 days. If the vacancy is due to resignation, the Board must fill it within 30 days, and the appointment must also be approved by the company in a general meeting within 3 months of the Board's recommendation.

subject: Law
prompt: Within what period must a casual vacancy arising due to the resignation of an auditor be approved by the company in a general meeting after the Board makes the appointment?
optionA: 1 month
optionB: 2 months
optionC: 3 months
optionD: 6 months
answerText: 3 months
explanation: Under the proviso to Section 139(8)(i), where a casual vacancy is caused by the resignation of an auditor, the appointment by the Board must be approved by the company in a general meeting convened within 3 months of the recommendation of the Board.

subject: Law
prompt: Who fills a casual vacancy in the office of an auditor of a Government company under Section 139(8)(ii)?
optionA: The Board of Directors within 30 days
optionB: The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India within 30 days
optionC: The members of the company in an AGM
optionD: The Central Government directly
answerText: The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India within 30 days
explanation: Section 139(8)(ii) dictates that in the case of a Government company, a casual vacancy in the office of an auditor shall be filled by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India within 30 days. If CAG fails, the Board fills it within the next 30 days.

subject: Law
prompt: Under Section 140(1), what is the requisite procedural step required for the removal of an auditor before the expiry of their term?
optionA: Ordinary resolution passed at any general meeting with 7 days notice
optionB: Special resolution passed by the Board of Directors
optionC: Prior approval of the Central Government and passing a special resolution after giving a reasonable opportunity of being heard
optionD: Simple written notice to the Registrar of Companies
answerText: Prior approval of the Central Government and passing a special resolution after giving a reasonable opportunity of being heard
explanation: Section 140(1) prescribes that an auditor may be removed from office before the expiry of their term only after obtaining the prior approval of the Central Government and passing a special resolution in a general meeting, after giving the auditor a reasonable opportunity of being heard.
conceptTags: Removal of Auditor | Central Government Approval | Section 140(1)

subject: Law
prompt: What form must an auditor file with the company and the Registrar upon resigning from their office, as mandated by Section 140(2) and Rule 8?
optionA: Form ADT-1
optionB: Form ADT-3
optionC: Form ADT-4
optionD: Form INC-22
answerText: Form ADT-3
explanation: Under Section 140(2) and Rule 8 of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014, an auditor who resigns from the company must file a statement in Form ADT-3 with the company and the Registrar (and also with the CAG in case of Government companies) within 30 days of resignation.

subject: Law
prompt: What specific information must an auditor include in Form ADT-3 upon resignation before their term expires?
optionA: Only the resignation letter addressed to the managing director.
optionB: A detailed statement of reasons for resignation and any other facts relevant to the resignation.
optionC: The bank account details for final settlement of audit fees.
optionD: A copy of the audit report already submitted for previous years.
answerText: A detailed statement of reasons for resignation and any other facts relevant to the resignation.
explanation: Section 140(2) requires the resigning auditor to indicate the detailed reasons and facts relevant to their resignation in the statement filed with the company and the Registrar.

subject: Law
prompt: What penalty can be imposed on the auditor under Section 140(3) if they fail to comply with the statutory requirements of filing the resignation statement under Section 140(2)?
optionA: Fine of Rs. 10,000 only
optionB: Fine ranging from Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 5,00,000 or remuneration of the auditor, whichever is less
optionC: Imprisonment up to 1 year mandatory
optionD: Cancellation of Certificate of Practice for 5 years
answerText: Fine ranging from Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 5,00,000 or remuneration of the auditor, whichever is less
explanation: Section 140(3) provides that if the auditor does not comply with Section 140(2), they shall be punishable with a fine which shall not be less than Rs. 50,000 or the remuneration of the auditor, whichever is less, and which may extend to Rs. 5,00,000.

subject: Law
prompt: Under Section 140(5), if the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) is satisfied that an auditor has acted in a fraudulent manner or abetted or colluded in any fraud, what order can it pass?
optionA: Direct the auditor to pay a fine to the shareholders directly.
optionB: Direct the company to change its auditor, and such auditor shall not be eligible to be appointed as an auditor of any company for 5 years.
optionC: Suspend the auditor's practicing membership for life without tribunal hearing.
optionD: Order liquidation of the company immediately.
answerText: Direct the company to change its auditor, and such auditor shall not be eligible to be appointed as an auditor of any company for 5 years.
explanation: Section 140(5) empowers NCLT (suo motu or upon application) to direct the company to change its auditor if the auditor acted fraudulently. Additionally, such auditor is barred from being appointed as an auditor of any company for a period of 5 years.
conceptTags: NCLT Powers | Fraud by Auditor | Section 140(5)

subject: Law
prompt: Which section of the Companies Act, 2013 deals with the remuneration of auditors?
optionA: Section 139
optionB: Section 140
optionC: Section 142
optionD: Section 143
answerText: Section 142
explanation: Section 142 of the Companies Act, 2013 governs the remuneration of auditors, specifying that it shall be fixed in a general meeting or in such manner as the company in general meeting may determine.

subject: Law
prompt: According to Section 143(1), what right of access does an auditor have during the performance of their duties?
optionA: Access at all times to any books of account and vouchers of the company, whether kept at the registered office or elsewhere.
optionB: Access only to the physical books of account located at the principal factory during working hours.
optionC: Access to books of account solely upon giving 14 days advance written notice to the directors.
optionD: Access to personal bank accounts of all shareholders and directors.
answerText: Access at all times to any books of account and vouchers of the company, whether kept at the registered office or elsewhere.
explanation: Section 143(1) gives every auditor of a company a right of access at all times to the books of account and vouchers of the company, whether kept at the registered office or elsewhere, and requires them to be entitled to require from officers of the company such information and explanation as they may think necessary.
conceptTags: Auditor Rights | Access to Books | Section 143(1)

subject: Law
prompt: In carrying out their duties regarding fraud reporting under Section 143(12), if an auditor has reason to believe that an offense involving fraud is being or has been committed against the company by officers or employees, what is the first step they must take if the fraud amount is below rupees 1 crore?
optionA: Report directly to the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) within 2 days.
optionB: Report the matter to the Board or Audit Committee within 2 days of knowledge.
optionC: Publish a notice in a national daily newspaper.
optionD: Immediately resign and file Form ADT-3.
answerText: Report the matter to the Board or Audit Committee within 2 days of knowledge.
explanation: Under Rule 13 of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014 pursuant to Section 143(12), if the fraud involves an amount below Rs. 1 crore, the auditor must report the matter to the Board or the Audit Committee within 2 days of becoming aware of the fraud.

subject: Law
prompt: Under Section 143(12) and Rule 13, if a fraud involves an amount of rupees 1 crore or above, within how many days must the auditor report the matter to the Central Government (Ministry of Corporate Affairs)?
optionA: 2 days
optionB: 15 days
optionC: 60 days
optionD: Within 60 days, after first reporting to the Board/Audit Committee within 2 days to seek their reply or observations
answerText: Within 60 days, after first reporting to the Board/Audit Committee within 2 days to seek their reply or observations
explanation: For frauds involving Rs. 1 crore or more, the auditor must report to the Board/Audit Committee within 2 days seeking their comments within 45 days. Upon receiving comments or expiry of 45 days, the auditor must forward the report to the Central Government within 15 days (making total timeline structured around the 60-day reporting framework).

subject: Law
prompt: Which of the following services are explicitly prohibited to be rendered by an auditor to a company, its holding, or subsidiary company under Section 144?
optionA: Tax audit under the Income Tax Act, 1961
optionB: Design and implementation of any financial information system
optionC: Issuing comfort letters required for public issue of shares
optionD: Performing statutory audit of subsidiary companies
answerText: Design and implementation of any financial information system
explanation: Section 144 lists non-audit services that an auditor cannot provide, which include design and implementation of any financial information system, internal audit, bookkeeping, actuarial services, investment advisory services, etc.

subject: Law
prompt: Who is required to sign the auditor's report under Section 145 of the Companies Act, 2013?
optionA: Only the managing director of the company
optionB: The person appointed as auditor, or where a firm is appointed, only the partners practicing in India can sign
optionC: Any senior articled assistant authorized by the audit firm
optionD: The Company Secretary along with the internal auditor
answerText: The person appointed as auditor, or where a firm is appointed, only the partners practicing in India can sign
explanation: Section 145 mandates that the person appointed as auditor of the company, or where a firm is appointed, only the partners practicing in India can sign the auditor's report or sign or authenticate any other document of the company required by law.
conceptTags: Signing Audit Report | Section 145 | Auditor Signature

subject: Law
prompt: Under Section 146, is the auditor required to attend general meetings of the company?
optionA: No, attendance at general meetings is entirely voluntary for auditors.
optionB: Yes, the auditor must attend every general meeting unless exempted by the Board.
