optionC: Yes, unless specifically exempted by the company, the auditor or their authorized representative must attend all general meetings where financial statements are discussed.
optionD: Only when summoned by the National Company Law Tribunal.
answerText: Yes, unless specifically exempted by the company, the auditor or their authorized representative must attend all general meetings where financial statements are discussed.
explanation: Section 146 stipulates that all notices of and other communications relating to any general meeting shall be forwarded to the auditor, and the auditor shall attend either by themselves or through their authorized representative (who is also qualified to be an auditor) any general meeting and shall have right to be heard.

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Aura Cosmetics Limited is a listed public company registered on 1st April 2025. The Board of Directors met on 20th April 2025 to appoint 'M/s Sharma & Associates', a Chartered Accountant firm, as the first auditor of the company. Mr. Sharma, a partner in the firm, has a relative who owns equity shares in Aura Cosmetics Limited of the face value of Rs. 80,000. Additionally, the firm was also asked to design and implement a new enterprise financial information system for the company.

subject: Law
prompt: Was the appointment of M/s Sharma & Associates as the first auditor by the Board of Directors within the legally prescribed time limit under Section 139(6)?
optionA: No, because first auditors of listed companies must be appointed by the CAG.
optionB: Yes, because the Board appointed them within 30 days from the date of registration.
optionC: No, because the Board can only appoint auditors after approval of the Registrar.
optionD: Yes, but only if approved by members within 15 days.
answerText: Yes, because the Board appointed them within 30 days from the date of registration.
explanation: Under Section 139(6), the Board of Directors of a non-Government company must appoint the first auditor within 30 days of registration. Aura Cosmetics Limited was registered on 1st April 2025, and the appointment on 20th April 2025 falls within the 30-day window.

subject: Law
prompt: Does the shareholding of Rs. 80,000 by Mr. Sharma's relative in Aura Cosmetics Limited disqualify M/s Sharma & Associates from being appointed as the auditor?
optionA: Yes, any shareholding by a relative creates immediate absolute disqualification.
optionB: No, because the face value of the shares held by the relative does not exceed the statutory limit of Rs. 1,00,000.
optionC: Yes, because relatives of partners cannot hold shares in listed companies under any circumstances.
optionD: No, provided the shares are sold within 7 days of appointment.
answerText: No, because the face value of the shares held by the relative does not exceed the statutory limit of Rs. 1,00,000.
explanation: Under Section 141(3)(d)(i), holding securities of face value up to Rs. 1,00,000 by a relative is permitted. Since the relative holds shares worth Rs. 80,000, it is within the permissible limit and does not trigger disqualification.

subject: Law
prompt: Is it permissible for M/s Sharma & Associates to design and implement the financial information system for Aura Cosmetics Limited?
optionA: Yes, if approved by a special resolution of shareholders.
optionB: No, because designing and implementing financial information systems is a prohibited non-audit service under Section 144.
optionC: Yes, because design of IT systems is part of normal statutory audit duties.
optionD: No, unless the fee for this service does not exceed 10% of total audit fees.
answerText: No, because designing and implementing financial information systems is a prohibited non-audit service under Section 144.
explanation: Section 144 explicitly prohibits an auditor appointed under the Act from providing design and implementation of any financial information system to the company, its holding, or subsidiary companies.

subject: Law
prompt: If M/s Sharma & Associates completes its first term of 5 years as auditor of Aura Cosmetics Limited, what is the maximum continuous tenure they can hold before a mandatory cooling period applies?
optionA: Only 1 term of 5 years with no renewal
optionB: Two terms of 5 consecutive years each (total 10 years)
optionC: Three terms of 5 consecutive years each (total 15 years)
optionD: Unlimited tenure for listed companies
answerText: Two terms of 5 consecutive years each (total 10 years)
explanation: Section 139(2) allows an audit firm to be appointed for a maximum of two terms of 5 consecutive years each in a listed company, after which a mandatory cooling period of 5 years applies.

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Vanguard Engineering Ltd. is an unlisted public company with a paid-up share capital of Rs. 15 crore and turnover of Rs. 120 crore. During the annual audit for the financial year ended 31st March 2026, the statutory auditor, CA. Raman, discovers that the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) has manipulated accounts to siphon off Rs. 75,00,000. CA. Raman wishes to understand his statutory obligations regarding reporting this fraud.

subject: Law
prompt: Does Vanguard Engineering Ltd. fall under the mandatory rotation of auditor provisions under Rule 5 of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014?
optionA: No, because it is an unlisted company.
optionB: Yes, because it is an unlisted public company having paid-up share capital of Rs. 10 crore or more.
optionC: No, because its turnover is below Rs. 200 crore.
optionD: Yes, but only if the Central Government issues a special notification.
answerText: Yes, because it is an unlisted public company having paid-up share capital of Rs. 10 crore or more.
explanation: Rule 5 mandates rotation for unlisted public companies having a paid-up share capital of Rs. 10 crore or more. Since Vanguard Engineering Ltd. has a paid-up share capital of Rs. 15 crore, rotation rules apply to it.
conceptTags: Rotation Thresholds | Rule 5 | Unlisted Public Company

subject: Law
prompt: Since the fraud discovered involves an amount of Rs. 75,00,000 (which is below Rs. 1 crore), what is CA. Raman's immediate reporting obligation under Rule 13 of Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014?
optionA: Report directly to the Central Government within 15 days.
optionB: Report the matter to the Board or Audit Committee within 2 days of his knowledge.
optionC: Report to the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.
optionD: File a criminal complaint with the local police station within 24 hours.
answerText: Report the matter to the Board or Audit Committee within 2 days of his knowledge.
explanation: Under Rule 13(1) pursuant to Section 143(12), if the fraud involves an amount less than Rs. 1 crore, the auditor must report the matter to the Board or the Audit Committee within 2 days of becoming aware of it.

subject: Law
prompt: What must CA. Raman do after reporting the fraud below Rs. 1 crore to the Audit Committee/Board?
optionA: Wait for the Board's reply and include the same in the Board's report as specified in the rules.
optionB: Immediately resign and file Form ADT-3 with ROC.
optionC: Publish the details in local newspapers for public awareness.
optionD: File an appeal before the National Company Law Tribunal.
answerText: Wait for the Board's reply and include the same in the Board's report as specified in the rules.
explanation: When reporting fraud below Rs. 1 crore, the auditor must report to the Board/Audit Committee within 2 days, seeking their receipt and comments, which must be disclosed in the Board's report in the prescribed manner.

subject: Law
prompt: If CA. Raman fails to report the fraud as required under Section 143(12), what penalty is he liable to pay?
optionA: A fixed fine of rupees 10,000
optionB: A fine not less than rupees 1,00,000 which may extend to rupees 25,00,000
optionC: Mandatory imprisonment of 5 years
optionD: Fine equal to the entire audit fee of the company
answerText: A fine not less than rupees 1,00,000 which may extend to rupees 25,00,000
explanation: Section 143(15) specifies that if any auditor does not comply with the provisions of sub-section (12), they shall be punishable with a fine of not less than Rs. 1,00,000 which may extend to Rs. 25,00,000.

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Pharma Ltd., a listed company, appointed 'M/s Apex & Co.', a Chartered Accountant firm, as its statutory auditor at the 5th Annual General Meeting held in September 2024 for a term of 5 years. In July 2025, due to professional pre-occupation, the audit firm decided to resign before completing its term. The firm submitted its resignation letter directly to the company.

subject: Law
prompt: What procedural filing requirement must 'M/s Apex & Co.' fulfill upon resignation under Section 140(2) and Rule 8?
optionA: File Form ADT-1 with the Board of Directors within 15 days.
optionB: File a statement in Form ADT-3 with the company and the Registrar within 30 days of resignation, indicating reasons.
optionC: File Form ADT-4 directly with the NCLT without notifying the company.
optionD: No filing is required if resignation is due to professional pre-occupation.
answerText: File a statement in Form ADT-3 with the company and the Registrar within 30 days of resignation, indicating reasons.
explanation: Section 140(2) and Rule 8 mandate that an auditor who resigns must file Form ADT-3 with the company and the Registrar within 30 days, detailing the reasons for resignation.

subject: Law
prompt: How shall the casual vacancy caused by the resignation of M/s Apex & Co. be filled under Section 139(8)?
optionA: Filled exclusively by the Comptroller and Auditor-General within 30 days.
optionB: Filled by the Board of Directors within 30 days, and such appointment must also be approved by the company in a general meeting within 3 months.
optionC: Filled by the Registrar of Companies automatically.
optionD: The office must remain vacant until the next Annual General Meeting.
answerText: Filled by the Board of Directors within 30 days, and such appointment must also be approved by the company in a general meeting within 3 months.
explanation: Under Section 139(8)(i), a casual vacancy caused by resignation must be filled by the Board within 30 days, and the appointment must be approved by the company in a general meeting convened within 3 months of the Board's recommendation.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the consequence if M/s Apex & Co. fails to file Form ADT-3 within the prescribed 30 days?
optionA: Penalty under Section 140(3) ranging from Rs. 50,000 or the remuneration of the auditor, whichever is less, up to Rs. 5,00,000.
optionB: Automatic extension of audit term by 1 year.
optionC: Only a warning letter from the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India.
optionD: Fine of a flat Rs. 10,000 with no other penal consequences.
answerText: Penalty under Section 140(3) ranging from Rs. 50,000 or the remuneration of the auditor, whichever is less, up to Rs. 5,00,000.
explanation: Section 140(3) prescribes a penalty for non-compliance with Section 140(2) ranging from Rs. 50,000 or the auditor's remuneration (whichever is less) up to Rs. 5,00,000.

subject: Law
prompt: Who is authorized to sign the audit report on behalf of 'M/s Apex & Co.'?
optionA: Any paid assistant employed by the firm who holds a valid membership.
optionB: Only the partner practicing in India as appointed and authorized by the firm.
optionC: The managing partner residing outside India.
optionD: Any Company Secretary employed by the audit firm.
answerText: Only the partner practicing in India as appointed and authorized by the firm.
explanation: Section 145 specifies that when an audit firm is appointed, only the partner practicing in India can sign the audit report or authenticate documents on behalf of the firm.
conceptTags: Signing Audit Report | Section 145 | Audit Firm

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Bharat Power Corporation Ltd. is a Government company in which the Central Government holds 65% of the paid-up share capital. The company was incorporated on 10th May 2025. The Board of Directors assumed that they had 30 days to appoint the first auditor. Meanwhile, the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India (CAG) also initiated steps for appointing the first auditor.

subject: Law
prompt: Who holds the legal authority to appoint the first auditor of Bharat Power Corporation Ltd. under Section 139(7)?
optionA: The Board of Directors within 30 days
optionB: The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India (CAG) within 60 days from registration
optionC: The members in the first Annual General Meeting
optionD: The National Company Law Tribunal
answerText: The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India (CAG) within 60 days from registration
explanation: Section 139(7) explicitly states that in the case of a Government company, the first auditor shall be appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India within 60 days from the date of registration.

subject: Law
prompt: What happens if the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India fails to appoint the first auditor within the stipulated 60 days in Bharat Power Corporation Ltd.?
optionA: The company remains without an auditor for the entire financial year.
optionB: The Board of Directors shall appoint the auditor within the next 30 days.
optionC: The Registrar of Companies automatically becomes the auditor.
optionD: The shareholders elect the auditor at an extraordinary general meeting within 7 days.
answerText: The Board of Directors shall appoint the auditor within the next 30 days.
explanation: Under Section 139(7), if the CAG fails to appoint the first auditor within 60 days, the Board of Directors of the Government company shall appoint the auditor within the next 30 days.
conceptTags: Government Company | CAG Default | Board Appointment

subject: Law
prompt: How is a subsequent auditor appointed in Bharat Power Corporation Ltd. under Section 139(5)?
optionA: Appointed by the shareholders at each Annual General Meeting.
optionB: Appointed by the CAG within 180 days before the commencement of the financial year.
optionC: Appointed by the Central Government directly.
optionD: Appointed by the Board of Directors every year.
answerText: Appointed by the CAG within 180 days before the commencement of the financial year.
explanation: Section 139(5) specifies that in the case of a Government company or any other company owned/controlled by the Central/State Government, the sub-sequent auditor shall be appointed by the CAG within 180 days from the commencement of the financial year.

subject: Law
prompt: If a casual vacancy arises in the office of the auditor of Bharat Power Corporation Ltd., who is empowered to fill such vacancy under Section 139(8)(ii)?
optionA: The Board of Directors within 7 days
optionB: The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India within 30 days
optionC: The members in an extraordinary general meeting
optionD: The Central Government immediately
answerText: The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India within 30 days
explanation: Section 139(8)(ii) dictates that a casual vacancy in the case of a Government company shall be filled by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India within 30 days. If CAG fails, the Board fills it within the next 30 days.

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: CA. Manoj is a practicing Chartered Accountant and sole proprietor of 'Manoj & Co.'. He is offered the statutory audit of 22 companies. Out of these 22 companies, 2 are dormant companies, 3 are One Person Companies (OPCs), 2 are small companies, and the remaining 15 are active public and private limited companies. CA. Manoj is evaluating whether accepting all these audits complies with the statutory ceiling limits.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the statutory ceiling limit on the number of audit assignments an auditor can hold under Section 141(3)(f)?
optionA: 10 companies
optionB: 20 companies
optionC: 30 companies
optionD: 50 companies
answerText: 20 companies
explanation: Section 141(3)(f) specifies that a person cannot hold office as an auditor in more than 20 companies at the same time.

subject: Law
prompt: Which of the following categories of companies are excluded while calculating the ceiling limit of 20 companies under Section 141(3)(f)?
optionA: All listed companies and private companies
optionB: Dormant companies, One Person Companies, small companies, and private companies having paid-up share capital of less than Rs. 100 crore
optionC: Government companies only
optionD: Foreign subsidiary companies
answerText: Dormant companies, One Person Companies, small companies, and private companies having paid-up share capital of less than Rs. 100 crore
explanation: Section 141(3)(f) excludes dormant companies, OPCs, small companies, and private companies having paid-up share capital of less than Rs. 100 crore from the computation of the 20-company ceiling limit.

subject: Law
prompt: Based on the exclusions, how many companies out of CA. Manoj's offered 22 companies will be counted towards his 20-company ceiling limit?
optionA: All 22 companies
optionB: 15 companies (active public and private companies)
optionC: 17 companies
optionD: 20 companies
answerText: 15 companies (active public and private companies)
explanation: Out of 22 companies, 2 dormant, 3 OPCs, and 2 small companies (total 7) are excluded. Thus, only 15 companies count toward the ceiling limit.

subject: Law
prompt: Can CA. Manoj accept the audit of all 22 companies offered to him without violating the Companies Act, 2013?
optionA: No, because total offers exceed 20.
optionB: Yes, because his countable audits (15) are well within the ceiling limit of 20 companies.
optionC: No, because individual auditors cannot audit more than 10 companies.
optionD: Yes, if he obtains prior permission from the ICAI president.
answerText: Yes, because his countable audits (15) are well within the ceiling limit of 20 companies.
explanation: Since only 15 companies count towards the ceiling limit (which is below the maximum limit of 20), CA. Manoj can legally accept all 22 companies offered to him.

subject: Law
prompt: Under the Companies Act, 2013, what is the timeline within which a foreign company must deliver documents to the Registrar of Companies (RoC) upon establishing a place of business in India?
optionA: 15 days
optionB: 30 days
optionC: 60 days
optionD: 90 days
answerText: 30 days
explanation: Section 380 of the Companies Act, 2013 mandates that every foreign company shall, within 30 days of the establishment of place of business in India, deliver specified documents to the Registrar. This is a crucial procedural requirement for foreign entities operating in India.

subject: Law
prompt: Which of the following documents is NOT statutorily required to be delivered by a foreign company to the RoC under Section 380 upon establishing a place of business in India?
optionA: Certified copy of the charter, statutes or memorandum and articles of the company
optionB: Full address of the registered or principal office of the company
optionC: List of all past and present directors and secretary of the company
optionD: Audited balance sheet and profit and loss account for the preceding three financial years
answerText: Audited balance sheet and profit and loss account for the preceding three financial years
explanation: Section 380 requires filing of the charter, full address, list of directors, and details of principal place of business in India, among others. Audited financial statements of the Indian business are required to be filed annually under Section 381, but initial incorporation filings under Section 380 do not require three years of audited accounts.

subject: Law
prompt: If any alteration is made or occurs in any of the documents delivered to the RoC by a foreign company under Section 380, within what period must the foreign company file a return containing particulars of such alteration?
optionA: 15 days
optionB: 30 days
optionC: 60 days
optionD: 90 days
answerText: 30 days
explanation: According to Section 380(3), if any alteration is made or occurs in the documents delivered to the Registrar, the foreign company must file a return containing the particulars of the alteration within 30 days of such alteration.

subject: Law
prompt: Every foreign company is required to prepare and file financial statements relating to its Indian business operations with the RoC in Form:
optionA: FC-1
optionB: FC-3
optionC: AOC-4
optionD: MGT-7
answerText: FC-3
explanation: Under Rule 4 of the Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules, 2014, every foreign company must file balance sheet and profit and loss account in Form FC-3 along with a list of all places of business established by the company in India.
conceptTags: Financial Statements | Form FC-3 | Foreign Company

subject: Law
prompt: Within what period from the close of the financial year must a foreign company file its financial statements and list of places of business in India with the RoC?
optionA: 30 days
optionB: 6 months
optionC: 180 days
optionD: 90 days
answerText: 6 months
explanation: As per Rule 4(1) of the Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules, 2014, every foreign company shall file with the Registrar, along with the financial statements, a list of all places of business established by the company in India within 6 months of the close of the financial year.

subject: Law
prompt: Who is empowered by the Central Government to direct that any foreign company or class of foreign companies shall comply with specific provisions regarding accounts and audit?
optionA: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
optionB: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
optionC: Central Government by notification
optionD: National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
answerText: Central Government by notification
explanation: Section 381(3) states that the Central Government may, by notification, direct that the provisions of Chapter IX (Accounts of Companies) or any specified provisions thereof shall apply to any foreign company or class of foreign companies with such exceptions or modifications as may be specified.

subject: Law
prompt: Where a foreign company keeps its books of account outside India, what is the statutory requirement regarding copies of such books of account to be kept at its principal place of business in India?
optionA: No books need to be kept in India
optionB: Periodic returns reflecting the financial position of business in India must be kept at the principal place of business
optionC: Complete original ledger books must be shipped to India monthly
optionD: Certified translated copies of all global accounts must be maintained in India
answerText: Periodic returns reflecting the financial position of business in India must be kept at the principal place of business
explanation: Section 381(1) proviso requires that a foreign company must keep at its principal place of business in India books of account containing sufficient particulars to show the true and fair view of the transactions of the company and explain its receipts and payments, as well as periodic returns reflecting the financial position of the business in India.
conceptTags: Books of Account | Principal Place | Section 381

subject: Law
prompt: Under Section 382, every foreign company must paint or affix its name and the name of the country in which it is incorporated outside every office or place of business in India in:
optionA: English language only
optionB: Official language of the state where the office is located
optionC: English and local language of the place where its office is situated
optionD: Hindi only
answerText: English and local language of the place where its office is situated
explanation: Section 382 requires every foreign company to exhibit its name and the country of incorporation in English and in the local language of the place where its office or place of business is situated, outside every office or place of business in India.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the penalty under Section 392 for a foreign company that fails to comply with any of the provisions of Chapter XXII (Companies Incorporated Outside India)?
optionA: Fine ranging from ₹10,000 to ₹1,00,000 only
optionB: Fine not less than ₹1,00,000 which may extend to ₹3,00,000, and in case of continuing offence with a further fine up to ₹50,000 per day
optionC: Imprisonment of directors only
optionD: Automatic winding up of the foreign company
answerText: Fine not less than ₹1,00,000 which may extend to ₹3,00,000, and in case of continuing offence with a further fine up to ₹50,000 per day
explanation: Section 392 prescribes a fine for the company not less than ₹1,00,000 extending up to ₹3,00,000, and in case of continuing offence, an additional fine up to ₹50,000 per day for every officer in default or the company. This ensures strict compliance.

subject: Law
prompt: Which of the following defines a 'foreign company' under Section 2(42) of the Companies Act, 2013?
optionA: Any company incorporated outside India which has a share capital
optionB: Any company or body corporate incorporated outside India which has a place of business in India whether by itself or through an agent, physically or through electronic mode
optionC: Any company owned by non-resident Indians operating outside India
optionD: Any multinational corporation trading with Indian entities without any physical office
answerText: Any company or body corporate incorporated outside India which has a place of business in India whether by itself or through an agent, physically or through electronic mode
explanation: Section 2(42) defines a foreign company as any company or body corporate incorporated outside India which has a place of business in India whether by itself or through an agent, physically or through electronic mode, and conducts any business activity in India in any other manner.

subject: Law
prompt: Can a foreign company issue prospectus in India without complying with Chapter XXII provisions?
optionA: Yes, if it is listed on a recognized foreign stock exchange
optionB: No, it must comply with all statutory prospectus provisions under Sections 389 to 393
optionC: Yes, if approved by SEBI independently
optionD: No, foreign companies are completely barred from issuing prospectuses in India
answerText: No, it must comply with all statutory prospectus provisions under Sections 389 to 393
explanation: Sections 389 to 393 govern the issue of prospectus by foreign companies. No prospectus can be issued by or on behalf of a foreign company unless it complies with the stringent disclosure and delivery requirements specified in the Act.

subject: Law
prompt: When a prospectus is issued by a foreign company in India, a copy thereof must be delivered to:
optionA: Securities and Exchange Board of India
optionB: Registrar of Companies at Delhi
optionC: Reserve Bank of India
optionD: Ministry of Corporate Affairs directly
answerText: Registrar of Companies at Delhi
explanation: Section 389 stipulates that no person shall issue, circulate or distribute in India any prospectus offering for subscription shares or debentures of a company incorporated outside India, unless a copy has been delivered to the Registrar of Companies (specifically designated RoC, typically Delhi).

subject: Law
prompt: Which rule defines 'electronic mode' for the purpose of a foreign company conducting business in India?
optionA: Rule 2 of Companies (Specification of Definitions Details) Rules, 2014
optionB: Rule 3 of Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules, 2014
optionC: Rule 5 of Companies (Prospectus and Allotment of Securities) Rules, 2014
optionD: Rule 10 of Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014
answerText: Rule 3 of Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules, 2014
explanation: Rule 3 of the Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules, 2014 defines 'electronic mode' encompassing business-to-business and business-to-consumer transactions, data interchange, online services, digital supply chains, etc., conducted via electronic media.

subject: Law
prompt: What must be stated prominently on the outside of every office and in all business letters, bill heads, and notices of a foreign company in India?
optionA: The PAN and GSTIN of the Indian branch
optionB: Whether the company is limited or not, along with its name and country of incorporation
optionC: The name of the Chief Executive Officer of the Indian operations
optionD: The authorized share capital in Indian Rupees
answerText: Whether the company is limited or not, along with its name and country of incorporation
explanation: Under Section 382, foreign companies must state the name of the company, the country of incorporation, and if the liability of members is limited, state that fact clearly on bill heads, notices, letter papers, and outside every office.

subject: Law
prompt: If a foreign company fails to deliver documents under Section 380, what liability do the officers in default face?
optionA: Only civil damages
optionB: Punishable under Section 392 with fine and imprisonment
optionC: Only administrative warning by RoC
optionD: Immediate deportation of directors
answerText: Punishable under Section 392 with fine and imprisonment
explanation: Section 392 provides that any failure by a foreign company to comply with Chapter XXII makes the company and every officer in default punishable with fine and imprisonment or both as specified under the penal provisions.

subject: Law
prompt: Are the provisions of Chapter VI (Registration of Charges) applicable to a foreign company in relation to charges on property situated in India?
optionA: No, charges of foreign companies are governed entirely by foreign laws
optionB: Yes, Section 384 applies the provisions relating to registration of charges to charges created by a foreign company on property in India
optionC: Only if approved by the Reserve Bank of India
optionD: Yes, but only for floating charges
answerText: Yes, Section 384 applies the provisions relating to registration of charges to charges created by a foreign company on property in India
explanation: Section 384 specifically applies the provisions of Chapter VI (Registration of Charges) to a foreign company as if it were a company incorporated in India, in respect of property situated in India.
conceptTags: Section 384 | Registration of Charges | Foreign Company

subject: Law
prompt: What is the requirement regarding the audit of accounts of a foreign company's Indian business operations?
optionA: Accounts must be audited by a chartered accountant in practice in India
optionB: Accounts can be audited by any auditor qualified in the home country
optionC: No audit is required if audited globally
optionD: Audit must be conducted exclusively by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
answerText: Accounts must be audited by a chartered accountant in practice in India
explanation: Section 381(2) requires that the balance sheet and profit and loss account of a foreign company shall be audited by a practicing Chartered Accountant in India, or a firm of chartered accountants.

subject: Law
prompt: Which form is filed by a foreign company to register its particulars upon establishing a place of business in India under Section 380?
optionA: Form INC-1
optionB: Form FC-1
optionC: Form FC-2
optionD: Form FC-4
answerText: Form FC-1
explanation: Rule 3 of the Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules, 2014 specifies that an application for registration by a foreign company must be made in Form FC-1 along with necessary attachments.

subject: Law
prompt: Does the definition of foreign company under Section 2(42) include an entity operating exclusively through electronic mode?
optionA: No, electronic mode business is exempt from company law regulations
optionB: Yes, provided it conducts business activity in India through electronic mode
optionC: Only if it maintains a physical warehouse in India
optionD: Only if turnover exceeds 100 crores INR
answerText: Yes, provided it conducts business activity in India through electronic mode
explanation: Section 2(42) explicitly includes companies incorporated outside India that have a place of business in India 'whether by itself or through an agent, physically or through electronic mode', expanding the scope to e-commerce and digital platforms.

subject: Law
prompt: Within what period must a foreign company file particulars of any alteration in its directors or secretary with the RoC?
optionA: 15 days
optionB: 30 days
optionC: 60 days
optionD: 90 days
answerText: 30 days
explanation: Under Section 380(3), any alteration in the documents filed initially, including changes in directors or secretary, must be filed with the RoC within 30 days of the alteration.

subject: Law
prompt: If a foreign company ceases to have a place of business in India, what is its obligation regarding notice to the RoC?
optionA: It can simply abandon operations without notice
optionB: It must forthwith give notice to the Registrar, and from the date of such notice, its obligation to file ceases
optionC: It must wait for 5 years before giving notice
optionD: Notice must be published in international newspapers only
answerText: It must forthwith give notice to the Registrar, and from the date of such notice, its obligation to file ceases
explanation: Under the Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules, 2014, when a foreign company ceases to have a place of business in India, it shall forthwith give notice to the Registrar, and thereafter the obligation of the company to deliver any document to the Registrar ceases.
conceptTags: Cessation | Notice to RoC | Foreign Company

subject: Law
prompt: Which of the following is considered part of 'electronic mode' under Rule 3?
optionA: B2B and B2C web-based transactions
optionB: Offline telephonic conversations
optionC: Physical courier shipments
optionD: Postal mail correspondence
answerText: B2B and B2C web-based transactions
explanation: Rule 3 of the Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules, 2014 defines electronic mode to include business-to-business and business-to-consumer transactions, data interchange, and other digital business services.

subject: Law
prompt: Who must sign the annual financial statement and return filed by a foreign company in India?
optionA: Only the home country auditor
optionB: Authorized representative of the foreign company in India
optionC: The Prime Minister of the home country
optionD: Any random employee in India
answerText: Authorized representative of the foreign company in India
explanation: The financial statements and annual returns filed by a foreign company under Section 381 must be authenticated by the authorized representative of the foreign company in India.

subject: Law
prompt: Can a foreign company accept deposits in India under the provisions of Chapter XXII read with RBI guidelines?
optionA: Yes, freely from the general public
optionB: No foreign company can accept or renew deposits in India unless in compliance with RBI regulations and applicable company law deposit rules
optionC: Yes, without any restriction
optionD: Only if incorporated in Mauritius
answerText: No foreign company can accept or renew deposits in India unless in compliance with RBI regulations and applicable company law deposit rules
explanation: Acceptance of deposits by foreign companies in India is strictly regulated and restricted, requiring compliance with RBI regulations and provisions applicable to deposit acceptance.

subject: Law
prompt: What documents must be attached when a foreign company files Form FC-1 for establishing a place of business?
optionA: Charter, statutes, or memorandum and articles translated into English
optionB: Personal tax returns of all shareholders
optionC: Land title deeds of properties in home country
optionD: Passports of all global customers
answerText: Charter, statutes, or memorandum and articles translated into English
explanation: Form FC-1 must be accompanied by certified translated copies of the charter, statutes, or memorandum and articles of association of the foreign company if they are not in English.

subject: Law
prompt: Which section of the Companies Act, 2013 deals specifically with the accounts of foreign companies?
optionA: Section 128
optionB: Section 381
optionC: Section 390
optionD: Section 379
answerText: Section 381
explanation: Section 381 of the Companies Act, 2013 contains specific provisions regarding the accounts of a foreign company, requiring maintenance of books of account in India and annual financial statement filing.

subject: Law
prompt: If a foreign company fails to pay the fine imposed under Section 392, who can be held liable among its officers?
optionA: Only the external auditors
optionB: Every officer in default who is in default of compliance
optionC: No one, the liability is extinguished
optionD: Only shareholders holding more than 50% shares
answerText: Every officer in default who is in default of compliance
explanation: Section 392 penalizes 'every officer of the foreign company who is in default', subjecting them to fines and imprisonment as stipulated under the Act.

subject: Law
prompt: Under Section 386, what is the meaning of 'certified copy' when required for documents delivered to the RoC by a foreign company?
optionA: Certified in the manner prescribed for documents originating in the home country as a true copy
optionB: Certified by any Indian citizen living abroad
optionC: Self-attested by a company clerk
optionD: Certified by local police
answerText: Certified in the manner prescribed for documents originating in the home country as a true copy
explanation: Section 386 defines 'certified copy' as a copy certified in the manner prescribed by rules, typically certified as a true copy in the country of incorporation in accordance with local laws and notarized/apostilled.

subject: Law
prompt: Are Indian companies laws regarding corporate social responsibility (CSR) automatically applicable to foreign companies having a branch in India?
optionA: Yes, all foreign branches must spend 2% of global profits on CSR
optionB: Applicability is determined based on the net worth, turnover, or net profit thresholds of the Indian business operations of the foreign company as per Section 135
optionC: No, CSR does not apply to foreign companies at all
optionD: Only if explicitly ordered by the Supreme Court
answerText: Applicability is determined based on the net worth, turnover, or net profit thresholds of the Indian business operations of the foreign company as per Section 135
explanation: CSR provisions under Section 135 apply to foreign companies having a branch office or project office in India, based on the financial thresholds computed for their Indian business operations.

subject: Law
prompt: Which office of the Registrar of Companies has jurisdiction over all foreign companies registered in India?
optionA: RoC Mumbai
optionB: RoC Delhi
optionC: RoC Chennai
optionD: RoC Kolkata
answerText: RoC Delhi
explanation: By notification and administrative allocation under the Companies Act, the Registrar of Companies at Delhi (RoC Delhi) has centralized jurisdiction for registration and filing of documents by all foreign companies in India.

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Global Tech Inc., a corporation incorporated in Delaware, USA, establishes a branch office in Bengaluru, India, on 1st April 2026 to provide software consulting services. The company commences its physical operations immediately. Mr. Smith is appointed as the authorized representative in India. The company delivers its charter, list of directors, and address details to RoC Delhi on 25th May 2026.

subject: Law
prompt: Did Global Tech Inc. comply with the initial document delivery timeline under Section 380?
optionA: Yes, because documents were delivered within 60 days
optionB: No, because documents must be delivered within 30 days of establishing a place of business
optionC: Yes, because foreign companies get 90 days grace period
optionD: No, because filing must be done before commencing business
answerText: No, because documents must be delivered within 30 days of establishing a place of business
explanation: Section 380 requires a foreign company to deliver documents within 30 days of establishing a place of business. Global Tech Inc. established its place on 1st April and filed on 25th May (54 days later), thereby missing the 30-day statutory timeline.

subject: Law
prompt: To which Registrar of Companies should Global Tech Inc. have delivered its registration documents?
optionA: RoC Bengaluru
optionB: RoC Mumbai
optionC: RoC Delhi
optionD: RoC Delaware
answerText: RoC Delhi
explanation: As per administrative jurisdiction under the Companies Act, 2013, all foreign companies register and file their initial incorporation documents with the Registrar of Companies, Delhi, regardless of where their Indian branch is physically located.

subject: Law
prompt: If Global Tech Inc. later appoints a new director in Delaware on 1st July 2026, within what timeframe must it file the return of alteration with the RoC?
optionA: 15 days
optionB: 30 days
optionC: 60 days
optionD: 90 days
answerText: 30 days
explanation: Section 380(3) stipulates that any alteration in the documents delivered to the Registrar (including change in directors) must be filed by submitting a return within 30 days of such alteration.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the consequence of Global Tech Inc. failing to file its initial documents within the prescribed 30-day window?
optionA: Automatic confiscation of Bengaluru office property
optionB: Penalty under Section 392 on the company and every officer in default
optionC: Revocation of Delaware incorporation
optionD: Mandatory imprisonment of all US shareholders
answerText: Penalty under Section 392 on the company and every officer in default
explanation: Section 392 prescribes penal consequences including fines ranging from ₹1,00,000 to ₹3,00,000 and continuing daily fines for non-compliance with Section 380 by the company and officers in default.

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Nippon Auto Ltd., a company incorporated in Japan, operates an online e-commerce platform targeting Indian consumers without having any physical warehouses or offices in India. All transactions, digital contracts, and product deliveries are handled through electronic mode. Nippon Auto Ltd. generates significant revenue from Indian territory during the financial year 2025-26.

subject: Law
prompt: Is Nippon Auto Ltd. classified as a 'foreign company' under the Companies Act, 2013?
optionA: No, because it lacks a physical office or brick-and-mortar store in India
optionB: Yes, because Section 2(42) includes companies incorporated outside India conducting business in India through electronic mode
optionC: No, foreign e-commerce is regulated exclusively by IT Act
optionD: Yes, but only if it registers a subsidiary in India
answerText: Yes, because Section 2(42) includes companies incorporated outside India conducting business in India through electronic mode
explanation: Section 2(42) explicitly includes companies incorporated outside India that conduct business in India through electronic mode, even without a physical office, within the definition of a foreign company.

subject: Law
prompt: Which rules define the scope of 'electronic mode' applicable to Nippon Auto Ltd.?
optionA: Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules, 2014
optionB: Information Technology Rules, 2021
optionC: Foreign Exchange Management Rules, 2016
optionD: SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015
answerText: Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules, 2014
explanation: Rule 3 of the Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules, 2014 defines electronic mode for foreign companies operating in India.

subject: Law
prompt: Does Nippon Auto Ltd. need to comply with annual financial statement filing requirements under Section 381?
optionA: No, electronic mode businesses are exempt from accounting filings
optionB: Yes, every foreign company must prepare and file financial statements relating to Indian business operations
optionC: Only if turnover exceeds USD 10 million in Japan
optionD: Only if directed by the Supreme Court
answerText: Yes, every foreign company must prepare and file financial statements relating to Indian business operations
explanation: Section 381 applies to all foreign companies, which includes those operating via electronic mode, requiring them to file financial statements and a list of places of business with the RoC annually.

subject: Law
prompt: Who must audit the financial statements prepared for Nippon Auto Ltd.'s Indian business operations?
optionA: Any auditor in Japan
optionB: A Chartered Accountant in practice in India
optionC: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
optionD: Internal auditor of the parent company
answerText: A Chartered Accountant in practice in India
explanation: Section 381(2) mandates that the financial statements of a foreign company's Indian business must be audited by a practicing Chartered Accountant in India or a firm of chartered accountants.

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: EuroRetail AG, incorporated in Germany, sets up a retail liaison office in Mumbai. The company creates a charge over its machinery situated in Mumbai in favor of an Indian bank. EuroRetail AG fails to register this charge with the RoC within the stipulated time under the Companies Act, 2013.

subject: Law
prompt: Are the provisions regarding registration of charges applicable to EuroRetail AG?
optionA: No, foreign companies are exempt from charge registration
optionB: Yes, Section 384 applies Chapter VI provisions to charges created by foreign companies on property situated in India
optionC: Only if the charge exceeds ₹100 crores
optionD: Yes, but registration must be done in Germany only
answerText: Yes, Section 384 applies Chapter VI provisions to charges created by foreign companies on property situated in India
explanation: Section 384 explicitly applies Chapter VI (Registration of Charges) to foreign companies in respect of property situated in India as if they were Indian companies.
conceptTags: Section 384 | Registration of Charges | Foreign Company

subject: Law
prompt: Within what period must a charge on property in India be registered by EuroRetail AG?
optionA: 10 days
optionB: 30 days
optionC: 60 days
optionD: 90 days
answerText: 30 days
explanation: Charges created by a company (including a foreign company under Section 384) on property in India must be registered within 30 days of creation, extendable with approval.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the legal consequence of failing to register the charge created by EuroRetail AG?
optionA: The charge becomes void against the liquidator and any creditor of the company
optionB: The German directors are imprisoned immediately
optionC: The machinery is auctioned by RBI
optionD: The loan agreement becomes illegal
answerText: The charge becomes void against the liquidator and any creditor of the company
explanation: Non-registration of a charge under Chapter VI (applied via Section 384) renders the charge void against the liquidator and any creditor of the company.

subject: Law
prompt: Where must EuroRetail AG maintain its books of account regarding its Indian operations?
optionA: Exclusively in Frankfurt, Germany
optionB: At its principal place of business in India
optionC: At the Reserve Bank of India headquarters
optionD: At the Ministry of Corporate Affairs office in Delhi
answerText: At its principal place of business in India
explanation: Section 381(1) requires a foreign company to keep at its principal place of business in India proper books of account with respect to monies received/expended, sales/purchases, and assets/liabilities of the Indian business.
conceptTags: Books of Account | Principal Place | Section 381

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Pacific Holdings Ltd., incorporated in Singapore, establishes a place of business in Chennai. The company displays its name outside its Chennai office only in English. It omits mentioning its country of incorporation and whether its members' liability is limited on its business letterheads used in India.

subject: Law
prompt: Did Pacific Holdings Ltd. comply with Section 382 regarding name display outside its office?
optionA: Yes, English is sufficient
optionB: No, it must exhibit its name and country of incorporation in English and in the local language of the place where its office is situated
optionC: Yes, if approved by RoC Delhi
optionD: No, it must display only in Tamil
answerText: No, it must exhibit its name and country of incorporation in English and in the local language of the place where its office is situated
explanation: Section 382 mandates that every foreign company shall paint or affix its name and the country of incorporation outside every office in English and in the local language of the place.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the requirement regarding business letterheads under Section 382 for Pacific Holdings Ltd.?
optionA: It must state the company name, country of incorporation, and whether liability of members is limited
optionB: It must state the PAN and GSTIN only
optionC: It must state the home country stock exchange ticker
optionD: No particulars are required on letterheads
answerText: It must state the company name, country of incorporation, and whether liability of members is limited
explanation: Section 382 requires that business letter heads, bill heads, and notices must state the name of the foreign company, country of incorporation, and whether the liability of members is limited.

subject: Law
prompt: If Pacific Holdings Ltd. decides to close down its Chennai place of business, what procedure must it follow?
optionA: Abandon premises without informing anyone
optionB: Give notice forthwith to the Registrar of Companies, after which filing obligations cease
optionC: Wait 3 years before notifying RoC
optionD: File a winding-up petition in Singapore High Court
answerText: Give notice forthwith to the Registrar of Companies, after which filing obligations cease
explanation: Under the rules framed for foreign companies, when a foreign company ceases to have a place of business in India, it must forthwith give notice to the Registrar, upon which its obligation to deliver documents ceases.

subject: Law
prompt: What penalty can be imposed for non-compliance with the name display and letterhead requirements under Section 382?
optionA: Fine under Section 392 ranging between ₹1,00,000 and ₹3,00,000 with continuing daily fine
optionB: Warning letter only
optionC: Immediate forfeiture of office furniture
optionD: Deportation of local employees
answerText: Fine under Section 392 ranging between ₹1,00,000 and ₹3,00,000 with continuing daily fine
explanation: General penalty provision under Section 392 applies to any contravention of Chapter XXII, which includes failure to comply with Section 382 name display and letterhead rules.

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Alpha Corp, a company incorporated in the UK, decides to issue a prospectus in India offering shares to the Indian public. Alpha Corp delivers a copy of the prospectus to RoC Delhi. However, the prospectus fails to state the specific details of the instruments and material contracts required under Section 390 read with Section 389.

subject: Law
prompt: To which RoC must Alpha Corp deliver its prospectus prior to issue in India?
optionA: RoC London
optionB: RoC Mumbai
optionC: RoC Delhi
optionD: RoC Kolkata
answerText: RoC Delhi
explanation: Section 389 specifies that a copy of the prospectus must be delivered to the Registrar of Companies (specifically RoC Delhi) before it is issued, circulated, or distributed in India.

subject: Law
prompt: What is a mandatory prerequisite for issuing a prospectus by a foreign company in India?
optionA: Consent of SEBI alone
optionB: Delivery of a copy of the prospectus to the RoC signed by all directors or their authorized agents
optionC: Approval from British High Commission
optionD: Listing on London Stock Exchange
answerText: Delivery of a copy of the prospectus to the RoC signed by all directors or their authorized agents
explanation: Section 389 requires that no prospectus shall be issued unless a copy thereof has been delivered to the Registrar, signed by every director or his agent authorized in writing.

subject: Law
prompt: If Alpha Corp issues a defective prospectus in India, what liability do persons authorizing the issue face?
optionA: Only contractual liability in the UK
optionB: Criminal liability for misstatement in prospectus under Section 447 and general penal provisions
optionC: No liability in India
optionD: Civil damages limited to ₹10,000
answerText: Criminal liability for misstatement in prospectus under Section 447 and general penal provisions
explanation: Section 390 makes provisions relating to prospectus applicable to foreign companies, and misstatements or omissions attract penal consequences including criminal liability under Section 447 and general penalty provisions.

subject: Law
prompt: Must the prospectus issued by Alpha Corp specify the date and incorporate details of material contracts?
optionA: No, foreign prospectuses are exempt from material contract disclosures
optionB: Yes, Section 390/391 mandates disclosures similar to domestic prospectuses including material contracts and consents
optionC: Only if shares exceed 50% of capital
optionD: Only at the discretion of the UK directors
answerText: Yes, Section 390/391 mandates disclosures similar to domestic prospectuses including material contracts and consents
explanation: Sections 390 and 391 prescribe detailed disclosures to be contained in a foreign company's prospectus, including particulars of contracts, time and place of inspection, and expert consents.

subject: Law
prompt: Under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, what is the minimum number of designated partners required to be individuals for a valid LLP incorporation?
optionA: At least one
optionB: At least two
optionC: At least three
optionD: At least four
answerText: At least two
explanation: Section 7 of the LLP Act, 2008 mandates that every LLP must have at least two designated partners who are individuals, and at least one of them must be a resident in India. Therefore, the minimum number of designated partners is two.

subject: Law
prompt: Which of the following bodies corporate is specifically competent to be a partner in a Limited Liability Partnership as per the LLP Act, 2008?
optionA: A Hindu Undivided Family (HUF)
optionB: A Foreign Limited Liability Partnership
optionC: A sole proprietorship firm
optionD: An unregistered association of persons
answerText: A Foreign Limited Liability Partnership
explanation: Section 2(1)(d) defines a body corporate to include a company, an LLP, a limited liability partnership incorporated outside India, but excludes a corporation not incorporated under any law and any other entity notified by the Central Government. A foreign LLP is a body corporate and can be a partner.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the consequence if the number of partners in an LLP is reduced below two for a continuous period of more than six months?
optionA: The LLP is automatically dissolved
optionB: The remaining partner becomes personally liable for all liabilities of the LLP incurred during that period
optionC: The Registrar of Companies converts the LLP into a partnership firm
optionD: The LLP is penalized with a fine up to Rs. 10,000 only
answerText: The remaining partner becomes personally liable for all liabilities of the LLP incurred during that period
explanation: Under Section 6 of the LLP Act, 2008, if at any time the number of partners of an LLP is reduced below two and the LLP carries on business for more than six months while the number is so reduced, the person, who is the only partner of the LLP during the time that it so carries on business after those six months, is liable personally for the obligations of the LLP incurred during that period.
conceptTags: Minimum Partners | Personal Liability | Continuation of Business

subject: Law
prompt: Within how many days of incorporation must the Limited Liability Partnership Agreement be filed with the Registrar in Form 3?
optionA: 15 days
optionB: 30 days
optionC: 60 days
optionD: 90 days
answerText: 30 days
explanation: As per Section 23(2) read with Rule 21 of the LLP Rules, 2009, information concerning the LLP agreement signed at the time of incorporation, or any changes made therein, must be filed with the Registrar in Form 3 within 30 days of incorporation or change.

subject: Law
prompt: Can a minor be admitted as a partner or designated partner in a Limited Liability Partnership under the LLP Act, 2008?
optionA: Yes, as both a partner and a designated partner
optionB: Yes, as a partner only with the consent of all partners
optionC: No, a minor cannot be admitted as a partner or designated partner, nor can they hold any beneficial interest in the LLP
optionD: Yes, through a natural guardian
answerText: No, a minor cannot be admitted as a partner or designated partner, nor can they hold any beneficial interest in the LLP
explanation: Under the LLP Act, 2008, individuals eligible to be partners must have contractual capacity. A minor lacks capacity to contract, and unlike partnership law under the Partnership Act, 1932, a minor cannot be admitted to the benefits of an LLP nor become a partner or designated partner.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the primary document required for incorporating a Limited Liability Partnership, which incorporates the application for reservation of name, incorporation, and allotment of DIN?
optionA: Form FiLLiP (Form for incorporation of Limited Liability Partnership)
optionB: Form INC-32 (SPICe)
optionC: Form LLP-1
optionD: Form RUN-LLP
answerText: Form FiLLiP (Form for incorporation of Limited Liability Partnership)
explanation: Rule 16 of the LLP Rules, 2009 prescribes Form FiLLiP (Form for incorporation of Limited Liability Partnership) for incorporating an LLP, replacing the earlier separate name reservation and incorporation steps.

subject: Law
prompt: Under the LLP Act, 2008, what is the extent of liability of a partner for the wrongful act or omission of another partner?
optionA: Joint and several liability for all debts of the LLP
optionB: Unlimited personal liability for acts of all partners
optionC: No personal liability, except for their own wrongful act or omission
optionD: Liability limited to their unpaid capital contribution only
answerText: No personal liability, except for their own wrongful act or omission
explanation: Section 28(2) of the LLP Act states that an LLP is not bound by anything done by a partner in dealing with a person if the partner has no authority to act for the LLP and the person knows that. Furthermore, a partner is not personally liable, directly or indirectly, for an obligation solely by reason of being a partner of the LLP, protecting them from another partner's wrongful acts unless they participated in it.
conceptTags: Extent of Liability | Wrongful Acts | Partnership Authority

subject: Law
prompt: What constitutes a 'resident in India' for the purpose of being a designated partner under Section 7 of the LLP Act, 2008?
optionA: A person who has stayed in India for not less than 120 days during the financial year
optionB: A person who has stayed in India for not less than 182 days during the immediately preceding one financial year
optionC: An Indian citizen regardless of their residential status
optionD: Any person holding an Indian passport
answerText: A person who has stayed in India for not less than 182 days during the immediately preceding one financial year
explanation: Section 7(1) explanation specifies that for the purposes of this section, 'resident in India' means a person who has stayed in India for a period of not less than 182 days during the immediately preceding one financial year.
conceptTags: Designated Partner | Resident in India | Definition

subject: Law
prompt: In the absence of an agreement between the partners regarding mutual rights and duties, what shall govern the relationship of the partners and the LLP?
optionA: The Indian Partnership Act, 1932 provisions
optionB: The Companies Act, 2013 schedules
optionC: First Schedule to the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008
optionD: Rules framed by the Central Government on a case-by-case basis
answerText: First Schedule to the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008
explanation: Section 23(4) of the LLP Act, 2008 provides that in the absence of agreement as to any matter, the mutual rights and duties of the partners and the mutual rights and duties of the LLP and its partners shall be determined by the provisions relating to that matter as are set out in the First Schedule.
conceptTags: LLP Agreement | First Schedule | Default Rules

subject: Law
prompt: Which authority is empowered to order the investigation of the affairs of an LLP under the LLP Act, 2008?
optionA: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
optionB: The Central Government
optionC: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
optionD: The Registrar of Companies directly without government approval
answerText: The Central Government
explanation: Section 43 of the LLP Act, 2008 empowers the Central Government to appoint one or more competent inspectors to investigate the affairs of an LLP and to report thereon in such manner as it may direct.
conceptTags: Investigation | Central Government | Affairs of LLP

subject: Law
prompt: What is the maximum number of partners permitted in a Limited Liability Partnership under the LLP Act, 2008?
optionA: 50 partners
optionB: 100 partners
optionC: 200 partners
optionD: No upper limit
answerText: No upper limit
explanation: Unlike companies or traditional partnerships, the LLP Act, 2008 does not prescribe any upper limit on the maximum number of partners that an LLP can have.

subject: Law
prompt: When can an LLP be wound up voluntarily by its partners?
optionA: At any time by a simple majority of partners
optionB: Only when the Tribunal passes an order
optionC: In accordance with the LLP agreement or by passing a resolution to wind up voluntarily
optionD: Voluntary winding up of an LLP is not permitted under the law
answerText: In accordance with the LLP agreement or by passing a resolution to wind up voluntarily
explanation: Section 63 of the LLP Act, 2008 provides that an LLP may be wound up voluntarily if the LLP passes a resolution to wind up voluntarily and the partners have agreed in the LLP agreement or by a separate resolution.
conceptTags: Winding Up | Voluntary Winding Up | Resolution

subject: Law
prompt: What is the penalty for carrying on business with an intent to defraud creditors or any other fraudulent purpose under Section 30 of the LLP Act?
optionA: Imprisonment up to 1 year and fine up to Rs. 50,000
optionB: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to 5 years and fine which shall not be less than Rs. 50,000 but may extend to Rs. 5 lakhs
optionC: Fine only up to Rs. 1 lakh
optionD: Automatic disqualification of all partners without fine
answerText: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to 5 years and fine which shall not be less than Rs. 50,000 but may extend to Rs. 5 lakhs
explanation: Section 30 deals with fraudulent trading. If an LLP or any of its partners carries on business with intent to defraud creditors or for any fraudulent purpose, every partner who was knowingly a party to it shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term up to 5 years and a fine of Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 5 lakhs.

subject: Law
prompt: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the name of a Limited Liability Partnership?
optionA: The name must end with the words 'Limited Liability Partnership' or the acronym 'LLP'.
optionB: The name can be identical to an existing company without any restriction.
optionC: The name cannot contain any geographical identifier.
optionD: The word 'LLP' is optional for service-oriented LLPs.
answerText: The name must end with the words 'Limited Liability Partnership' or the acronym 'LLP'.
explanation: Section 15(1) of the LLP Act, 2008 mandates that every limited liability partnership shall have either the words 'limited liability partnership' or the acronym 'LLP' as the last words of its name.

subject: Law
prompt: Under Section 34 of the LLP Act, 2008, every LLP is required to maintain books of account which must be preserved for how many years from the date on which they are prepared?
optionA: 3 years
optionB: 5 years
optionC: 8 years
optionD: 10 years
answerText: 8 years
explanation: Rule 24 of the LLP Rules, 2009 read with Section 34 mandates that the books of account of an LLP shall be maintained on cash or accrual basis and according to double entry system of accounting, and shall be preserved for eight years from the date on which they are prepared.

subject: Law
prompt: Can a corporate body act as a 'designated partner' in a Limited Liability Partnership?
optionA: Yes, any body corporate can be a designated partner directly.
optionB: No, only individuals can be designated partners.
optionC: Yes, provided its net worth exceeds Rs. 5 crores.
optionD: Yes, through its nominee who must be an individual.
answerText: Yes, through its nominee who must be an individual.
explanation: Section 7(1) states that designated partners must be individuals. If a body corporate is a partner, it may nominate an individual to act as a designated partner through its resolution.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the consequence of registering an LLP under a name which is identical with or too nearly resembles that of an existing partnership firm or LLP?
optionA: The Central Government can direct the LLP to change its name within a specified period.
optionB: The registration is void ab initio.
optionC: The partners face immediate imprisonment.
optionD: The Registrar automatically liquidates the LLP.
answerText: The Central Government can direct the LLP to change its name within a specified period.
explanation: Section 17 empowers the Central Government to direct an LLP to change its name if it is identical with or too nearly resembles that of any other partnership firm, LLP, or body corporate, or trademark registered under the Trade Marks Act, 1999.
conceptTags: Name Change | Central Government Direction | Trademarks

subject: Law
prompt: Which statement best describes the concept of 'Limited Liability' in an LLP?
optionA: Partners have no liability whatsoever for any business debts.
optionB: The liability of the partners is limited to their agreed contribution to the LLP.
optionC: The liability of the LLP is limited, but partners have unlimited personal liability.
optionD: Liability is limited only in the event of winding up.
answerText: The liability of the partners is limited to their agreed contribution to the LLP.
explanation: Section 28 and basic principles of LLP establish that partners are agents of the LLP but not of other partners, and their liability is limited to their agreed contribution to the LLP as specified in the LLP agreement.

subject: Law
prompt: Within what period must an LLP file its Annual Return (Form 11) with the Registrar from the close of its financial year?
optionA: Within 30 days
optionB: Within 60 days
optionC: Within 90 days
optionD: Within 6 months
answerText: Within 60 days
explanation: Section 35(1) of the LLP Act, 2008 read with Rule 25 requires every LLP to file an annual return with the Registrar in Form 11 within 60 days of closure of its financial year.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the consequence if an LLP fails to file its Statement of Account and Solvency (Form 8) within the prescribed time?
optionA: The LLP and every designated partner shall be punishable with a fine of Rs. 100 for every day during which the failure continues, subject to a maximum penalty.
optionB: The LLP is automatically struck off by the Registrar without notice.
optionC: The partners face compulsory imprisonment for 6 months.
optionD: All business bank accounts are permanently frozen.
answerText: The LLP and every designated partner shall be punishable with a fine of Rs. 100 for every day during which the failure continues, subject to a maximum penalty.
explanation: Section 34(5) specifies that if any LLP fails to comply with the provisions of filing the Statement of Account and Solvency, the LLP and every designated partner of the LLP shall be punishable with a fine of Rs. 100 for each day during which the failure continues, subject to statutory limits.

subject: Law
prompt: Can an existing partnership firm convert into a Limited Liability Partnership under the LLP Act, 2008?
optionA: No, conversion is not permitted under the law.
optionB: Yes, provided all partners of the partnership firm agree and the procedure in the Second Schedule is followed.
optionC: Yes, only with the prior approval of the Supreme Court.
optionD: Yes, but only if the partnership firm was registered under the Companies Act.
answerText: Yes, provided all partners of the partnership firm agree and the procedure in the Second Schedule is followed.
explanation: Section 55 read with the Second Schedule of the LLP Act, 2008 permits the conversion of a firm into an LLP by fulfilling specified criteria and filing the necessary application with the Registrar.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the status of an LLP after its incorporation certificate is issued?
optionA: It becomes a body corporate capable of suing and being sued in its own name, having perpetual succession.
optionB: It remains a partnership until the LLP agreement is registered.
optionC: It is a trust subject to the Indian Trusts Act.
optionD: It requires separate registration as a commercial enterprise with local authorities to gain corporate status.
answerText: It becomes a body corporate capable of suing and being sued in its own name, having perpetual succession.
explanation: Section 3 of the LLP Act, 2008 provides that an LLP is a body corporate formed and incorporated under this Act and is a legal entity separate from its partners, having perpetual succession.
conceptTags: Body Corporate | Perpetual Succession | Legal Entity

subject: Law
prompt: In the case of a whistleblowing provision under Section 31 of the LLP Act, the Tribunal may reduce or waive the penalty against a partner or employee if they:
optionA: Resign from the LLP immediately.
optionB: Provide useful information during investigation or proceedings leading to conviction or penalty under the Act.
optionC: Pay double the penalty amount voluntarily.
optionD: Transfer their share to a third party.
answerText: Provide useful information during investigation or proceedings leading to conviction or penalty under the Act.
explanation: Section 31 provides for relief to partners/employees in certain cases. The Tribunal or Central Government may reduce or waive any penalty against any partner or employee of an LLP if he has given information leading to a conviction or penalty under the Act.

subject: Law
prompt: Which statement is correct regarding the contribution of partners in a Limited Liability Partnership?
optionA: Contribution can consist of tangible, intangible property, or other benefits to the LLP.
optionB: Contribution must be strictly in cash deposited in a nationalized bank.
optionC: Contribution can only be in the form of immovable property.
optionD: Partners are not required to make any contribution whatsoever under any circumstance.
answerText: Contribution can consist of tangible, intangible property, or other benefits to the LLP.
explanation: Section 32 states that the contribution of a partner may consist of tangible, movable or immovable or intangible property or other benefit to the LLP, including money, promissory notes, other agreements to contribute cash or property, and contracts for services performed or to be performed.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the timeline for filing a notice of any change in the partners of an LLP with the Registrar after such change takes place?
optionA: 15 days
optionB: 30 days
optionC: 60 days
optionD: 90 days
answerText: 30 days
explanation: Section 25(1) requires an LLP to ensure that a notice of any change in its partners (with details and consent) is filed with the Registrar within 30 days of such change.
conceptTags: Change in Partners | Filing Notice | Section 25

subject: Law
prompt: Who is responsible for signing and verifying the Statement of Account and Solvency of an LLP?
optionA: Any employee designated by the accountant
optionB: All partners of the LLP unconditionally
optionC: The designated partners of the LLP
optionD: The Registrar of Companies
answerText: The designated partners of the LLP
explanation: Section 34(3) stipulates that the Statement of Account and Solvency shall be signed on behalf of the LLP by the designated partners of the LLP.
conceptTags: Statement of Account | Signing | Designated Partners

subject: Law
prompt: When can the Central Government order the winding up of an LLP by the Tribunal?
optionA: If the LLP acts against the sovereignty and integrity of India or security of the State.
optionB: If the LLP fails to make a profit for two consecutive financial years.
optionC: If any partner resigns without giving notice.
optionD: If the LLP changes its registered office from one state to another.
answerText: If the LLP acts against the sovereignty and integrity of India or security of the State.
explanation: Section 64 sets out grounds for winding up by the Tribunal, which includes if the LLP has acted against the interests of the sovereignty and integrity of India, the security of the State, or public order.
conceptTags: Winding Up by Tribunal | Grounds | Sovereignty

subject: Law
prompt: Which of the following documents forms the constitutional basis for internal governance and management of a Limited Liability Partnership?
optionA: Memorandum of Association
optionB: Articles of Association
optionC: Limited Liability Partnership Agreement
optionD: Partnership Deed under the Partnership Act
answerText: Limited Liability Partnership Agreement
explanation: Section 2(1)(o) and Section 23 define the LLP Agreement as any written agreement between the partners of the LLP or between the LLP and its partners which determines the mutual rights and duties of the partners and their rights and duties in relation to that LLP.

subject: Law
prompt: What is the legal effect of registering a charge created by an LLP under Section 37 of the LLP Act?
optionA: It makes the charge holder the owner of the LLP's assets.
optionB: It provides constructive notice of the charge to any person acquiring an interest in the property or asset charged.
optionC: It guarantees repayment of the loan by the Central Government.
optionD: It is only an internal record with no legal consequences.
answerText: It guarantees repayment of the loan by the Central Government.
explanation: Registration of charges under the LLP Act operates as constructive notice to third parties who deal with the LLP's assets, ensuring transparency and priority of claims.
conceptTags: Registration of Charges | Constructive Notice | Section 37

subject: Law
prompt: Under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, can an individual cease to be a partner of an LLP by giving notice in writing?
optionA: No, cessation requires unanimous court order.
optionB: Yes, in accordance with the LLP agreement, or by giving 30 days notice to the other partners in the absence of agreement.
optionC: Yes, instantly without any notice condition.
optionD: No, partners are locked in for the entire life of the LLP.
answerText: Yes, in accordance with the LLP agreement, or by giving 30 days notice to the other partners in the absence of agreement.
explanation: Section 24(1) provides that a person may cease to be a partner in accordance with the agreement or, in the absence of agreement, by giving 30 days' notice to the other partners of their intention to resign.

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Advisory LLP was incorporated in Mumbai with three partners: Alpha Corp (a body corporate incorporated in Singapore), Mr. Rohan (an Indian resident), and Ms. Priya (who stays in London and visits India for only 30 days in a financial year). Due to a business dispute, Alpha Corp decides to withdraw its nominee designated partner without appointing a replacement, and Ms. Priya refuses to act as a designated partner. The LLP agreement is silent on the mechanism of appointing designated partners.

subject: Law
prompt: Considering the residency requirement under Section 7, which of the partners in Zenith Advisory LLP is qualified to act as a 'resident in India' designated partner?
optionA: Alpha Corp
optionB: Mr. Rohan
optionC: Ms. Priya
optionD: None of them
answerText: Mr. Rohan
explanation: Section 7 requires at least one designated partner to be resident in India (stay in India for not less than 182 days in the preceding financial year). Mr. Rohan is an Indian resident, whereas Ms. Priya stayed for only 30 days, failing the test.

subject: Law
prompt: If Alpha Corp withdraws its nominee and no replacement is appointed, what is the minimum number of designated partners Zenith Advisory LLP must maintain under the Act?
optionA: At least one
optionB: At least two
optionC: At least three
optionD: No minimum is required if total partners are above two
answerText: At least two
explanation: Section 7 mandates that every LLP must have at least two designated partners who are individuals. If the number falls below two, the LLP is in default.

subject: Law
prompt: Can Ms. Priya, being a partner who stays abroad for most of the year, be appointed as a designated partner of Zenith Advisory LLP?
optionA: Yes, provided she holds an Indian PAN card
optionB: Yes, as an ordinary designated partner, but she cannot fulfill the resident-in-India requirement
optionC: No, individuals who are non-residents can never be designated partners under any circumstance
optionD: Yes, if Alpha Corp guarantees her residency
answerText: Yes, as an ordinary designated partner, but she cannot fulfill the resident-in-India requirement
explanation: An individual who is a non-resident can be a designated partner, but they will not satisfy the specific requirement that at least one designated partner must be resident in India.

subject: Law
prompt: If the LLP fails to maintain the minimum required designated partners for more than 6 months, who faces penal consequences under the LLP Act?
optionA: Only Alpha Corp as the foreign body corporate
optionB: The LLP and every partner/defaulting officer of the LLP
optionC: Only the Registrar of Companies
optionD: No penalty applies if the total partners exceed two
answerText: The LLP and every partner/defaulting officer of the LLP
explanation: Section 7 and associated penalty provisions state that if an LLP contravenes the provisions relating to designated partners, the LLP and every designated partner/partner in default are punishable with a fine.

subject: Law
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: A partnership firm named 'M/s Quick Logistics', consisting of three partners (A, B, and C), decided to convert into a Limited Liability Partnership under the name 'Quick Logistics LLP' following the Second Schedule of the LLP Act, 2008. At the time of conversion, the firm had outstanding unsecured loans from various creditors.
