explanation: Just like any newly set-up business or newly incorporated entity, the first previous year for a company starts from the date of its incorporation (10th February) and ends on 31st March of that same financial year.
conceptTags: Previous Year | Newly Incorporated Company | Section 3

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the primary objective of levying surcharge under the Income-tax Act?
optionA: To raise additional revenue from high-income earners (progressive taxation)
optionB: To fund local municipal corporations
optionC: To penalize tax evaders
optionD: To replace the corporate tax structure
answerText: To raise additional revenue from high-income earners (progressive taxation)
explanation: Surcharge is an additional levy on higher income brackets, embodying the principle of progressive taxation where those with higher financial capacity contribute a higher effective tax percentage.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under Section 2(7), 'Assassessee' means any person by whom any tax or other sum of money is payable under the Act. Which of the following is ALSO included in the definition of assessee?
optionA: A person in respect of whom proceedings under the Act have been taken for the assessment of his income
optionB: A salaried employee whose employer deducts TDS correctly with no pending liability
optionC: A foreign tourist visiting India for 5 days with zero Indian income
optionD: A retail buyer purchasing goods subject to GST
answerText: A person in respect of whom proceedings under the Act have been taken for the assessment of his income
explanation: An assessee includes any person by whom any tax, interest, or penalty is payable, as well as every person in respect of whom any proceeding under the Act has been taken for the assessment of his income, loss, or refund.
conceptTags: Definition of Assassessee | Section 2(7) | Basic Concepts

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following constitutional provisions empowers the Parliament of India to make laws in respect of taxes on income other than agricultural income?
optionA: Article 246, Seventh Schedule, Union List, Entry 82
optionB: Article 270, State List, Entry 46
optionC: Article 265, Concurrent List, Entry 12
optionD: Article 300A
answerText: Article 246, Seventh Schedule, Union List, Entry 82
explanation: Entry 82 of the Union List (List I) in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India empowers Parliament to legislate on taxes on income other than agricultural income. Entry 46 of the State List covers agricultural income taxes.
conceptTags: Constitutional Validity | Union List Entry 82 | Taxing Power

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Raghav, a resident Indian aged 42, sets up a new retail garment business on 1st August 2025. During the financial year 2025-26, he earns income under various heads including business income, capital gains, and bank interest. He is evaluating whether to opt out of the default tax regime under Section 115BAC.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What will be the duration of the first previous year for Mr. Raghav's newly set-up retail garment business?
optionA: 1st April 2025 to 31st March 2026
optionB: 1st August 2025 to 31st March 2026
optionC: 1st August 2025 to 31st July 2026
optionD: 1st April 2025 to 31st July 2025
answerText: 1st August 2025 to 31st March 2026
explanation: As per Section 3, for a newly set-up business, the first previous year commences on the date of setting up of the business (1st August 2025) and ends on the last day of the financial year (31st March 2026).
conceptTags: Previous Year | Newly Set-up Business | Section 3

subject: Taxation
prompt: In which assessment year will the income earned by Mr. Raghav during the financial year 2025-26 normally be assessed to tax?
optionD: At the option of Mr. Raghav
explanation: Under the general rule of Section 4, income of a previous year (FY 2025-26) is assessed to tax in the immediately following assessment year, which is AY 2026-27.
conceptTags: Assessment Year | Previous Year | Charging Section

subject: Taxation
prompt: If Mr. Raghav chooses to remain under the default tax regime of Section 115BAC for AY 2026-27, which of the following deductions will he generally NOT be permitted to claim?
optionA: Deduction under Section 80CCD(2) for employer's NPS contribution
optionB: Deduction under Section 80C for life insurance premium
optionC: Deduction under Section 80JJAA for new workmen
optionD: Standard deduction from salary (if applicable)
answerText: Deduction under Section 80C for life insurance premium
explanation: Under the default tax regime of Section 115BAC, general Chapter VI-A deductions such as Section 80C are disallowed, whereas Section 80CCD(2), 80JJAA, and standard deduction under Section 16(ia) are available.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under which head of income will Mr. Raghav's earnings from the retail garment business be computed?
optionA: Income from Salary
optionB: Income from House Property
optionC: Profits and gains of business or profession
optionD: Income from Other Sources
answerText: Profits and gains of business or profession
explanation: Income derived from running a retail garment business falls under the head 'Profits and gains of business or profession' (PGBP) pursuant to Section 28 of the Income-tax Act.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Apex Associates, a partnership firm, has total income of Rs. 1,02,00,000 for the financial year 2025-26. The firm comprises three resident partners who share profits equally. The firm is calculating its total tax liability including surcharge and cess.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the normal income-tax rate applicable to partnership firm M/s. Apex Associates under the Income-tax Act for AY 2026-27?
optionD: Maximum Marginal Rate
explanation: Partnership firms (including LLPs) are taxable at a flat rate of 30% on their total income under the normal provisions of the Income-tax Act.
conceptTags: Partnership Firm | Tax Rates | Flat Rate

subject: Taxation
prompt: Since the total income of M/s. Apex Associates exceeds Rs. 1 crore, what is the applicable surcharge rate?
explanation: For a partnership firm (domestic non-corporate entity), a surcharge of 12% is levied when total income exceeds Rs. 1 crore (and up to Rs. 10 crores).

subject: Taxation
prompt: How is Health and Education Cess calculated for M/s. Apex Associates?
optionA: 3% of basic tax
optionB: 4% of basic tax plus surcharge
optionC: 4% of total income
optionD: 1% of turnover
answerText: 4% of basic tax plus surcharge
explanation: Health and Education Cess is levied at 4% on the aggregate of income-tax and applicable surcharge for all categories of assessees.
conceptTags: Health and Education Cess | Tax Computation | Cess Rate

subject: Taxation
prompt: Are the shares of profits received by the individual partners from M/s. Apex Associates taxable in the hands of the partners?
optionA: Yes, fully taxable under PGBP
optionB: No, share of profit received from a firm is exempt under Section 10(2A) in the hands of the partners
optionC: Taxable only if total income of partner exceeds Rs. 10 lakhs
optionD: Taxable as capital gains
answerText: No, share of profit received from a firm is exempt under Section 10(2A) in the hands of the partners
explanation: Under Section 10(2A), the share of profit received by a partner from a firm is exempt from tax in the partner's hands, because the firm has already paid tax on its profits.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Dr. Meera, a resident individual aged 61, earns rental income from a commercial property, salary from a university, and agricultural income from her ancestral land in Kerala amounting to Rs. 4,50,000. Her non-agricultural total income for AY 2026-27 is Rs. 9,50,000.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under which head of income is the rental income from Dr. Meera's commercial property taxable?
optionA: Income from Salary
optionB: Income from House Property
optionC: Profits and gains of business or profession
optionD: Income from Other Sources
answerText: Income from House Property
explanation: Rental income from property (whether residential or commercial) owned by the assessee is taxable under the head 'Income from House Property' under Section 22.
conceptTags: House Property | Section 22 | Heads of Income

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the tax treatment of Dr. Meera's agricultural income of Rs. 4,50,000 under Section 10(1)?
optionA: Fully taxable under Income from Other Sources
optionB: Exempt under Section 10(1), but subject to partial integration for rate purposes
optionC: Fully taxable at slab rates
optionD: Exempt and completely ignored for all tax computations
answerText: Exempt under Section 10(1), but subject to partial integration for rate purposes
explanation: Agricultural income in India is exempt under Section 10(1). However, since her non-agricultural income exceeds the basic exemption limit and agricultural income exceeds Rs. 5,000, it is subject to partial integration for determining the tax rate on non-agricultural income.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the basic exemption limit applicable to Dr. Meera (aged 61) under the normal provisions (old tax regime) for AY 2026-27?
explanation: Under the normal provisions (old tax regime), for a resident senior citizen (aged 60 years or more but less than 80 years), the basic exemption limit is Rs. 3,00,000.
conceptTags: Senior Citizen | Exemption Limit | Old Tax Regime

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can Dr. Meera claim standard deduction against her salary income under the old tax regime?
optionA: No, standard deduction is only for corporate employees
optionB: Yes, standard deduction under Section 16(ia) is available to salaried assessees
optionC: Yes, but only up to Rs. 10,000
optionD: Only if she opts out of Section 115BAC
answerText: Yes, standard deduction under Section 16(ia) is available to salaried assessees
explanation: Standard deduction under Section 16(ia) is available to salaried taxpayers under both the old tax regime and the default tax regime.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Vikram, a resident individual, leaves India on 15th December 2025 for permanent employment abroad with no intention of returning to India in the foreseeable future. He earned substantial capital gains and other income prior to his departure during the financial year 2025-26.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which specific provision empowers the Assessing Officer to assess Mr. Vikram's income for the period up to 15th December 2025 in the same assessment year?
optionA: Section 174
optionB: Section 175
optionC: Section 176
optionD: Section 4
answerText: Section 174
explanation: Section 174 deals with assessment of income of a person leaving India, empowering the Assessing Officer to assess the total income of such person up to the date of departure in the same assessment year.
conceptTags: Section 174 | Leaving India | Assessment in PY

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the assessment year for the income assessed under Section 174 in Mr. Vikram's case for the period up to his departure?
optionD: Assessment year is not applicable
explanation: Under Section 174, income of a person leaving India permanently is assessed in the same previous year/assessment year in which they leave (i.e., AY 2025-26, since departure is in FY 2025-26).
conceptTags: Assessment Year | Section 174 | Exceptions to PY Rule

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is required from Mr. Vikram before he leaves India in terms of tax clearance?
optionA: He must obtain a tax clearance certificate under Section 230 where applicable
optionB: He must pay advance tax for the next 5 years in advance
optionC: He must surrender his PAN card permanently
optionD: No formalities are required if he is leaving for employment
answerText: He must obtain a tax clearance certificate under Section 230 where applicable
explanation: Persons leaving India in certain circumstances (such as financial liabilities or specific categories) are required to obtain a tax clearance certificate under Section 230 before boarding transport from India.
conceptTags: Tax Clearance Certificate | Section 230 | Leaving India

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under the definition of 'Person' in Section 2(31), Mr. Vikram is classified as:
optionA: Artificial juridical person
optionB: Individual
optionC: Association of Persons
optionD: Non-resident entity
answerText: Individual
explanation: Mr. Vikram, being a human being, is classified as an 'Individual' under Section 2(31)(i) of the Income-tax Act.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: XYZ Ltd., a domestic company, has a total taxable income of Rs. 10,20,00,000 for the financial year 2025-26. The company is evaluating its tax liabilities under the normal provisions and checking the applicability of surcharge thresholds.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the base corporate tax rate for a domestic company under the normal provisions (assuming turnover conditions do not qualify it for 25%)?
explanation: Under the normal provisions of the Income-tax Act, domestic companies are generally taxable at 30% (unless specific turnover or concessional rates like Section 115BAA/115BAB apply).
conceptTags: Domestic Company | Corporate Tax Rate | Normal Provisions

subject: Taxation
prompt: Since XYZ Ltd.'s total income exceeds Rs. 10 crore, what is the applicable surcharge rate?
optionD: 7% or 12% depending on section opted
explanation: For a domestic company, when total income exceeds Rs. 10 crores under normal provisions, the applicable surcharge rate is 12% (if total income is between Rs. 1 crore and Rs. 10 crores, it is 7%; exceeding Rs. 10 crores, it is 12%).

subject: Taxation
prompt: Is marginal relief available to XYZ Ltd. when its total income exceeds Rs. 10 crores?
optionA: No marginal relief is ever available to companies
optionB: Yes, marginal relief ensures that additional tax due to surcharge does not exceed income above Rs. 10 crores
optionC: Marginal relief is only available to individuals and HUFs
optionD: Marginal relief applies automatically without any computation
answerText: Yes, marginal relief ensures that additional tax due to surcharge does not exceed income above Rs. 10 crores
explanation: Marginal relief is available to companies as well when total income exceeds threshold limits (like Rs. 10 crores), ensuring the incremental tax and surcharge liability does not exceed the incremental income over the threshold.
conceptTags: Marginal Relief | Company Surcharge | Tax Computation

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which statutory authority enacted the rates of income-tax and surcharge for XYZ Ltd. for AY 2026-27?
optionA: Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) via notification
optionB: The Finance Act passed by Parliament
optionC: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
optionD: Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA)
answerText: The Finance Act passed by Parliament
explanation: The rates of income-tax, surcharge, and cess for any assessment year are enacted annually by the Finance Act passed by Parliament.
conceptTags: Finance Act | Tax Rates | Basic Concepts

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under section 6(1), an individual is a resident in India during the previous year if he satisfies the basic condition of being in India for a period of ___ days or more in that previous year.
explanation: According to section 6(1)(a), an individual is resident in India if he is in India for a period of 182 days or more during the relevant previous year. This is the primary basic condition applicable to all individuals.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following individuals can substitute the 60-day period with a 182-day period under section 6(1)?
optionA: An Indian citizen who leaves India during the previous year for the purpose of employment outside India
optionB: An Indian citizen engaged in a managerial position in a foreign company
optionC: A foreign citizen of non-Indian origin visiting India on a holiday
optionD: A person of Indian origin residing in the UK visiting India for a short vacation
answerText: An Indian citizen who leaves India during the previous year for the purpose of employment outside India
explanation: Section 6(1) provides an exception where the 60-day threshold is replaced by 182 days for an Indian citizen who leaves India during the previous year for the purpose of employment outside India, or as a member of the crew of an Indian ship.
conceptTags: Residential Status | Exceptions to 60 days | Employment Abroad

subject: Taxation
prompt: For a citizen of India or a person of Indian origin who, being outside India, comes on a visit to India during the previous year, the 60-day period is substituted by ___ days, provided his total income (other than income from foreign sources) does not exceed Rs. 15 lakhs.
explanation: As per the proviso to section 6(1)(c), for an Indian citizen or person of Indian origin visiting India whose total income (other than income from foreign sources) does not exceed Rs. 15 lakhs, the period of 60 days is substituted by 120 days.
conceptTags: PIO | Indian Citizen | Visit to India | 120 days rule

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the threshold limit of total income (other than income from foreign sources) under Explanation 1(b) to section 6(1) for an Indian citizen or person of Indian origin visiting India, above which the 60-day period is substituted by 182 days instead of 120 days?
optionA: Rs. 10 lakhs
optionB: Rs. 15 lakhs
optionC: Rs. 50 lakhs
optionD: Rs. 1 crore
answerText: Rs. 15 lakhs
explanation: If the total income (other than income from foreign sources) of an Indian citizen or person of Indian origin visiting India exceeds Rs. 15 lakhs during the previous year, the 60-day period is substituted by 182 days.
conceptTags: PIO | Indian Citizen | Visit to India | Income Threshold

subject: Taxation
prompt: An Indian citizen having total income (other than income from foreign sources) of Rs. 18 lakhs comes on a visit to India during the previous year 2025-26 and stays for 150 days. His residential status for AY 2026-27 is:
optionA: Resident and Ordinarily Resident
optionB: Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident
optionC: Non-Resident
optionD: Deemed Resident
answerText: Non-Resident
explanation: Since his total income (excluding foreign sources) exceeds Rs. 15 lakhs, the exception rule for visiting India does not apply the 120-day threshold; instead, the 182-day rule applies. Since his stay is 150 days (less than 182 days), he fails the basic conditions and is a Non-Resident.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is a 'deemed resident' under section 6(1A)?
optionA: An individual who is a citizen of India, having total income (other than foreign sources) exceeding Rs. 15 lakhs, and who is not liable to tax in any other country or territory by reason of his domicile or residence.
optionB: Any foreign citizen who stays in India for 182 days or more.
optionC: An Indian citizen who resides abroad for more than 182 days.
optionD: A company incorporated in India with foreign management.
answerText: An individual who is a citizen of India, having total income (other than foreign sources) exceeding Rs. 15 lakhs, and who is not liable to tax in any other country or territory by reason of his domicile or residence.
explanation: Section 6(1A) states that an individual being a citizen of India, having total income (other than income from foreign sources) exceeding Rs. 15 lakhs during the previous year, shall be deemed to be resident in India in that previous year, if he is not liable to tax in any other country or territory by reason of his domicile or residence or any other criteria of similar nature.

subject: Taxation
prompt: An individual who is deemed to be resident in India under section 6(1A) is always classified for that previous year as:
optionA: Resident and Ordinarily Resident (ROR)
optionB: Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR)
optionC: Non-Resident (NR)
optionD: Either ROR or RNOR depending on past history
answerText: Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR)
explanation: As per the proviso to section 6(6), an individual who is deemed to be resident in India under section 6(1A) shall be treated as Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR) in India.

subject: Taxation
prompt: To be classified as 'Resident and Ordinarily Resident' (ROR) in India, an individual must satisfy:
optionA: Only any one of the basic conditions under section 6(1)
optionB: Both the additional conditions under section 6(6) in addition to satisfying at least one basic condition
optionC: Only the additional conditions without satisfying any basic condition
optionD: Both basic conditions and all four additional conditions
answerText: Both the additional conditions under section 6(6) in addition to satisfying at least one basic condition
explanation: An individual is Resident and Ordinarily Resident (ROR) if he is a resident under section 6(1) and also satisfies both the additional conditions specified under section 6(6) (i.e., resident in 2 out of 10 preceding previous years and stay of 730 days or more in 7 preceding previous years).

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following is NOT an additional condition under section 6(6) for determining whether an individual is Ordinarily Resident?
optionA: Resident in India in at least 2 out of 10 previous years preceding the relevant previous year
optionB: Present in India for 730 days or more during the 7 previous years preceding the relevant previous year
optionC: Present in India for 365 days or more during the 4 previous years preceding the relevant previous year
optionD: He is not a deemed resident under section 6(1A)
answerText: Present in India for 365 days or more during the 4 previous years preceding the relevant previous year
explanation: Option C mentions '365 days or more during 4 previous years', whereas the actual requirement under section 6(6)(a) is 730 days or more during the 7 preceding previous years. Thus, option C is incorrect and represents a distractor.

subject: Taxation
prompt: An individual is a Hindu Undivided Family (HUF). When is the HUF considered a 'Resident' in India?
optionA: If the Karta is an Indian citizen
optionB: If the control and management of its affairs is situated wholly or partly in India
optionC: If all the coparceners reside in India for at least 182 days
optionD: If its turnover exceeds Rs. 50 crores in India
answerText: If the control and management of its affairs is situated wholly or partly in India
explanation: Under section 6(2), an HUF is resident in India if the control and management of its affairs is situated wholly or partly in India during the previous year.
conceptTags: HUF | Residential Status | Control and Management

subject: Taxation
prompt: An HUF is considered 'Resident and Ordinarily Resident' (ROR) in India if its Karta or manager satisfies:
optionA: Both additional conditions under section 6(6)(b) (resident in 2 out of 10 years and 730+ days in 7 years)
optionB: Only the basic conditions under section 6(1)
optionC: The control and management is wholly in India
optionD: The family has been in existence for over 5 years
answerText: Both additional conditions under section 6(6)(b) (resident in 2 out of 10 years and 730+ days in 7 years)
explanation: An HUF is ROR in India if its Karta or manager satisfies both the additional conditions under section 6(6)(b), i.e., he has been resident in India in at least 2 out of 10 preceding previous years and has been present in India for 730 days or more during the 7 preceding previous years.

subject: Taxation
prompt: A company is said to be resident in India in any previous year if:
optionA: It is an Indian company, OR its Place of Effective Management (POEM) in that year is in India
optionB: It is registered under the Companies Act, 2013 only
optionC: Its entire shareholding is held by Indian residents
optionD: Its registered office is outside India but board meetings are held in India
answerText: It is an Indian company, OR its Place of Effective Management (POEM) in that year is in India
explanation: Under section 6(3), a company is resident in India if it is an Indian company, or if its Place of Effective Management (POEM) in that year is in India.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is meant by 'Place of Effective Management' (POEM) for a company?
optionA: The place where the annual general meeting is held
optionB: The place where key management and commercial decisions that are necessary for the conduct of business of an entity as a whole are, in substance made
optionC: The place where the statutory audit is conducted
optionD: The place where the company's manufacturing plant is located
answerText: The place where key management and commercial decisions that are necessary for the conduct of business of an entity as a whole are, in substance made
explanation: POEM is defined as a place where key management and commercial decisions that are necessary for the conduct of the business of an entity as a whole are in substance made.

subject: Taxation
prompt: A Firm, AOP, or BOI is resident in India if:
optionA: Control and management of its affairs is situated wholly or partly in India
optionB: Control and management is situated wholly outside India
optionC: All partners/members are resident in India
optionD: At least 50% of the profits arise in India
answerText: Control and management of its affairs is situated wholly or partly in India
explanation: Under section 6(2), a partnership firm, AOP, or BOI is resident in India if the control and management of its affairs is situated wholly or partly in India during the previous year. It is non-resident only if control and management is wholly outside India.
conceptTags: Firm | AOP | BOI | Control and Management

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following persons is always considered 'Non-Resident' in India, regardless of their management location?
optionA: Foreign Institutional Investor
optionB: Local Authority
optionC: None of the above (Every person other than an individual/HUF/Company can be resident if control is in India)
optionD: Foreign Company with POEM outside India
answerText: Foreign Company with POEM outside India
explanation: A foreign company whose POEM is outside India is always non-resident. For local authorities and artificial juridical persons, residency depends on whether control and management is situated wholly or partly in India.

subject: Taxation
prompt: For a 'Resident and Ordinarily Resident' (ROR) individual, the scope of total income under section 5(1) includes:
optionA: Income received or deemed to be received in India + Income accruing or arising or deemed to accrue or arise in India + Income accruing or arising outside India
optionB: Only income received in India
optionC: Only Indian income
optionD: Income received in India and income accruing in India from a business controlled from India
answerText: Income received or deemed to be received in India + Income accruing or arising or deemed to accrue or arise in India + Income accruing or arising outside India
explanation: The total income of an ROR includes all incomes from all sources, whether received, accruing, or arising inside or outside India, as per section 5(1).
conceptTags: Scope of Total Income | ROR | Section 5(1)

subject: Taxation
prompt: For a 'Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident' (RNOR) individual, which of the following incomes is taxable in India?
optionA: Income accruing or arising outside India from a business controlled from outside India
optionB: Income accruing or arising outside India from a business controlled from or set up in India
optionC: Only foreign income remitted to India
optionD: Income from any source outside India
answerText: Income accruing or arising outside India from a business controlled from or set up in India
explanation: Under section 5(1), for an RNOR, income accruing or arising outside India is taxable only if it is derived from a business controlled from or set up in India.
conceptTags: Scope of Total Income | RNOR | Section 5(1)

subject: Taxation
prompt: For a Non-Resident (NR) individual, the scope of total income under section 5(2) includes:
optionA: Only income received or deemed to be received in India AND income accruing or arising or deemed to accrue or arise in India
optionB: All global incomes
optionC: Income received in India plus foreign business income
optionD: Income remitted to India during the previous year
answerText: Only income received or deemed to be received in India AND income accruing or arising or deemed to accrue or arise in India
explanation: As per section 5(2), a Non-Resident is taxable in India only for Indian income—meaning income received/deemed received in India and income accruing/arising/deemed to accrue or arise in India.
conceptTags: Scope of Total Income | Non-Resident | Section 5(2)

subject: Taxation
prompt: Income earned and received outside India from a foreign business controlled from India is taxable in the hands of:
optionA: ROR only
optionB: ROR and RNOR
optionC: ROR, RNOR, and Non-Resident
optionD: None of the persons
answerText: ROR and RNOR
explanation: Foreign income from a business controlled from India is taxable for both ROR and RNOR, but NOT for a Non-Resident.
conceptTags: Scope of Total Income | RNOR | Business Controlled from India

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following incomes is deemed to accrue or arise in India under section 9?
optionA: Income from any business connection in India
optionB: Salary earned for service rendered outside India to an Indian citizen by a foreign employer
optionC: Dividend paid by a foreign company outside India to an Indian resident
optionD: Interest paid by a non-resident on a foreign currency loan utilized outside India
answerText: Income from any business connection in India
explanation: Under section 9(1)(i), all income accruing or arising, whether directly or indirectly, through or from any business connection in India, or through or from any property in India, is deemed to accrue or arise in India.
conceptTags: Deemed to Accrue or Arise | Section 9 | Business Connection

subject: Taxation
prompt: Salary payable by the Government of India to an Indian citizen for services rendered outside India is:
optionA: Exempt from tax
optionB: Deemed to accrue or arise in India
optionC: Taxable only if remitted to India
optionD: Taxable only if the citizen is ROR
answerText: Deemed to accrue or arise in India
explanation: Under section 9(1)(iii), salary payable by the Government to a citizen of India for services rendered outside India is deemed to accrue or arise in India. (Note: Allowances and perquisites are exempt under section 10(7)).

subject: Taxation
prompt: Dividend paid by an Indian company outside India is:
optionA: Deemed to accrue or arise in India under section 9(1)(iv)
optionB: Exempt under section 10(34)
optionC: Taxable only in the hands of Non-Residents
optionD: Exempt in all cases
answerText: Deemed to accrue or arise in India under section 9(1)(iv)
explanation: Under section 9(1)(iv), dividend paid by an Indian company outside India is deemed to accrue or arise in India and is taxable.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Interest paid by a non-resident is deemed to accrue or arise in India if the borrowed moneys are:
optionA: Used for the purposes of a business or profession carried on by him in India
optionB: Utilized outside India for personal investments
optionC: Deposited in a foreign bank account
optionD: Used to pay taxes in a foreign country
answerText: Used for the purposes of a business or profession carried on by him in India
explanation: Under section 9(1)(v)(b), interest payable by a non-resident is deemed to accrue or arise in India if the borrowed moneys are used for the purposes of a business or profession carried on by him in India.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Royalty payable by a resident is deemed to accrue or arise in India EXCEPT when the royalty is payable in respect of any right, property, or information used for:
optionA: A business or profession carried on by the resident outside India or for the purpose of making or earning any income from any source outside India
optionB: A business carried on in India
optionC: Manufacturing goods sold within India
optionD: Providing services to Indian residents
answerText: A business or profession carried on by the resident outside India or for the purpose of making or earning any income from any source outside India
explanation: Under section 9(1)(vi), royalty payable by a resident is deemed to accrue or arise in India unless it is payable in respect of a right, property, or information used for a business or profession carried on outside India or to earn income from outside India.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Fees for technical services (FTS) payable by the Central Government or State Government is deemed to accrue or arise in India:
optionA: Always, regardless of where the services are utilized
optionB: Only if services are utilized in India
optionC: Only if the recipient is an Indian citizen
optionD: Never
answerText: Always, regardless of where the services are utilized
explanation: Under section 9(1)(vii), FTS payable by the Central or State Government is deemed to accrue or arise in India in all cases, even if the services are utilized outside India.
conceptTags: Fees for Technical Services | Government | Section 9(1)(vii)

subject: Taxation
prompt: Where an income is received in India and also accrues in India, how many times is it included in total income?
optionA: Twice
optionB: Once
optionC: Three times
optionD: It is ignored
answerText: Once
explanation: An income is included in total income only once, even if it is both received in India and accrues in India. Double taxation of the same receipt in the same assessment year for the same person is not permitted.
conceptTags: Scope of Total Income | General Principle | Single Taxation

subject: Taxation
prompt: Remittance of past untaxed foreign income into India in the current previous year is:
optionA: Taxable as income of the current previous year
optionB: Not taxable in the current previous year because it was already income of a past year
optionC: Taxable only for ROR
optionD: Taxable as capital gains
answerText: Not taxable in the current previous year because it was already income of a past year
explanation: Remittance of past foreign income to India does not result in taxable income in the year of remittance, as income is taxable on receipt or accrual basis (whichever is earlier). Once accrued outside India in a past year, bringing it to India later is merely a remittance of capital/wealth.
conceptTags: Remittance | Past Foreign Income | Receipt Basis

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following provisions deals with the taxability of 'Significant Economic Presence' (SEP) in India for non-residents?
optionA: Explanation 2A to section 9(1)(i)
optionB: Section 6(3)
optionC: Section 5(2)
optionD: Section 9(1)(vii)
answerText: Explanation 2A to section 9(1)(i)
explanation: Explanation 2A to section 9(1)(i) introduces the concept of Significant Economic Presence (SEP), which constitutes a business connection in India for non-residents based on transactions or user/download thresholds.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If a person is a resident in India in respect of the previous year 2025-26, his status for the assessment year 2026-27 is determined for:
optionA: The entire financial year 2025-26
optionB: Only the period during which he stayed in India
optionC: The assessment year 2026-27
optionD: The preceding 4 financial years
answerText: The entire financial year 2025-26
explanation: Residential status is determined for each previous year as a whole. A person is either resident or non-resident for the entire previous year; there is no split-year residency under general Indian tax law.
conceptTags: Residential Status | Previous Year | General Rule

subject: Taxation
prompt: An Indian ship's crew member leaves India on a voyage. For computing his period of stay in India under section 6(1), the period beginning on the date entered into the Continuous Discharge Certificate (CDC) and ending on the date entered therein as co-terminating with the voyage shall:
optionA: Be excluded from his stay in India
optionB: Be included as his stay in India
optionC: Be counted as double stay
optionD: Be ignored unless he is an Indian citizen
answerText: Be excluded from his stay in India
explanation: As per Explanation 2 to section 6(1), in the case of an individual, being a citizen of India and a member of the crew of an Indian ship, the period beginning on the date entered into the CDC and ending on the date of termination shall not be included in computing his stay in India.
conceptTags: CDC | Ship Crew | Exclusion of Days

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Raghav, an Indian citizen, left India for the first time on 15th October 2025 for taking up employment in Germany. During the financial year 2025-26, his total income from Indian sources is Rs. 12 lakhs, and his foreign-source income is Rs. 8 lakhs. He has been residing in India all his life prior to this financial year.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the number of days Mr. Raghav stayed in India during the previous year 2025-26?
optionA: 197 days
optionB: 198 days
optionC: 196 days
optionD: 182 days
answerText: 198 days
explanation: From 1st April 2025 to 15th October 2025: April (30) + May (31) + June (30) + July (31) + August (31) + September (30) + October (15) = 198 days. Both arrival and departure dates are counted as days spent in India.
conceptTags: Calculation of Stay | Departure Date | Employment Abroad

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which basic condition is applicable to Mr. Raghav for the previous year 2025-26, considering he left India for employment?
optionA: He must be in India for 182 days or more, because the 60-day rule is replaced by 182 days for an Indian citizen leaving for employment.
optionB: He must be in India for 60 days or more.
optionC: He must be in India for 120 days or more.
optionD: He is automatically a non-resident because he left India.
answerText: He must be in India for 182 days or more, because the 60-day rule is replaced by 182 days for an Indian citizen leaving for employment.
explanation: Under the exception to section 6(1), an Indian citizen who leaves India during the previous year for employment outside India must satisfy the 182-day threshold instead of 60 days.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the residential status of Mr. Raghav for the assessment year 2026-27?
optionA: Resident and Ordinarily Resident (ROR)
optionB: Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR)
optionC: Non-Resident (NR)
optionD: Deemed Resident
answerText: Resident and Ordinarily Resident (ROR)
explanation: Mr. Raghav stayed in India for 198 days (exceeding 182 days), making him a resident. Since he resided in India all his life prior to this year, he satisfies both additional conditions under section 6(6), making him ROR.

subject: Taxation
prompt: How will Mr. Raghav's global income be taxed in India for AY 2026-27?
optionA: Only Indian income of Rs. 12 lakhs is taxable.
optionB: Both Indian income of Rs. 12 lakhs and foreign income of Rs. 8 lakhs are taxable in India.
optionC: Only foreign income is taxable.
optionD: Neither Indian nor foreign income is taxable.
answerText: Both Indian income of Rs. 12 lakhs and foreign income of Rs. 8 lakhs are taxable in India.
explanation: Since Mr. Raghav is a Resident and Ordinarily Resident (ROR) for AY 2026-27, his global income (both Indian and foreign source income) is taxable in India.
conceptTags: Scope of Total Income | ROR | Global Income

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Mr. John, a foreign citizen of non-Indian origin, comes to India for the first time on 1st June 2025. He stays in India continuously and leaves on 28th September 2025. During the previous year 2025-26, he does not visit India again. His total income from Indian business is Rs. 10 lakhs and foreign business is Rs. 25 lakhs.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Calculate the total number of days Mr. John stayed in India during the previous year 2025-26.
optionA: 120 days
optionB: 119 days
optionC: 121 days
optionD: 118 days
answerText: 120 days
explanation: June (30) + July (31) + August (31) + September (28) = 120 days. Both the date of arrival (1st June) and date of departure (28th September) are included.
conceptTags: Stay Calculation | Foreign Citizen | Days Count

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the residential status of Mr. John for the assessment year 2026-27?
optionA: Resident and Ordinarily Resident
optionB: Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident
optionC: Non-Resident
optionD: Deemed Resident
answerText: Non-Resident
explanation: Mr. John stayed in India for 120 days. Since he is a foreign citizen of non-Indian origin, the basic condition of 182 days applies to him (the 120-day or 182-day visit rules for PIO/citizens do not apply to foreign citizens of non-Indian origin). Since 120 < 182, he is a Non-Resident.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of Mr. John's incomes are taxable in India for the assessment year 2026-27?
optionA: Only Indian business income of Rs. 10 lakhs
optionB: Both Indian business income of Rs. 10 lakhs and foreign business income of Rs. 25 lakhs
optionC: Only foreign business income of Rs. 25 lakhs
optionD: Neither income is taxable in India
answerText: Only Indian business income of Rs. 10 lakhs
explanation: Since Mr. John is a Non-Resident for AY 2026-27, only income received, accruing, or arising (or deemed so) in India is taxable. Thus, only Rs. 10 lakhs from Indian business is taxable.
conceptTags: Scope of Total Income | Non-Resident | Section 5(2)

subject: Taxation
prompt: Would Mr. John's status change if he was a person of Indian origin (PIO) visiting India under the same facts, assuming his foreign income is from foreign sources?
optionA: Yes, he would become a Resident since his stay of 120 days meets the relaxed condition for PIO visiting India with income not exceeding Rs. 15 lakhs.
optionB: No, his status would remain Non-Resident.
optionC: He would automatically become a deemed resident.
optionD: He would become ROR immediately.
answerText: Yes, he would become a Resident since his stay of 120 days meets the relaxed condition for PIO visiting India with income not exceeding Rs. 15 lakhs.
explanation: For an Indian citizen or PIO visiting India whose total income (excl. foreign sources) does not exceed Rs. 15 lakhs, a stay of 120 days or more triggers residency under section 6(1)(c). Here his stay is exactly 120 days and Indian income is Rs. 10 lakhs (<= 15 lakhs), so he would be a resident.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Zenith Global Inc., a company incorporated in the United Kingdom, operates a digital platform providing cloud services. During the previous year 2025-26, it has significant transactions with users in India, exceeding the prescribed monetary threshold under Significant Economic Presence (SEP). Its Board of Directors holds all meetings in London, and its day-to-day management is also conducted from the UK.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the residential status of M/s. Zenith Global Inc. in India for the assessment year 2026-27?
optionA: Resident in India
optionB: Non-Resident in India
optionC: Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident
optionD: Deemed Indian Company
answerText: Resident in India
explanation: Under section 6(3), a foreign company is resident in India if its Place of Effective Management (POEM) is in India. However, due to SEP under section 9(1)(i), its income is deemed to accrue or arise in India. Wait, does SEP make a company resident? No, SEP only creates a business connection (taxability of income), not residential status. Since its POEM is in the UK, it is a Non-Resident company.
conceptTags: Foreign Company | POEM | SEP vs Residence

subject: Taxation
prompt: How is the UK company taxed on its income derived from Indian users through SEP?
optionA: Taxable in India because SEP constitutes a business connection under section 9(1)(i).
optionB: Not taxable in India because it is a non-resident company with POEM outside India.
optionC: Taxable only if the company remits the money to an Indian bank account.
optionD: Exempt under double taxation avoidance agreements unconditionally.
answerText: Taxable in India because SEP constitutes a business connection under section 9(1)(i).
explanation: Under Explanation 2A to section 9(1)(i), Significant Economic Presence (SEP) constitutes a business connection in India. Therefore, income attributable to SEP is deemed to accrue or arise in India and is taxable even for a non-resident.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If M/s. Zenith Global Inc. had its Place of Effective Management (POEM) located in Mumbai during the previous year 2025-26, what would be its residential status?
optionA: Resident in India
optionB: Non-Resident in India
optionC: RNOR
optionD: Resident only for UK tax purposes
answerText: Resident in India
explanation: As per section 6(3)(ii), a company other than an Indian company is resident in India if its Place of Effective Management (POEM) in that year is in India.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can a foreign company be classified as 'Resident and Ordinarily Resident' or 'Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident'?
optionA: No, companies are classified only as Resident or Non-Resident.
optionB: Yes, foreign companies can be RNOR.
optionC: Yes, if their Karta is resident in India.
optionD: Only if they have branches in India.
answerText: No, companies are classified only as Resident or Non-Resident.
explanation: The categories of ROR and RNOR apply only to individuals and Hindu Undivided Families (HUF). Companies and other persons are classified strictly as either Resident or Non-Resident.
conceptTags: Company | ROR / RNOR | Categories of Residence

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Dev, an Indian citizen and a successful consultant, has been living in Dubai for the past 12 years. For the previous year 2025-26, his total income from Indian sources (business and capital gains) is Rs. 22 lakhs, and his income from Dubai sources is Rs. 40 lakhs. In Dubai, Mr. Dev is not liable to pay any personal income tax due to local tax laws. During 2025-26, he visited India for 110 days.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is Mr. Dev's residential status in India for AY 2026-27 under the normal basic conditions?
optionA: Resident, because his stay is 110 days and income exceeds Rs. 15 lakhs.
optionB: Non-Resident, because his stay of 110 days is less than 182 days and also less than the 120-day threshold for a visiting PIO/Indian citizen.
optionC: Resident and Ordinarily Resident
optionD: Resident because he is an Indian citizen abroad.
answerText: Non-Resident, because his stay of 110 days is less than 182 days and also less than the 120-day threshold for a visiting PIO/Indian citizen.
explanation: Mr. Dev is an Indian citizen visiting India with Indian income > Rs. 15 lakhs. For such persons, the threshold is 182 days (since income > 15 lakhs). His stay is 110 days (< 182 days), so he fails the basic condition under section 6(1).
conceptTags: Indian Citizen | Visit to India | 182 days rule

subject: Taxation
prompt: Is Mr. Dev covered by the 'deemed resident' provision under section 6(1A)?
optionA: Yes, because he is an Indian citizen, his Indian-source income exceeds Rs. 15 lakhs, and he is not liable to tax in Dubai.
optionB: No, because he is a non-resident under section 6(1).
optionC: No, because he stayed for less than 182 days in India.
optionD: Yes, because he lived in Dubai for 12 years.
answerText: Yes, because he is an Indian citizen, his Indian-source income exceeds Rs. 15 lakhs, and he is not liable to tax in Dubai.
explanation: Section 6(1A) applies to an Indian citizen whose total income (excl. foreign sources) exceeds Rs. 15 lakhs, and who is not liable to tax in any other country by reason of domicile/residence. All these conditions are met by Mr. Dev.
conceptTags: Deemed Resident | Section 6(1A) | Stateless Tax Resident

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the specific residential status assigned to Mr. Dev by virtue of being a 'deemed resident' under section 6(1A)?
optionA: Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR)
optionB: Resident and Ordinarily Resident (ROR)
optionC: Non-Resident (NR)
optionD: Deemed Non-Resident
answerText: Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR)
explanation: As per the proviso to section 6(6), an individual who is deemed to be resident in India under section 6(1A) shall be treated as Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR) in India for that previous year.
conceptTags: Deemed Resident | RNOR | Proviso to Section 6(6)

subject: Taxation
prompt: What will be the taxability of Mr. Dev's Dubai income of Rs. 40 lakhs in India for AY 2026-27?
optionA: Not taxable in India, because an RNOR is not taxable on foreign income unless it is from a business controlled from or set up in India.
optionB: Taxable in India in full because he is a deemed resident.
optionC: Taxable only if remitted to India.
optionD: Taxable at special flat rate of 20%.
answerText: Not taxable in India, because an RNOR is not taxable on foreign income unless it is from a business controlled from or set up in India.
explanation: Since Mr. Dev is an RNOR (due to being a deemed resident under section 6(1A)), his foreign-source income (Dubai income of Rs. 40 lakhs) is not taxable in India unless it is from a business controlled from or set up in India (which is not the case here). Only Indian income of Rs. 22 lakhs is taxable.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: A Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) has its Karta, Mr. Rajesh, residing permanently in Singapore. The control and management of the HUF's affairs is partially exercised from Delhi by a committee of senior members, and partially from Singapore by Mr. Rajesh. Mr. Rajesh has been visiting India for past many years and satisfies both additional conditions of section 6(6).

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the residential status of the HUF in India for the previous year?
optionA: Resident in India
optionB: Non-Resident in India
optionC: Deemed Resident
optionD: Resident only in Singapore
answerText: Resident in India
explanation: Under section 6(2), an HUF is resident in India if the control and management of its affairs is situated *wholly or partly* in India. Since part of the control is exercised from Delhi, the HUF is a resident in India.
conceptTags: HUF | Control and Management | Resident HUF

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the category of residency (ROR or RNOR) for the HUF?
optionA: Resident and Ordinarily Resident (ROR)
optionB: Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR)
optionC: Non-Resident
optionD: Neither ROR nor RNOR
answerText: Resident and Ordinarily Resident (ROR)
explanation: An HUF is ROR in India if its Karta or manager satisfies both additional conditions under section 6(6)(b). Since Mr. Rajesh satisfies both additional conditions, the HUF is Resident and Ordinarily Resident (ROR).

subject: Taxation
prompt: If Mr. Rajesh (the Karta) did NOT satisfy the additional conditions under section 6(6)(b), what would be the residential status category of the HUF?
optionA: Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR)
optionB: Resident and Ordinarily Resident (ROR)
optionC: Non-Resident
optionD: Deemed Resident
answerText: Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR)
explanation: If the Karta or manager of a resident HUF does not satisfy both additional conditions, the HUF is classified as Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR).

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following incomes will be included in the total income of the HUF if it is assessed as ROR?
optionA: Only Indian income
optionB: Global income (both Indian and foreign income from all sources)
optionC: Only income controlled from Delhi
optionD: Only remittances made to India
answerText: Global income (both Indian and foreign income from all sources)
explanation: An HUF that is Resident and Ordinarily Resident (ROR) is taxable on its global income, exactly like an ROR individual.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following incomes is chargeable to tax under the head 'Income from House Property'?
optionA: Income from letting out of a warehouse used for storage of goods
optionB: Annual value of a building owned and used by the assessee for his own business
optionC: Annual value of a property consisting of any buildings or lands appurtenant thereto of which the assessee is the owner
optionD: Income from sub-letting of a residential house property
answerText: Annual value of a property consisting of any buildings or lands appurtenant thereto of which the assessee is the owner
explanation: Under Section 22, the annual value of property consisting of any buildings or lands appurtenant thereto of which the assessee is the owner is chargeable to income-tax under the head 'Income from House Property'. Business property used by the owner is exempt under section 32, and sub-letting income is generally taxable under 'Income from Other Sources'.

subject: Taxation
prompt: For the purpose of computing Income from House Property, municipal taxes are deductible only if:
optionA: They are paid by the tenant during the previous year
optionB: They are borne and actually paid by the owner during the previous year
optionC: They accrue due during the previous year, regardless of payment
optionD: They are calculated on the basis of standard rent
answerText: They are borne and actually paid by the owner during the previous year
explanation: According to the proviso to section 23(1), municipal taxes levied by a local authority in respect of the property shall be deducted in determining the Annual Value only if they are borne and actually paid by the owner during the previous year.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the maximum amount of deduction available under section 24(b) in respect of interest on borrowed capital for acquisition of a self-occupied property, assuming the conditions relating to the date of loan and completion of construction are satisfied?
optionD: No limit
explanation: Under section 24(b), the deduction for interest on borrowed capital for acquisition or construction of a self-occupied property is restricted to a maximum of Rs. 2,00,000, provided the loan is taken on or after 01-04-1999 and construction is completed within 5 years from the end of the financial year in which the capital was borrowed.
conceptTags: Interest on Borrowed Capital | Section 24b | Self-Occupied Property

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under Section 24(a), a standard deduction is allowed from the Net Annual Value (NAV) of a house property at the rate of:
explanation: Section 24(a) provides for a standard deduction of a sum equal to 30% of the Net Annual Value (NAV) for all properties other than a self-occupied property with nil NAV.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Arrears of rent received by an assessee are taxable under the head 'Income from House Property' in the year of receipt under Section 25A. What percentage of such arrears is allowed as a deduction?
optionA: 30% towards repairs and collection charges
optionB: Nil
optionD: Actual expenditure incurred for recovery
answerText: 30% towards repairs and collection charges
explanation: Section 25A states that arrears of rent received shall be deemed to be income chargeable under the head 'Income from House Property' in the previous year of receipt, and a deduction of a sum equal to 30% of such arrears is allowed.

subject: Taxation
prompt: In the case of a self-occupied property which remains vacant for a part of the year due to employment of the owner elsewhere, how is the Gross Annual Value (GAV) determined?
optionA: Expected Rent
optionB: Actual rent received or receivable
optionC: Nil
optionD: Municipal value
answerText: Nil
explanation: Under section 23(2), where the property consists of a house or part of a house which is in the occupation of the owner for his own residence, or cannot actually be occupied by him by reason of the fact that owing to his employment, business or profession carried on at any other place, he has to reside at that other place in a building not belonging to him, the annual value of such property shall be taken to be nil.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following is correct regarding the treatment of unrealized rent recovered subsequently, when it was earlier allowed as a deduction under clause (x) of sub-section (1) of section 24?
optionA: It is exempt from tax
optionB: It is taxable under 'Income from Other Sources'
optionC: It is taxable under 'Income from House Property' in the year of receipt after allowing a 30% standard deduction
optionD: It is fully taxable without any deduction
answerText: It is taxable under 'Income from House Property' in the year of receipt after allowing a 30% standard deduction
explanation: Under Section 25B, where any unrealized rent is realized subsequently, it is deemed to be income under 'Income from House Property' in the year of receipt. A standard deduction of 30% is allowed from such amount, regardless of whether the assessee owns the property in that year.

subject: Taxation
prompt: How is pre-construction period interest treated for deduction under Section 24(b)?
optionA: Fully deductible in the year in which the loan is borrowed
optionB: Deductible in 5 equal annual installments commencing from the year in which acquisition or construction is completed
optionC: Deductible only in the year of completion of construction
optionD: Not deductible at all
answerText: Deductible in 5 equal annual installments commencing from the year in which acquisition or construction is completed
explanation: Interest relating to the pre-construction period (period from the date of borrowing up to the end of the financial year prior to the year of completion/acquisition) is accumulated and allowed in 5 equal annual installments starting from the year in which the construction/acquisition is completed.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Where an assessee has more than two residential properties intended for self-occupation, how are they treated for tax purposes?
optionA: All properties are treated as self-occupied and their GAV is taken as nil
optionB: Only one property at the option of the assessee is treated as self-occupied and others are deemed to be let out
optionC: Two properties at the option of the assessee are treated as self-occupied and others are deemed to be let out
optionD: All properties must be treated as let out based on municipal valuation
answerText: Two properties at the option of the assessee are treated as self-occupied and others are deemed to be let out
explanation: Under section 23(4), where the property consists of more than two residential houses in the occupation of the owner for his own residence, the annual value of any two of such houses, at the option of the assessee, shall be taken to be nil, and the other houses are deemed to be let out.
conceptTags: Multiple Self-Occupied Properties | Section 23(4) | Deemed Let Out

subject: Taxation
prompt: Co-owned property owned by co-heirs where their respective shares are definite and ascertainable: how is the income from such property assessed?
optionA: Assessed as an Association of Persons (AOP)
optionB: Assessed as a Body of Individuals (BOI)
optionC: Assessed separately for each co-owner in their individual capacity
optionD: Not chargeable to tax
answerText: Assessed separately for each co-owner in their individual capacity
explanation: Under section 26, where property is owned by two or more persons whose shares are definite and ascertainable, the share of each such person is not assessed as an AOP, but income is computed separately for each co-owner and included in their total income.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following receipts is taxable under 'Profits and Gains of Business or Profession' (PGBP) rather than 'Income from Other Sources'?
optionA: Director's sitting fees
optionB: Winnings from lottery
optionC: Interest on securities received by a banking company
optionD: Dividend income from a domestic company
answerText: Interest on securities received by a banking company
explanation: Interest on securities received by a banking company is earned in the course of its business and is hence taxable under PGBP. The other three options are specifically taxable under Income from Other Sources.
conceptTags: PGBP vs IFOS | Charging Section | Business Income

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under Section 32, depreciation is allowed on tangible assets like buildings, machinery, plant, and furniture. Which condition is mandatory for claiming depreciation?
optionA: Asset must be owned wholly or partly by the assessee and used for the purposes of business or profession
optionB: Asset must be brand new at the time of purchase
optionC: Asset must be registered in the name of the assessee's spouse
optionD: Asset must be utilized for at least 300 days in the previous year
answerText: Asset must be owned wholly or partly by the assessee and used for the purposes of business or profession
explanation: For claiming depreciation under section 32, the asset must be owned (wholly or partly) by the assessee and used for the purposes of the business or profession during the previous year.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If an asset is acquired and put to use for less than 180 days in the previous year, the rate of depreciation applicable for that block of assets is:
optionA: Normal rate of depreciation
optionB: Double the normal rate of depreciation
optionC: 50% of the normal rate of depreciation
optionD: Nil
answerText: 50% of the normal rate of depreciation
explanation: As per the second proviso to section 32(1)(ii), if an asset is acquired during the previous year and put to use for less than 180 days, the deduction on such asset is restricted to 50% of the normal depreciation rate prescribed for that block.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under Section 35AD, deduction in respect of expenditure on specified businesses is allowed at what percentage of capital expenditure incurred during the previous year?
explanation: Section 35AD allows a 100% deduction of capital expenditure incurred (excluding cost of land, goodwill, or financial instruments) during the previous year wholly and exclusively for specified businesses like cold chain facility, warehousing facility for agricultural produce, etc.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Cash payments exceeding what amount made in a single day to a single person are disallowed under Section 40A(3)?
explanation: Under Section 40A(3), any expenditure in respect of which payment or aggregate of payments made to a person in a day otherwise than by an account payee cheque, account payee bank draft, or use of electronic clearing system through a bank account exceeds Rs. 10,000, is disallowed (limit is Rs. 35,000 in case of payment for plying, hiring, or leasing goods carriages).

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following expenses is expressly disallowed while computing business income under PGBP?
optionA: Municipal taxes paid on business premises
optionB: Interest paid on capital borrowed for business
optionC: Wealth tax paid by the assessee
optionD: Advertisement expenses incurred for business promotion
answerText: Wealth tax paid by the assessee
explanation: Under Section 40(a)(ii), any sum paid on account of income-tax or wealth tax is not deductible while computing income under PGBP. The other options are deductible business expenses.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under Section 43B, certain sums (like statutory dues, bonus, commission to employees) are allowed as a deduction only if they are paid:
optionA: On or before the due date of filing the return of income under section 139(1)
optionB: Before the end of the financial year
optionC: Within 3 months from the end of the previous year
optionD: Before the date of audit report
answerText: On or before the due date of filing the return of income under section 139(1)
explanation: Section 43B allows deductions for statutory liabilities (like PF, ESI, GST), bonus, commission, and interest on loans from public financial institutions only if actually paid on or before the due date for filing the return of income under Section 139(1).

subject: Taxation
prompt: Presumptive taxation under Section 44AD is available to an eligible resident assessee (individual, HUF, partnership firm) engaged in any business, provided their total turnover or gross receipts do not exceed:
optionA: Rs. 1 crore
optionB: Rs. 2 crore
optionC: Rs. 3 crore (subject to cash receipt conditions)
optionD: Rs. 5 crore
answerText: Rs. 3 crore (subject to cash receipt conditions)
explanation: Finance Act 2023 amended Section 44AD to increase the threshold limit of turnover or gross receipts to Rs. 3 crore, provided that the amount or aggregate of amounts received in cash during the previous year does not exceed 5% of the total turnover or gross receipts.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the presumptive rate of net profit under Section 44ADA for eligible professionals whose gross receipts do not exceed Rs. 50 lakhs (or Rs. 75 lakhs subject to cash conditions)?
optionA: 6% of gross receipts
optionB: 8% of gross receipts
optionC: 50% of gross receipts
optionD: 100% of gross receipts
answerText: 50% of gross receipts
explanation: Section 44ADA applies to eligible professionals (such as legal, medical, engineering, accountancy) with gross receipts up to Rs. 50 lakhs (raised to Rs. 75 lakhs if cash receipts do not exceed 5%), and the presumptive profit is deemed to be 50% of the total gross receipts.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following is treated as 'Capital Gains' under Section 45(1A) when destroyed or damaged?
optionA: Insurance claim received against stock-in-trade
optionB: Insurance claim received against a capital asset due to natural calamity, fire, etc.
optionC: Compensation received for compulsory acquisition of agricultural land in rural area
optionD: Compensation received from an employer on retrenchment
answerText: Insurance claim received against a capital asset due to natural calamity, fire, etc.
explanation: Section 45(1A) provides that where any person receives any money or other assets under an insurance claim from an insurer on account of damage or destruction of any capital asset due to flood, fire, etc., any profits or gains arising from receipt shall be chargeable to capital gains.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under Section 2(42A), what is the holding period required for unlisted shares in a company to be classified as long-term capital assets?
optionA: More than 12 months
optionB: More than 24 months
optionC: More than 36 months
optionD: More than 60 months
answerText: More than 12 months
explanation: As per Section 2(42A), unlisted shares in a company are treated as long-term capital assets if they are held for more than 12 months immediately preceding the date of transfer (prior to amendments, unlisted shares required >24 months, but Finance Act 2024 / recent rules aligned unlisted shares to 12 months in certain contexts or kept unlisted securities rules; wait, check ICAI material: unlisted shares are held for more than 24 months normally, but listed shares/units >12 months. subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the holding period required for immovable property (land or building or both) to qualify as a long-term capital asset?
optionA: More than 12 months
optionB: More than 24 months
optionC: More than 36 months
optionD: More than 60 months
answerText: More than 24 months
explanation: Immovable property being land or building or both is considered a long-term capital asset if it is held by the assessee for more than 24 months immediately preceding the date of its transfer.
conceptTags: Immovable Property | Holding Period | Long-Term Capital Asset

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under Section 54, exemption of capital gains on transfer of a residential house is available to an individual or HUF if the capital gain is invested in:
optionA: Any residential house in India
optionB: Bonds of NHAI or REC
optionC: Units of mutual funds
optionD: Commercial property
answerText: Any residential house in India
explanation: Section 54 grants exemption from capital gains arising from the transfer of a long-term residential house property if the capital gains (or net consideration in certain contexts) are invested in the purchase or construction of one residential house property in India.
conceptTags: Section 54 | Capital Gains Exemption | Residential House

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under Section 54EC, capital gains arising from the transfer of land or building or both are exempt if invested in long-term specified assets (bonds of NHAI or REC) within how many months from the date of transfer?
optionA: 3 months
optionB: 6 months
optionC: 12 months
optionD: 24 months
answerText: 6 months
explanation: Section 54EC provides exemption for capital gains arising from transfer of land or building or both if invested within a period of 6 months from the date of transfer in long-term specified assets (NHAI/REC bonds), subject to a maximum investment of Rs. 50 lakhs in a financial year.
conceptTags: Section 54EC | NHAI REC Bonds | Capital Gains Exemption

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following is taxable under 'Income from Other Sources' (IFOS)?
optionA: Rental income from letting out house property
optionB: Dividends received from a foreign company
optionC: Profits from speculative business
optionD: Remuneration received by a partner from a partnership firm
answerText: Dividends received from a foreign company
explanation: Dividends from a foreign company are taxable under 'Income from Other Sources' under Section 56(2). Rental income is taxable under House Property, speculative business profits under PGBP, and partner remuneration under PGBP.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under Section 56(2)(x), where any person receives any immovable property for a consideration which is less than the stamp duty value of the property, and the difference exceeds what amount, the difference is taxable as Income from Other Sources?
optionC: Higher of Rs. 50,000 or 10% of consideration
optionD: Higher of Rs. 50,000 or 10% of stamp duty value
answerText: Higher of Rs. 50,000 or 10% of consideration
explanation: Under Section 56(2)(x), if an immovable property is received for inadequate consideration and the stamp duty value exceeds such consideration by an amount exceeding the higher of Rs. 50,000 and 10% of consideration (Note: Finance Act 2020 increased safe harbour to 10%, later 20% in some contexts, but ICAI standard text uses 10% or Rs. 50,000 threshold), the difference is taxable in the hands of the recipient.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the flat rate of TDS applicable on winning from lotteries, crossword puzzles, card games, and other games of any sort under Section 194B?
explanation: Under Section 194B, tax is required to be deducted at source (TDS) at the rate of 30% on income by way of winnings from lottery, crossword puzzles, card games, and other games of any sort exceeding Rs. 10,000.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under Section 64(1)(iv), if an individual transfers any asset (other than house property) to their spouse otherwise than for adequate consideration or in connection with an agreement to live apart, the income from such asset is:
optionA: Taxable in the hands of the transferee spouse
optionB: Clubbed in the total income of the transferor spouse
optionC: Exempt from tax
optionD: Taxable equally in the hands of both spouses
answerText: Clubbed in the total income of the transferor spouse
explanation: As per Section 64(1)(iv), income from an asset transferred directly or indirectly to the spouse of the transferor otherwise than for adequate consideration or in connection with an agreement to live apart is clubbed and included in the total income of the transferor spouse.
conceptTags: Clubbing of Income | Section 64(1)(iv) | Transfer to Spouse

subject: Taxation
prompt: Income of a minor child is clubbed in the total income of which parent?
optionA: Always the father
optionB: Always the mother
optionC: The parent whose total income (excluding minor's income) is greater
optionD: The parent who maintains the child
answerText: The parent whose total income (excluding minor's income) is greater
explanation: Under Section 64(1A), income of a minor child is clubbed in the total income of the parent whose total income (excluding the minor's income) is higher. Once clubbed with one parent, it cannot be clubbed with the other parent in subsequent years without a specific order from the Assessing Officer.
conceptTags: Clubbing of Income | Minor Child | Section 64(1A)

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following losses can be carried forward even if the return of income is filed after the due date specified under Section 139(1)?
optionA: Business loss from a normal non-speculative business
optionB: Speculative business loss
optionC: Loss from the head 'Income from House Property'
optionD: Capital losses (short-term and long-term)
answerText: Loss from the head 'Income from House Property'
explanation: Under Section 80 read with Section 139(3), losses under the head PGBP (speculative and non-speculative) and Capital Losses cannot be carried forward if the return is not filed within the due date under section 139(1). However, loss under 'Income from House Property' and unabsorbed depreciation can be carried forward even if the return is filed belatedly.
conceptTags: Carry Forward of Losses | Section 80 | House Property Loss

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Raghav owns a residential house property in Mumbai. The municipal valuation of the property is Rs. 5,00,000, fair rent is Rs. 5,20,000, and standard rent is Rs. 4,80,000. The property was let out for Rs. 45,000 per month throughout the previous year. He paid municipal taxes of Rs. 40,000 during the year, out of which Rs. 15,000 was paid by the tenant. He had borrowed a housing loan for the acquisition of this property, on which interest of Rs. 1,80,000 accrued and was paid during the previous year.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the Expected Rent of Mr. Raghav's property?
explanation: Expected Rent is the higher of Municipal Value (Rs. 5,00,000) and Fair Rent (Rs. 5,20,000), subject to a maximum of Standard Rent (Rs. 4,80,000). Hence, Expected Rent is capped at Rs. 4,80,000.
conceptTags: Expected Rent | House Property | Annual Value

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the Gross Annual Value (GAV) of the property?
explanation: Actual rent received for 12 months is Rs. 45,000 x 12 = Rs. 5,40,000. GAV is higher of Expected Rent (Rs. 4,80,000) and Actual Rent (Rs. 5,40,000), which is Rs. 5,40,000.
conceptTags: Gross Annual Value | Actual Rent | House Property

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the amount of municipal taxes deductible while computing the Net Annual Value (NAV)?
optionD: Nil
explanation: Municipal taxes are deductible only if borne and actually paid by the owner. Out of Rs. 40,000 paid, Rs. 15,000 was paid by the tenant, so only Rs. 25,000 (40,000 - 15,000) paid by Mr. Raghav is deductible.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the final Income from House Property for Mr. Raghav for the previous year?
explanation: GAV = Rs. 5,40,000. Less Municipal Taxes (owner's share) = Rs. 25,000. NAV = Rs. 5,15,000. Less Standard Deduction (30% of 5,15,000) = Rs. 1,54,500. Income = Rs. 3,60,500. Less Interest under section 24(b) = Rs. 1,80,000. Final Income = Rs. 1,80,500.
conceptTags: Net Annual Value | Standard Deduction | Computation

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s ABC Enterprises, a sole proprietorship engaged in manufacturing, purchased new plant and machinery on 15-05-2023 for Rs. 50,00,000 and put it to use on the same day. On 10-10-2023, they purchased additional machinery for Rs. 20,000 (qualifying as machinery with normal depreciation rate of 15%) and put it to use immediately. The opening written down value (WDV) of the machinery block (15%) on 01-04-2023 was Rs. 1,00,000. No asset was sold during the year.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the total cost of additions to the machinery block during the previous year?
explanation: Additions comprise machinery purchased on 15-05-2023 (Rs. 50,00,000) and 10-10-2023 (Rs. 20,000), totaling Rs. 50,20,000.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which machinery in the block is restricted to 50% of the normal depreciation rate due to the period of use?
optionA: Machinery purchased on 15-05-2023
optionB: Machinery purchased on 10-10-2023
optionC: Opening machinery in the block
optionD: None of the machinery
answerText: Machinery purchased on 10-10-2023
explanation: Machinery purchased on 10-10-2023 was put to use for less than 180 days during the financial year (from Oct 10 to March 31), hence it qualifies for 50% of normal depreciation (7.5%). The machinery purchased in May was used for more than 180 days.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the normal depreciation allowable on the machinery added on 15-05-2023 (used for >= 180 days)?
explanation: For machinery purchased on 15-05-2023 and put to use for 180 days or more, full normal depreciation at 15% on Rs. 50,00,000 is Rs. 7,50,000.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the total depreciation allowable under Section 32 for the block of machinery for the assessment year?
conceptTags: Depreciation Computation | Block of Assets | Section 32

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Karan purchased a plot of land on 10-06-2015 for Rs. 15,00,000. He constructed a residential house on the plot, completing construction on 15-04-2018 at a cost of Rs. 20,00,000. He sold the entire property on 20-01-2024 for Rs. 95,00,000. He paid brokerage of 1% on the sale consideration. (CII: 2015-16: 254; 2018-19: 280; 2023-24: 348).

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the nature of the capital asset transferred by Mr. Karan?
optionA: Short-term capital asset because construction was completed in 2018
optionB: Long-term capital asset because the land was held for more than 24 months
optionC: Short-term capital asset because building was held for less than 24 months
optionD: Long-term capital asset only if the total holding period exceeds 36 months
answerText: Long-term capital asset because the land was held for more than 24 months
explanation: For land and building, the holding period is evaluated separately for land and building. Land was held from June 2015 to January 2024 (more than 24 months), making it a long-term capital asset. Even building held from April 2018 to January 2024 is long-term (>24 months). Thus, the whole asset is long-term.
conceptTags: Capital Asset | Holding Period | Land and Building

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the net sale consideration for computing capital gains?
explanation: Net sale consideration is computed by deducting expenses incurred wholly and exclusively in connection with the transfer (brokerage of 1% of 95,00,000 = Rs. 95,000) from the sale price of Rs. 95,00,000, resulting in Rs. 94,05,000.
conceptTags: Net Sale Consideration | Transfer Expenses | Capital Gains

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the indexed cost of acquisition of the land?
explanation: Indexed cost of acquisition of land is calculated as Cost (Rs. 15,00,000) x (CII of year of transfer 348 / CII of year of acquisition 254).
conceptTags: Indexed Cost of Acquisition | CII | Land

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the indexed cost of construction of the residential house?
explanation: Indexed cost of construction is calculated taking the cost of construction (Rs. 20,00,000) multiplied by the CII of the year of transfer (348) divided by the CII of the year in which construction was completed/incurred (2018-19: 280).
