prompt: If neither open market value nor the 90% proviso nor any other Rule 28 criteria can be applied, what fallback method does Rule 28 prescribe before resorting to residual rules?
optionA: Value shall be deemed to be zero
optionB: Cost of production plus 10% markup under Rule 30
optionC: 50% of the manufacturing cost
optionD: Book value certified by cost accountant
answerText: Cost of production plus 10% markup under Rule 30
explanation: Rule 28 directs that if value cannot be determined under clause (a) or (b) of Rule 28, it shall be determined under Rule 30 (110% of cost of production/manufacture) or Rule 31.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Swift Express Logistics acts as a pure agent for its client, M/s. Global Traders. Swift Express Logistics incurred the following expenses on behalf of Global Traders during the month of October: (i) Freight charges paid to transporters amounting to Rs. 50,000; (ii) Municipal octroi charges paid to the municipal corporation amounting to Rs. 5,000; (iii) Packing and sorting charges incurred by Swift Express Logistics in its own warehouse amounting to Rs. 8,000; (iv) Statutory inspection fee paid to the port authority amounting to Rs. 12,000. All out-of-pocket expenses (freight, octroi, and inspection fee) were billed to Global Traders at actuals in separate debit notes along with Swift's own service fee of Rs. 20,000 for logistical coordination.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which rule governs the exclusion of expenses incurred by a supplier acting as a pure agent from the value of supply?
optionA: Rule 27
optionB: Rule 30
optionC: Rule 32
optionD: Rule 33
answerText: Rule 33
explanation: Rule 33 of the CGST Rules, 2017 specifies the conditions and methodology for excluding expenditure incurred by a supplier as a pure agent of the recipient of supply.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following expenses incurred by Swift Express Logistics qualifies for exclusion under Rule 33 as a pure agent?
optionA: Packing and sorting charges of Rs. 8,000
optionB: Freight charges of Rs. 50,000, municipal octroi of Rs. 5,000, and inspection fee of Rs. 12,000
optionC: Logistical coordination service fee of Rs. 20,000
optionD: None of the expenses qualify
answerText: Freight charges of Rs. 50,000, municipal octroi of Rs. 5,000, and inspection fee of Rs. 12,000
explanation: Freight, municipal octroi, and port inspection fees were incurred by Swift as a pure agent on behalf of Global Traders, billed at actuals separately, and represent third-party statutory/service liabilities of the client. Packing/sorting charges are the supplier's own operational costs.
conceptTags: Rule 33 Conditions | Pure Agent Expenses | Exclusion Eligibility

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the taxable value of supply for Swift Express Logistics excluding the pure agent reimbursements?
optionA: Rs. 20,000 (Service fee only)
optionB: Rs. 28,000 (Service fee + packing charges)
optionC: Rs. 95,000 (Gross billing)
answerText: Rs. 28,000 (Service fee + packing charges)
explanation: The taxable value includes Swift's own service fee (Rs. 20,000) and its own operational expenses like packing/sorting (Rs. 8,000), totaling Rs. 28,000. Pure agent reimbursements (Rs. 50,000 + Rs. 5,000 + Rs. 12,000) are excluded under Rule 33.
conceptTags: Taxable Value Calculation | Pure Agent Exclusion | Service Fee

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following is NOT a mandatory condition for Swift Express Logistics to be treated as a pure agent under Rule 33?
optionA: Swift acts as a pure agent of Global Traders when making payment to third parties
optionB: Swift holds title to the goods procured and uses them for its own consumption
optionC: The supply of service procured by the pure agent is in addition to the primary service provided
optionD: The recovery is separately indicated in the invoice
answerText: Swift holds title to the goods procured and uses them for its own consumption
explanation: Holding title to goods or services and using them for one's own account violates the definition of a pure agent. A pure agent must not hold title to the goods or services procured.
conceptTags: Pure Agent Definition | Rule 33 Conditions | Title to Goods

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Zenith Forex Bureau, a registered person under GST, undertakes currency exchange transactions. During the week, it converts USD 10,000 into Indian Rupees (INR). On that day, the RBI reference rate for USD is Rs. 82.50 per USD. Zenith buys the USD from the customer at an exchange rate of Rs. 82.10 per USD. In another transaction, Zenith converts EUR 5,000 into INR, but the RBI reference rate for EUR is not announced/available on that day. For this EUR transaction, the gross amount of Indian Rupees provided to the customer is Rs. 4,50,000.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which rule of the CGST Rules, 2017 specifically governs the valuation of supply of foreign exchange services?
optionA: Rule 32(2)
optionB: Rule 32(4)
optionC: Rule 32(5)
optionD: Rule 33
answerText: Rule 32(2)
explanation: Rule 32(2) of the CGST Rules, 2017 prescribes the special valuation methods for the supply of services in relation to the purchase or sale of foreign currency, including money changing.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the taxable value of supply for the conversion of USD 10,000 under Rule 32(2)(a)?
explanation: Under Rule 32(2)(a), when one currency is INR, value = (RBI reference rate - buying rate) * total units = (82.50 - 82.10) * 10,000 = Rs. 0.40 * 10,000 = Rs. 4,000.
conceptTags: Rule 32(2)(a) | Forex Calculation | RBI Reference Rate

subject: Taxation
prompt: How is the value of supply determined for the EUR 5,000 transaction where the RBI reference rate is not available on that day?
optionA: 1% of the gross amount of Indian Rupees provided (1% of Rs. 4,50,000)
optionB: Difference between buying rate and selling rate
optionC: 0.5% of the total EUR converted
optionD: Exempt from GST due to absence of RBI rate
answerText: 1% of the gross amount of Indian Rupees provided (1% of Rs. 4,50,000)
explanation: As per the proviso to Rule 32(2)(a), where the RBI reference rate is not available, the value shall be 1% of the gross amount of Indian Rupees provided or received (1% of Rs. 4,50,000 = Rs. 4,500).
conceptTags: Rule 32(2) Proviso | Missing RBI Rate | Forex Valuation

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the alternative method available for valuing foreign exchange transactions under Rule 32(2)(b) if the taxpayer opts for slab-based valuation instead of Rule 32(2)(a)?
optionA: Fixed percentage of the total transaction value based on tiered slabs of currency converted
optionB: Flat Rs. 1,000 per transaction
optionC: 10% of the commission charged
optionD: Actual gross profit earned
answerText: Fixed percentage of the total transaction value based on tiered slabs of currency converted
explanation: Rule 32(2)(b) permits a taxable person to opt for valuation based on slab rates (e.g., 1% up to Rs. 1 lakh, etc.) of the gross amount of currency exchanged, once exercised for a financial year.
conceptTags: Rule 32(2)(b) | Slab-based Valuation | Money Changing Options

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Vintage Wheels, a registered second-hand car dealer, purchases a pre-owned luxury car from an unregistered individual for Rs. 15,00,000. Vintage Wheels undertakes minor cleaning, denting, and painting costing Rs. 50,000 (which does not alter the fundamental nature of the car) and sells the car to a retail customer for Rs. 18,50,000. In a separate transaction during the same month, Vintage Wheels purchases another old motorcycle for Rs. 40,000 and sells it for Rs. 35,000.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which specific valuation rule applies to the supply of second-hand goods by a dealer engaged in buying and selling second-hand goods?
optionA: Rule 32(3)
optionB: Rule 32(4)
optionC: Rule 32(5)
optionD: Rule 33
answerText: Rule 32(5)
explanation: Rule 32(5) of the CGST Rules, 2017 governs the valuation of taxable supplies of second-hand goods dealt in by a registered person after minor processing.
conceptTags: Rule 32(5) | Second-hand Goods | Margin Scheme Rule

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the taxable value of supply for the luxury car under Rule 32(5)?
explanation: Under Rule 32(5), the value of supply of second-hand goods is the difference between the selling price and the purchase price (Margin = Selling price Rs. 18,50,000 - Purchase price Rs. 15,00,000 = Rs. 3,50,000). Minor processing costs are ignored in computing the margin.
conceptTags: Rule 32(5) Calculation | Car Margin | Second-hand Valuation

subject: Taxation
prompt: How is the transaction involving the motorcycle (purchase Rs. 40,000, sale Rs. 35,000) treated for GST purposes under Rule 32(5)?
optionA: The negative margin of Rs. 5,000 can be set off against the car's positive margin
optionB: The negative margin of Rs. 5,000 is ignored, and the taxable value for this transaction is nil
optionC: GST refund is available for the negative margin
optionD: The purchase price is adjusted to Rs. 35,000
answerText: The negative margin of Rs. 5,000 is ignored, and the taxable value for this transaction is nil
explanation: The proviso to Rule 32(5) explicitly states that if the margin is negative (selling price is less than purchase price), it shall be ignored and cannot be used to offset margins of other transactions.
conceptTags: Rule 32(5) Proviso | Negative Margin | Second-hand Goods

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is a mandatory pre-condition for a dealer to adopt the margin scheme under Rule 32(5) for second-hand goods?
optionA: Input tax credit must have been availed on the purchase of the second-hand goods
optionB: No input tax credit has been availed on the purchase of such second-hand goods
optionC: The purchase must be made from a registered manufacturer only
optionD: The selling price must exceed 200% of the purchase price
answerText: No input tax credit has been availed on the purchase of such second-hand goods
explanation: Rule 32(5) applies only if no input tax credit (ITC) has been availed on the purchase of the second-hand goods from the unregistered supplier or person.
conceptTags: Rule 32(5) Condition | ITC Prohibition | Margin Scheme

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following conditions is NOT mandatory for a registered person to avail Input Tax Credit (ITC) under Section 16(2) of the CGST Act, 2017?
optionA: Possession of a tax invoice or debit note issued by a registered supplier
optionB: Receipt of goods or services or both
optionC: Filing of the annual return by the recipient for the relevant financial year
optionD: Furnishing of the return under Section 39 by the registered person
answerText: Filing of the annual return by the recipient for the relevant financial year
explanation: Section 16(2) prescribes four primary conditions for claiming ITC: possession of tax invoice/debit note, receipt of goods/services, tax charged has been paid to the government, and furnishing of the return under Section 39. Filing of the annual return is not a pre-condition for availing ITC during the financial year.

subject: Taxation
prompt: M/s. ABC Ltd. purchased machinery worth Rs. 10,00,000 (exclusive of GST at 18%) for factory use. The company capitalized the full invoice value including the GST component of Rs. 1,80,000 in its books of accounts and claimed depreciation on the total capitalized amount under the Income-tax Act, 1961. What is the correct position regarding ITC on this machinery?
optionA: ITC can be claimed fully along with depreciation on the GST component
optionB: ITC cannot be claimed on the GST component since depreciation has been claimed on it under the Income-tax Act
optionC: ITC can be claimed up to 50% of the GST amount and depreciation on the remaining 50%
optionD: ITC can be claimed by reversing the depreciation subsequently within 30 days
answerText: ITC cannot be claimed on the GST component since depreciation has been claimed on it under the Income-tax Act
explanation: As per the proviso to Section 16(3) of the CGST Act, 2017, if the registered person has claimed depreciation on the tax component of the cost of capital goods and plant and machinery under the Income-tax Act, 1961, the input tax on the said component shall not be allowed as ITC.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the time limit for availing Input Tax Credit under Section 16(4) of the CGST Act, 2017 for any invoice or debit note relating to a financial year?
optionA: Due date of filing return for the month of September of the subsequent financial year
optionB: Actual date of filing of the annual return for the relevant financial year or 30th November of the subsequent financial year, whichever is earlier
optionC: 31st December of the subsequent financial year
optionD: Actual date of filing of the annual return for the relevant financial year or 30th November of the subsequent financial year, whichever is later
answerText: Actual date of filing of the annual return for the relevant financial year or 30th November of the subsequent financial year, whichever is earlier
explanation: Section 16(4) mandates that ITC pertaining to any invoice or debit note can be availed up to the earlier of: (i) the thirtieth day of November following the end of financial year to which such invoice/debit note relates, or (ii) the date of furnishing of the relevant annual return.

subject: Taxation
prompt: An invoice was issued by a supplier on 15th October 2024 for FY 2024-25. Due to an oversight, the recipient did not claim the ITC in time. What is the maximum date up to which the recipient can avail ITC on this invoice, assuming the annual return for FY 2024-25 is filed on 31st December 2025?
optionA: 30th November 2025
optionB: 31st December 2025
optionC: 15th October 2025
optionD: 30th September 2025
answerText: 30th November 2025
explanation: As per Section 16(4), the time limit is the earlier of 30th November of the subsequent financial year (30th November 2025) or the date of filing the annual return (31st December 2025). Thus, 30th November 2025 is the correct date.

subject: Taxation
prompt: When goods are received in lots or installments by a registered person, when can the Input Tax Credit be claimed against the tax invoice?
optionA: When the first installment of goods is received
optionB: When the last lot or installment of the goods is received
optionC: Proportionately as and when each lot or installment is received
optionD: Only after the invoice is fully paid within 180 days
answerText: When the last lot or installment of the goods is received
explanation: As per the second proviso to Section 16(2), where the goods against an invoice are received in lots or installments, the registered person shall be entitled to take input tax credit upon the receipt of the last lot or installment.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If a recipient fails to pay to the supplier the value of goods or services along with the tax payable thereon within what period from the date of issue of invoice, an amount equal to the ITC availed is required to be added to output tax liability along with interest?
optionA: 90 days
optionB: 180 days
optionC: 270 days
optionD: 365 days
answerText: 180 days
explanation: As per the second proviso to Section 16(2), if the recipient fails to pay the value of supply plus tax within 180 days from the date of issue of invoice, an amount equal to the ITC availed shall be added to their output tax liability, along with applicable interest.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following inward supplies is NOT blocked under Section 17(5) of the CGST Act, 2017?
optionA: Motor vehicles for transportation of persons having approved seating capacity of not more than 13 persons (including driver), used for general business travel
optionB: Food and beverages, outdoor catering, beauty treatment, health services, except where outward taxable supply is of the same category
optionC: Goods or services used for personal consumption
optionD: Motor vehicles used for transportation of goods
answerText: Motor vehicles used for transportation of goods
explanation: Under Section 17(5), motor vehicles for transportation of goods are explicitly excluded from the blocked credit category, meaning ITC is available on them. The other three options represent blocked credits under Section 17(5).

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under Section 17(5), ITC is available on motor vehicles having a seating capacity of not more than 13 persons (including driver) when they are used for which of the following specified purposes?
optionA: Transportation of employees to and from workplace as a statutory obligation
optionB: Further supply of such vehicles, or transportation of passengers, or imparting training on driving such vehicles
optionC: General conveyance of the Managing Director for business meetings
optionD: Leasing or renting of vehicles for employee recreation trips
answerText: Further supply of such vehicles, or transportation of passengers, or imparting training on driving such vehicles
explanation: Section 17(5)(a) blocks ITC on motor vehicles for transportation of persons <= 13 capacity, except when they are used for making taxable supplies of: (i) further supply of such vehicles; (ii) transportation of passengers; or (iii) imparting training on driving such vehicles.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Rule 42 of the CGST Rules, 2017 deals with the reversal of Input Tax Credit in respect of inputs and input services used for which type of supplies?
optionA: Exclusively taxable supplies
optionB: Exclusively exempt supplies
optionC: Both effected for business purposes and non-business/personal purposes, or partly for taxable and partly for exempt supplies
optionD: Capital goods used for both taxable and exempt supplies
answerText: Both effected for business purposes and non-business/personal purposes, or partly for taxable and partly for exempt supplies
explanation: Rule 42 of the CGST Rules, 2017 prescribes the manner of determination of eligible input tax credit in respect of inputs or input services and reversal thereof when used partly for business/non-business or partly for taxable/exempt supplies. Rule 43 deals with capital goods.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the useful life in quarters considered for calculation of reversal of ITC on capital goods used commonly for taxable and exempt supplies under Rule 43 of the CGST Rules, 2017?
optionA: 20 quarters (5 years)
optionB: 60 quarters (15 years)
optionC: 10 quarters (2.5 years)
optionD: 36 quarters (9 years)
answerText: 20 quarters (5 years)
explanation: Under Rule 43 of the CGST Rules, 2017, the useful life of any capital goods is taken as 5 years from the date of invoice, which equates to 20 quarters. The common ITC attributable to exempt supplies is calculated on a quarterly pro-rata basis over this period.

subject: Taxation
prompt: When a registered person switches from the regular scheme to the Composition Scheme under Section 10, how must they treat the ITC lying in their electronic credit ledger on the day immediately preceding the date of switch?
optionA: They can carry forward and utilize the credit against future composition tax liability
optionB: They must pay an amount equivalent to the credit of input tax in respect of inputs held in stock and inputs contained in semi-finished or finished goods held in stock, and capital goods, by debiting electronic credit or cash ledger
optionC: The credit automatically lapses and cannot be adjusted
optionD: They can claim a full cash refund of the balance from the department
answerText: They must pay an amount equivalent to the credit of input tax in respect of inputs held in stock and inputs contained in semi-finished or finished goods held in stock, and capital goods, by debiting electronic credit or cash ledger
explanation: As per Section 18(4) read with Rule 44, a registered person opting for composition levy must pay an amount equal to the ITC in respect of inputs in stock, semi-finished/finished goods in stock, and capital goods, computed as prescribed, which results in reversal/payment.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Mr. X, an unregistered person, gets registered voluntarily under Section 25(3) on 15th August. What is his entitlement regarding ITC on inputs held in stock on the day immediately preceding the date of grant of registration?
optionA: He is eligible to claim ITC on inputs held in stock and inputs contained in semi-finished or finished goods held in stock on the day preceding registration
optionB: He is eligible to claim ITC on all capital goods and inputs held in stock for the past 2 years
optionC: He is not eligible for any ITC on prior stock since registration is voluntary
optionD: He can claim ITC only if the stock was purchased within 30 days prior to registration
answerText: He is eligible to claim ITC on inputs held in stock and inputs contained in semi-finished or finished goods held in stock on the day preceding registration
explanation: Under Section 18(1)(a), a person who applies for registration within 30 days of becoming liable to register, or voluntarily under Section 25(3), is entitled to take credit of input tax in respect of inputs held in stock and inputs contained in semi-finished or finished goods held in stock on the day immediately preceding the date of grant of registration.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the time limit for issuing the declaration in Form GST ITC-01 by a person who has become liable to register and seeks to claim ITC on inputs held in stock under Section 18(1)?
optionA: Within 30 days from the date of becoming liable to register
optionB: Within 30 days from the date of grant of registration
optionC: Within 90 days from the date of filing the registration application
optionD: Within the due date of filing the annual return
answerText: Within 30 days from the date of grant of registration
explanation: Rule 40(1)(a) requires any person who takes ITC under Section 18(1)(a) or (b) to make a declaration in FORM GST ITC-01 within 30 days from the date of becoming registered (i.e., grant of registration).

subject: Taxation
prompt: If a registered person transfers their business consequent to change in ownership (like amalgamation or merger), how is the unutilized ITC in the electronic credit ledger transferred to the new entity?
optionA: It lapses completely and cannot be transferred
optionB: It is transferred using Form GST ITC-02, provided the scheme of merger/amalgamation has specific provisions for transfer of liabilities
optionC: It can be transferred only with the written permission of the jurisdictional Commissioner
optionD: It is transferred via Form GST ITC-01
answerText: It is transferred using Form GST ITC-02, provided the scheme of merger/amalgamation has specific provisions for transfer of liabilities
explanation: As per Section 18(3) read with Rule 41, in case of amalgamation, merger, demerger, or change in ownership, the unutilized ITC can be transferred to the transferee entity using Form GST ITC-02, provided the restructuring specifics include liabilities.
conceptTags: Section 18(3) | Form GST ITC-02 | Business Reorganization

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following is treated as 'exempt supply' for the purpose of reversal of ITC under Rule 42 and Rule 43?
optionA: Supply of goods or services or both which attracts zero rate of tax
optionB: Supply of goods or services or both which are chargeable to nil rate of tax and non-taxable supplies, including transactions of private securities or sale of land/building (where specified)
optionC: Only supplies made to SEZ units
optionD: Export of goods under bond without payment of IGST
answerText: Supply of goods or services or both which are chargeable to nil rate of tax and non-taxable supplies, including transactions of private securities or sale of land/building (where specified)
explanation: Explanation to Chapter V (Rules 42 and 43) clarifies that 'exempt supply' includes supply of any goods or services or both which attracts nil rate of tax or which may be wholly exempt from tax, and includes non-taxable supply. However, export of goods/services and supplies to SEZ are not treated as exempt supplies for this reversal.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can a registered person claim Input Tax Credit on goods or services used for constructing an immovable property (other than plant and machinery) on their own account, even if such property is used in the course or furtherance of business?
optionA: Yes, full ITC is available since it is used for business
optionB: No, ITC is blocked under Section 17(5)(c) and (d) except in the case of plant and machinery
optionC: Yes, ITC is available up to 50%
optionD: No, ITC is blocked unless capitalization is avoided
answerText: No, ITC is blocked under Section 17(5)(c) and (d) except in the case of plant and machinery
explanation: Under Section 17(5)(c) and (d), ITC is blocked on works contract services and goods/services received by a taxable person for construction of an immovable property on their own account, other than plant and machinery, even if used in the course or furtherance of business.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What happens to the ITC availed on inputs that are subsequently written off or disposed of by way of gift or free samples?
optionA: It can be retained without any reversal
optionB: It must be reversed under Section 17(5)(h)
optionC: It must be claimed as an additional business expense under Income-tax Act
optionD: It is treated as outward taxable supply and tax is paid at market value
answerText: It must be reversed under Section 17(5)(h)
explanation: Section 17(5)(h) explicitly blocks ITC in respect of goods lost, stolen, destroyed, written off or disposed of by way of gift or free samples. Therefore, any ITC availed on such goods must be reversed.

subject: Taxation
prompt: According to Rule 36(4) of the CGST Rules, 2017, Input Tax Credit to be availed by a registered person in respect of invoices/debit notes not reported by suppliers in their GSTR-1/IFF can be availed up to what limit?
optionA: Up to 5% of the eligible credit available in respect of reported invoices
optionB: Up to 10% of the eligible credit available
optionC: Zero percent (ITC can be availed only to the extent details are communicated in GSTR-2B/GSTR-1)
optionD: Up to 20% of the eligible credit available
answerText: Zero percent (ITC can be availed only to the extent details are communicated in GSTR-2B/GSTR-1)
explanation: Rule 36(4) was amended to state that no ITC can be availed by a registered person in respect of invoices/debit notes unless the details of such invoices/debit notes have been furnished by the supplier in GSTR-1/IFF and communicated to the recipient in GSTR-2B. The earlier 20% and 5% conditional buffers are no longer applicable.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following persons is eligible to claim ITC under GST?
optionA: A person paying tax under the Composition Levy under Section 10
optionB: A non-resident taxable person for all inward supplies
optionC: A registered person making taxable supplies including zero-rated supplies
optionD: A person exclusively engaged in supplying goods/services that are wholly exempt from tax
answerText: A registered person making taxable supplies including zero-rated supplies
explanation: Only registered persons making taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) are eligible to claim ITC under Section 16(1). Composition dealers, exempt suppliers, and non-resident taxable persons (except on imported goods) cannot claim regular ITC.

subject: Taxation
prompt: When capital goods on which ITC has been availed are subsequently sold or supplied by a registered person, how is the tax payable on such disposal calculated?
optionA: GST is payable on the full transaction value
optionB: GST is payable on the higher of: (a) tax on the transaction value, or (b) tax on the ITC availed on such capital goods reduced by prescribed percentage points per quarter, whichever is higher
optionC: GST is exempted on second-hand capital goods
optionD: GST is payable only on the book value as per balance sheet
answerText: GST is payable on the higher of: (a) tax on the transaction value, or (b) tax on the ITC availed on such capital goods reduced by prescribed percentage points per quarter, whichever is higher
explanation: As per the proviso to Rule 40(2) / Section 18(6), where capital goods on which ITC has been taken are supplied, the registered person shall pay an amount equal to the ITC taken reduced by 5 percentage points per quarter from the date of invoice, or the tax on transaction value, whichever is higher.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can a principal claim ITC on inputs sent directly to a job worker's premises without the goods first coming to the principal's business premises?
optionA: No, goods must first be received at the principal's factory before being sent to a job worker
optionB: Yes, provided the principal receives the goods back within 1 year for inputs and 3 years for capital goods
optionC: Yes, the principal can take ITC upon receipt of goods by the job worker, provided other conditions are met
optionD: No, ITC is blocked when goods are delivered to third party locations
answerText: Yes, the principal can take ITC upon receipt of goods by the job worker, provided other conditions are met
explanation: As per the first proviso to Section 16(2)(b), for the purpose of claiming ITC, goods delivered by the supplier to a recipient's job worker on the direction of the registered person shall be deemed to have been received by the registered person.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the maximum time period within which inputs sent to a job worker must be brought back to the principal's place of business to avoid being treated as a deemed supply?
optionA: 1 year from the date of receipt by the job worker
optionB: 3 years from the date of receipt by the job worker
optionC: 180 days from the date of dispatch
optionD: 6 months from the end of the financial year
answerText: 1 year from the date of receipt by the job worker
explanation: Under Section 143 of the CGST Act, inputs sent to a job worker must be brought back within 1 year of being sent (or received by the job worker) failing which it shall be deemed to have been supplied by the principal to the job worker on the day the inputs were sent.
conceptTags: Section 143 | Job Work | Time Limit for Inputs

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the time limit for bringing back capital goods (other than moulds and dies, jigs and fixtures, and tools) sent to a job worker, to avoid deemed supply treatment under Section 143?
optionA: 1 year
optionB: 2 years
optionC: 3 years
optionD: 5 years
answerText: 3 years
explanation: Under Section 143(1)(b), capital goods sent to a job worker must be returned to the principal's place of business within 3 years of being sent, otherwise it is treated as a supply from the date of original dispatch.

subject: Taxation
prompt: In cases where a tax demand is confirmed against a taxpayer involving fraud, willful misstatement, or suppression of facts, can the taxpayer pay such tax demand utilizing the balance available in their electronic credit ledger?
optionA: Yes, electronic credit ledger can be used for any tax demand under the Act
optionB: No, Section 49(3) / Rule 86B restrict the use of electronic credit ledger for payment of self-assessed tax only, and Section 49(10) restricts payment of demands arising out of fraud
optionC: Yes, up to 50% of the demand can be paid from the credit ledger
optionD: No, tax demands can only be paid via cash ledger, but interest and penalty can be paid from credit ledger
answerText: No, Section 49(3) / Rule 86B restrict the use of electronic credit ledger for payment of self-assessed tax only, and Section 49(10) restricts payment of demands arising out of fraud
explanation: As per Rule 86(2) and Section 49, the electronic credit ledger cannot be used for payment of any tax demand that has been raised under Section 74 (fraud, willful misstatement, suppression of facts). Such amounts must be paid through the electronic cash ledger.
conceptTags: Section 49 | Electronic Credit Ledger | Tax Dues

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following expenditure incurred by an employer towards employees is NOT blocked for ITC under Section 17(5)?
optionA: Club membership, health and fitness centre membership
optionB: Travel benefits extended to employees on vacation such as Leave Travel Concession (LTC) or home travel concession
optionC: Food and beverages / outdoor catering when supplied under a statutory obligation imposed by any law for the time being in force
optionD: Life insurance and health insurance taken for employees voluntarily
answerText: Food and beverages / outdoor catering when supplied under a statutory obligation imposed by any law for the time being in force
explanation: Section 17(5)(b)(i) blocks ITC on food, beverages, and outdoor catering, but contains an explicit exception: where the government notifies services which are obligatory for an employer to provide to its employees under any law for the time being in force, ITC is allowed.

subject: Taxation
prompt: When a registered person dies, and their legal representative continues the business, can the unutilized ITC lying in the electronic credit ledger of the deceased person be transferred to the legal representative?
optionA: No, ITC lapses upon the death of a proprietor
optionB: Yes, via Form GST ITC-02, unutilized ITC can be transferred to the legal representative in case of death of sole proprietor
optionC: Yes, automatically without filing any specific form
optionD: No, only cash balance can be transferred, not credit balance
answerText: Yes, via Form GST ITC-02, unutilized ITC can be transferred to the legal representative in case of death of sole proprietor
explanation: Under Section 18(3) read with Rule 41, in case of death of a sole proprietor, transfer of business to a legal heir allows the transfer of unutilized ITC using Form GST ITC-02, provided the transferee is registered.
conceptTags: Section 18(3) | Death of Proprietor | Transfer of ITC

subject: Taxation
prompt: If an outward supply made by a registered person is treated as an exempt supply due to a retroactive notification, and the person has already claimed ITC on inputs used for such supply, what is the consequence?
optionA: The ITC already claimed remains fully valid and untouched
optionB: The person is required to reverse the ITC attributable to such exempt supply as per prescribed rules
optionC: The person must surrender their registration certificate
optionD: The person can claim a refund of the tax paid earlier
answerText: The person is required to reverse the ITC attributable to such exempt supply as per prescribed rules
explanation: If a supply becomes exempt subsequently or retrospectively, any ITC claimed earlier on inputs/input services used exclusively or commonly for such supply must be reversed in accordance with the relevant provisions (Rule 42/43).

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can Input Tax Credit be claimed on goods purchased for personal use or consumption of the proprietor or directors, even if paid through the business bank account?
optionA: Yes, because business bank account was used
optionB: No, Section 17(5)(g) blocks ITC on goods or services used for personal consumption
optionC: Yes, provided it is shown as staff welfare in financial statements
optionD: No, unless fringe benefit tax is paid
answerText: No, Section 17(5)(g) blocks ITC on goods or services used for personal consumption
explanation: Section 17(5)(g) specifically blocks ITC in respect of goods or services used for personal consumption. Any purchase for personal use of proprietor, partners, or directors is ineligible for ITC.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under Section 18(2), no ITC can be claimed by a person in respect of any stock of inputs after the expiry of how many months from the date of issue of invoice relating to such inputs?
optionA: 12 months
optionB: 18 months
optionC: 24 months
optionD: 36 months
answerText: 12 months
explanation: As per the proviso to Section 18(2), no ITC under sub-sections (1) (a) and (1) (b) shall be granted in respect of inputs held in stock or inputs contained in semi-finished or finished goods held in stock after the expiry of 1 year (12 months) from the date of issue of invoice relating to such inputs.
conceptTags: Section 18(2) | Stock ITC Time Limit | Registration

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the restriction on the use of the electronic credit ledger under Rule 86B?
optionA: Rule 86B restricts a registered person from using the electronic credit ledger to discharge more than 99% of their output tax liability in cases where taxable supplies exceed Rs. 50 lakhs in a month, subject to specified exceptions.
optionB: Rule 86B completely prohibits the use of electronic credit ledger for all taxpayers with turnover above Rs. 5 crores.
optionC: Rule 86B restricts ITC utilization for exempt supplies only.
optionD: Rule 86B is applicable to all taxpayers irrespective of their tax liability.
answerText: Rule 86B restricts a registered person from using the electronic credit ledger to discharge more than 99% of their output tax liability in cases where taxable supplies exceed Rs. 50 lakhs in a month, subject to specified exceptions.
explanation: Rule 86B of the CGST Rules, 2017 restricts the use of the electronic credit ledger for discharging output tax liability to 99% in cases where the monthly taxable supply exceeds Rs. 50 lakhs, leaving at least 1% to be paid in cash, subject to certain exceptions like income tax paid in previous years.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Zenith Enterprises, a registered GST taxpayer in Maharashtra, purchased a machine for Rs. 20,00,000 plus GST @ 18% on 10th July 2024 for use in its manufacturing unit. The machine was received in two lots: first lot on 1st August 2024 and second lot on 10th August 2024. Zenith Enterprises capitalized the machine in its books including the GST component and claimed depreciation under the Income-tax Act, 1961. The supplier filed GSTR-1 reflecting the invoice on time, and Zenith filed its annual return for FY 2024-25 on 30th September 2025.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the correct date on which Zenith Enterprises is entitled to avail Input Tax Credit on the machinery, assuming all conditions are met otherwise?
optionA: 1st August 2024
optionB: 10th August 2024
optionC: 10th July 2024
optionD: 30th September 2025
answerText: 10th August 2024
explanation: As per the second proviso to Section 16(2), when goods are received in lots or installments, ITC can be availed only upon the receipt of the last lot or installment. Since the second lot was received on 10th August 2024, ITC entitlement arises on that date.
conceptTags: Section 16(2) | Goods in Lots | Capital Goods

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can Zenith Enterprises claim ITC on the GST component of Rs. 3,60,000 paid on the machinery?
optionA: Yes, full ITC can be claimed alongside depreciation
optionB: No, because depreciation has been claimed on the GST component under the Income-tax Act
optionC: Yes, 50% ITC and 50% depreciation can be claimed simultaneously
optionD: No, because machinery is blocked under Section 17(5)
answerText: No, because depreciation has been claimed on the GST component under the Income-tax Act
explanation: Under the proviso to Section 16(3), if a registered person claims depreciation on the tax component of the cost of capital goods under the Income-tax Act, 1961, the input tax credit on such tax component is not allowed.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What would have been the last date for availing ITC on this machinery under Section 16(4), had they not claimed depreciation?
optionA: 30th November 2025
optionB: 31st December 2025
optionC: 30th September 2025
optionD: 31st March 2025
answerText: 30th November 2025
explanation: As per Section 16(4), the time limit for availing ITC for FY 2024-25 is the earlier of 30th November 2025 or the date of filing the annual return (30th September 2025). Wait, since 30th September 2025 is earlier than 30th November 2025, let's check: the annual return was filed on 30th September 2025. Therefore, the earlier of 30th November 2025 and 30th September 2025 is 30th September 2025.
conceptTags: Section 16(4) | Time Limit | Annual Return Date

subject: Taxation
prompt: If Zenith Enterprises had used this machinery exclusively for manufacturing goods that are wholly exempt from GST, would they have been eligible for ITC?
optionA: Yes, full ITC is available on machinery used for exempt supplies
optionB: No, ITC is not available on inputs or capital goods used exclusively for making exempt supplies
optionC: Yes, up to 50% ITC is allowed
optionD: No, but a cash refund of the tax paid can be claimed
answerText: No, ITC is not available on inputs or capital goods used exclusively for making exempt supplies
explanation: Under Section 17(2), where the goods or services are used by the registered person partly for effecting taxable supplies and partly for exempt supplies, the ITC is restricted to the quantum attributable to taxable supplies. If used exclusively for exempt supplies, no ITC is available.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Sharma commenced a trading business in Delhi and obtained registration under GST on 1st October 2024. Prior to obtaining registration, he had purchased inputs in stock worth Rs. 5,00,000 (exclusive of GST @ 12%) on 15th August 2024. He also purchased a car for business use on 10th September 2024 for Rs. 10,00,000 plus GST @ 28% (seating capacity 5 persons) and capitalized it. On 1st December 2024, he sent inputs worth Rs. 2,00,000 to a job worker for processing.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Is Mr. Sharma eligible to claim ITC on the inputs held in stock on 30th September 2024 (the day preceding registration)?
optionA: No, because he was unregistered at the time of purchase
optionB: Yes, under Section 18(1)(a) for inputs held in stock on the day preceding registration, provided invoices are within 1 year
optionC: Yes, for all purchases made in the last 3 years
optionD: No, unless he pays a special composition fee
answerText: Yes, under Section 18(1)(a) for inputs held in stock on the day preceding registration, provided invoices are within 1 year
explanation: Under Section 18(1)(a), a person who registers within 30 days of becoming liable is entitled to ITC on inputs held in stock on the day preceding registration, provided the invoice date is not older than 1 year.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the correct treatment of GST paid on the car purchased on 10th September 2024 for business use (seating capacity 5 persons)?
optionA: Full ITC can be claimed since it is used for business
optionB: ITC is blocked under Section 17(5)(a) as it is a motor vehicle for transportation of persons <= 13 capacity and not used for specified exceptions
optionC: ITC can be claimed up to 50%
optionD: ITC can be claimed if depreciation is foregone
answerText: ITC is blocked under Section 17(5)(a) as it is a motor vehicle for transportation of persons <= 13 capacity and not used for specified exceptions
explanation: Under Section 17(5)(a), ITC is blocked on motor vehicles for transportation of persons with seating capacity <= 13 persons, unless used for specified exempt purposes like further supply, passenger transport, or driving school. General business travel does not qualify.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the maximum time limit within which the inputs sent to the job worker on 1st December 2024 must be brought back to Mr. Sharma's premises to avoid deemed supply?
optionA: 6 months
optionB: 1 year
optionC: 3 years
optionD: 180 days
answerText: 1 year
explanation: As per Section 143(1)(a), inputs sent to a job worker must be brought back within 1 year of being sent, failing which the transaction is deemed to be a supply from the date of dispatch.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which form is required to be filed by Mr. Sharma to claim ITC on inputs held in stock prior to registration?
optionA: FORM GST ITC-01
optionB: FORM GST ITC-02
optionC: FORM GST ITC-03
optionD: FORM GST REG-01
answerText: FORM GST ITC-01
explanation: Rule 40(1)(a) requires a registered person claiming ITC under Section 18(1) on inputs in stock to file a declaration in FORM GST ITC-01 within 30 days of becoming registered.
conceptTags: Rule 40 | FORM GST ITC-01 | Stock ITC

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Apex Technologies Ltd., a registered software company in Bengaluru, undertook construction of an office building on its own account during FY 2024-25. It incurred expenses on works contract services of Rs. 50,00,000 (plus GST 18%) and purchased cement and iron bars locally worth Rs. 30,00,000 (plus GST 18%) used in the construction. Simultaneously, Apex Technologies Ltd. purchased computers worth Rs. 20,00,000 (plus GST 18%) for office use. The company also provided outdoor catering for its employees during an annual corporate event, incurring Rs. 5,00,000 plus GST 18%.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Is Apex Technologies Ltd. eligible to claim ITC on works contract services used for the construction of its office building?
optionA: Yes, because the office building is used for business
optionB: No, ITC is blocked under Section 17(5)(c) on works contract services for construction of immovable property, other than plant and machinery
optionC: Yes, up to 50%
optionD: No, unless capitalization is avoided
answerText: No, ITC is blocked under Section 17(5)(c) on works contract services for construction of immovable property, other than plant and machinery
explanation: Under Section 17(5)(c), ITC is blocked in respect of works contract services when supplied for construction of immovable property, other than plant and machinery, even if used for business.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the eligibility of ITC on cement and iron bars purchased for the construction of the office building?
optionA: Full ITC is available
optionB: ITC is blocked under Section 17(5)(d) for goods received for construction of immovable property on own account
optionC: ITC is available subject to 180 days payment condition
optionD: ITC is available since they are inputs
answerText: ITC is blocked under Section 17(5)(d) for goods received for construction of immovable property on own account
explanation: Section 17(5)(d) blocks ITC on goods or services received by a taxable person for construction of an immovable property on their own account (including building), other than plant and machinery.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can Apex Technologies Ltd. claim ITC on the computers purchased for office use?
optionA: No, computers are treated as capital goods and ineligible for ITC
optionB: Yes, computers are not blocked under Section 17(5) and qualify as capital goods/inputs used in business
optionC: Yes, but only if depreciation is not claimed
optionD: No, electronics are blocked
answerText: Yes, computers are not blocked under Section 17(5) and qualify as capital goods/inputs used in business
explanation: Computers used in business are eligible capital goods/inputs for ITC. They are not covered under any blocked credit category in Section 17(5), provided depreciation is not claimed on the tax component.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the tax treatment of GST paid on outdoor catering services for the corporate event?
optionA: ITC can be claimed fully
optionB: ITC is blocked under Section 17(5)(b)(ii) unless outward supply is of the same category or provided under statutory obligation
optionC: ITC can be claimed up to 50%
optionD: ITC is allowed as staff welfare expense
answerText: ITC is blocked under Section 17(5)(b)(ii) unless outward supply is of the same category or provided under statutory obligation
explanation: Section 17(5)(b)(ii) blocks ITC on outdoor catering, food, and beverages, except where an outward taxable supply of the same category is made or where it is obligatory for an employer to provide under any law.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Beta Industries operates a factory making both taxable goods and exempt goods. During the month of October 2024, it received common inputs worth Rs. 10,00,000 on which total GST paid was Rs. 1,80,000. Total turnover of Beta Industries for the month was Rs. 50,00,000, out of which taxable supplies amounted to Rs. 30,00,000, exempt supplies amounted to Rs. 15,00,000, and zero-rated supplies (exports) amounted to Rs. 5,00,000. Additionally, Beta Industries had availed ITC of Rs. 25,000 on inputs that were destroyed by fire during the month.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which rule governs the reversal of common Input Tax Credit on inputs and input services used for both taxable and exempt supplies?
optionA: Rule 36
optionB: Rule 42
optionC: Rule 43
optionD: Rule 44
answerText: Rule 42
explanation: Rule 42 of the CGST Rules, 2017 prescribes the formula and procedure for determination of common ITC attributable to exempt supplies and its subsequent reversal.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the treatment of ITC amounting to Rs. 25,000 on inputs destroyed by fire?
optionA: It can be retained in full
optionB: It must be reversed under Section 17(5)(h) since goods were destroyed
optionC: It can be carried forward as loss
optionD: It is adjusted against export benefits
answerText: It must be reversed under Section 17(5)(h) since goods were destroyed
explanation: Under Section 17(5)(h), ITC in respect of goods lost, stolen, destroyed, written off or disposed of by way of gift or free samples is blocked and must be reversed.

subject: Taxation
prompt: In computing the proportion of exempt supplies for Rule 42, how are zero-rated supplies (exports) treated?
optionA: Treated as exempt supplies
optionB: Treated as taxable supplies (not included in exempt turnover for reversal computation)
optionC: Ignored entirely from total turnover
optionD: Treated separately as non-business supplies
answerText: Treated as taxable supplies (not included in exempt turnover for reversal computation)
explanation: For the purpose of Rule 42, zero-rated supplies (exports and supplies to SEZ) are treated as taxable supplies and are not counted as exempt supplies while calculating the reversal ratio.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If Beta Industries fails to pay the supplier for the common inputs within 180 days from the invoice date, what action is required?
optionA: Nothing, since goods were received
optionB: An amount equal to ITC availed plus applicable interest must be added to output tax liability
optionC: Registration is liable to cancellation
optionD: Supplier must refund the tax
answerText: An amount equal to ITC availed plus applicable interest must be added to output tax liability
explanation: As per the second proviso to Section 16(2), if payment is not made within 180 days, an amount equal to ITC availed must be added to output tax liability along with interest.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Delta Logistics, a registered transport operator, was previously registered under the regular GST scheme. On 1st November 2024, Delta Logistics opted to switch to the Composition Scheme under Section 10. On 31st October 2024, the electronic credit ledger of Delta Logistics showed a balance of Rs. 1,50,000. On the same date, they held inputs in stock valued at Rs. 10,00,000 (GST paid @ 18%, total Rs. 1,80,000) and capital goods on which ITC of Rs. 3,00,000 had been claimed earlier (purchased 1 year ago).

subject: Taxation
prompt: What are the statutory obligations of Delta Logistics regarding the unutilized ITC and ITC on stock upon opting for the Composition Scheme?
optionA: They can continue to carry forward the credit balance
optionB: They must pay an amount equivalent to the ITC in respect of inputs in stock and capital goods by debiting electronic credit or cash ledger, and remaining credit lapses
optionC: They can claim a cash refund of Rs. 1,50,000
optionD: The credit ledger balance is transferred to the Government revenue without any calculation
answerText: They must pay an amount equivalent to the ITC in respect of inputs in stock and capital goods by debiting electronic credit or cash ledger, and remaining credit lapses
explanation: Under Section 18(4) read with Rule 44, when shifting to the composition scheme, the registered person must pay an amount equivalent to the ITC on inputs in stock and capital goods (reduced by percentage points), and the remaining balance in the electronic credit ledger lapses.

subject: Taxation
prompt: How is the ITC reversal on capital goods calculated when shifting to the composition scheme under Rule 44?
optionA: Full ITC originally claimed must be paid back
optionB: ITC is calculated on the remaining useful life in months/quarters on a pro-rata basis
optionC: No reversal is required for capital goods
optionD: 50% of the original ITC is reversed flat
answerText: ITC is calculated on the remaining useful life in months/quarters on a pro-rata basis
explanation: Under Rule 44(6), for capital goods held in stock, the ITC taken is computed on the basis of remaining useful life in quarters (taking useful life as 5 years / 20 quarters), and the proportionate amount is added to liability.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the time limit for filing the stock declaration in FORM GST ITC-03 when opting for the composition scheme?
optionA: Within 30 days from the date of switch
optionB: Within 60 days from the commencement of the relevant financial year or within 30 days of opting for composition
optionC: Within 180 days
optionD: Along with the annual return
answerText: Within 60 days from the commencement of the relevant financial year or within 30 days of opting for composition
explanation: Rule 44(4) mandates that the details of stock and capital goods for payment/reversal under Section 18(4) must be furnished in FORM GST ITC-03 within 60 days of the commencement of the relevant financial year or within 30 days of opting for composition levy.
conceptTags: Rule 44 | FORM GST ITC-03 | Time Limit

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can a composition taxpayer under Section 10 issue a tax invoice to their customers to pass on Input Tax Credit?
optionA: Yes, exactly like a regular taxpayer
optionB: No, a composition taxpayer cannot collect tax from recipients nor issue a tax invoice; they must issue a bill of supply
optionC: Yes, but only for inter-state supplies
optionD: No, but they can issue a delivery challan
answerText: No, a composition taxpayer cannot collect tax from recipients nor issue a tax invoice; they must issue a bill of supply
explanation: As per Section 10(4) read with Section 31(2), a composition taxpayer cannot collect any tax from the recipient on supplies made by them and cannot issue a tax invoice; instead, they must issue a Bill of Supply and cannot pass on any ITC.
conceptTags: Section 10 | Composition Scheme | Bill of Supply

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the threshold limit for registration under GST for a person making exclusive taxable supplies of goods in the State of Manipur?
optionA: Rs. 10 Lakhs
optionB: Rs. 20 Lakhs
optionC: Rs. 40 Lakhs
optionD: Rs. 50 Lakhs
answerText: Rs. 10 Lakhs
explanation: As per Section 22 read with Notification No. 10/2019-CT, Manipur is listed among the Special Category States where the threshold limit for exclusive supply of goods is Rs. 10 lakhs. Therefore, Rs. 10 Lakhs is the correct threshold limit.
conceptTags: Threshold Limit | Goods | Special Category States

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following persons is mandatorily required to obtain registration under Section 24 of the CGST Act, 2017, irrespective of the turnover threshold?
optionA: Persons making intra-state taxable supplies of goods
optionB: Casual taxable persons making taxable supplies
optionC: Persons making inter-state supplies of goods with aggregate turnover up to Rs. 20 lakhs
optionD: Persons making taxable supplies of goods on behalf of other taxable persons as an agent with turnover below Rs. 10 lakhs
answerText: Casual taxable persons making taxable supplies
explanation: Section 24 mandates compulsory registration for casual taxable persons making taxable supplies, regardless of their turnover. Inter-state supply of goods up to Rs. 20 lakhs is exempt from mandatory registration vide Notification No. 10/2017-IT, and agents making taxable supplies on behalf of others are also compulsorily registrable without threshold benefit.
conceptTags: Compulsory Registration | Casual Taxable Person | Section 24

subject: Taxation
prompt: Within how many days from the date on which liability to register arises must a person apply for GST registration?
optionA: 15 days
optionB: 30 days
optionC: 45 days
optionD: 60 days
answerText: 30 days
explanation: According to Section 25(1) of the CGST Act, 2017, every person who becomes liable to registration under section 22 or section 24 shall apply for registration within 30 days from the date on which he becomes liable to registration.
conceptTags: Time Limit | Application for Registration | Section 25

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the validity period of the certificate of registration granted to a Casual Taxable Person (CTP)?
optionA: 90 days from registration
optionB: Maximum period of 90 days or period specified in the application, whichever is earlier
optionC: 1 year from the date of issue
optionD: Till the completion of business event
answerText: Maximum period of 90 days or period specified in the application, whichever is earlier
explanation: As per Section 27(1), the certificate of registration issued to a casual taxable person shall be valid for a period specified in the application for registration or 90 days from the effective date of registration, whichever is earlier.
conceptTags: Casual Taxable Person | Validity Period | Section 27

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can a supplier having multiple places of business in the same State obtain separate registrations for each such place of business?
optionA: No, only one state registration is permitted per entity
optionB: Yes, provided all such places of business are engaged in identical supply of goods
optionC: Yes, under Section 25(2), a person having multiple places of business in a State may be granted a separate registration for each such place of business
optionD: Yes, but only if aggregate turnover exceeds Rs. 1.5 crores
answerText: Yes, under Section 25(2), a person having multiple places of business in a State may be granted a separate registration for each such place of business
explanation: Section 25(2) of the CGST Act allows a person having multiple places of business in a State or Union territory to be granted a separate registration for each such place of business, subject to prescribed conditions.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the consequence if the proper officer fails to take any action on an application for registration within the prescribed time limit, and no notice is issued?
optionA: The application is deemed to be rejected
optionB: The registration is deemed to have been granted after 7 working days from application submission
optionC: The registration is deemed to have been granted after verification of Aadhaar
optionD: The registration shall be deemed to have been granted after the expiry of the period specified under rule 9(5)
answerText: The registration shall be deemed to have been granted after the expiry of the period specified under rule 9(5)
explanation: Under Rule 9(5) of the CGST Rules, 2017, if the proper officer fails to take any action within the prescribed period of 3 days (or 7 days if Aadhaar authentication is required/failed), the application for grant of registration shall be deemed to have been approved.
conceptTags: Deemed Registration | CGST Rules | Proper Officer

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following entities is required to obtain a Unique Identity Number (UIN) under Section 25(9)?
optionA: Any regular supplier with turnover exceeding Rs. 40 lakhs
optionB: Specialized agency of the United Nations Organisation or any Multilateral Financial Institution
optionC: Casual taxable person operating in multiple states
optionD: Non-resident taxable person providing OIDAR services
answerText: Specialized agency of the United Nations Organisation or any Multilateral Financial Institution
explanation: Section 25(9) provides that a specialized agency of the United Nations Organisation or any Multilateral Financial Institution and Organization notified under the United Nations (Privileges and Immunities) Act, 1947, Consulate or Embassy of foreign countries shall obtain a Unique Identity Number (UIN) for claiming refund of taxes.

subject: Taxation
prompt: In cases where Aadhaar authentication is successfully completed, from which date does the registration become effective?
optionA: Date of submission of application if applied within 30 days of liability
optionB: Date of approval by the proper officer
optionC: Date of generation of application reference number (ARN)
optionD: Date of authentication or 30th day from submission, whichever is earlier
answerText: Date of submission of application if applied within 30 days of liability
explanation: As per Rule 10 of CGST Rules, where Aadhaar authentication is successfully completed, the application is deemed approved and registration is effective from the date on which the person became liable to registration, provided the application was submitted within 30 days.

subject: Taxation
prompt: An electronic commerce operator (ECO) who is required to collect tax at source under Section 52 must obtain:
optionA: Voluntary registration only if turnover crosses Rs. 20 lakhs
optionB: Compulsory registration under Section 24 irrespective of threshold
optionC: UIN instead of regular GSTIN
optionD: Registration only if operating in more than two States
answerText: Compulsory registration under Section 24 irrespective of threshold
explanation: Section 24(x) explicitly mandates that every electronic commerce operator who is required to collect tax at source under section 52 must obtain registration compulsorily, regardless of their aggregate turnover threshold.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the time limit for a Non-Resident Taxable Person (NRTP) to apply for registration prior to the commencement of business?
optionA: At least 5 days prior
optionB: At least 15 days prior
optionC: At least 30 days prior
optionD: No prior time limit is prescribed
answerText: At least 5 days prior
explanation: As per Section 27(1) read with Rule 12, a non-resident taxable person shall make an application for registration at least 5 days prior to the commencement of business.
conceptTags: Non-Resident Taxable Person | Advance Application | Section 27

subject: Taxation
prompt: When a registered person applies for cancellation of registration, what happens to their tax liability for the period prior to cancellation?
optionA: It gets waived automatically
optionB: It remains unaffected and the person is liable to pay all pending dues
optionC: It is transferred to the successor automatically
optionD: It can only be recovered after 5 years
answerText: It remains unaffected and the person is liable to pay all pending dues
explanation: Cancellation of registration under Section 29 does not affect the liability of the taxable person to pay tax and other dues for any period prior to the date of cancellation, which remains recoverable.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can a person having multiple business verticals within a State obtain separate registrations for each vertical under the CGST Act, 2017?
optionA: No, separate registration is allowed only for different States
optionB: Yes, under Section 25(2) proviso, a person having multiple business verticals within a State may obtain separate registration for each vertical
optionC: Yes, but only if turnover of each vertical exceeds Rs. 10 Crores
optionD: No, business verticals provision was omitted/amended
answerText: Yes, under Section 25(2) proviso, a person having multiple business verticals within a State may obtain separate registration for each vertical
explanation: The proviso to Section 25(2) allows a person having multiple business verticals within a State or Union territory to be granted a separate registration for each business vertical, subject to prescribed conditions.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following actions can be taken by the proper officer if a registered person has contravened provisions relating to anti-profiteering or furnishing returns?
optionA: Directly seize all bank accounts without notice
optionB: Cancel the registration under Section 29(2)
optionC: Force conversion of registration into UIN
optionD: Impose imprisonment without trial
answerText: Cancel the registration under Section 29(2)
explanation: Under Section 29(2) of the CGST Act, the proper officer may cancel the registration of a person who has contravened such provisions of the Act or the rules made thereunder as may be prescribed.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the penalty for failure to obtain registration when legally mandated under the CGST Act, 2017?
optionA: Fixed penalty of Rs. 5,000
optionB: 10% of the tax due or Rs. 10,000, whichever is higher
optionC: Imprisonment for 7 years straight
optionD: Confiscation of all personal assets
answerText: 10% of the tax due or Rs. 10,000, whichever is higher
explanation: As per Section 122(1)(i), a taxable person who supplies any taxable goods or services without issue of invoice or suppresses turnover is liable to a penalty of Rs. 10,000 or an amount equivalent to the tax evaded or tax short deducted/collected, whichever is higher.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If a registered person dies, what happens to their GST registration?
optionA: It continues in the name of the deceased indefinitely
optionB: It is cancelled immediately and cannot be transferred
optionC: The legal heir/transferee is permitted to carry on business under the same registration/amended registration
optionD: It is converted into a casual taxable person registration
answerText: The legal heir/transferee is permitted to carry on business under the same registration/amended registration
explanation: As per Section 29(1)(a) read with Rule 21A/relevant rules, in the event of the death of a sole proprietor, the business can be continued by the legal heir, and application for amendment/transfer is made so that the transferee can operate.
conceptTags: Death of Proprietor | Transfer of Business | Section 29

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following is NOT required to obtain GST registration?
optionA: An agriculturist, to the extent of supply of produce out of cultivation of land
optionB: An Input Service Distributor (ISD)
optionC: A person making inter-state supplies of taxable goods with turnover of Rs. 25 lakhs
optionD: A non-resident taxable person making taxable supplies
answerText: An agriculturist, to the extent of supply of produce out of cultivation of land
explanation: Section 23(1)(a) explicitly states that an agriculturist shall not be liable to registration to the extent of supply of produce out of cultivation of land. The others listed are either compulsorily registrable or crossed thresholds.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the threshold limit for registration for a person engaged exclusively in intra-state taxable supply of goods in the State of Arunachal Pradesh?
optionA: Rs. 10 Lakhs
optionB: Rs. 20 Lakhs
optionC: Rs. 40 Lakhs
optionD: Rs. 50 Lakhs
answerText: Rs. 20 Lakhs
explanation: Notification No. 10/2019-CT specifies Rs. 20 lakhs threshold for states like Arunachal Pradesh for exclusive supply of goods (unlike Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura which have Rs. 10 lakhs).

subject: Taxation
prompt: When can a person voluntarily obtain registration under Section 25(3), even though their aggregate turnover is below the threshold limit?
optionA: Only after obtaining prior permission from the GST Council
optionB: At any time, and all provisions of the Act shall apply to such registered person
optionC: Only if they make inter-state supplies to unregistered persons
optionD: Voluntary registration is not permitted under CGST Act
answerText: At any time, and all provisions of the Act shall apply to such registered person
explanation: Section 25(3) allows a person not liable to be registered under section 22 or section 24 to get registered voluntarily, and once registered, all provisions of the Act apply as if they are a regular taxable person.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the status of a registration certificate if the proper officer initiates suo-motu cancellation proceedings?
optionA: It remains fully active until final order is passed
optionB: It may be suspended by the proper officer pending the cancellation proceedings
optionC: It is automatically revoked within 24 hours
optionD: It is converted into voluntary registration
answerText: It may be suspended by the proper officer pending the cancellation proceedings
explanation: Rule 21A of the CGST Rules provides that where the proper officer has reasons to believe that the registration of a person is liable to be cancelled, he may suspend the registration pending the cancellation proceedings.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Who among the following is empowered to notify categories of services where tax on intra-state supplies shall be paid by the electronic commerce operator?
optionA: Central Government on the recommendations of the GST Council
optionB: Commissioner of State Tax independently
optionC: Jurisdictional Superintendent
optionD: Reserve Bank of India
answerText: Central Government on the recommendations of the GST Council
explanation: Section 9(5) of the CGST Act empowers the Government, on the recommendations of the Council, to specify categories of services the tax on intra-state supplies of which shall be paid by the electronic commerce operator.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can a person having a PAN in India obtain multiple GST registrations across different States without having multiple business verticals?
optionA: No, only one GSTIN per PAN is allowed nationwide
optionB: Yes, a person having multiple places of business in different States must obtain a separate registration for each such State
optionC: Yes, but only if turnover exceeds Rs. 10 Crores per State
optionD: No, inter-state operations require only one central registration
answerText: Yes, a person having multiple places of business in different States must obtain a separate registration for each such State
explanation: As per Section 25(1), a person obtaining registration has to obtain a separate registration for each State or Union territory in which he has a business and is liable to register, meaning multiple state registrations per PAN are mandatory.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the time period within which a person whose registration has been cancelled suo-motu can apply for revocation of cancellation?
optionA: Within 15 days of service of cancellation order
optionB: Within 30 days of service of cancellation order (extendable by Commissioner)
optionC: Within 90 days without any extension
optionD: Within 1 year from the date of issue
answerText: Within 30 days of service of cancellation order (extendable by Commissioner)
explanation: Under Section 30 of the CGST Act, any registered person whose registration is cancelled suo-motu may apply for revocation within 30 days from the date of service of the cancellation order, which can be extended by the Commissioner/Additional/Joint Commissioner.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which form is used for submitting an application for registration under CGST Rules, 2017?
optionA: FORM GST REG-01
optionB: FORM GST REG-06
optionC: FORM GST REG-16
optionD: FORM GST REG-21
answerText: FORM GST REG-01
explanation: Rule 8 prescribes FORM GST REG-01 for making an application for electronic registration. FORM GST REG-06 is the certificate of registration, and FORM GST REG-16 is for cancellation.
conceptTags: Registration Forms | FORM GST REG-01 | CGST Rules

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the threshold limit for registration for a person engaged exclusively in intra-state supply of services in the State of Uttarakhand?
optionA: Rs. 10 Lakhs
optionB: Rs. 20 Lakhs
optionC: Rs. 40 Lakhs
optionD: Rs. 50 Lakhs
answerText: Rs. 20 Lakhs
explanation: For services, the threshold limit is generally Rs. 20 lakhs (or Rs. 10 lakhs for specific special category states). Uttarakhand has a threshold of Rs. 20 lakhs for services (and Rs. 40 lakhs for goods).

subject: Taxation
prompt: In the case of transfer of business as a going concern, what happens to the unutilized input tax credit (ITC) lying in the electronic credit ledger of the transferor?
optionA: It lapses permanently
optionB: It can be refunded in cash to the transferor
optionC: It is transferred to the transferee through FORM GST ITC-02
optionD: It must be reversed and cannot be utilized
answerText: It is transferred to the transferee through FORM GST ITC-02
explanation: As per Section 18(3) read with Rule 41, in case of amalgamation, merger, or transfer of business as a going concern, the unutilized ITC can be transferred to the transferee using FORM GST ITC-02.
conceptTags: Transfer of Business | Input Tax Credit | FORM GST ITC-02

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the consequence of furnishing false information during the registration process under the CGST Act?
optionA: Only a warning letter is issued
optionB: The proper officer can reject or cancel the registration and penalize the applicant
optionC: The registration is automatically upgraded to voluntary status
optionD: No action can be taken after ARN generation
answerText: The proper officer can reject or cancel the registration and penalize the applicant
explanation: Furnishing false information or suppression of facts during registration empowers the proper officer to reject or cancel registration and initiate penal proceedings under the Act.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following is considered while computing 'aggregate turnover' for determining registration threshold?
optionA: Central tax, State tax, Integrated tax, and Cess
optionB: Exempt supplies of goods and services
optionC: Inward supplies on which tax is payable under reverse charge basis
optionD: Value of goods supplied directly from customs bonded warehouses before clearance
answerText: Exempt supplies of goods and services
explanation: As per Section 2(6), 'aggregate turnover' includes taxable supplies, exempt supplies, exports, and inter-state supplies of persons having the same PAN, computed on all-India basis, excluding central/state/integrated taxes and cess, and reverse charge inward supplies.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can a person having multiple registrations within the same State transfer ITC from one GSTIN to another GSTIN of the same entity?
optionA: No, transfer of ITC between different GSTINS of same PAN in same state is not allowed
optionB: Yes, through FORM GST ITC-02A
optionC: Yes, automatically without any form
optionD: Only with High Court permission
answerText: Yes, through FORM GST ITC-02A
explanation: Rule 41A allows a registered person who has obtained separate registrations for multiple places of business within the same State to transfer unutilized ITC lying in one GSTIN to another GSTIN using FORM GST ITC-02A.
conceptTags: Transfer of ITC | Same State | FORM GST ITC-02A

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the requirement for a Non-Resident Taxable Person regarding furnishing of returns?
optionA: Annual return only in FORM GSTR-9
optionB: Quarterly return in FORM GSTR-4
optionC: Monthly return in FORM GSTR-5
optionD: No returns are required to be filed
answerText: Monthly return in FORM GSTR-5
explanation: Section 39(5) mandates that a non-resident taxable person shall furnish a return in FORM GSTR-5 for every calendar month within 20 days after the end of a calendar month or within 7 days after the last day of validity of registration.
conceptTags: Non-Resident Taxable Person | Returns | FORM GSTR-5

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which authority issues the registration certificate in FORM GST REG-06?
optionA: GST Council Secretariat
optionB: The proper officer after approval of application
optionC: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) Chairman directly
optionD: Registrar of Companies
answerText: The proper officer after approval of application
explanation: The proper officer grants the certificate of registration in FORM GST REG-06 after successful verification and approval of the registration application.
conceptTags: Registration Certificate | FORM GST REG-06 | Proper Officer

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Apex Traders, a sole proprietorship firm based in Jaipur, Rajasthan, is engaged in trading of electronic appliances. During the financial year, the aggregate turnover of M/s. Apex Traders crossed Rs. 40 Lakhs on 15th October. The proprietor, Mr. Anand, failed to apply for registration within the statutory 30-day period and ultimately submitted an online application for registration on 25th November. Mr. Anand also wishes to know whether his Jaipur branch (warehouse) requires a separate registration within the same State.

subject: Taxation
prompt: By what date was M/s. Apex Traders required to apply for GST registration?
optionA: 15th October
optionB: 30th October
optionC: 14th November
optionD: 25th November
answerText: 14th November
explanation: Since the liability to register arose on 15th October, as per Section 25(1), the application must be made within 30 days from that date. Counting 30 days from 15th October leads to 14th November.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the threshold limit applicable to M/s. Apex Traders for registration of goods in Rajasthan?
optionA: Rs. 10 Lakhs
optionB: Rs. 20 Lakhs
optionC: Rs. 40 Lakhs
optionD: Rs. 1.5 Crores
answerText: Rs. 40 Lakhs
explanation: Notification No. 10/2019-CT prescribes a threshold limit of Rs. 40 Lakhs for exclusive supply of goods in states like Rajasthan, provided certain conditions (such as not dealing in notified goods like ice cream, pan masala, tobacco) are met.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Is Mr. Anand legally mandated to obtain a separate registration for his warehouse in Jaipur under the CGST Act?
optionA: Yes, every branch or warehouse must have a separate registration mandatorily
optionB: No, obtaining separate registration for multiple places of business within the same State is optional under Section 25(2)
optionC: Yes, if turnover of warehouse exceeds Rs. 20 Lakhs
optionD: No, intra-state warehouses are prohibited from registration
answerText: No, obtaining separate registration for multiple places of business within the same State is optional under Section 25(2)
explanation: Under Section 25(2) of the CGST Act, a person having multiple places of business in the same State *may* be granted a separate registration for each place of business, making it an option rather than a mandatory requirement.
conceptTags: Multiple Places of Business | Same State | Section 25

subject: Taxation
prompt: Assuming Mr. Anand successfully completes Aadhaar authentication, what will be the effective date of registration for M/s. Apex Traders?
optionA: 15th October (date on which liability to register arose)
optionB: 25th November (date of submission of application)
optionC: Date of approval by proper officer
optionD: 1st April of the financial year
answerText: 25th November (date of submission of application)
