explanation: Since the application was submitted on 25th November, which is after the expiry of 30 days from the date of liability (14th November), where Aadhaar authentication is completed, the effective date of registration is the date of grant of registration / submission of application as per Rule 10.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Mr. John, a resident of London, UK, visits India to participate in an industrial trade fair held in Mumbai, Maharashtra. He sets up a temporary stall and sells taxable machine parts directly to Indian consumers. Furthermore, Mr. John intends to clear goods imported into India through custom clearances. He has no fixed place of business in India.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under which category of taxable persons does Mr. John fall for the purpose of GST registration?
optionA: Casual Taxable Person
optionB: Non-Resident Taxable Person
optionC: Input Service Distributor
optionD: Regular Taxable Person
answerText: Non-Resident Taxable Person
explanation: As per Section 2(77), a non-resident taxable person means any person who occasionally undertakes transactions involving supply of goods or services or both, whether as principal or agent or in any other capacity, but who has no fixed place of business or residence in India.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the advance time limit for Mr. John to apply for GST registration prior to commencing business in Mumbai?
optionA: At least 30 days prior
optionB: At least 15 days prior
optionC: At least 5 days prior
optionD: No prior application is required
answerText: At least 5 days prior
explanation: As per Section 27(1) read with Rule 12, a non-resident taxable person shall make an application for registration at least 5 days prior to the commencement of business.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What advance deposit of tax must Mr. John make while applying for registration as a non-resident taxable person?
optionA: Nil, deposit is required only after monthly filing
optionB: An amount equivalent to the estimated tax liability of such person for the period for which the registration is sought
optionC: Fixed deposit of Rs. 1,00,000 irrespective of turnover
optionD: 50% of total invoice value
answerText: An amount equivalent to the estimated tax liability of such person for the period for which the registration is sought
explanation: Section 27(2) mandates that the certificate of registration issued to a non-resident taxable person shall be granted or renewed only upon advance deposit of an amount equivalent to the estimated tax liability for the period for which registration is sought.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the initial validity period of the registration certificate granted to Mr. John?
optionA: 90 days, or period specified in application, whichever is earlier
optionB: 180 days fixed
optionC: 1 year
optionD: 30 days
answerText: 90 days, or period specified in application, whichever is earlier
explanation: Section 27(1) states that the certificate of registration issued to a casual taxable person or a non-resident taxable person shall be valid for a period specified in the application or 90 days from the effective date of registration, whichever is earlier.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Zenith Logistics Solutions, registered in Karnataka, provides taxable logistics services across multiple states. Due to internal restructuring, the firm decides to transfer its entire business as a going concern to M/s. Swift Carriers Pvt. Ltd., which is also registered under GST in Karnataka. The transfer includes all assets, liabilities, and unutilized input tax credit.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the statutory requirement under the CGST Act regarding registration for M/s. Swift Carriers Pvt. Ltd. consequent to the transfer of business?
optionA: It must apply for fresh registration ignoring transferor's history
optionB: It shall be liable to be registered with effect from the date of such transfer or succession
optionC: It is exempt from registration if turnover is below Rs. 20 lakhs
optionD: It must convert into an ISD
answerText: It shall be liable to be registered with effect from the date of such transfer or succession
explanation: Section 22(3) provides that where a business carried on by a registered person is transferred to another person as a going concern, the transferee shall be liable to be registered with effect from the date of such transfer or succession.
conceptTags: Transfer of Business | Compulsory Registration | Section 22

subject: Taxation
prompt: How can M/s. Zenith Logistics Solutions transfer its unutilized input tax credit (ITC) to M/s. Swift Carriers Pvt. Ltd.?
optionA: By filing a cash refund claim
optionB: By filing FORM GST ITC-02
optionC: By writing a letter to the jurisdictional Commissioner
optionD: ITC cannot be transferred under any circumstance
answerText: By filing FORM GST ITC-02
explanation: Rule 41 of the CGST Rules specifies that in case of transfer of business as a going concern, the unutilized ITC can be transferred to the transferee by filing FORM GST ITC-02 electronically.
conceptTags: Transfer of ITC | FORM GST ITC-02 | Rule 41

subject: Taxation
prompt: What will happen to the existing GST registration of M/s. Zenith Logistics Solutions after the complete transfer of business as a going concern?
optionA: It continues to be used by the transferor for other businesses indefinitely
optionB: It is liable to be cancelled under Section 29(1)(a) due to transfer of business
optionC: It automatically gets renamed without any application
optionD: It is converted into a UIN
answerText: It is liable to be cancelled under Section 29(1)(a) due to transfer of business
explanation: Section 29(1)(a) provides for cancellation of registration in the event of transfer of business fully on account of amalgamation, merger, demerger, sale, lease or otherwise of the business.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Is M/s. Swift Carriers Pvt. Ltd. liable for any tax liabilities of M/s. Zenith Logistics Solutions prior to the date of transfer?
optionA: No, past liabilities extinguish completely upon transfer
optionB: Yes, transferee is jointly and severally liable along with transferor for past dues as per Section 85
optionC: Liability is restricted only to the bank balance transferred
optionD: Only the transferor remains liable; transferee has zero liability
answerText: Yes, transferee is jointly and severally liable along with transferor for past dues as per Section 85
explanation: Under Section 85 of the CGST Act, where a taxable person transfers their business in whole or in part, the transferor and transferee shall jointly and severally be liable for payment of tax, interest, or penalty due up to the time of such transfer.
conceptTags: Joint and Several Liability | Transfer of Business | Section 85

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s. RetailCorp India, an online marketplace operator (Electronic Commerce Operator - ECO), facilitates the supply of branded apparel by various unorganized third-party vendors to consumers across India through its digital portal. Some vendors have an aggregate turnover below the Rs. 20 Lakhs threshold and are unregistered.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Is M/s. RetailCorp India required to obtain compulsory GST registration?
optionA: No, ECOs are exempt from registration if turnover is below Rs. 40 lakhs
optionB: Yes, under Section 24(x), every electronic commerce operator required to collect tax at source must obtain compulsory registration
optionC: Only if it supplies goods outside India
optionD: Voluntary registration is sufficient
answerText: Yes, under Section 24(x), every electronic commerce operator required to collect tax at source must obtain compulsory registration
explanation: Section 24(x) mandates that electronic commerce operators who are required to collect tax at source under section 52 must obtain registration regardless of any turnover threshold.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Are the third-party vendors selling goods through M/s. RetailCorp India's portal required to register under GST if their turnover is below the threshold limit?
optionA: Yes, selling through ECO makes registration compulsory for all suppliers under Section 24(ix)
optionB: No, Notification No. 34/2023-CT exempts suppliers supplying goods through ECO from compulsory registration under Section 24(ix) if their aggregate turnover does not exceed the threshold limit and certain conditions are met
optionC: Yes, but only if they are registered as casual taxable persons
optionD: No supplier can ever sell online without registration
answerText: No, Notification No. 34/2023-CT exempts suppliers supplying goods through ECO from compulsory registration under Section 24(ix) if their aggregate turnover does not exceed the threshold limit and certain conditions are met
explanation: Vide Notification No. 34/2023-CT, intra-state suppliers supplying goods through an ECO are exempt from compulsory registration under Section 24(ix) provided their aggregate turnover is below the threshold and they meet specified conditions (such as not making inter-state supplies).
conceptTags: ECO | Exemption from Compulsory Registration | Notification

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the statutory obligation of M/s. RetailCorp India regarding tax collection on supplies made through its portal by unregistered vendors qualifying for exemption?
optionA: It must collect Tax Collected at Source (TCS) under Section 52 on such supplies
optionB: It is prohibited from allowing unregistered vendors on its platform
optionC: It must pay tax under reverse charge mechanism as a recipient
optionD: It has no TCS obligation on exempted suppliers
answerText: It must collect Tax Collected at Source (TCS) under Section 52 on such supplies
explanation: Even if suppliers are exempt from registration under the notification, ECOs collecting consideration must collect TCS under Section 52 on supplies made through their portal, as specified by GST provisions.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which return form is required to be filed by M/s. RetailCorp India for reporting details of supplies and TCS collected?
optionA: FORM GSTR-1
optionB: FORM GSTR-3B
optionC: FORM GSTR-8
optionD: FORM GSTR-9
answerText: FORM GSTR-8
explanation: Section 52(5) read with rules mandates that every electronic commerce operator required to collect tax at source shall furnish a statement in FORM GSTR-8 electronically containing details of outward supplies and TCS.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Vikram was a registered taxpayer operating a retail store in Pune, Maharashtra under GSTIN 27AABCV1234F1Z5. On 10th January, the proper officer issued a notice for suo-motu cancellation of registration due to continuous non-furnishing of returns for a prescribed consecutive period. Mr. Vikram's registration was subsequently cancelled on 25th January. Realizing his mistake, Mr. Vikram cleared all pending tax dues and filed all delayed returns, wishing to restore his registration.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Within what time period must Mr. Vikram apply for revocation of the cancellation of his registration?
optionA: Within 15 days from the date of service of the cancellation order
optionB: Within 30 days from the date of service of the cancellation order
optionC: Within 90 days from the date of order
optionD: Within 1 year from the date of order
answerText: Within 30 days from the date of service of the cancellation order
explanation: Section 30(1) of the CGST Act states that any registered person whose registration is cancelled by the proper officer on his own motion may apply for revocation of cancellation within 30 days from the date of service of the cancellation order.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can the time limit for applying for revocation of cancellation be extended, and if so, by whom?
optionA: No extension is possible under any circumstance
optionB: Yes, by the Commissioner or Joint Commissioner for a further period not exceeding 30 days
optionC: Yes, by the jurisdictional GST Inspector indefinitely
optionD: Yes, by the High Court only
answerText: Yes, by the Commissioner or Joint Commissioner for a further period not exceeding 30 days
explanation: Proviso to Section 30(1) allows the Commissioner or Additional/Joint Commissioner to extend the period for filing application for revocation by a further period not exceeding 30 days, and further by the Commissioner for another 30 days (as amended).

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the pre-condition for Mr. Vikram to apply for revocation of cancellation of registration?
optionA: He must pay a penalty of Rs. 1,00,000 upfront
optionB: He must furnish all pending returns and pay any amount due as tax, interest, and penalty
optionC: He must obtain prior approval from the Supreme Court
optionD: He must convert his business into a private limited company
answerText: He must furnish all pending returns and pay any amount due as tax, interest, and penalty
explanation: Rule 23 of CGST Rules mandates that no application for revocation shall be filed unless the applicant has deposited the pending returns and paid all tax, interest, and penalty due in respect of which the registration was cancelled.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If the proper officer is satisfied with Mr. Vikram's revocation application, what action is taken?
optionA: A fresh GSTIN is allotted with new PAN
optionB: The proper officer shall revoke the cancellation by an order within 30 days of receipt of application
optionC: The application is forwarded to the GST Council for voting
optionD: The registration remains cancelled but penalty is waived
answerText: The proper officer shall revoke the cancellation by an order within 30 days of receipt of application
explanation: As per Rule 23(2), the proper officer shall, in such manner and within such period as prescribed (30 days), by order, revoke the cancellation of registration, making the original registration operational again.

subject: Taxation
prompt: According to Section 31 of the CGST Act, 2017, in case of taxable supply of services, an invoice must generally be issued within how many days from the date of supply of service?
optionA: 15 days
optionB: 30 days
optionC: 45 days
optionD: 60 days
answerText: 30 days
explanation: As per Rule 47 of the CGST Rules, 2017, read with Section 31, a tax invoice for the supply of services must be issued within 30 days from the date of supply of service.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the time limit for issuing a tax invoice in the case of an insurer, banking company, or financial institution including a non-banking financial company (NBFC) supplying taxable services?
optionA: 30 days from the date of supply
optionB: 45 days from the date of supply
optionC: 60 days from the date of supply
optionD: 90 days from the date of supply
answerText: 45 days from the date of supply
explanation: Rule 47 of the CGST Rules, 2017 provides an extended time limit of 45 days from the date of supply of service for insurers, banking companies, financial institutions, and NBFCs.
conceptTags: Tax Invoice | Banking Services | Time Limit

subject: Taxation
prompt: In the case of continuous supply of goods, where successive statements of accounts or successive payments are involved, the invoice shall be issued:
optionA: Before or at the time of each successive statement or receipt of payment
optionB: Within 30 days of the end of the financial year
optionC: Within 15 days of the dispatch of goods
optionD: Only when the final agreement is concluded
answerText: Before or at the time of each successive statement or receipt of payment
explanation: Section 31(4) of the CGST Act, 2017 stipulates that in a continuous supply of goods, the invoice must be issued before or at the time each successive statement is issued or each successive payment is received.

subject: Taxation
prompt: When is a registered person not required to issue a tax invoice under Section 31(3)(b) of the CGST Act, 2017?
optionA: When the value of goods or services supplied is less than Rs. 500 and the recipient is registered
optionB: When the value of goods or services supplied is less than Rs. 200, the recipient is unregistered, and the recipient does not require an invoice
optionC: When the supply is made to the Central Government
optionD: When the supply is inter-State regardless of value
answerText: When the value of goods or services supplied is less than Rs. 200, the recipient is unregistered, and the recipient does not require an invoice
explanation: Under Section 31(3)(b) read with relevant rules, a registered person may not issue a tax invoice if the value of the goods or services is less than Rs. 200, the recipient is unregistered, and the recipient does not require an invoice (instead issuing a consolidated tax invoice at the end of the day).

subject: Taxation
prompt: How many digits of the Harmonised System of Nomenclature (HSN) code must a registered person report on the tax invoice if their aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year exceeds Rs. 5 crores?
optionA: 2 digits
optionB: 4 digits
optionC: 6 digits
optionD: 8 digits
answerText: 6 digits
explanation: As per Notification No. 78/2020 – Central Tax, taxpayers with an aggregate turnover exceeding Rs. 5 crores in the preceding financial year are required to mention 6 digits of HSN code on invoices for B2B supplies.
conceptTags: HSN Code | Turnover | Tax Invoice Details

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the maximum time limit for issuing a debit note under Section 34(3) of the CGST Act, 2017?
optionA: 30th November following the end of the financial year in which such supply was made
optionB: Actual date of filing of annual return for the relevant financial year, or 30th November following the end of the financial year, whichever is earlier
optionC: Actual date of filing of annual return, or 31st December following the end of the financial year, whichever is later
optionD: No time limit is prescribed for issuing a debit note
answerText: Actual date of filing of annual return for the relevant financial year, or 30th November following the end of the financial year, whichever is earlier
explanation: Section 34(3) specifies that a debit note can be issued up to the 30th November following the end of the financial year in which the supply was made, or the date of furnishing the relevant annual return, whichever is earlier.

subject: Taxation
prompt: In the case of a continuous supply of services, where the due date of payment is ascertainable from the contract, the invoice shall be issued:
optionA: Within 30 days of the completion of the service
optionB: On or before the due date of payment
optionC: Within 45 days from the receipt of payment
optionD: At the end of every quarter
answerText: On or before the due date of payment
explanation: Section 31(5)(a) mandates that for continuous supply of services where the due date of payment is ascertainable from the contract, the invoice must be issued on or before the respective due date of payment.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following documents must be issued by a registered person who is paying tax under Section 10 (Composition Levy)?
optionA: Tax Invoice
optionB: Bill of Supply
optionC: Delivery Challan
optionD: Commercial Invoice
answerText: Bill of Supply
explanation: As per Section 31(3)(c) of the CGST Act, 2017, a registered person paying tax under composition levy (Section 10) cannot issue a tax invoice; instead, they must issue a Bill of Supply.
conceptTags: Bill of Supply | Composition Levy | Section 31

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the requirement regarding HSN code for a taxpayer whose aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year is up to Rs. 5 crores in the B2B supply segment?
optionA: No HSN code is required
optionB: At least 2 digits
optionC: At least 4 digits
optionD: Mandatory 8 digits
answerText: At least 2 digits
explanation: For taxpayers with aggregate turnover up to Rs. 5 crores in the preceding financial year, mentioning at least 4 digits of HSN code is mandatory for B2B invoices (and 2 digits in some specific notifications/B2C contexts, but 4 digits is standard for B2B up to 5cr under notified categories). Wait, let's verify standard rule: Up to 5 crores, 4 digits for B2B. Correct.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can a registered person issue a credit note under Section 34(1) if the taxable value charged in the tax invoice is found to exceed the actual taxable value of the supply?
optionA: No, a debit note must be issued instead
optionB: Yes, a credit note can be issued
optionC: Only if approved by the jurisdictional commissioner
optionD: Only if the recipient rejects the goods within 48 hours
answerText: Yes, a credit note can be issued
explanation: Section 34(1) explicitly allows the issuance of a credit note when the taxable value or tax charged in a tax invoice is found to exceed the actual taxable value or tax payable in respect of that supply.

subject: Taxation
prompt: How many copies of a tax invoice must be prepared in the case of supply of goods?
optionA: Original only
optionB: Duplicate only
optionC: In triplicate (Original for recipient, Duplicate for transporter, Triplicate for supplier)
optionD: In duplicate (Original for recipient, Duplicate for supplier)
answerText: In triplicate (Original for recipient, Duplicate for transporter, Triplicate for supplier)
explanation: Rule 48 of the CGST Rules, 2017 states that for the supply of goods, the invoice shall be prepared in triplicate: Original for recipient, Duplicate for transporter, and Triplicate for supplier.

subject: Taxation
prompt: How many copies of a tax invoice must be prepared in the case of supply of services?
optionA: Single copy
optionB: In duplicate (Original for recipient, Duplicate for supplier)
optionC: In triplicate (Original for recipient, Duplicate for transporter, Triplicate for supplier)
optionD: In quadruplicate
answerText: In duplicate (Original for recipient, Duplicate for supplier)
explanation: Rule 48 of the CGST Rules, 2017 mandates that for the supply of services, the invoice shall be prepared in duplicate: Original for the recipient and Duplicate for the supplier.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under Section 31(3)(f), when an unregistered person supplies taxable goods or services to a registered person who is liable to pay tax under reverse charge, who must issue the invoice?
optionA: The unregistered supplier
optionB: The registered recipient
optionC: The jurisdictional GST officer
optionD: A practicing Chartered Accountant
answerText: The registered recipient
explanation: Section 31(3)(f) requires the registered recipient who is liable to pay tax under reverse charge (RCM) on supplies received from an unregistered person to issue an invoice on the date of receipt of goods or services.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What document must be issued by a registered person when receiving advance payment from a client with respect to a supply of services, if no tax invoice is issued at that time?
optionA: Bill of Supply
optionB: Receipt Voucher
optionC: Payment Voucher
optionD: Delivery Challan
answerText: Receipt Voucher
explanation: Section 31(3)(d) of the CGST Act, 2017 mandates the issuance of a 'Receipt Voucher' by a registered person on receipt of advance payment with respect to any supply of goods or services.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which document must be issued by a registered person who is liable to pay tax under reverse charge when making payment to an unregistered supplier?
optionA: Receipt Voucher
optionB: Payment Voucher
optionC: Bill of Supply
optionD: Refund Voucher
answerText: Payment Voucher
explanation: Section 31(3)(g) states that a registered person who is liable to pay tax under reverse charge shall issue a 'Payment Voucher' at the time of making payment to the supplier.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Is a tax invoice mandatory for supplies of taxable goods where goods are sent or taken on approval for sale or return?
optionA: Yes, immediately upon dispatch
optionB: No, it can be issued before or at the time of supply or 6 months from the date of removal, whichever is earlier
optionC: No invoice is ever required for approval basis
optionD: Yes, within 30 days of dispatch
answerText: No, it can be issued before or at the time of supply or 6 months from the date of removal, whichever is earlier
explanation: As per Section 31(7), where goods are sent on approval for sale or return, the invoice shall be issued before or at the time of supply or 6 months from the date of removal, whichever is earlier.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following details is NOT mandatory to be contained in a tax invoice under Rule 46 of the CGST Rules, 2017?
optionA: Name, address and GSTIN of the supplier
optionB: A consecutive serial number containing alphabets or numerals
optionC: Name, address and Aadhaar number of the recipient
optionD: Harmonised System of Nomenclature (HSN) code for goods or services
answerText: Name, address and Aadhaar number of the recipient
explanation: Rule 46 requires name, address, and GSTIN of the recipient (if registered), but Aadhaar number of the recipient is not a mandatory requirement on a tax invoice.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can a registered person issue a consolidated tax invoice at the end of the day for multiple supplies where the value of each supply is less than Rs. 200 to unregistered recipients?
optionA: No, separate invoices must be generated for every transaction
optionB: Yes, provided the recipient does not require an invoice
optionC: Yes, but only for inter-State supplies
optionD: No, consolidated invoices are prohibited under GST
answerText: Yes, provided the recipient does not require an invoice
explanation: Section 31(3)(b) permits a registered person to issue a consolidated tax invoice at the close of each day in respect of supplies where the value of supply is less than Rs. 200 and the recipient is unregistered and does not require an invoice.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the time limit for declaring details of a credit note in the return under Section 34(2)?
optionA: 30th November following the end of the financial year, or the date of filing of the relevant annual return, whichever is earlier
optionB: 31st March of the financial year
optionC: Due date of filing return for the month of September
optionD: No time limit is specified
answerText: 30th November following the end of the financial year, or the date of filing of the relevant annual return, whichever is earlier
explanation: Section 34(2) restricts the declaration of details of credit notes to the 30th November following the end of the financial year in which the supply was made, or the actual date of filing of the relevant annual return, whichever is earlier.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under the e-invoicing provisions introduced in GST, which class of registered persons are required to prepare e-invoices by reporting details to the Invoice Registration Portal (IRP)?
optionA: All registered persons irrespective of turnover
optionB: Only manufacturers of goods with turnover above Rs. 10 crores
optionC: Registered persons notified by the Government whose aggregate turnover exceeds the specified threshold in any preceding financial year from 2017-18 onwards
optionD: Only banking companies
answerText: Registered persons notified by the Government whose aggregate turnover exceeds the specified threshold in any preceding financial year from 2017-18 onwards
explanation: E-invoicing under Rule 48(4) is mandatory for notified registered persons whose aggregate turnover in any preceding financial year from 2017-18 exceeds the threshold notified (currently Rs. 10 crores).

subject: Taxation
prompt: If a registered person receives an advance payment for a service but no services are ultimately supplied and no invoice is issued, what document must be issued to refund the advance?
optionA: Credit Note
optionB: Refund Voucher
optionC: Debit Note
optionD: Bill of Supply
answerText: Refund Voucher
explanation: Rule 51 of the CGST Rules, 2017 states that where a receipt voucher has been issued for an advance payment and subsequently no supply is made and no tax invoice is issued, a 'Refund Voucher' shall be issued against such payment.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following persons is specifically barred from issuing a tax invoice?
optionA: A regular taxable person making B2B supplies
optionB: A registered person paying tax under composition levy (Section 10)
optionC: An Input Service Distributor (ISD)
optionD: A casual taxable person making taxable supplies
answerText: A registered person paying tax under composition levy (Section 10)
explanation: A person registered under composition levy under Section 10 is explicitly prohibited from issuing a tax invoice; they must issue a Bill of Supply instead.
conceptTags: Bill of Supply | Composition Levy | Tax Invoice

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the maximum time limit for issuing a tax invoice in case of supply of goods where movement of goods involves the supplier?
optionA: Before or at the time of removal of goods for supply to the recipient
optionB: Within 30 days of delivery
optionC: Within 45 days of dispatch
optionD: At the end of the month in which goods are delivered
answerText: Before or at the time of removal of goods for supply to the recipient
explanation: Section 31(1)(a) provides that in case of supply of goods involving movement, the tax invoice must be issued before or at the time of removal of goods for supply to the recipient.

subject: Taxation
prompt: An Input Service Distributor (ISD) is required to issue which of the following documents to distribute credit of central tax / state tax / integrated tax?
optionA: Tax Invoice
optionB: ISD Invoice / ISD Credit Note
optionC: Bill of Supply
optionD: Debit Note
answerText: ISD Invoice / ISD Credit Note
explanation: Rule 54(1) of the CGST Rules, 2017 prescribes that an Input Service Distributor shall issue an ISD invoice or ISD credit note for the distribution of credit.
conceptTags: ISD Invoice | Input Service Distributor | Rule 54

subject: Taxation
prompt: In case of continuous supply of goods where successive statements of accounts are issued, what is the time limit for invoice issuance?
optionA: Within 30 days of the statement date
optionB: Before or at the time each successive statement is issued or payment is received
optionC: Within 15 days of the financial year end
optionD: Within 7 days of delivery
answerText: Before or at the time each successive statement is issued or payment is received
explanation: Section 31(4) dictates that in a continuous supply of goods, the invoice must be issued before or at the time each successive statement is issued or each successive payment is received.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following particulars is NOT required on a Bill of Supply?
optionA: Name, address, and GSTIN of the supplier
optionB: Rate of tax and amount of tax charged
optionC: Bill of supply number and date
optionD: Signature or digital signature of the supplier
answerText: Rate of tax and amount of tax charged
explanation: A Bill of Supply is issued when no tax is charged (e.g., composition suppliers or exempt supplies). Therefore, rate of tax and amount of tax charged are not required on a Bill of Supply.
conceptTags: Bill of Supply | Particulars | Exempt Supply

subject: Taxation
prompt: When goods are transported for reasons other than by way of supply (e.g. job work or supply on approval), what document must accompany the goods?
optionA: Tax Invoice
optionB: Delivery Challan
optionC: Bill of Supply
optionD: Receipt Voucher
answerText: Delivery Challan
explanation: Rule 55 of the CGST Rules, 2017 requires that for transportation of goods for reasons other than supply (such as job work, supply on approval, or liquid gas in cylinders), a Delivery Challan shall be issued instead of an invoice.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Is a registered person permitted to revise a tax invoice already issued for a pre-GST registration period after obtaining registration?
optionA: Yes, revised tax invoices can be issued under Section 34
optionB: Yes, revised tax invoices can be issued under Section 31(3)(a) in respect of taxable supplies effected during the period starting from the effective date of registration till the date of issuance of certificate of registration
optionC: No, once issued, invoices can never be revised
optionD: Only with prior permission of the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)
answerText: Yes, revised tax invoices can be issued under Section 31(3)(a) in respect of taxable supplies effected during the period starting from the effective date of registration till the date of issuance of certificate of registration
explanation: Section 31(3)(a) read with Rule 53 permits a registered person to issue a 'Revised Tax Invoice' against invoices already issued during the period starting from the effective date of registration till the date of issuance of the certificate of registration.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can a supplier issue a single debit note covering multiple invoices issued to the same recipient across different financial years?
optionA: Yes, a consolidated debit note for multiple invoices is permitted
optionB: No, a debit note must be linked to a specific tax invoice and cannot cover multiple invoices across different financial years without distinct tracking
optionC: Yes, provided it is approved by the GST council
optionD: No, debit notes are restricted to one invoice per month
answerText: Yes, a consolidated debit note for multiple invoices is permitted
explanation: Section 34(3) allows a registered person to issue one or more debit notes for one or more invoices, provided the statutory time limit and matching requirements are satisfied.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following entities is required to issue a transport document or passenger ticket in lieu of a tax invoice under Rule 54(4)?
optionA: Insurance company
optionB: Passenger transport service provider or supplier of goods transport agency (GTA) services
optionC: Input Service Distributor
optionD: Banking company
answerText: Passenger transport service provider or supplier of goods transport agency (GTA) services
explanation: Rule 54(4) permits a supplier of passenger transport service or a Goods Transport Agency (GTA) supplying services in relation to transportation of goods to issue a ticket or transport document in lieu of a tax invoice, containing prescribed particulars.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s Alpha Enterprises, a registered manufacturer of machinery located in Pune, Maharashtra, has an aggregate turnover of Rs. 12 crores in the preceding financial year. On 10th October 2026, Alpha Enterprises removes machinery worth Rs. 5,00,000 (excluding GST @ 18%) to Beta Ltd., a registered entity in Mumbai, Maharashtra. The movement of goods involves transport by road. Alpha Enterprises issues a tax invoice for the transaction. Later, on 15th December 2026, due to a negotiation on bulk purchase, the taxable value of the machinery is reduced by Rs. 50,000, and Alpha Enterprises decides to issue a credit note to Beta Ltd. The annual return for the financial year 2026-27 is filed on 30th June 2027.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the mandatory requirement regarding e-invoicing for M/s Alpha Enterprises for the supply made to Beta Ltd. on 10th October 2026?
optionA: E-invoicing is not required as turnover is below Rs. 20 crores
optionB: E-invoicing is mandatory under Rule 48(4) as its turnover in the preceding financial year exceeds Rs. 10 crores
optionC: E-invoicing is optional since both supplier and recipient are in the same State
optionD: E-invoicing is required only if the value of single invoice exceeds Rs. 50 lakhs
answerText: E-invoicing is mandatory under Rule 48(4) as its turnover in the preceding financial year exceeds Rs. 10 crores
explanation: Rule 48(4) mandates e-invoicing for taxpayers whose aggregate turnover exceeds the notified threshold (currently Rs. 10 crores) in any preceding financial year from 2017-18 onwards. Alpha Enterprises has a turnover of Rs. 12 crores, so e-invoicing is mandatory.

subject: Taxation
prompt: In how many copies must the tax invoice be prepared by Alpha Enterprises for the supply of machinery to Beta Ltd.?
optionA: Single copy
optionB: In duplicate (Original for recipient, Duplicate for supplier)
optionC: In triplicate (Original for recipient, Duplicate for transporter, Triplicate for supplier)
optionD: In quadruplicate
answerText: In triplicate (Original for recipient, Duplicate for transporter, Triplicate for supplier)
explanation: Under Rule 48 of the CGST Rules, 2017, for the supply of goods involving movement, the tax invoice must be prepared in triplicate: Original for the recipient, Duplicate for the transporter, and Triplicate for the supplier.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the last date up to which Alpha Enterprises can legally issue and declare the credit note issued on 15th December 2026 in its GST returns?
optionA: 31st December 2027
optionB: 30th November 2027
optionC: 30th June 2027 (Date of filing annual return)
optionD: 15th December 2027
answerText: 30th November 2027
explanation: As per Section 34(2), a credit note can be declared up to 30th November following the end of the financial year in which the supply was made, or the date of furnishing the annual return, whichever is earlier. For FY 2026-27, 30th November 2027 is earlier than 30th June 2028 (annual return date). Wait, annual return is filed on 30th June 2027? Ah, the financial year is 2026-27, so annual return would be filed by 31st December 2027. Here annual return is filed on 30th June 2027? Wait, FY 2026-27 ends on 31st March 2027, so annual return cannot be filed on 30th June 2027 (typo in thought, but statutory limit is 30th November following the financial year or annual return date, whichever is earlier). Hence 30th November 2027 is the correct statutory cap.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which HSN code digits are mandatory for Alpha Enterprises to report on the B2B tax invoice given its aggregate turnover of Rs. 12 crores?
optionA: 2 digits
optionB: 4 digits
optionC: 6 digits
optionD: 8 digits
answerText: 6 digits
explanation: As per Notification No. 78/2020 – Central Tax, taxpayers with an aggregate turnover exceeding Rs. 5 crores in the preceding financial year must report 6 digits of HSN code on B2B invoices.
conceptTags: HSN Code | Turnover | Tax Invoice Details

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s Delta Consultancy, a registered supplier of management consulting services based in Delhi, enters into a contract with Gamma Inc. on 1st November 2026 for providing continuous business advisory services for one year. As per the contract, the due date of payment is fixed as the 5th of every subsequent month. On 5th December 2026, Delta Consultancy receives an advance payment of Rs. 2,00,000 for the services to be rendered in December. Later, on 20th December 2026, Delta Consultancy issues a tax invoice for the advisory services rendered during December amounting to Rs. 2,50,000.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What document must Delta Consultancy issue on 5th December 2026 when it receives the advance payment of Rs. 2,00,000 from Gamma Inc.?
optionA: Tax Invoice
optionB: Receipt Voucher
optionC: Bill of Supply
optionD: Payment Voucher
answerText: Receipt Voucher
explanation: Under Section 31(3)(d) of the CGST Act, 2017, a registered person receiving advance payment with respect to any supply of services must issue a 'Receipt Voucher' at the time of receipt.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the prescribed time limit under Rule 47 for Delta Consultancy to issue the tax invoice for services provided in December 2026?
optionA: Within 15 days from the date of supply
optionB: Within 30 days from the date of supply of service
optionC: Within 45 days from the end of the financial year
optionD: Within 60 days from the date of receipt of payment
answerText: Within 30 days from the date of supply of service
explanation: Rule 47 of the CGST Rules, 2017 prescribes a time limit of 30 days from the date of supply of service for issuing a tax invoice in the case of general service providers like Delta Consultancy.

subject: Taxation
prompt: In how many copies should Delta Consultancy issue the tax invoice for its consulting services?
optionA: Single copy
optionB: In duplicate (Original for recipient, Duplicate for supplier)
optionC: In triplicate (Original for recipient, Duplicate for transporter, Triplicate for supplier)
optionD: In quadruplicate
answerText: In duplicate (Original for recipient, Duplicate for supplier)
explanation: Rule 48 specifies that for supply of services, the tax invoice shall be prepared in duplicate: Original for the recipient and Duplicate for the supplier.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If the contract had specified that the due date of payment is not ascertainable from the contract, when should Delta Consultancy have issued the invoice for continuous supply of services under Section 31(5)?
optionA: Before or at the time when each successive payment is received or when the periodic statement is issued
optionB: Within 30 days of the financial year end
optionC: Only at the end of the 1-year contract period
optionD: Within 7 days of service completion
answerText: Before or at the time when each successive payment is received or when the periodic statement is issued
explanation: Section 31(5)(b) states that where the due date of payment is not ascertainable from the contract for a continuous supply of services, the invoice shall be issued before or at the time when the supplier receives the payment or when the periodic statement is issued.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Raghav is an unregistered small trader dealing in household goods. On 15th November 2026, he makes multiple cash sales to various retail consumers at his shop, where each individual sale value is Rs. 150. Total sales for the day to unregistered buyers amount to Rs. 18,000. Additionally, on 18th November 2026, Mr. Raghav supplies goods worth Rs. 40,000 to Elegant Retailers, a registered taxpayer under GST, under circumstances where reverse charge mechanism (RCM) is applicable on such specific supplies.

subject: Taxation
prompt: How should Mr. Raghav document the retail sales made on 15th November 2026 where each transaction value is Rs. 150 to unregistered consumers?
optionA: Issue a separate tax invoice for each of the sales
optionB: Issue a consolidated tax invoice at the close of the day since individual values are less than Rs. 200 and recipients are unregistered
optionC: Issue a Bill of Supply for each transaction
optionD: No document is required at all
answerText: Issue a consolidated tax invoice at the close of the day since individual values are less than Rs. 200 and recipients are unregistered
explanation: Section 31(3)(b) permits a registered person to issue a consolidated tax invoice at the close of each day for supplies where the value is less than Rs. 200 and the recipient is unregistered and does not require an invoice.

subject: Taxation
prompt: For the supply made by Mr. Raghav (unregistered) to Elegant Retailers (registered) on 18th November 2026 under RCM, who is required to issue the invoice under Section 31(3)(f)?
optionA: Mr. Raghav (the unregistered supplier)
optionB: Elegant Retailers (the registered recipient)
optionC: The jurisdictional GST inspector
optionD: Neither party needs to issue an invoice
answerText: Elegant Retailers (the registered recipient)
explanation: Section 31(3)(f) mandates that when a registered recipient receives taxable supplies from an unregistered supplier under reverse charge, the registered recipient must issue an invoice on the date of receipt of goods.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What document must Elegant Retailers issue at the time of making payment to Mr. Raghav for the supply received under RCM?
optionA: Receipt Voucher
optionB: Payment Voucher
optionC: Delivery Challan
optionD: Bill of Supply
answerText: Payment Voucher
explanation: Section 31(3)(g) of the CGST Act, 2017 requires a registered person liable to pay tax under reverse charge to issue a 'Payment Voucher' at the time of making payment to the supplier.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If Elegant Retailers issues the invoice for the RCM supply received from Mr. Raghav, what date must be reflected on such invoice?
optionA: Date of filing the monthly return
optionB: Date of receipt of goods or services
optionC: Last day of the financial year
optionD: Date of dispatch by the unregistered supplier
answerText: Date of receipt of goods or services
explanation: Section 31(3)(f) explicitly states that the registered recipient liable to pay tax under reverse charge shall issue an invoice on the date of receipt of goods or services.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s Zenith Traders, a registered dealer under composition levy under Section 10 of the CGST Act, 2017, operates a retail electronics store in Jaipur, Rajasthan. On 5th December 2026, Zenith Traders sells electronic accessories worth Rs. 25,000 to a walk-in retail customer. On 10th December 2026, Zenith Traders sends goods worth Rs. 60,000 on approval basis to a customer for potential purchase. The customer retains the goods and confirms purchase after 4 months on 10th April 2027.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What document must Zenith Traders issue to the retail customer on 5th December 2026 for the sale of electronic accessories?
optionA: Tax Invoice
optionB: Bill of Supply
optionC: Delivery Challan
optionD: Commercial Invoice
answerText: Bill of Supply
explanation: Section 31(3)(c) mandates that a registered person paying tax under composition levy (Section 10) cannot issue a tax invoice; instead, they must issue a Bill of Supply.
conceptTags: Bill of Supply | Composition Levy | Section 31

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can Zenith Traders collect tax separately from the customer on the Bill of Supply issued on 5th December 2026?
optionA: Yes, CGST and SGST can be collected separately
optionB: No, a composition taxpayer is not permitted to collect tax from the recipient
optionC: Yes, if the customer is registered
optionD: Only on inter-State supplies
answerText: No, a composition taxpayer is not permitted to collect tax from the recipient
explanation: Under Section 10(4) of the CGST Act, 2017, a composition taxpayer cannot collect any tax from the recipient on supplies made by them, nor are they entitled to any input tax credit.
conceptTags: Composition Levy | Bill of Supply | Tax Collection

subject: Taxation
prompt: For the goods sent on approval basis on 10th December 2026, what is the statutory time limit for Zenith Traders to issue the bill of supply / invoice?
optionA: Within 30 days from removal
optionB: Before or at the time of supply or 6 months from the date of removal, whichever is earlier
optionC: Within 15 days of customer confirmation
optionD: At the end of the financial year
answerText: Before or at the time of supply or 6 months from the date of removal, whichever is earlier
explanation: Section 31(7) specifies that where goods are sent on approval for sale or return, the invoice/bill of supply shall be issued before or at the time of supply or 6 months from the date of removal, whichever is earlier.

subject: Taxation
prompt: When did the supply take place for the goods sent on approval on 10th December 2026 and confirmed on 10th April 2027?
optionA: 10th December 2026
optionB: 10th June 2027 (6 months from removal)
optionC: 10th April 2027 when the customer confirmed the purchase
optionD: 31st March 2027
answerText: 10th April 2027 when the customer confirmed the purchase
explanation: Since the customer confirmed the purchase within 6 months (on 10th April 2027), the time of supply occurs when the recipient communicates approval/acceptance, i.e., 10th April 2027.
conceptTags: Approval Basis | Time of Supply | Goods

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s Apex Logistics Ltd., a registered Goods Transport Agency (GTA) providing transportation of goods by road, makes a supply of transport services to various clients in January 2027. Apex Logistics opts to pay tax at 5% (with ITC on inputs restricted) on its services. On 12th January 2027, it transports a consignment of textiles for a registered textile manufacturer and issues a transport document in lieu of a tax invoice. Separately, on 20th January 2027, Apex Logistics moves its own internal office equipment to a branch office in another city without any transfer of ownership or sale.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What document is Apex Logistics permitted to issue in lieu of a tax invoice for the transportation of goods service provided on 12th January 2027 under Rule 54(4)?
optionA: Bill of Supply
optionB: Transport document (Consignment Note)
optionC: Delivery Challan
optionD: Receipt Voucher
answerText: Transport document (Consignment Note)
explanation: Rule 54(4) of the CGST Rules, 2017 allows a supplier of GTA services or passenger transport services to issue a transport document (such as a Consignment Note) containing prescribed particulars in lieu of a tax invoice.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What document must accompany the movement of office equipment on 20th January 2027 since it is transported for reasons other than by way of supply?
optionA: Tax Invoice
optionB: Delivery Challan
optionC: Bill of Supply
optionD: Payment Voucher
answerText: Delivery Challan
explanation: Rule 55 stipulates that for transportation of goods for reasons other than supply (such as branch transfer or shifting of assets), a Delivery Challan must accompany the goods instead of a tax invoice.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Is Apex Logistics required to issue an e-invoice for the GTA services provided if its aggregate turnover exceeds the e-invoicing threshold?
optionA: Yes, GTA services are subject to e-invoicing if turnover exceeds the threshold
optionB: No, GTA services supplying passenger or goods transport where a transport document is issued in lieu of tax invoice under Rule 54(4) are specifically exempt from e-invoicing
optionC: Yes, regardless of rule 54(4)
optionD: Only if the recipient is unregistered
answerText: No, GTA services supplying passenger or goods transport where a transport document is issued in lieu of tax invoice under Rule 54(4) are specifically exempt from e-invoicing
explanation: As per notifications governing e-invoicing, specified categories of supplies including GTA services where a transport document is issued under Rule 54(4) instead of a tax invoice are exempt from e-invoicing requirements.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What mandatory details must be contained in the transport document issued by Apex Logistics under Rule 54(4)?
optionA: Gross weight, name of consignor and consignee, registration number of vehicle, details of goods, and GSTIN of GTA (if registered)
optionB: Only the vehicle number and date
optionC: Only the recipient's PAN and Aadhaar
optionD: Bank account details of the supplier only
answerText: Gross weight, name of consignor and consignee, registration number of vehicle, details of goods, and GSTIN of GTA (if registered)
explanation: Rule 54(4) read with relevant provisions requires transport documents like consignment notes to contain serial number, gross weight, details of consignor/consignee, registration number of vehicle, origin/destination, and GSTIN of the GTA.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Where must a registered person maintain the books of accounts and other records under Section 35 of the CGST Act, 2017?
optionA: At the principal place of business mentioned in the certificate of registration
optionB: At the registered office of the company anywhere outside India
optionC: At the residence of the managing director of the company
optionD: At any branch office, regardless of whether it is registered or not
answerText: At the principal place of business mentioned in the certificate of registration
explanation: Section 35(1) of the CGST Act, 2017 mandates that every registered person shall keep and maintain all records at his principal place of business as mentioned in the certificate of registration. If more than one place of business is specified in the certificate, the accounts relating to each place of business shall be kept at such places of business.
conceptTags: Place of Maintenance | Section 35 | Books of Accounts

subject: Taxation
prompt: For how many years must a registered person maintain books of accounts and records under Section 35(1) of the CGST Act, 2017?
optionA: 36 months from the due date of furnishing of annual return
optionB: 72 months from the due date of furnishing of annual return
optionC: 60 months from the end of the financial year
optionD: 84 months from the end of the calendar year
answerText: 72 months from the due date of furnishing of annual return
explanation: According to Section 35(1), books of accounts and other records must be retained until the expiry of seventy-two months (6 years) from the due date of furnishing of the annual return for the year pertaining to such accounts and records.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the additional retention period for records in a case where an appeal or revision or proceedings are pending before any appellate authority or court?
optionA: Until one year after final disposal of such appeal or proceedings
optionB: For a period of one year after final disposal of such appeal or proceedings, or until the expiry of the regular 72 months, whichever is later
optionC: For a period of two years after final disposal of such appeal
optionD: No additional period is required if 72 months have passed
answerText: For a period of one year after final disposal of such appeal or proceedings, or until the expiry of the regular 72 months, whichever is later
explanation: Proviso to Section 35(1) states that a registered person who is a party to an appeal or revision or any other proceedings before any appellate authority or court or is under investigation for an offence, shall retain the books of accounts pertaining to the subject matter for a period of one year after final disposal of such appeal/proceedings or until the expiry of seventy-two months, whichever is later.
conceptTags: Retention Period | Appeals | Proviso to Section 35

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following specific records must a manufacturer maintain under Rule 56 of the CGST Rules, 2017?
optionA: Monthly balance sheet and cash flow statements only
optionB: Monthly production accounts showing quantitative details of raw materials or services used and finished goods produced
optionC: Stock details of only imported goods
optionD: Details of all employees and their salaries
answerText: Monthly production accounts showing quantitative details of raw materials or services used and finished goods produced
explanation: Rule 56(1) of the CGST Rules, 2017 requires every registered person to keep books of accounts. Specifically, manufacturers must maintain monthly production accounts showing quantitative details of raw materials or services used in manufacture and finished goods produced.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What records must a stockist, broker, or agent dealing in goods maintain under the GST framework?
optionA: Only bank statements and invoices
optionB: True and complete records of goods received and supplied, along with names and addresses of suppliers and buyers
optionC: Only tax invoices issued to final consumers
optionD: Annual audit reports
answerText: True and complete records of goods received and supplied, along with names and addresses of suppliers and buyers
explanation: Under Rule 56(3), every agent, broker, or stockist must maintain true and complete records of the quantity of goods received and supplied by them, along with the particulars of the suppliers and buyers.

subject: Taxation
prompt: In what format must accounts and records be maintained and preserved under the GST provisions?
optionA: Only in physical paper files bound with hard covers
optionB: Exclusively on cloud servers hosted within India
optionC: Either electronically or manually, provided that electronic records are backed up and accessible
optionD: Exclusively in handwritten ledgers authenticated by a Chartered Accountant
answerText: Either electronically or manually, provided that electronic records are backed up and accessible
explanation: Section 35(1) read with Rule 56 permits the maintenance of books of accounts and other records in electronic form or manually. If maintained electronically, they must be authenticated by way of digital signature and proper backup mechanisms must be in place.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What responsibility is cast upon a registered person maintaining electronic records if called upon by a proper officer?
optionA: To courier the entire server to the GST office
optionB: To provide the details of passwords, access codes, and files in hard copy or readable format along with a signed certification
optionC: To allow the officer to change the encryption keys
optionD: To print all records and get them notarized
answerText: To provide the details of passwords, access codes, and files in hard copy or readable format along with a signed certification
explanation: Rule 57(2) stipulates that the person maintaining electronic records shall produce, on demand, the relevant files, passwords, access codes and numbers, and hard copies of the records as required by the proper officer.
conceptTags: Electronic Records | Rule 57 | Production of Records

subject: Taxation
prompt: Who is required to maintain a stock register showing receipts, supplies, losses, and balance of goods under Rule 56(4)?
optionA: Only government undertakings
optionB: Every registered person
optionC: Only composition taxpayers
optionD: Only persons having turnover exceeding Rs. 100 crores
answerText: Every registered person
explanation: Rule 56(4) mandates that every registered person shall keep a true and correct account of stock in respect of goods received and supplied by him, including inventories, receipts, dispatches, wastage, and shortage.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under Section 35(2), if a registered person fails to maintain accounts and records as specified, what action can the Commissioner or officer authorized take regarding goods?
optionA: Impose a penalty of Rs. 10,000 only
optionB: Determine the amount of tax payable on goods unaccounted for as if such goods had been supplied by him
optionC: Cancel the registration without any show-cause notice
optionD: Auction the entire factory immediately
answerText: Determine the amount of tax payable on goods unaccounted for as if such goods had been supplied by him
explanation: Section 35(2) provides that where the registered person fails to account for the goods or services in accordance with the provisions, the proper officer shall determine the amount of tax payable on the goods or services that are not accounted for, as if such goods or services had been supplied by such person.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What additional records must a godown or warehouse keeper or owner of a transport agency maintain, even if not registered?
optionA: Only balance sheets of their business
optionB: Records of the consigner, consignee, and other relevant details of goods transported, stored, or delivered
optionC: Income tax returns of all clients
optionD: Audited financial statements for the past 10 years
answerText: Records of the consigner, consignee, and other relevant details of goods transported, stored, or delivered
explanation: Section 35(2) and Rule 58 mandate that every owner or operator of warehouse or godown or any other place used for storage of goods and every transporter, irrespective of whether he is a registered person or not, shall maintain records of consigner, consignee, and goods stored or transported.

subject: Taxation
prompt: When must transporters and warehouse operators enroll or register on the GST portal if they are not otherwise registered under GST?
optionA: Within 30 days of starting operations
optionB: They are required to enroll and obtain a unique enrollment number in FORM GST ENR-01
optionC: They must obtain a regular GSTIN in all states
optionD: Enrollment is completely voluntary with no form requirement
answerText: They are required to enroll and obtain a unique enrollment number in FORM GST ENR-01
explanation: Rule 58 states that persons engaged in transporting goods or operating warehouses, if not registered under GST, shall maintain records and submit an application in FORM GST ENR-01 on the common portal to obtain a unique enrollment number.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What details regarding Input Tax Credit (ITC) must a registered person maintain in their books of accounts under Rule 56?
optionA: Only the total ITC claimed in the annual return
optionB: Monthly accounts showing input tax credit availed, utilized, and balance
optionC: Bank certificates of ITC payment
optionD: Only the ITC pertaining to capital goods
answerText: Monthly accounts showing input tax credit availed, utilized, and balance
explanation: Rule 56(2) requires every registered person to keep books of accounts including records of input tax credit availed, utilized, and the balance of ITC available.
conceptTags: ITC Records | Rule 56 | Books of Accounts

subject: Taxation
prompt: Who is required to get their accounts audited by a Chartered Accountant or Cost Accountant under Section 35(5) of the CGST Act?
optionA: Every registered person with turnover exceeding Rs. 2 crores
optionB: All registered persons
optionC: Section 35(5) requiring mandatory GST audit by a CA/CMA has been omitted, and registered persons now submit an Annual Return along with a self-certified Reconciliation Statement (GSTR-9C)
optionD: Only companies registered under the Companies Act, 2013
answerText: Section 35(5) requiring mandatory GST audit by a CA/CMA has been omitted, and registered persons now submit an Annual Return along with a self-certified Reconciliation Statement (GSTR-9C)
explanation: Section 35(5) which mandated GST audit by a Chartered Accountant or Cost Accountant was omitted by the Finance Act, 2021. Registered persons now furnish an annual return in GSTR-9 along with a self-certified reconciliation statement in GSTR-9C under Section 44.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under Rule 56(11), if a registered person has multiple places of business, where should the accounts relating to each place be kept?
optionA: At the head office only
optionB: At the respective place of business mentioned in the certificate of registration
optionC: Anywhere within the home state
optionD: At the office of their principal tax consultant
answerText: At the respective place of business mentioned in the certificate of registration
explanation: Rule 56(11) specifies that books of accounts relating to multiple places of business shall be kept at such respective places of business as mentioned in the certificate of registration.
conceptTags: Multiple Places of Business | Rule 56 | Maintenance

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following records must be maintained regarding tax invoice, debit note, and credit note under Rule 56?
optionA: Only outward invoices issued
optionB: Full details of tax invoices, bills of supply, delivery challans, credit notes, and debit notes issued and received
optionC: Only copies of invoices exceeding Rs. 50,000
optionD: Invoices received from unregistered persons only
answerText: Full details of tax invoices, bills of supply, delivery challans, credit notes, and debit notes issued and received
explanation: Rule 56(1) requires maintenance of accounts of all goods and services supplied, including invoices, bills of supply, debit notes, credit notes, and delivery challans issued or received.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If a registered person destroys or misplaces their electronic records, can they plead defense that the computer crashed?
optionA: Yes, system crashes exempt the person from maintaining records
optionB: No, maintaining backup and ensuring safety and recoverability of electronic records is the statutory responsibility of the registered person
optionC: Yes, if reported to the police within 24 hours
optionD: Only if the server was located outside India
answerText: No, maintaining backup and ensuring safety and recoverability of electronic records is the statutory responsibility of the registered person
explanation: Rule 57 mandates that the person maintaining electronic records must produce them on demand and ensure proper backups. Failure to maintain or produce records due to system failure without backup does not absolve the taxpayer from statutory penalties.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the consequence if a registered person fails to maintain books of accounts as required under Section 35?
optionA: Only a warning letter is issued
optionB: General penalty provisions under Section 125 may apply along with tax determination on unaccounted goods under Section 35(2)
optionC: Automatic imprisonment for 5 years
optionD: Suspension of bank accounts by the RBI
answerText: General penalty provisions under Section 125 may apply along with tax determination on unaccounted goods under Section 35(2)
explanation: Failure to maintain books of accounts attracts general penalties under Section 125 of the CGST Act, and the proper officer can also invoke Section 35(2) to determine tax on unaccounted goods/services.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Are the accounts maintained by a registered person open to inspection by GST officers?
optionA: No, inspection requires a court warrant
optionB: Yes, upon authorization by an officer not below the rank of Joint Commissioner
optionC: Only during the annual filing period
optionD: Only if the taxpayer consents in writing
answerText: Yes, upon authorization by an officer not below the rank of Joint Commissioner
explanation: Under Section 67 of the CGST Act, proper officers authorized by the Commissioner (not below the rank of Joint Commissioner) can inspect places of business and examine books of accounts and records.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What particulars must be maintained regarding 'advance payments' received or made by a registered person?
optionA: Advance payments are not required to be recorded in GST books
optionB: Full details of advances received, adjustments made against supplies, and advance payments made to suppliers
optionC: Only advances received in foreign currency
optionD: Only advances exceeding Rs. 10 lakhs
answerText: Full details of advances received, adjustments made against supplies, and advance payments made to suppliers
explanation: Rule 56(1) explicitly requires maintaining accounts of advances received and paid, along with adjustments made against invoices, as tax liability on advances for services (and earlier goods) requires proper tracking.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can a registered person maintain records at a place other than the principal place of business?
optionA: No, never
optionB: Yes, if an additional place of business is declared in the registration certificate or if approved by the Commissioner for specific accounts
optionC: Yes, anywhere in the world without notification
optionD: Only if the turnover is below Rs. 40 lakhs
answerText: Yes, if an additional place of business is declared in the registration certificate or if approved by the Commissioner for specific accounts
explanation: Records must be kept at the principal place of business and additional place(s) of business mentioned in the registration certificate. If records are maintained at multiple places, they must correspond to those specific registered locations.
conceptTags: Place of Business | Additional Place | Section 35

subject: Taxation
prompt: What specific records must a works contract service provider maintain under Rule 56?
optionA: Names and addresses of all sub-contractors, property owners, and details of payment, materials consumed, and invoices raised
optionB: Only architectural blueprints
optionC: Only municipal corporation approvals
optionD: Balance sheet of the building owner
answerText: Names and addresses of all sub-contractors, property owners, and details of payment, materials consumed, and invoices raised
explanation: Rule 56(13) mandates that a works contract supplier shall keep separate accounts for each works contract showing names and addresses of employers, suppliers, sub-contractors, description, value, and quantity of goods or services used.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Is a transporter required to maintain records of goods even if the goods are exempt from GST?
optionA: No, exempt goods need no documentation
optionB: Yes, transporters and warehouse keepers must maintain records of all goods transported or stored, regardless of taxability
optionC: Only if the value exceeds Rs. 50,000
optionD: Only if requested by the transporter association
answerText: Yes, transporters and warehouse keepers must maintain records of all goods transported or stored, regardless of taxability
explanation: Section 35(2) and Rule 58 apply to transporters and warehouse operators for all goods handled by them, irrespective of whether the goods are taxable or exempt from GST.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the consequence of failing to produce electronic records in readable format when demanded by a proper officer?
optionA: The officer will print them free of cost
optionB: It is treated as non-compliance, inviting penal action for failure to maintain/produce records
optionC: The taxpayer gets an automatic 30-day extension
optionD: The records are permanently deleted from the portal
answerText: It is treated as non-compliance, inviting penal action for failure to maintain/produce records
explanation: Failure to produce electronic records, access codes, and passwords on demand violates Rule 57 and attracts penalties under the provisions of the CGST Act.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following persons is NOT specifically mentioned under Section 35(1) to maintain books of accounts?
optionA: A registered person
optionB: A custodian of goods who is not a registered person
optionC: A clearing and forwarding agent
optionD: An unregistered individual buying goods for personal consumption
answerText: An unregistered individual buying goods for personal consumption
explanation: Unregistered individuals buying goods for personal consumption are final consumers and do not carry on business; hence, they have no statutory obligation to maintain books of accounts under Section 35.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If records are maintained in electronic form, who must authenticate them?
optionA: Any employee of the company
optionB: The registered person or an authorized representative using a digital signature
optionC: The jurisdictional GST Inspector
optionD: A statutory auditor
answerText: The registered person or an authorized representative using a digital signature
explanation: Rule 57 requires that electronic records must be authenticated by way of digital signature by the registered person or their authorized representative.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What details regarding outward supplies must be kept in the accounts under Rule 56?
optionA: Total sales figure for the year only
optionB: Invoices, debit notes, credit notes, statements of outward supplies, and tax collected and paid
optionC: Only cash sales records
optionD: Only B2B export supplies
answerText: Invoices, debit notes, credit notes, statements of outward supplies, and tax collected and paid
explanation: Rule 56(2) requires maintaining accounts of goods and services imported or exported, and supplies foothills/outward supplies along with tax charged.

subject: Taxation
prompt: How should a registered person handle corrections or alterations made in manual books of accounts?
optionA: Correction fluid must be used to erase the wrong entry
optionB: Incorrect entry should be scored out under signature, and the correct entry recorded, preserving audit trail
optionC: Pages containing errors should be torn out
optionD: No corrections are allowed under any circumstances
answerText: Incorrect entry should be scored out under signature, and the correct entry recorded, preserving audit trail
explanation: Rule 56(5) mandates that manual accounts, registers, and documents shall be maintained sequentially, and any entry shall not be erased, obliterated, or scraped. Corrections should be made properly with initials.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under Rule 56, what records must be maintained by an owner or operator of a hotel regarding accommodation?
optionA: Names and addresses of guests, arrival and departure dates, and room tariff charged
optionB: Only food and beverage sales
optionC: Only electricity consumption bills
optionD: Only employee attendance registers
answerText: Names and addresses of guests, arrival and departure dates, and room tariff charged
explanation: Rule 56(7) requires owners or operators of hotels, inns, guest houses, clubs, or similar places to maintain accounts containing details of guests staying, including names and addresses, duration of stay, and room tariff.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the prescribed retention period for accounts and records if an assessment year is under scrutiny for fraud, suppression, or wilful misstatement?
optionA: 72 months from the due date of annual return
optionB: Up to 72 months, but extended if proceedings/appeals are pending or investigation for an offence is active
optionC: 10 years from the end of the calendar year
optionD: Permanent retention
answerText: Up to 72 months, but extended if proceedings/appeals are pending or investigation for an offence is active
explanation: Under the proviso to Section 35(1), when proceedings/appeals or investigations for an offence are active, records must be retained for one year after final disposal or 72 months, whichever is later.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which authority has the power to notify a class of taxable persons to maintain additional records under Section 35(1)?
optionA: The State GST Commissioner alone
optionB: The Government on the recommendations of the GST Council
optionC: The jurisdictional Superintendent of Central Tax
optionD: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)
answerText: The Government on the recommendations of the GST Council
explanation: Section 35(1) empowers the Government, on the recommendations of the GST Council, to notify a class of taxable persons to maintain any additional records or accounts as specified.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s Apex Traders, a registered taxpayer under GST in Mumbai, deals in electronic appliances. They have a principal place of business in Andheri and an additional warehouse in Bhiwandi. Due to expansion, they switch from manual ledgers to an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) software for maintaining electronic records. The due date for furnishing the annual return for FY 2023-24 was 31st December 2024.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Until what date must M/s Apex Traders mandatorily retain their books of accounts and records for FY 2023-24 under Section 35(1)?
optionA: 31st December 2029
optionB: 31st December 2030
optionC: 31st March 2030
optionD: 31st December 2031
answerText: 31st December 2030
explanation: Section 35(1) requires records to be retained for 72 months (6 years) from the due date of furnishing the annual return. Since the due date is 31st December 2024, 72 months expire on 31st December 2030.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Where must M/s Apex Traders keep the accounts pertaining to their Bhiwandi warehouse?
optionA: Exclusively at their corporate head office in Delhi
optionB: At the Bhiwandi warehouse if specified as an additional place of business in the registration certificate
optionC: At the residence of the accountant in Mumbai
optionD: Anywhere in the State of Maharashtra without registration declaration
answerText: At the Bhiwandi warehouse if specified as an additional place of business in the registration certificate
explanation: Under Section 35(1) and Rule 56(11), accounts relating to each place of business must be kept at such respective place of business mentioned in the certificate of registration.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Since M/s Apex Traders maintain electronic records on ERP software, what is their statutory obligation when demanded by a proper officer?
optionA: To allow the officer to delete unwanted files
optionB: To produce the relevant files, passwords, access codes, and hard copies as required
optionC: To provide physical handwritten copies of all ERP entries
optionD: To purchase a new server for the GST department
answerText: To produce the relevant files, passwords, access codes, and hard copies as required
explanation: Rule 57(2) stipulates that the person maintaining electronic records shall produce passwords, access codes, and files on demand by the proper officer.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Suppose an investigation for an offence under GST is initiated against M/s Apex Traders for FY 2023-24, and proceedings are pending on 31st December 2030. When does their record retention obligation end?
optionA: 31st December 2030 itself
optionB: One year after the final disposal of such proceedings or 31st December 2030, whichever is later
optionC: Immediately upon the start of investigation
optionD: After 10 years from the financial year end
answerText: One year after the final disposal of such proceedings or 31st December 2030, whichever is later
explanation: Proviso to Section 35(1) dictates that if proceedings or investigations are pending, records must be retained for one year after final disposal of such proceedings or until the expiry of 72 months, whichever is later.
conceptTags: Retention Period | Investigation | Proviso to Section 35

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Shreeji Transport Agency operates a fleet of trucks transporting goods across multiple states, but is not registered as a taxable supplier under GST. They store goods temporarily in transit godowns located in Gujarat. The proper officer during a verification drive requests Shreeji Transport Agency to produce records of consignments handled during the past quarter.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Is Shreeji Transport Agency legally required to maintain records of goods despite not being a registered taxable person?
optionA: No, only registered persons under Section 22/24 must maintain records
optionB: Yes, under Section 35(2) and Rule 58, transporters and godown owners must maintain records of consigner, consignee, and goods
optionC: Only if their annual turnover exceeds Rs. 20 crores
optionD: Only if they cross state borders
answerText: Yes, under Section 35(2) and Rule 58, transporters and godown owners must maintain records of consigner, consignee, and goods
explanation: Section 35(2) and Rule 58 mandate that transporters, warehouse keepers, and godown owners must maintain records of goods transported, stored, or delivered, irrespective of whether they are registered taxpayers.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What registration/enrollment requirement applies to Shreeji Transport Agency on the GST portal if they are not registered under GST?
optionA: They must obtain a regular GSTIN in Gujarat
optionB: They must enroll and obtain a unique enrollment number in FORM GST ENR-01
optionC: They must register under the Shops and Establishment Act only
optionD: No portal interaction is required
answerText: They must enroll and obtain a unique enrollment number in FORM GST ENR-01
explanation: Rule 58 specifies that transporters not registered under GST shall submit an application in FORM GST ENR-01 on the common portal to obtain a unique enrollment number.

subject: Taxation
