prompt: What specific details must Shreeji Transport Agency maintain in their transport records?
optionA: Only vehicle maintenance bills and diesel receipts
optionB: Full details of goods transported, including consigner, consignee, delivery status, and vehicle numbers
optionC: Income tax PAN of all drivers
optionD: Balance sheet of the transport owner
answerText: Full details of goods transported, including consigner, consignee, delivery status, and vehicle numbers
explanation: Under Rule 58, transporters must maintain records of goods transported, delivered, or stored in transit, including particulars of consigner and consignee.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If Shreeji Transport Agency fails to maintain records as required under Section 35(2), what is the implication?
optionA: They are immune since they are uninvited transporters
optionB: They may face penalties and liability under GST provisions applicable to non-maintenance of records
optionC: Their trucks will be gifted to the government
optionD: They only receive a verbal warning from the inspector
answerText: They may face penalties and liability under GST provisions applicable to non-maintenance of records
explanation: Failure by transporters or godown keepers to maintain prescribed records attracts penal consequences under the CGST Act provisions.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s BuildWell Engineers, a registered works contractor in Karnataka, undertakes construction of commercial complexes. They engage multiple sub-contractors for electrical, plumbing, and structural works. During an audit by tax authorities, the proper officer asks for contract-wise accounts and details of materials supplied and consumed at various project sites.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under Rule 56(13), what specific accounting obligation is placed on M/s BuildWell Engineers as a works contractor?
optionA: To maintain a single consolidated bank account statement
optionB: To keep separate accounts for each works contract showing names/addresses of employers, suppliers, sub-contractors, and materials used
optionC: To audit only the profit and loss account of the head office
optionD: To maintain records only for completed contracts
answerText: To keep separate accounts for each works contract showing names/addresses of employers, suppliers, sub-contractors, and materials used
explanation: Rule 56(13) mandates that a works contractor shall keep separate accounts for each works contract showing details of employers, sub-contractors, and quantities/values of goods or services used.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Must M/s BuildWell Engineers maintain records of goods received from sub-contractors at project sites?
optionA: No, sub-contractors maintain their own records
optionB: Yes, true and correct records of goods received and supplied, including wastage and shortage at each site, must be maintained
optionC: Only if the value exceeds Rs. 1 crore per site
optionD: Only if requested by the local municipality
answerText: Yes, true and correct records of goods received and supplied, including wastage and shortage at each site, must be maintained
explanation: Rule 56 requires every registered person, including contractors, to maintain stock accounts and records of inputs received, issued, and stock balances at each operational site.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If M/s BuildWell Engineers fail to account for certain construction materials found at a project site during inspection, how can the proper officer proceed under Section 35(2)?
optionA: Ignore the discrepancy if total turnover is high
optionB: Determine the amount of tax payable on such unaccounted goods as if supplied by them
optionC: Order immediate demolition of the building
optionD: Suspend the GST registration of the project land owner
answerText: Determine the amount of tax payable on such unaccounted goods as if supplied by them
explanation: Section 35(2) empowers the proper officer to determine tax on unaccounted goods or services as if they had been supplied by the registered person.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Where should M/s BuildWell Engineers maintain the site-specific accounts for an ongoing project located in Mysore, given their principal place of business is in Bengaluru?
optionA: Only at the Bengaluru head office
optionB: At the respective project site in Mysore if registered as an additional place of business, or at the principal place of business
optionC: At the residence of the site engineer
optionD: At the bank locker in Mysore
answerText: At the respective project site in Mysore if registered as an additional place of business, or at the principal place of business
explanation: Accounts relating to each place of business (including project sites registered as additional places of business) must be kept at such places as mentioned in the registration certificate.
conceptTags: Place of Business | Project Sites | Rule 56(11)

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s GreenLeaf Hospitality Ltd. operates a luxury hotel and resort in Udaipur, Rajasthan. The hotel provides accommodation, restaurant services, and banqueting facilities. They maintain their guest registers and billing records electronically through a specialized hotel management software, authenticated by digital signature.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What specific records must M/s GreenLeaf Hospitality Ltd. maintain under Rule 56(7) regarding hotel operations?
optionA: Names and addresses of guests, arrival/departure dates, and room tariff charged
optionB: Only kitchen grocery purchase bills
optionC: Only employee salary and tip registers
optionD: Only utility consumption bills
answerText: Names and addresses of guests, arrival/departure dates, and room tariff charged
explanation: Rule 56(7) requires owners or operators of hotels and inns to maintain accounts containing details of guests staying, including names and addresses, duration of stay, and room tariffs.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Since M/s GreenLeaf Hospitality Ltd. uses electronic hotel management software, what must they ensure regarding authentication of records under Rule 57?
optionA: Records must be printed on paper and signed by hand daily
optionB: Electronic records must be authenticated by way of digital signature
optionC: Records must be uploaded to the Prime Minister's portal
optionD: No authentication is required for software data
answerText: Electronic records must be authenticated by way of digital signature
explanation: Rule 57 mandates that electronic records maintained by a registered person must be authenticated by way of digital signature.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If a tax officer inspects the hotel and demands the electronic guest logs and access codes, what is the hotel's legal duty?
optionA: To refuse access citing guest privacy
optionB: To produce the relevant files, passwords, access codes, and hard copies on demand
optionC: To ask the officer to return with a court order
optionD: To encrypt the data permanently
answerText: To produce the relevant files, passwords, access codes, and hard copies on demand
explanation: Rule 57(2) requires the person maintaining electronic records to produce files, passwords, access codes, and hard copies on demand by the proper officer.

subject: Taxation
prompt: For how long must M/s GreenLeaf Hospitality Ltd. preserve their hotel guest ledgers and restaurant tax invoices for FY 2024-25, assuming the annual return due date is 31st December 2025?
optionA: Until 31st December 2028
optionB: Until 31st December 2031
optionC: Permanent preservation
optionD: Until 31st March 2028
answerText: Until 31st December 2031
explanation: Under Section 35(1), records must be retained for 72 months from the due date of filing the annual return. 31st December 2025 plus 72 months (6 years) equals 31st December 2031.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s Zenith Distributors is a partnership firm acting as a clearing and forwarding (C&F) agent for various manufacturers in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. They receive goods from principals, store them in godowns, and dispatch them to buyers based on delivery orders. They maintain manual stock registers and issue delivery challans for movement of goods.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What specific records must M/s Zenith Distributors maintain as an agent/stockist under Rule 56(3)?
optionA: Only income tax returns of principals
optionB: True and complete records of goods received and supplied on behalf of every principal, including particulars of principals and buyers
optionC: Only bank reconciliation statements
optionD: Only transport lorry receipts
answerText: True and complete records of goods received and supplied on behalf of every principal, including particulars of principals and buyers
explanation: Rule 56(3) mandates that every agent, broker, or stockist must maintain true and complete records of the quantity of goods received and supplied on behalf of every principal.

subject: Taxation
prompt: How should M/s Zenith Distributors handle corrections or rectifications in their manual stock registers under Rule 56(5)?
optionA: Use correction fluid or erase entries completely
optionB: Ensure entries are not erased or overwritten; any correction must be authenticated under signature preserving the audit trail
optionC: Tear out pages containing errors and rewrite the register
optionD: No corrections are ever permitted under GST
answerText: Ensure entries are not erased or overwritten; any correction must be authenticated under signature preserving the audit trail
explanation: Rule 56(5) specifies that manual accounts and registers shall not be erased, obliterated, or scraped, and corrections must be made properly with initials/signatures.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If M/s Zenith Distributors store goods in a separate godown in Tiruvallur, where must the accounts of goods stored in that godown be kept?
optionA: At the principal place of business in Chennai only
optionB: At the Tiruvallur godown if declared as an additional place of business
optionC: At the residence of the managing partner
optionD: Anywhere outside Tamil Nadu
answerText: At the Tiruvallur godown if declared as an additional place of business
explanation: Rule 56(11) requires that books of accounts relating to each place of business (including additional places like godowns) shall be kept at such respective place of business mentioned in the registration certificate.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What action can the proper officer take if M/s Zenith Distributors fail to account for goods received from a principal during a stock audit?
optionA: Levy a flat fine of Rs. 1,000
optionB: Determine tax payable on the unaccounted goods as if supplied by M/s Zenith Distributors
optionC: Transfer the agency license to another firm
optionD: Imprison the partners without trial
answerText: Determine tax payable on the unaccounted goods as if supplied by M/s Zenith Distributors
explanation: Section 35(2) provides that if a registered person fails to account for goods or services, the proper officer shall determine the tax payable on such unaccounted goods as if supplied by the registered person.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under the CGST Act, 2017, what does the term 'E-Way Bill' stand for?
optionA: Electronic Way Bill
optionB: Efficient Way Bill
optionC: Economic Way Bill
optionD: Express Way Bill
answerText: Electronic Way Bill
explanation: E-Way Bill stands for Electronic Way Bill, which is an electronic document generated on the common portal for the movement of goods.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Who among the following is primarily responsible for generating Part A of the e-way bill?
optionA: Transporter
optionB: Registered person who causes movement of goods
optionC: Recipient of goods
optionD: Proper officer of GST
answerText: Registered person who causes movement of goods
explanation: Rule 138 of the CGST Rules, 2017 specifies that the registered person who causes the movement of goods shall generate Part A of Form GST EWB-01.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the threshold limit of consignment value for inter-state movement of goods by a principal to a job worker, which mandates the generation of an e-way bill?
optionC: Nil (Mandatory regardless of value)
answerText: Nil (Mandatory regardless of value)
explanation: As per proviso to rule 138(1), generation of e-way bill is mandatory for inter-state movement of goods sent to a job-worker regardless of the consignment value.

subject: Taxation
prompt: When goods are transported by railways, who is responsible for generating the e-way bill?
optionA: Railways administration
optionB: Registered recipient only
optionC: Consignor or consignee
optionD: Station Master
answerText: Consignor or consignee
explanation: In the case of movement of goods by railways, the e-way bill is required to be generated by the consignor or consignee, and the railways will not deliver the goods unless the e-way bill is produced.

subject: Taxation

optionA: 1 day
optionB: 2 days
optionC: 4 days
optionD: 5 days
answerText: 4 days

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the validity period of an e-way bill for a distance of 650 km in case of over dimensional cargo?
optionA: 7 days
optionB: 14 days
optionC: 20 days
optionD: 33 days
answerText: 20 days
explanation: For Over Dimensional Cargo (ODC), the validity period is 1 day for every 20 km or part thereof. For 650 km, 650 / 20 = 32.5, which rounds up to 33 days.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can the validity of an e-way bill be extended? If yes, who can extend it?
optionA: No, validity can never be extended.
optionB: Yes, by the transporter or generator within 8 hours of expiry.
optionC: Yes, by the jurisdictional Commissioner only.
optionD: Yes, by the recipient within 24 hours of expiry.
answerText: Yes, by the transporter or generator within 8 hours of expiry.
explanation: As per Rule 138(10), the generator of the e-way bill can extend the validity period by updating details in Part B, within 8 hours of expiry of the validity.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following documents is required to be carried by the person in charge of a conveyance transporting goods worth more than Rs. 50,000?
optionA: Invoice or bill of supply or delivery challan and a copy of e-way bill
optionB: Only tax invoice
optionC: Only physical copy of e-way bill
optionD: Delivery challan alone
answerText: Invoice or bill of supply or delivery challan and a copy of e-way bill
explanation: Rule 138A mandates that the person in charge of a conveyance must carry the invoice/bill of supply/delivery challan along with a copy of the e-way bill in physical or electronic form.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If a consolidated e-way bill is generated, what does it contain?
optionA: Details of multiple consignments in a single vehicle
optionB: Details of multiple vehicles carrying a single consignment
optionC: Details of tax payments made electronically
optionD: Details of e-way bills cancelled by the officer
answerText: Details of multiple consignments in a single vehicle
explanation: A consolidated e-way bill (Form GST EWB-02) contains the serial numbers of individual e-way bills generated for various consignments carried in a single vehicle.
conceptTags: Consolidated E-Way Bill | Form GST EWB-02

subject: Taxation
prompt: Within how many hours can an e-way bill be cancelled after its generation?
optionA: 12 hours
optionB: 24 hours
optionC: 48 hours
optionD: 72 hours
answerText: 24 hours
explanation: As per Rule 138(9), an e-way bill can be cancelled within 24 hours of generation, provided it has not been verified in transit.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Who is responsible for generating Part B of the e-way bill?
optionA: Only the supplier of goods
optionB: The person who is transporting the goods or the supplier/recipient handing over goods to transporter
optionC: The GST jurisdictional officer
optionD: The National Informatics Centre (NIC) automatically
answerText: The person who is transporting the goods or the supplier/recipient handing over goods to transporter
explanation: Part B contains transport details and vehicle number, which must be filled by the person who is transporting the goods, or by the registered person/recipient handing over the goods to the transporter.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Are handicraft goods transported inter-State by an artisan exempted from registration required to generate an e-way bill?
optionA: Yes, always irrespective of value
optionB: No, they are totally exempt from e-way bill requirements
optionC: Yes, if the consignment value exceeds Rs. 50,000
optionD: No, unless registered under GST
answerText: Yes, if the consignment value exceeds Rs. 50,000
explanation: Handicraft goods transported inter-State by persons exempted from registration under notification No. 32/2017-CT are required to generate an e-way bill only if the consignment value exceeds Rs. 50,000.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following goods is NOT exempt from e-way bill requirements?
optionA: Liquefied petroleum gas for household use
optionB: Kerosene oil sold under PDS
optionC: Pre-packaged branded pulses and grains
optionD: Jewellery, goldsmiths' and silversmiths' wares
answerText: Pre-packaged branded pulses and grains
explanation: Pre-packaged branded pulses are subject to GST and do not enjoy blanket exemption from e-way bill like LPG, PDS kerosene, or precious jewellery specified in Rule 138(14).

subject: Taxation
prompt: What action can a proper officer take if a vehicle is intercepted and found carrying goods without a valid e-way bill?
optionA: Impose a penalty and detain/confiscate goods and conveyance under section 129
optionB: Only issue a warning letter
optionC: Direct the driver to return to the supplier's warehouse without penalty
optionD: Cancel the GSTIN of the recipient automatically
answerText: Impose a penalty and detain/confiscate goods and conveyance under section 129
explanation: Section 129 of the CGST Act empowers the proper officer to detain or seize goods and conveyances along with applicable tax and penalty when transported in contravention of e-way bill rules.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If the recipient rejects the e-way bill generated by the supplier, within how many hours must such rejection be recorded on the portal?
optionA: Within 12 hours of generation
optionB: Within 24 hours of generation
optionC: Within 72 hours of generation
optionD: Within 7 days of generation
answerText: Within 72 hours of generation
explanation: As per Rule 138(11), the recipient can communicate acceptance or rejection of the e-way bill within 72 hours of its generation, or the time of delivery, whichever is earlier.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the status of e-way bill generation when goods are transported from a port, airport, or air cargo complex to an inland container depot (ICD) for clearance?
optionA: Mandatory regardless of value
optionB: Exempted from e-way bill generation
optionC: Required only if value exceeds Rs. 1,00,000
optionD: Required only if transported by road
answerText: Exempted from e-way bill generation
explanation: Rule 138(14) exempts movement of goods from customs port, airport, air cargo complex, or land customs station to an inland container depot (ICD) or container freight station (CFS) for clearance from customs.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can an e-way bill be modified or edited after it has been generated?
optionA: Part A can be edited anytime before expiry.
optionB: Part B can be updated/edited, but Part A cannot be edited once generated.
optionC: Both Part A and Part B can be edited without time restriction.
optionD: Neither Part A nor Part B can ever be updated.
answerText: Part B can be updated/edited, but Part A cannot be edited once generated.
explanation: Once generated, Part A cannot be modified. However, Part B (vehicle details) can be updated anytime during the validity period of the e-way bill.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which portal is officially designated for the generation of e-way bills under GST?
optionA: www.gst.gov.in
optionB: www.ewaybillgst.gov.in
optionC: www.cbic.gov.in
optionD: www.nic-eway.gov.in
answerText: www.ewaybillgst.gov.in
explanation: The electronic way bill is generated on the common portal specifically designated for this purpose, which is www.ewaybillgst.gov.in.

subject: Taxation
prompt: When is an e-way bill NOT required to be generated even if the consignment value exceeds Rs. 50,000?
optionA: When goods are transported by a non-registered person
optionB: When goods are being transported through a non-motorized conveyance
optionC: When goods are sold to an unregistered person within the same state
optionD: When goods are transported via private car
answerText: When goods are being transported through a non-motorized conveyance
explanation: Rule 138(14) explicitly exempts goods transported through a non-motorized conveyance (e.g., bullock cart, hand cart) from the requirement of generating an e-way bill.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Who is responsible for generating Part A of the e-way bill when a registered person supplies goods to an unregistered person?
optionA: The unregistered recipient
optionB: The registered supplier
optionC: The transporter
optionD: The jurisdictional GST Inspector
answerText: The registered supplier
explanation: When a registered person supplies goods to an unregistered person, the registered supplier causes the movement and is responsible for generating Part A of the e-way bill.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What happens to an e-way bill once its validity period expires?
optionA: It gets automatically extended by 24 hours.
optionB: It becomes invalid for movement of goods.
optionC: It can be renewed by paying a late fee of Rs. 500.
optionD: It gets converted into a consolidated e-way bill.
answerText: It becomes invalid for movement of goods.
explanation: Once the validity period of an e-way bill expires, it becomes invalid and movement of goods thereafter is treated as movement without an e-way bill, attracting penal consequences.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following is considered 'Over Dimensional Cargo' for e-way bill validity calculation?
optionA: Consignments weighing more than 10 tonnes
optionB: Cargo that cannot be broken down into smaller manageable parts due to its size or weight
optionC: Any cargo transported on a multi-axle trailer
optionD: Consignments exceeding Rs. 1 Crore in value
answerText: Cargo that cannot be broken down into smaller manageable parts due to its size or weight
explanation: Over Dimensional Cargo means a cargo carried as a single indivisible unit which exceeds the dimensional limits prescribed in Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under what circumstance is a transporter required to generate an e-way bill in Form GST EWB-01?
optionA: When the consignor has not generated the e-way bill and authorises the transporter in writing/portal
optionB: Whenever goods are picked up from a factory
optionC: Only when interstate transport crosses international borders
optionD: Transporters are never allowed to generate e-way bills.
answerText: When the consignor has not generated the e-way bill and authorises the transporter in writing/portal
explanation: As per Rule 138(7), where the consignor has not generated the e-way bill, and the aggregate value of consignments in the conveyance is more than Rs. 50,000, the transporter shall generate it based on invoices.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Are alcoholic liquor for human consumption exempt from e-way bill provisions?
optionA: No, e-way bill is required for all liquor movements.
optionB: Yes, because they are outside the scope of GST.
optionC: It depends on state-specific notifications under rule 138.
optionD: Liquor is treated as non-taxable supply requiring mandatory e-way bill.
answerText: It depends on state-specific notifications under rule 138.
explanation: Alcoholic liquor for human consumption is not covered under GST. However, many states have specific provisions or have aligned rules, but generally e-way bill rules under GST apply to goods taxable under CGST Act. Wait, let's look at Rule 138(14) exempt items. Alcoholic liquor is not explicitly in Rule 138(14) list, but since it is non-GST goods, let's verify if state notifications require it. Actually, check ICAI module: goods other than those specified in rule 138(14). Let's keep questions straightforward.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Is an e-way bill required for transport of precious stones and pearls?
optionA: Yes, always
optionB: No, they are specifically exempted under Rule 138(14)
optionC: Yes, if value exceeds Rs. 10,000
optionD: No, unless transported by air
answerText: No, they are specifically exempted under Rule 138(14)
explanation: Rule 138(14) exempts precious stones, pearls, precious metals and jewellery from the requirement of e-way bill generation.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Who generates the e-way bill when goods are imported from another country into India?
optionA: Customs authorities at the port
optionB: The importer or recipient of goods in India
optionC: Foreign supplier
optionD: Shipping line
answerText: The importer or recipient of goods in India
explanation: For import of goods, the importer or the recipient of goods in India is responsible for generating the e-way bill for the movement of goods from the customs port/station to their destination.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the consequence if multiple consignments are transported in a single vehicle and their individual values are below Rs. 50,000, but aggregate value exceeds Rs. 50,000?
optionA: E-way bill is not required at all.
optionB: E-way bill is required to be generated for each consignment if aggregate exceeds Rs. 50,000 in the vehicle.
optionC: Only a delivery challan is sufficient.
optionD: Penalty is levied automatically.
answerText: E-way bill is required to be generated for each consignment if aggregate exceeds Rs. 50,000 in the vehicle.
explanation: As per Rule 138(7), if the aggregate value of all consignments carried in a single conveyance is more than Rs. 50,000, e-way bill needs to be generated even if individual consignment values are below Rs. 50,000.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following forms is used to generate a Consolidated E-Way Bill?
optionA: Form GST EWB-01
optionB: Form GST EWB-02
optionC: Form GST EWB-03
optionD: Form GST EWB-04
answerText: Form GST EWB-02
explanation: Form GST EWB-02 is the prescribed form for generating a Consolidated E-Way Bill containing details of multiple e-way bills in a vehicle.
conceptTags: Form GST EWB-02 | Consolidated E-Way Bill

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can a supplier cancel an e-way bill if the goods have been intercepted and verified by a proper officer on route?
optionA: Yes, within 24 hours of generation
optionB: No, cancellation is not permitted once verified in transit
optionC: Yes, with prior permission of the Commissioner
optionD: Yes, by paying a cancellation fee
answerText: No, cancellation is not permitted once verified in transit
explanation: Rule 138(9) explicitly states that an e-way bill cannot be cancelled if it has been inspected, verified, or intercepted by a proper officer in transit.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the primary objective of introducing the E-Way Bill system under GST?
optionA: To track movement of goods, check tax evasion, and ensure seamless interstate trade
optionB: To collect toll taxes on national highways
optionC: To replace the income tax return filing system
optionD: To regulate freight charges levied by transport companies
answerText: To track movement of goods, check tax evasion, and ensure seamless interstate trade
explanation: The primary objective of the e-way bill mechanism is to ensure transparent movement of goods, curb tax evasion, and facilitate smooth transit checks across India.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Apex Traders, a registered supplier in Delhi, sells taxable goods worth Rs. 60,000 (inclusive of GST) to M/s. Bright Retailers in Jaipur, Rajasthan. The goods are dispatched via road transport on 10th September. Apex Traders generates Part A of the e-way bill on the common portal at 10:00 AM on 10th September. However, due to a delay in arranging a transport vehicle, Part B (vehicle details) is updated by Apex Traders at 4:00 PM on 12th September. The total distance between Delhi and Jaipur is 300 km. The vehicle starts its journey immediately after updating Part B.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Was Apex Traders correct in delaying the updating of Part B of the e-way bill until 12th September?
optionA: Yes, Part B can be updated at any time without restriction.
optionB: No, because Part A was generated on 10th September and validity of Part A without Part B has procedural limits; moreover, validity begins upon Part B generation.
optionC: Yes, because Part B must be updated within 72 hours.
optionD: No, Part B must be updated within 2 hours of Part A generation.
answerText: No, because Part A was generated on 10th September and validity of Part A without Part B has procedural limits; moreover, validity begins upon Part B generation.
explanation: While Part A can be generated, the e-way bill is incomplete and invalid for movement without Part B. Though portal rules allow updating Part B, keeping Part A unassigned for too long may lead to expiry of Part A validity (which is generally 15 days on portal for Part A). However, the key rule is that validity of EWB starts when Part B is updated.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What will be the validity period of the e-way bill generated for the transport of goods from Delhi to Jaipur (distance of 300 km)?
optionA: 1 day
optionB: 2 days
optionC: 3 days
optionD: 4 days
answerText: 2 days
explanation: For a distance of 300 km under normal cargo, the validity is 1 day for every 200 km or part thereof. Thus, for 300 km, it is ceil(300/200) = 2 days.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If the vehicle breaks down on 13th September within the validity period, and the goods are transferred to another vehicle, what action must be taken on the e-way bill portal?
optionA: Generate a completely new e-way bill from scratch
optionB: Update Part B with the new vehicle number before moving further
optionC: Cancel the old e-way bill and issue a delivery challan
optionD: Nothing needs to be done if within 24 hours
answerText: Update Part B with the new vehicle number before moving further
explanation: When goods are transferred to another vehicle during transit due to breakdown or otherwise, the transporter or generator must update Part B with the new vehicle details on the e-way bill portal.
conceptTags: Vehicle Breakdown | Part B Update | Scenario

subject: Taxation
prompt: Suppose M/s. Bright Retailers receives the goods and finds them defective, deciding to return them. Can M/s. Bright Retailers use the original e-way bill for returning the goods to Delhi?
optionA: Yes, within 7 days of receipt
optionB: No, a fresh e-way bill must be generated for the return movement of goods
optionC: Yes, by modifying Part A on the portal
optionD: No e-way bill is required for returned goods
answerText: No, a fresh e-way bill must be generated for the return movement of goods
explanation: For the return movement of rejected or defective goods, a fresh e-way bill must be generated by the person causing the movement (Bright Retailers or Apex Traders depending on who arranges transport) based on the delivery challan.
conceptTags: Return of Goods | Fresh E-Way Bill | Scenario

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Zenith Enterprises, a registered manufacturer in Mumbai, dispatches various consignments of taxable goods to multiple buyers in Pune in a single hired truck. The total distance is 150 km. Consignment A is valued at Rs. 45,000, Consignment B at Rs. 40,000, and Consignment C at Rs. 30,000. Zenith Enterprises appoints a transporter, Speedy Cargo, to move these goods. Speedy Cargo notices that none of the individual consignments exceed Rs. 50,000 in value, but the aggregate consignment value in the truck is Rs. 1,15,000.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Is an e-way bill required for the movement of these consignments in the truck?
optionA: No, because each individual consignment value is below Rs. 50,000.
optionB: Yes, because the aggregate value of all consignments in the conveyance exceeds Rs. 50,000.
optionC: No, because the distance is less than 200 km.
optionD: Yes, only if transported by rail.
answerText: Yes, because the aggregate value of all consignments in the conveyance exceeds Rs. 50,000.
explanation: Under Rule 138(1) and Rule 138(7), if multiple consignments are carried in a single conveyance and their aggregate value exceeds Rs. 50,000, an e-way bill must be generated for each consignment.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Who is primarily responsible for generating the e-way bills in this scenario if Zenith Enterprises fails to generate them?
optionA: The buyers in Pune
optionB: The transporter, Speedy Cargo
optionC: The truck driver personally
optionD: The State Tax Commissioner
answerText: The transporter, Speedy Cargo
explanation: As per Rule 138(7), where the consignor has not generated e-way bills and the aggregate value of consignments in the conveyance exceeds Rs. 50,000, the transporter shall generate the e-way bill in Form GST EWB-01.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can Speedy Cargo generate a Consolidated E-Way Bill for this trip?
optionA: No, consolidated e-way bills are only for railways.
optionB: Yes, in Form GST EWB-02 after individual e-way bills are generated.
optionC: Yes, instead of individual e-way bills.
optionD: No, consolidated e-way bills were abolished under the new GST scheme.
answerText: Yes, in Form GST EWB-02 after individual e-way bills are generated.
explanation: A consolidated e-way bill in Form GST EWB-02 can be generated by the transporter or generator containing serial numbers of individual e-way bills for consignments carried in the vehicle.
conceptTags: Form GST EWB-02 | Consolidated E-Way Bill | Scenario

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the validity period of the e-way bill for a distance of 150 km?
optionA: 1 day
optionB: 2 days
optionC: 3 days
optionD: 5 days
answerText: 1 day
explanation: The validity period is 1 day for every 200 km or part thereof. For 150 km, it is 1 day (since 150 is part of 200).

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Techno Corp, a registered taxpayer in Kolkata, imports specialized heavy machinery from Germany. The goods arrive at Kolkata Port. Techno Corp engages a custom broker and a transport agency to move the machinery directly from Kolkata Port to its factory in Durgapur, West Bengal (distance of 170 km). The machinery is categorized as Over Dimensional Cargo (ODC) due to its indivisible massive dimensions. The value of the consignment is Rs. 85 Lakhs.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Is an e-way bill required for transporting goods from Kolkata Port directly to the factory in Durgapur?
optionA: No, because movement from a port is totally exempt.
optionB: Yes, because the exemption only applies to movement from port to an ICD/CFS, not to a factory/business place directly.
optionC: No, because it is an import consignment.
optionD: Yes, only if transport is by rail.
answerText: Yes, because the exemption only applies to movement from port to an ICD/CFS, not to a factory/business place directly.
explanation: Exemption under Rule 138(14) applies strictly to movement from customs port/airport to an ICD/CFS for clearance. Movement from port to the factory premises requires an e-way bill.
conceptTags: Port to Factory | Exemption Analysis | Scenario

subject: Taxation
prompt: Who is responsible for generating the e-way bill for this import consignment?
optionA: The foreign supplier in Germany
optionB: The customs officer at Kolkata Port
optionC: Techno Corp (the importer/recipient)
optionD: The shipping line
answerText: Techno Corp (the importer/recipient)
explanation: For import transactions, the importer or recipient located in India is responsible for generating the e-way bill.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What will be the validity period of the e-way bill considering the cargo is Over Dimensional Cargo (ODC) and the distance is 170 km?
optionA: 1 day
optionB: 5 days
optionC: 9 days
optionD: 17 days
answerText: 9 days
explanation: For Over Dimensional Cargo (ODC), the validity is 1 day for every 20 km or part thereof. For 170 km, 170 / 20 = 8.5, which rounds up to 9 days.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If Techno Corp notices an error in the invoice number entered in Part A of the e-way bill after 26 hours of generation, what is the remedy?
optionA: Modify Part A directly on the portal
optionB: Cancel the e-way bill and generate a fresh one with correct details
optionC: Since 24 hours have passed, cancellation is not possible; a new e-way bill must be generated without cancelling the old one, keeping cross-reference records.
optionD: Inform the jurisdictional commissioner in writing to correct it.
answerText: Since 24 hours have passed, cancellation is not possible; a new e-way bill must be generated without cancelling the old one, keeping cross-reference records.
explanation: Part A cannot be modified, and cancellation is only allowed within 24 hours. If 24 hours have passed, the taxpayer cannot cancel it; hence, a new e-way bill with correct details must be generated.
conceptTags: Error Correction | Cancellation Time Limit | Scenario

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Green Fields, an unregistered artisan producing handmade bamboo crafts in Assam, sends a consignment of handicraft goods worth Rs. 75,000 to an emporium in Mumbai, Maharashtra, under an inter-State transaction. They also send another batch of handmade bamboo crafts worth Rs. 40,000 locally within Assam to a local retail shop.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Is an e-way bill required for the inter-State movement of handicraft goods worth Rs. 75,000 by Green Fields?
optionA: No, because artisans dealing in handicrafts are totally exempt from e-way bills.
optionB: Yes, because the consignment value exceeds Rs. 50,000 for inter-State movement by exempted artisans.
optionC: No, because the supplier is unregistered.
optionD: Yes, regardless of the consignment value.
answerText: Yes, because the consignment value exceeds Rs. 50,000 for inter-State movement by exempted artisans.
explanation: Handicraft goods transported inter-State by artisans exempted from registration are required to generate an e-way bill if the consignment value exceeds Rs. 50,000.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Who is required to generate the e-way bill for the inter-State consignment of handicrafts worth Rs. 75,000?
optionA: The unregistered artisan cannot generate an e-way bill under any circumstance.
optionB: The artisan (Green Fields) or the recipient in Mumbai can generate the e-way bill.
optionC: The central GST department automatically generates it.
optionD: The transporter alone must generate it.
answerText: The artisan (Green Fields) or the recipient in Mumbai can generate the e-way bill.
explanation: An unregistered artisan or person can generate an e-way bill on the portal, or the registered recipient in Mumbai can generate it on their behalf.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Is an e-way bill required for the local intra-State movement of handicrafts worth Rs. 40,000 within Assam?
optionA: Yes, because intra-State limit in Assam is Rs. 20,000.
optionB: No, because the value is below Rs. 50,000 and it is an intra-State movement (and also below notified state thresholds if any).
optionC: Yes, all handicrafts require intra-state e-way bills.
optionD: No, because handicrafts are never subject to intra-state e-way bills.
answerText: No, because the value is below Rs. 50,000 and it is an intra-State movement (and also below notified state thresholds if any).
explanation: For intra-State movement, e-way bill is generally required if consignment value exceeds Rs. 50,000 (or higher as notified by the State). Since it is Rs. 40,000, no e-way bill is required.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If Green Fields utilizes a non-motorized conveyance (like a hand-drawn cart) to transport the local goods, how does it affect the e-way bill requirement?
optionA: E-way bill becomes mandatory.
optionB: Goods transported through non-motorized conveyance are exempt from e-way bill.
optionC: Special permission from tax officer is needed.
optionD: Double penalty applies.
answerText: Goods transported through non-motorized conveyance are exempt from e-way bill.
explanation: Rule 138(14) specifically exempts goods transported through a non-motorized conveyance from e-way bill provisions.

subject: Taxation
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Pioneer Industries dispatches a machine part worth Rs. 5,00,000 from its factory in Surat, Gujarat, to a client in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. The transport involves multi-modal transportation: first by road from factory to railway station in Surat, then by railways from Surat to Chennai, and finally by road from Chennai railway station to the client's premises.

subject: Taxation
prompt: When goods are transported by railways, who has the obligation to generate the e-way bill?
optionA: Railways administration
optionB: The consignor (Pioneer Industries) or the consignee
optionC: The station master at Chennai
optionD: The loading contractor
answerText: The consignor (Pioneer Industries) or the consignee
explanation: In case of railway transport, the consignor or consignee is responsible for generating the e-way bill, and railways will not deliver goods without it.

subject: Taxation
prompt: How should the validity of the e-way bill be calculated when goods move via railways combined with road transport?
optionA: Only road distance is counted at 1 day per 200 km.
optionB: Total distance (road + rail + road) is calculated at 1 day per 200 km, and validity is not interrupted by rail transit time.
optionC: Rail transit time is excluded from validity calculation.
optionD: Validity is fixed at 30 days for rail transport.
answerText: Total distance (road + rail + road) is calculated at 1 day per 200 km, and validity is not interrupted by rail transit time.
explanation: The validity of the e-way bill is based on the total distance from origin to destination across all modes of transport, calculated at 1 day for every 200 km.

subject: Taxation
prompt: During the final road leg from Chennai railway station to the client's premises, what document must the person in charge of the vehicle carry?
optionA: Only railway receipt
optionB: Tax invoice/delivery challan and physical/electronic copy of e-way bill
optionC: Only e-way bill without invoice
optionD: Customs clearance certificate
answerText: Tax invoice/delivery challan and physical/electronic copy of e-way bill
explanation: Rule 138A requires carrying the invoice/challan and a copy of the e-way bill during any leg of conveyance transport.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Is the railway administration permitted to deliver the goods to the consignee without the production of an e-way bill?
optionA: Yes, railways are exempt from checking e-way bills.
optionB: No, railways shall not deliver goods unless the e-way bill required under rules is produced.
optionC: Yes, if the freight is fully paid in advance.
optionD: No, but they can deliver after collecting a fine.
answerText: No, railways shall not deliver goods unless the e-way bill required under rules is produced.
explanation: Rule 138(2A) specifies that the railways shall not deliver goods to the consignee unless the e-way bill required under the rules is produced at the time of delivery.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following electronic ledgers maintained on the GST portal is considered as the 'Common Portal' ledger where all tax, interest, penalty, fee or any other amount payable by a taxable person is debited?
optionA: Electronic Credit Ledger
optionB: Electronic Cash Ledger
optionC: Electronic Liability Register
optionD: Electronic Tax Ledger
answerText: Electronic Liability Register
explanation: As per Section 49(7) of the CGST Act, the Electronic Liability Register maintains the total tax, interest, penalty, fee or any other amount payable by a taxable person. All liabilities created under the Act are debited to this register. Thus, it acts as the consolidated statement of liabilities.
conceptTags: Electronic Liability Register | Section 49 | GST Ledgers

subject: Taxation
prompt: Mr. A deposited Rs. 50,000 under the 'Tax' head in his Electronic Cash Ledger. However, he has an unpaid penalty of Rs. 10,000 and tax liability of Rs. 40,000. Can the amount available under the 'Tax' head be utilized for payment of 'Penalty'?
optionA: Yes, any amount in the Electronic Cash Ledger can be utilized for any head without cross-utilization restrictions.
optionB: No, cross-utilization between major heads (Tax, Interest, Penalty, Fee) is not permitted in the Electronic Cash Ledger.
optionC: Yes, but only after exhausting the Electronic Credit Ledger.
optionD: No, penalty can only be paid through the Electronic Credit Ledger.
answerText: No, cross-utilization between major heads (Tax, Interest, Penalty, Fee) is not permitted in the Electronic Cash Ledger.
explanation: Rule 87 of the CGST Rules provides that the amount available in the Electronic Cash Ledger under any major head (Tax, Interest, Penalty, Fee, or Others) cannot be utilized for cross-utilization against another major head unless specifically transferred through Form GST PMT-09.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the order of discharge of tax and other dues as per Section 49(8) of the CGST Act, 2017?
optionA: First dues related to current period, then dues related to previous periods, then other dues.
optionB: First dues related to previous tax periods, then dues related to current period, then other dues.
optionC: First self-assessed tax, then other dues, then disputed dues.
optionD: First penalty, then interest, then tax.
answerText: First dues related to previous tax periods, then dues related to current period, then other dues.
explanation: Section 49(8) prescribes that the liability of a taxable person shall be discharged in the following order: first, dues related to previous tax periods; second, dues related to the current tax period; and finally, any other amount payable (like demand under Section 73 or 74).
conceptTags: Order of Discharge | Section 49 | Tax Dues

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following modes of payment CANNOT be used for generating a challan in Form GST PMT-06?
optionA: Internet Banking through authorized banks
optionB: Over the Counter (OTC) payment through authorized banks up to Rs. 10,000 per challan
optionC: Direct Cash deposit at the jurisdictional GST office
optionD: NEFT/RTGS from any bank
answerText: Direct Cash deposit at the jurisdictional GST office
explanation: Rule 87 allows payment via Internet Banking, Credit/Debit cards, NEFT/RTGS, and Over the Counter (OTC) up to Rs. 10,000 per challan per period (except for certain specified persons). Cash deposit directly at the jurisdictional GST office is not an authorized mode of GST payment.
conceptTags: Challan Generation | Form GST PMT-06 | Modes of Payment

subject: Taxation
prompt: A registered person has mistakenly deposited tax under the 'Central Tax' head instead of 'Integrated Tax'. Can this error be rectified, and if yes, how?
optionA: No, tax deposited under the wrong head is non-refundable and cannot be adjusted.
optionB: Yes, by filing an online refund application in Form GST RFD-01.
optionC: Yes, by transferring the amount from one head to another using Form GST PMT-09.
optionD: Yes, by issuing a debit note to the proper officer.
answerText: Yes, by transferring the amount from one head to another using Form GST PMT-09.
explanation: Under Section 49(10) read with Rule 87(13), a registered person can transfer any amount of tax, interest, penalty, fee or other amount available in any of the major heads of the Electronic Cash Ledger to another major or minor head through Form GST PMT-09 on the common portal.
conceptTags: Form GST PMT-09 | Transfer of Funds | Section 49

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the maximum limit for Over the Counter (OTC) payment through authorized banks per challan, for normal taxpayers, without any exceptions?
optionD: No limit
explanation: As per Rule 87(6), Over the Counter (OTC) payment using cash, cheque, or demand draft through authorized banks is permitted up to Rs. 10,000 per challan per tax period, except for certain categories like TDS/TCS deductors, proper officer recoveries, etc.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can the Electronic Credit Ledger be utilized for payment of output tax liability under the IGST, CGST, and SGST acts?
optionA: Yes, for all taxes, interest, penalty, and late fees.
optionB: Yes, only for payment of output tax, and strictly subject to cross-utilization rules under Section 49.
optionC: No, it can only be used for payment of IGST.
optionD: Yes, but only after exhausting the Electronic Cash Ledger completely.
answerText: Yes, only for payment of output tax, and strictly subject to cross-utilization rules under Section 49.
explanation: Section 49(3) and (4) specify that the amount available in the Electronic Credit Ledger may be used for making payment of output tax only under the CGST, SGST/UTGST, or IGST Act. It cannot be used for payment of interest, penalty, or late fees.
conceptTags: Electronic Credit Ledger | Output Tax | Section 49

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the validity period of a challan generated in Form GST PMT-06 on the common portal?
optionA: 7 days
optionB: 15 days
optionC: 30 days
optionD: No validity period; it remains active until paid
answerText: 15 days
explanation: As per Rule 87(8), the challan generated in Form GST PMT-06 is valid for a period of 15 days. If the payment is not made within 15 days, the challan gets purged from the system, and a fresh challan needs to be generated.
conceptTags: Form GST PMT-06 | Challan Validity | Rule 87

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under what circumstance does the date of credit to the Government account in the authorized bank/RBI determine the date of deposit of tax?
optionA: Always, irrespective of when challan was generated.
optionB: When payment is made via internet banking or NEFT/RTGS.
optionC: Only when payment is made through physical cash deposit at bank counters.
optionD: Never; date of filing return is always the date of deposit.
answerText: When payment is made via internet banking or NEFT/RTGS.
explanation: Rule 87(7) provides that the date of crediting the amount to the authorized bank's account or the Government's account maintained in the RBI shall be deemed to be the date of deposit in the Electronic Cash Ledger, especially for online modes like net banking, NEFT, and RTGS.
conceptTags: Date of Deposit | Electronic Cash Ledger | Rule 87

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following amounts CANNOT be credited to the Electronic Cash Ledger?
optionA: Advance tax paid by the taxpayer
optionB: Interest and penalty paid through challan
optionC: Input tax credit self-assessed in monthly returns
optionD: TDS/TCS deposited by deductors
answerText: Input tax credit self-assessed in monthly returns
explanation: Input tax credit (ITC) self-assessed in returns is credited directly to the Electronic Credit Ledger (Form GST PMT-02), whereas cash, advance tax, interest, penalty, fees, TDS, and TCS are credited to the Electronic Cash Ledger.
conceptTags: Electronic Cash Ledger | ITC | Ledgers Comparison

subject: Taxation
prompt: Mr. X filed his GSTR-3B for the month of July 2026 on 25th September 2026 (due date was 20th August 2026). The tax due was Rs. 1,00,000. Interest is payable under Section 50(1). How is this interest calculated?
optionA: On gross tax liability of Rs. 1,00,000 for the period of delay (36 days).
optionB: On net tax liability paid through cash, for the period of delay (36 days), assuming timely ITC was available.
optionC: No interest is payable if the delay is less than 60 days.
optionD: Interest is calculated at 24% per annum from the due date of return.
answerText: On net tax liability paid through cash, for the period of delay (36 days), assuming timely ITC was available.
explanation: As per the proviso to Section 50(1), interest on delayed payment of tax is levied at 18% p.a. on the *net tax liability* paid through the electronic cash ledger for the period of delay, provided the return is filed after the due date and self-assessed ITC was duly available in the credit ledger.
conceptTags: Section 50 | Interest on Delayed Payment | Net Tax Liability

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can the Electronic Credit Ledger be used for payment of any tax liability arising out of demand notices issued under Section 74 (fraud/suppression cases)?
optionA: Yes, fully without any restrictions.
optionB: No, Electronic Credit Ledger can only be used for payment of self-assessed output tax.
optionC: Yes, up to 50% of the demand.
optionD: Yes, with the prior approval of the Commissioner.
answerText: No, Electronic Credit Ledger can only be used for payment of self-assessed output tax.
explanation: Rule 86A and Section 49(3) restrict the use of Electronic Credit Ledger strictly to 'output tax'. Tax payable under reverse charge or demand proceedings (Sections 73/74) cannot be discharged from the Electronic Credit Ledger unless explicitly permitted (self-assessed output tax).
conceptTags: Electronic Credit Ledger | Output Tax | Demand Proceedings

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the rate of interest prescribed under Section 50(1) for delayed payment of GST?
optionA: 12% per annum
optionB: 15% per annum
optionC: 18% per annum
optionD: 24% per annum
answerText: 18% per annum
explanation: As per Notification No. 13/2017-Central Tax, issued under Section 50(1), the rate of interest for delayed payment of central tax is 18 percent per annum.

subject: Taxation
prompt: If a taxpayer wrongfully utilizes Input Tax Credit (ITC) and subsequently pays back the amount along with interest before any notice is issued, does this constitute a discharge of liability under Section 50?
optionA: Yes, interest is payable at 24% p.a. under Section 50(3) for wrongful availment and utilization of ITC.
optionB: No interest is payable if reversed before notice.
optionC: Interest is payable at 18% p.a. under Section 50(1).
optionD: Penal action is mandatory, and interest does not apply.
answerText: Yes, interest is payable at 24% p.a. under Section 50(3) for wrongful availment and utilization of ITC.
explanation: As per Section 50(3) read with Rule 88B, where input tax credit has been *wrongfully availed and utilized*, interest is payable at 24% per annum for the period starting from the date of utilization till the date of reversal/payment.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which electronic ledger acts as a summary of all tax demands, pending proceedings, and amounts refunded or adjusted against a registered person?
optionA: Electronic Cash Ledger
optionB: Electronic Credit Ledger
optionC: Electronic Liability Register
optionD: Electronic Tax Return Ledger
answerText: Electronic Liability Register
explanation: The Electronic Liability Register (Part-I, Part-II, etc.) records all liabilities of a taxable person arising from returns, notices, demands, interest, and penalty, as well as payments made against them, providing a complete trail of dues.
conceptTags: Electronic Liability Register | GST Compliance | Section 49

subject: Taxation
prompt: What happens to the Unique Identification Number (UIN) generated on the GST portal when a challan is created via NEFT/RTGS?
optionA: It becomes the bank account number for fund transfer.
optionB: It acts as the CPIN (Common Portal Identification Number) which must be quoted to the remitting bank.
optionC: It is a temporary password for login.
optionD: It represents the refund tracking number.
answerText: It acts as the CPIN (Common Portal Identification Number) which must be quoted to the remitting bank.
explanation: When a challan is generated using NEFT/RTGS mode, a CPIN (Common Portal Identification Number) is generated along with a mandate form. The taxpayer uses this CPIN as the beneficiary account number with their bank to push funds via NEFT/RTGS to RBI.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can a taxable person transfer an amount from the Electronic Cash Ledger of CGST to the Electronic Cash Ledger of SGST of another registered person (e.g., a related entity)?
optionA: Yes, freely transferrable between any two GSTINs under the same PAN.
optionB: Yes, with the consent of the jurisdictional officer.
optionC: No, transfer via Form GST PMT-09 is only permitted between major/minor heads for the *same* GSTIN.
optionD: No, cross-GSTIN cash transfers are completely prohibited under all circumstances.
answerText: No, transfer via Form GST PMT-09 is only permitted between major/minor heads for the *same* GSTIN.
explanation: Form GST PMT-09 allows transfer of funds between major and minor heads *within* the same Electronic Cash Ledger of a registered person (GSTIN). Transfer to another GSTIN (even under the same PAN) is not permitted through PMT-09.
conceptTags: Form GST PMT-09 | Same GSTIN Restriction | Transfer of Funds

subject: Taxation
prompt: In case of a mismatch between the tax declared in GSTR-3B and GSTR-1, leading to a short payment of tax, where is the liability first recorded on the portal?
optionA: Directly debited to Electronic Credit Ledger
optionB: Recorded in Part-I of the Electronic Liability Register
optionC: Sent as a physical notice before portal entry
optionD: Debited to Electronic Cash Ledger automatically
answerText: Recorded in Part-I of the Electronic Liability Register
explanation: Any liability self-assessed in returns (like GSTR-3B) or determined through proceedings is debited to the Electronic Liability Register (Part-I: Return related liabilities), establishing the formal demand on the portal.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the consequence if a taxpayer fails to pay tax within the prescribed due date, and no ITC is available in the credit ledger?
optionA: Tax must be paid through Electronic Cash Ledger along with interest under Section 50(1) at 18% p.a.
optionB: Tax can be paid later without any interest if turnover is below Rs. 5 Crores.
optionC: Registration is cancelled automatically on the 1st of the next month.
optionD: Penalty of Rs. 50,000 is levied immediately without notice.
answerText: Tax must be paid through Electronic Cash Ledger along with interest under Section 50(1) at 18% p.a.
explanation: Delayed payment of tax requires payment through the Electronic Cash Ledger along with mandatory interest under Section 50(1) at 18% per annum for the period of delay.
conceptTags: Section 50 | Delayed Payment | Electronic Cash Ledger

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which of the following forms is prescribed for filing a refund claim of excess balance available in the Electronic Cash Ledger?
optionA: Form GST PMT-09
optionB: Form GST RFD-01
optionC: Form GST PMT-03
optionD: Form GST TRAN-1
answerText: Form GST RFD-01
explanation: Application for refund of balance in the Electronic Cash Ledger is filed electronically in Form GST RFD-01 under Section 54 read with Rule 89.
conceptTags: Refund | Form GST RFD-01 | Electronic Cash Ledger

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can interest payable under Section 50 be paid by debiting the Electronic Credit Ledger?
optionA: Yes, for all registered taxpayers.
optionB: No, interest under Section 50 must always be paid through the Electronic Cash Ledger.
optionC: Yes, if the cash balance is zero.
optionD: Yes, with prior permission of the Assistant Commissioner.
answerText: No, interest under Section 50 must always be paid through the Electronic Cash Ledger.
explanation: As per Section 49(3) and Section 49(4), the Electronic Credit Ledger can *only* be used for payment of output tax. Interest, penalty, late fee, and tax under reverse charge must always be paid via the Electronic Cash Ledger.
conceptTags: Electronic Credit Ledger | Interest Payment | Section 49

subject: Taxation
prompt: When is a challan considered 'paid' and credited to the Electronic Cash Ledger when payment is made via NEFT/RTGS?
optionA: Immediately upon generation of CPIN.
optionB: When the remitting bank confirms the debit from the taxpayer's bank account.
optionC: When the RBI confirms receipt of funds and communicates the CIN (Challan Identification Number) to the GST portal.
optionD: After manual verification by the jurisdictional GST officer.
answerText: When the RBI confirms receipt of funds and communicates the CIN (Challan Identification Number) to the GST portal.
explanation: For NEFT/RTGS, once the remitting bank transfers the funds to the RBI account designated for GST, the RBI generates a CIN (Challan Identification Number), which is communicated to the GST portal, reflecting the credit in the Electronic Cash Ledger.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the penalty for failure to pay tax deducted at source (TDS) under Section 51 within the prescribed time?
optionA: No penalty if paid within 90 days.
optionB: Interest under Section 50 and late fee under Section 47, along with recovery provisions under Section 73/74.
optionC: Fixed penalty of Rs. 10,000 only.
optionD: Imprisonment up to 3 years mandatory.
answerText: Interest under Section 50 and late fee under Section 47, along with recovery provisions under Section 73/74.
explanation: A deductor who fails to pay TDS to the government is liable to pay interest under Section 50, late fee, and the amount becomes recoverable as arrears of tax along with applicable penalties.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Is transfer of unutilized balance of CGST from Electronic Cash Ledger to IGST Electronic Cash Ledger permitted?
optionA: No, inter-head transfers are prohibited.
optionB: Yes, CGST major head can be transferred to IGST major head using Form GST PMT-09.
optionC: Yes, but only through a refund claim in Form GST RFD-01.
optionD: No, CGST cash balance can only be used for CGST liabilities.
answerText: Yes, CGST major head can be transferred to IGST major head using Form GST PMT-09.
explanation: Under Section 49(10) and Rule 87(13), a registered person can transfer any amount from one major/minor head (e.g., CGST Tax) to another major/minor head (e.g., IGST Tax) within their Electronic Cash Ledger using Form GST PMT-09.
conceptTags: Form GST PMT-09 | Inter-head Transfer | Electronic Cash Ledger

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under Rule 88C, if there is a significant difference between liability reported in GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B that exceeds the specified threshold, what action is triggered?
optionA: Immediate arrest of the managing director.
optionB: An intimation is issued in Part A of Form GST DRB-01 / Form GST DRC-01B requiring explanation or payment.
optionC: Cancellation of registration without show cause notice.
optionD: Automatic debit of Electronic Credit Ledger.
answerText: An intimation is issued in Part A of Form GST DRB-01 / Form GST DRC-01B requiring explanation or payment.
explanation: Rule 88C addresses differences in liability between GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B. The taxpayer is intimated in Part A of Form GST DRC-01B to either pay the differential tax with interest or explain the difference within the specified time.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can a taxable person utilize the balance in the Electronic Credit Ledger to pay tax under Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM)?
optionA: Yes, RCM liability is treated as output tax.
optionB: No, tax payable under reverse charge must be paid through the Electronic Cash Ledger.
optionC: Yes, if output tax liability is nil.
optionD: Yes, up to 50% of the RCM liability.
answerText: No, tax payable under reverse charge must be paid through the Electronic Cash Ledger.
explanation: Tax payable under reverse charge (RCM) is not considered 'output tax' for the recipient for the purpose of credit ledger utilization. Therefore, RCM liability must be paid in cash via the Electronic Cash Ledger.
conceptTags: Reverse Charge | Electronic Credit Ledger | Cash Payment

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the time limit for a registered person to file an appeal against a tax demand order before paying the mandatory pre-deposit of 10% of the disputed tax?
optionA: Pre-deposit of 10% is a mandatory condition for filing the appeal itself.
optionB: Pre-deposit can be paid within 30 days after filing the appeal.
optionC: Pre-deposit is not required if appeal is filed within 15 days.
optionD: Pre-deposit can be paid through Electronic Credit Ledger.
answerText: Pre-deposit of 10% is a mandatory condition for filing the appeal itself.
explanation: As per Section 107(6) of the CGST Act, no appeal can be filed unless the appellant has deposited a sum equal to 10% of the remaining amount of tax in dispute arising from the order, subject to a maximum of Rs. 25 crores.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which electronic ledger reflects the net ITC available for utilization after subtracting all eligible reversals and distributions?
optionA: Electronic Cash Ledger
optionB: Electronic Credit Ledger
optionC: Electronic Liability Register
optionD: Electronic ITC Summary Ledger
answerText: Electronic Credit Ledger
explanation: The Electronic Credit Ledger (Form GST PMT-02) records all input tax credit self-assessed and allowed, minus reversals, providing the balance available for utilization against output tax.
conceptTags: Electronic Credit Ledger | Form GST PMT-02 | ITC

subject: Taxation
prompt: Under Rule 88B, for calculating interest on delayed payment of tax, if the return is filed *after* the due date, the interest on net cash liability is calculated from:
optionA: The date of generation of invoice.
optionB: The due date of filing the return, up to the date of actual payment of tax.
optionC: The beginning of the financial year.
optionD: The date of issuance of show cause notice.
answerText: The due date of filing the return, up to the date of actual payment of tax.
explanation: Rule 88B clarifies that interest under Section 50(1) on delayed payment of tax through the electronic cash ledger runs from the day immediately following the due date of filing the return for the respective tax period, up to the date of payment of such tax.

subject: Taxation
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Vertex Enterprises, a registered taxpayer in Maharashtra, filed its GSTR-3B for the month of October 2026 on 10th December 2026. The prescribed due date for filing GSTR-3B for October 2026 was 20th November 2026. 

For the said tax period, Vertex Enterprises had a gross tax liability of Rs. 2,00,000. It had sufficient eligible Input Tax Credit (ITC) of Rs. 1,50,000 in its Electronic Credit Ledger on the due date, and the net tax liability of Rs. 50,000 was paid through the Electronic Cash Ledger on 10th December 2026. 

Additionally, the proper officer noticed that in August 2026, Vertex Enterprises had wrongly availed and utilized ITC of Rs. 30,000, which was reversed on 1st December 2026 along with interest.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the period of delay for calculating interest under Section 50(1) on the net tax liability of Rs. 50,000 for October 2026?
optionA: 20 days (from 21st November to 10th December)
optionB: 21 days (from 20th November to 10th December)
optionC: 51 days (from 20th October to 10th December)
optionD: Nil, since ITC was available.
answerText: 20 days (from 21st November to 10th December)
explanation: The due date was 20th November 2026. The tax was paid on 10th December 2026. As per Rule 88B, the period of delay starts from the day following the due date (21st November 2026) up to the date of payment (10th December 2026), which equals 20 days.

subject: Taxation
prompt: On what amount is interest under Section 50(1) calculated for the delayed filing of the October 2026 return?
optionA: Gross tax liability of Rs. 2,00,000
optionB: Net tax liability of Rs. 50,000 paid through Electronic Cash Ledger
optionC: Only on the ITC portion of Rs. 1,50,000
optionD: Total turnover of October 2026
answerText: Net tax liability of Rs. 50,000 paid through Electronic Cash Ledger
explanation: Since self-assessed ITC (Rs. 1,50,000) was available in the Electronic Credit Ledger on the due date, interest under Section 50(1) (proviso) is payable only on the net tax liability paid through the Electronic Cash Ledger (Rs. 50,000).
conceptTags: Section 50 | Net Tax Liability | Proviso to Section 50(1)

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the applicable rate of interest under Section 50(3) for the wrongful availment and utilization of ITC of Rs. 30,000 in August 2026?
optionA: 12% per annum
optionB: 18% per annum
optionC: 24% per annum
optionD: 36% per annum
answerText: 24% per annum
explanation: As per Section 50(3) read with Rule 88B, where input tax credit has been wrongfully availed and utilized, interest is levied at 24% per annum for the period starting from the date of utilization till the date of reversal.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can Vertex Enterprises utilize the balance in its Electronic Credit Ledger to pay the interest arising from delayed return filing for October 2026?
optionA: Yes, because the total credit exceeds the interest amount.
optionB: No, interest must be paid via the Electronic Cash Ledger.
optionC: Yes, with permission from the jurisdictional commissioner.
optionD: Only if CGST credit is used.
answerText: No, interest must be paid via the Electronic Cash Ledger.
explanation: Section 49(3) and (4) restrict the use of the Electronic Credit Ledger strictly to the payment of 'output tax'. Interest under Section 50 must be discharged through the Electronic Cash Ledger.
conceptTags: Electronic Credit Ledger | Interest Payment | Section 49

subject: Taxation
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Zenith Traders, a registered GST taxpayer in Gujarat, has deposited Rs. 1,00,000 under the 'CGST - Tax' head in its Electronic Cash Ledger. During the month, Zenith Traders realizes that it has no CGST tax liability, but it has an outstanding IGST tax liability of Rs. 60,000, a CGST penalty of Rs. 10,000, and an IGST interest liability of Rs. 15,000. 

Zenith Traders wishes to reallocate funds within its Electronic Cash Ledger to settle these liabilities efficiently without making a fresh cash deposit.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Which form should Zenith Traders file on the common portal to transfer funds from 'CGST - Tax' to 'IGST - Tax' and 'CGST - Penalty'?
optionA: Form GST PMT-03
optionB: Form GST PMT-09
optionC: Form GST RFD-01
optionD: Form GST DRC-03
answerText: Form GST PMT-09
explanation: Form GST PMT-09 is prescribed under Section 49(10) and Rule 87(13) for transferring any amount from one major or minor head to another within the Electronic Cash Ledger.
conceptTags: Form GST PMT-09 | Transfer of Funds | Section 49

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can Zenith Traders transfer an amount from the 'CGST - Tax' head directly to the 'CGST - Penalty' head using Form GST PMT-09?
optionA: No, transfer from Tax head to Penalty head is prohibited.
optionB: Yes, transfer between major and minor heads is fully permissible under Form GST PMT-09.
optionC: Yes, but only after exhausting the Electronic Credit Ledger.
optionD: No, penalty can only be paid by cash deposit through a new challan.
answerText: Yes, transfer between major and minor heads is fully permissible under Form GST PMT-09.
explanation: Form GST PMT-09 allows taxpayers to transfer amounts across major heads (like CGST to IGST) as well as minor heads (like Tax to Penalty) within the Electronic Cash Ledger.
conceptTags: Form GST PMT-09 | Minor Heads | Cross-head Transfer

subject: Taxation
prompt: After transferring Rs. 60,000 to IGST Tax and Rs. 10,000 to CGST Penalty, what will be the remaining balance under 'CGST - Tax' in Zenith Traders' Electronic Cash Ledger?
optionD: Nil
explanation: Initial deposit under CGST-Tax was Rs. 1,00,000. Transferred to IGST-Tax: Rs. 60,000. Transferred to CGST-Penalty: Rs. 10,000. Remaining balance = 1,00,000 - 60,000 - 10,000 = Rs. 30,000 under CGST-Tax head.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can Zenith Traders use its Electronic Credit Ledger to pay the IGST interest liability of Rs. 15,000?
optionA: Yes, since IGST credit is available.
optionB: No, interest can never be paid from the Electronic Credit Ledger.
optionC: Yes, up to 50% of the interest.
optionD: Yes, if the jurisdictional officer grants approval.
answerText: No, interest can never be paid from the Electronic Credit Ledger.
explanation: As per Section 49(4), the Electronic Credit Ledger can only be utilized for payment of output tax. Interest, penalty, and late fees must always be paid through the Electronic Cash Ledger.
conceptTags: Electronic Credit Ledger | Interest Payment | Restriction

subject: Taxation
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: Mr. Vikram, a registered taxable person in Delhi, generated a challan in Form GST PMT-06 on the GST portal on 5th October 2026 for a tax liability of Rs. 75,000 using the Over the Counter (OTC) payment mode through an authorized bank. 

Due to certain banking holidays, Vikram tendered cash at the bank counter on 22nd October 2026. The bank accepted the cash and issued a receipt. However, the GST portal did not reflect the credit in Vikram's Electronic Cash Ledger, and instead raised a notice for non-payment.

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the validity period of a challan generated in Form GST PMT-06?
optionA: 7 days
optionB: 10 days
optionC: 15 days
optionD: 30 days
answerText: 15 days
explanation: As per Rule 87(8) of the CGST Rules, a challan generated in Form GST PMT-06 is valid for a period of 15 days from the date of generation.
conceptTags: Form GST PMT-06 | Challan Validity | Rule 87

subject: Taxation
prompt: Why did the GST portal fail to reflect the deposit made by Mr. Vikram on 22nd October 2026?
optionA: Because OTC payments take 15 working days to process.
optionB: Because the challan had expired on 20th October 2026 (15 days validity) and was purged/invalidated.
optionC: Because cash payments are prohibited in Delhi.
optionD: Because the tax amount exceeded Rs. 50,000.
answerText: Because the challan had expired on 20th October 2026 (15 days validity) and was purged/invalidated.
explanation: The challan was generated on 5th October and its 15-day validity expired on 20th October 2026. Payment made on 22nd October was against an expired/purged challan, hence the system did not credit the Electronic Cash Ledger.
conceptTags: Challan Expiry | Form GST PMT-06 | Rule 87

subject: Taxation
prompt: What is the maximum limit per challan for Over the Counter (OTC) payment through authorized banks for normal taxpayers?
optionD: No limit
explanation: Rule 87(6) prescribes a maximum limit of Rs. 10,000 per challan per tax period for OTC payments through authorized bank counters using cash, cheque, or demand draft (except for specific authorized categories).

subject: Taxation
prompt: What action should Mr. Vikram take to resolve the issue regarding the expired challan and uncredited deposit?
optionA: File an appeal before the High Court.
optionB: Generate a fresh challan, make the payment, and approach the bank/jurisdictional officer for refund or adjustment of the erroneous deposit made on the expired challan.
optionC: Debit his Electronic Credit Ledger for Rs. 75,000.
optionD: File GSTR-9 annual return to regularize the payment.
answerText: Generate a fresh challan, make the payment, and approach the bank/jurisdictional officer for refund or adjustment of the erroneous deposit made on the expired challan.
explanation: Since the challan expired, the payment made on it is treated as a deposit against an invalid reference. Vikram must generate a valid challan to clear his tax liability and coordinate with the bank/tax authorities to claim a refund or adjustment of the erroneous deposit.
conceptTags: Expired Challan | Remedial Action | GST Payment

subject: Taxation
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Dynamic Logistics, a transport contractor registered under GST in Tamil Nadu, received a demand order under Section 73 of the CGST Act on 10th September 2026 demanding tax of Rs. 5,00,000, interest of Rs. 60,000, and a penalty of Rs. 50,000 for FY 2023-24. 

Dynamic Logistics has an accumulated balance of Rs. 4,00,000 in its Electronic Credit Ledger and Rs. 1,50,000 in its Electronic Cash Ledger. The management wants to discharge the entire demand liability using the balances available in these ledgers without bringing in any additional external funds immediately.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can Dynamic Logistics utilize the balance in its Electronic Credit Ledger (Rs. 4,00,000) to pay the tax demand of Rs. 5,000,000 under Section 73?
optionA: Yes, up to the extent of credit available.
optionB: No, Electronic Credit Ledger can only be used for self-assessed output tax, not for demand dues under Section 73.
optionC: Yes, with the permission of the Commissioner.
optionD: Yes, because Section 73 demands are treated as output tax.
answerText: No, Electronic Credit Ledger can only be used for self-assessed output tax, not for demand dues under Section 73.
explanation: Section 49(3) and (4) restrict the utilization of the Electronic Credit Ledger strictly to 'output tax'. Tax payable pursuant to demand proceedings under Section 73/74 cannot be paid using the credit ledger.
conceptTags: Electronic Credit Ledger | Demand Proceedings | Section 73

subject: Taxation
prompt: How must the tax, interest, and penalty demanded under Section 73 be paid?
optionA: Entirely through the Electronic Credit Ledger.
optionB: Entirely through the Electronic Cash Ledger.
optionC: Tax through Credit Ledger, Interest and Penalty through Cash Ledger.
optionD: Through physical cash deposited at the treasury.
answerText: Entirely through the Electronic Cash Ledger.
explanation: All components of a demand order under Section 73 (tax, interest, and penalty) must be paid strictly through the Electronic Cash Ledger, as credit ledger utilization is barred for demands.
conceptTags: Electronic Cash Ledger | Demand Payment | Section 73

subject: Taxation
prompt: Dynamic Logistics decides to file an appeal against the order under Section 107. What is the mandatory pre-deposit percentage of the disputed tax that must be paid before filing the appeal?
optionA: 5% of disputed tax
optionB: 10% of disputed tax
optionC: 20% of disputed tax
optionD: 50% of disputed tax
answerText: 10% of disputed tax
explanation: Section 107(6) mandates a pre-deposit of 10% of the remaining amount of tax in dispute arising from the order, subject to a maximum of Rs. 25 crores, before an appeal can be entertained.

subject: Taxation
prompt: Can the pre-deposit for filing an appeal under Section 107 be paid from the Electronic Cash Ledger?
optionA: No, pre-deposit must be paid via bank draft only.
optionB: Yes, pre-deposit can be paid by debiting the Electronic Cash Ledger.
optionC: Yes, but only from the Electronic Credit Ledger.
optionD: No, pre-deposit requires cash deposit directly to the appellate authority.
answerText: Yes, pre-deposit can be paid by debiting the Electronic Cash Ledger.
explanation: Any pre-deposit required for filing an appeal under GST is treated as payment of tax/amount under the Act and can be discharged through the Electronic Cash Ledger generated via challan.

subject: Taxation
prompt:
CASE SCENARIO: M/s. Omega Traders filed its GSTR-3B for January 2026 on 20th February 2026. While scrutinizing returns, the proper officer observed that Omega Traders had reported outward taxable supplies of Rs. 50,00,000 in GSTR-1, but declared taxable supplies of only Rs. 40,000,000 in GSTR-3B, resulting in a tax short-fall of Rs. 1,80,000 (assuming 18% average rate).
