optionB: Whether the company is regular in depositing undisputed statutory dues, and if not regular, the extent of arrears outstanding for more than six months from the date they became payable
optionC: Only whether income tax has been deducted at source
optionD: Whether the company owes money to foreign tax authorities
answerText: Whether the company is regular in depositing undisputed statutory dues, and if not regular, the extent of arrears outstanding for more than six months from the date they became payable
explanation: Paragraph 3(vii)(a) of CARO 2020 requires reporting on whether the company is regular in depositing undisputed statutory dues and, where not regular, the extent of arrears outstanding for a period of more than six months.

subject: Audit
prompt: Under SA 701, how does the auditor determine which matters are 'Key Audit Matters'?
optionA: By selecting matters that resulted in a modified opinion only
optionB: By selecting matters of most significance in the audit of the financial statements of the current period, based on areas of higher assessed risk of material misstatement or significant auditor attention
optionC: By listing all items that appeared in the audit program
optionD: By asking the Board of Directors to nominate five items for disclosure
answerText: By selecting matters of most significance in the audit of the financial statements of the current period, based on areas of higher assessed risk of material misstatement or significant auditor attention
explanation: SA 701 defines Key Audit Matters as those matters that, in the auditor's professional judgment, were of most significance in the audit of the financial statements of the current period, drawn from areas of significant auditor attention.
conceptTags: SA 701 | Key Audit Matters | Professional Judgment

subject: Audit
prompt: Can an auditor communicate Key Audit Matters in the auditor's report if the audit opinion is a Disclaimer of Opinion?
optionA: Yes, whenever required by law or regulation
optionB: No, SA 701 prohibits communicating KAM when the auditor disclaims an opinion on the financial statements, unless required by law or regulation
optionC: Yes, provided management gives written consent
optionD: No, KAM is only permitted when an adverse opinion is issued
answerText: No, SA 701 prohibits communicating KAM when the auditor disclaims an opinion on the financial statements, unless required by law or regulation
explanation: According to SA 701, when the auditor disclaims an opinion on the financial statements, the auditor shall not communicate key audit matters in the auditor's report, unless required by law or regulation, because doing so might contradict the disclaimer.
conceptTags: SA 701 | Disclaimer of Opinion | KAM Prohibition

subject: Audit
prompt: If a material uncertainty related to going concern is adequately disclosed in the financial statements, how should the auditor report on it under SA 570 (Revised)?
optionA: Issue an adverse opinion due to fundamental uncertainty
optionB: Issue an unmodified opinion and include a separate section under the heading 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern'
optionC: Omit any reference to it to avoid alarming shareholders
optionD: Issue a disclaimer of opinion because of the existence of uncertainty
answerText: Issue an unmodified opinion and include a separate section under the heading 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern'
explanation: Under SA 570 (Revised), if adequate disclosure of a material uncertainty is made in the financial statements, the auditor shall express an unmodified opinion and include a separate section in the auditor's report titled 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern'.

subject: Audit
prompt: What is the consequence under SA 570 (Revised) if management's assessment of going concern discloses a material uncertainty, but that uncertainty is NOT adequately disclosed in the financial statements?
optionA: The auditor shall express a qualified opinion or an adverse opinion
optionB: The auditor shall express an unmodified opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph
optionC: The auditor shall issue a clean report with an Other Matter paragraph
optionD: The auditor shall take no action if the business is profitable
answerText: The auditor shall express a qualified opinion or an adverse opinion
explanation: Per SA 570 (Revised), if adequate disclosure is not made in the financial statements, the auditor shall express a qualified opinion or an adverse opinion, as appropriate, in accordance with SA 705.
conceptTags: SA 570 | Inadequate Disclosure | Qualified or Adverse Opinion

subject: Audit
prompt: Under Section 143(3) of the Companies Act, 2013, what must the auditor report regarding the financial statements' compliance with Accounting Standards?
optionA: Whether the financial statements comply with the Accounting Standards referred to in Section 133
optionB: Whether the financial statements comply with International Financial Reporting Standards exclusively
optionC: Whether the financial statements comply with tax audit guidelines issued by CBDT
optionD: Whether the financial statements comply with the internal policies of the parent company
answerText: Whether the financial statements comply with the Accounting Standards referred to in Section 133
explanation: Section 143(3)(e) of the Companies Act, 2013 requires the auditor to state whether, in their opinion, the financial statements comply with the Accounting Standards referred to in Section 133.

subject: Audit
prompt: What should the date of the independent auditor's report be, according to SA 700 (Revised)?
optionA: The date on which the annual general meeting (AGM) is held
optionB: The date on which the auditor has obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base the opinion on the financial statements
optionC: The date on which management signs the directors' report
optionD: The financial year-end date
answerText: The date on which the auditor has obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base the opinion on the financial statements
explanation: SA 700 (Revised) specifies that the auditor's report shall be dated no earlier than the date on which the auditor has obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base the opinion on the financial statements, including evidence that the financial statements have been prepared.
conceptTags: SA 700 | Date of Audit Report | Audit Evidence

subject: Audit
prompt: Under CARO 2020, does the auditor need to report on whether any proceedings have been initiated or are pending against the company for holding any benami property under the Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act, 1988?
optionA: No, this is outside the scope of CARO 2020
optionB: Yes, reporting on benami property proceedings is specifically required under CARO 2020 clause (xi)
optionC: Only if the company is a public sector undertaking
optionD: Only if requested by the Income Tax Department
answerText: Yes, reporting on benami property proceedings is specifically required under CARO 2020 clause (xi)
explanation: Clause (xi) of paragraph 3 of CARO 2020 requires reporting on whether any proceedings have been initiated or are pending against the company for holding any benami property under the Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act, 1988 and rules made thereunder.

subject: Audit
prompt: Which of the following describes an 'Adverse Opinion' issued under SA 705 (Revised)?
optionA: The auditor expresses no opinion because of a severe scope limitation
optionB: The auditor states that the financial statements give a true and fair view except for specific misstatements
optionC: The auditor states that the financial statements do not give a true and fair view in accordance with the financial reporting framework due to pervasive misstatements
optionD: The auditor highlights a significant uncertainty without modifying the core opinion
answerText: The auditor states that the financial statements do not give a true and fair view in accordance with the financial reporting framework due to pervasive misstatements
explanation: An adverse opinion is expressed when the auditor, having obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence, concludes that misstatements, individually or in the aggregate, are both material and pervasive to the financial statements.
conceptTags: SA 705 | Adverse Opinion | True and Fair View

subject: Audit
prompt: In an audit report, if an Emphasis of Matter paragraph is included, can it be placed before the Opinion section?
optionA: Yes, if management prefers it to be prominent
optionB: No, SA 706 (Revised) requires the EOM paragraph to be included subsequent to the Opinion and Basis for Opinion sections
optionC: Yes, provided it is highlighted in bold font
optionD: It can be placed anywhere in the Notes to Accounts
answerText: No, SA 706 (Revised) requires the EOM paragraph to be included subsequent to the Opinion and Basis for Opinion sections
explanation: SA 706 (Revised) mandates that if the auditor includes an Emphasis of Matter paragraph in the auditor's report, the auditor shall locate it separately with an appropriate heading, after the Opinion and Basis for Opinion sections.
conceptTags: SA 706 | Emphasis of Matter | Paragraph Placement

subject: Audit
prompt: Under Section 143(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, what inquiry is the auditor specifically required to make regarding loans and advances?
optionA: Whether loans and advances made by the company are properly secured and whether terms are prejudicial to the interest of the company or its members
optionB: Whether loans and advances exceed 50% of the share capital
optionC: Whether all loans carry an interest rate higher than the bank rate
optionD: Whether loans were disbursed in cash exceeding INR 10,000
answerText: Whether loans and advances made by the company are properly secured and whether terms are prejudicial to the interest of the company or its members
explanation: Section 143(1)(a) requires the auditor to inquire whether loans and advances made by the company on the basis of security have been properly secured and whether the terms on which they have been made are prejudicial to the interests of the company or its members.
conceptTags: Companies Act 2013 | Section 143(1) | Loans and Advances

subject: Audit
prompt: When can an auditor sign the independent auditor's report of a company?
optionA: Before the financial statements are approved by the Board of Directors
optionB: After the financial statements have been approved by the Board of Directors and signed by authorized signatories
optionC: At any time during the financial year regardless of financial statement preparation
optionD: Only after the Annual General Meeting concludes
answerText: After the financial statements have been approved by the Board of Directors and signed by authorized signatories
explanation: The auditor can sign the audit report only after the financial statements have been approved by the Board of Directors under Section 134(5) of the Companies Act, 2013 and signed in accordance with statutory requirements.
conceptTags: Companies Act 2013 | Board Approval | Audit Report Signature

subject: Audit
prompt: What is the requirement under CARO 2020 regarding unrecorded income surrendered or disclosed as income in tax assessments?
optionA: No reporting required under CARO 2020
optionB: Whether any transactions not recorded in the books of account have been surrendered or disclosed as income during the year in the tax assessments under the Income Tax Act, and whether such income has been properly recorded in the books
optionC: Only report if tax penalty exceeds INR 1 crore
optionD: Report whether income tax returns were filed before the due date
answerText: Whether any transactions not recorded in the books of account have been surrendered or disclosed as income during the year in the tax assessments under the Income Tax Act, and whether such income has been properly recorded in the books
explanation: Clause (xix) of paragraph 3 of CARO 2020 requires the auditor to report on whether any unrecorded transactions have been surrendered or disclosed as income in tax assessments and whether they were recorded in the books.

subject: Audit
prompt: Under SA 700 (Revised), what constitutes the signature of the auditor in the independent auditor's report?
optionA: Only the name of the audit firm in block letters
optionB: The personal name of the engagement partner along with the firm's registration number and membership number, signed in the personal name of the individual auditor
optionC: A digital QR code generated by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs
optionD: The signature of the Managing Director of the auditee company
answerText: The personal name of the engagement partner along with the firm's registration number and membership number, signed in the personal name of the individual auditor
explanation: The auditor's report must be signed in the personal name of the auditor and/or engagement partner, along with their membership number and the firm's registration number assigned by ICAI.
conceptTags: SA 700 | Auditor Signature | Firm Registration Number

subject: Audit
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Zenith Pharma Ltd., a listed pharmaceutical company, is undergoing its annual audit for the year ended March 31, 2026. During the audit, the statutory auditors discovered that a massive inventory valuation dispute with tax authorities has been ongoing. The amount involved is material but restricted to specific inventory batches in one manufacturing plant. Furthermore, the management refused to allow the auditor to inspect third-party confirmation replies for trade receivables amounting to 4% of total assets, citing confidentiality agreements with overseas clients.

subject: Audit
prompt: Based on the inventory valuation dispute (which is material but restricted to specific batches), how should the auditor evaluate its impact on the audit opinion under SA 705?
optionA: Issue an Adverse opinion because inventory is a core asset
optionB: Issue a Qualified opinion because the misstatement is material but not pervasive
optionC: Issue a Disclaimer of opinion due to lack of cooperation
optionD: Issue an Unmodified opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph
answerText: Issue a Qualified opinion because the misstatement is material but not pervasive
explanation: Under SA 705, when misstatements are material but not pervasive (confined to specific batches/items), the appropriate modification is a qualified opinion.

subject: Audit
prompt: Regarding the management's refusal to permit inspection of third-party receivable confirmations (representing 4% of total assets), how should the auditor classify this situation?
optionA: A management-imposed scope limitation
optionB: A routine accounting policy disagreement
optionC: A subsequent event disclosure requirement
optionD: A key audit matter only
answerText: A management-imposed scope limitation
explanation: Denying access to necessary audit evidence, such as receivable confirmations, constitutes a scope limitation imposed by management under SA 705.

subject: Audit
prompt: Since Zenith Pharma Ltd. is a listed entity, what standard governs the communication of significant audit matters like the inventory dispute in the audit report?
optionA: SA 700 (Revised)
optionB: SA 701
optionC: SA 706 (Revised)
optionD: SA 570 (Revised)
answerText: SA 701
explanation: SA 701 governs the communication of Key Audit Matters for listed entities, highlighting matters of most significance.
conceptTags: SA 701 | Listed Entity | Key Audit Matters

subject: Audit
prompt: Where in the independent auditor's report should the specific reasons for modifying the opinion due to the inventory and receivable issues be articulated?
optionA: In the Basis for Qualified Opinion section immediately following the Auditor's Opinion
optionB: In the Notes to Accounts prepared by management
optionC: In the Director's Report under Corporate Governance
optionD: In the Other Information section
answerText: In the Basis for Qualified Opinion section immediately following the Auditor's Opinion
explanation: SA 705 requires that when the opinion is modified, the 'Basis for Qualified Opinion' section must be placed immediately after the Auditor's Opinion section to explain the reasons.
conceptTags: SA 705 | Basis for Opinion | Report Structure

subject: Audit
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Sunrise Textiles Ltd., an unlisted public company, has incurred net operating losses for three consecutive years. Its current liabilities exceed its current assets by INR 45 crores. The company's key lender has issued a formal notice recalling a term loan due to covenant breaches. However, management has prepared cash flow projections showing that an impending sale of surplus land in the next quarter will generate adequate liquidity to settle the term loan and fund operations. Management has made adequate disclosures regarding these conditions and plans in the notes to the financial statements.

subject: Audit
prompt: Which auditing standard primarily governs the auditor's responsibilities relating to going concern in this audit engagement?
optionA: SA 500
optionB: SA 570 (Revised)
optionC: SA 701
optionD: SA 710
answerText: SA 570 (Revised)
explanation: SA 570 (Revised) deals with the auditor's responsibilities in the audit of financial statements relating to going concern.

subject: Audit
prompt: Given that a material uncertainty exists regarding going concern but adequate disclosure has been made in the financial statements, how should the auditor report on this?
optionA: Issue a Disclaimer of opinion
optionB: Issue an Unmodified opinion with a separate section titled 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern'
optionC: Issue an Adverse opinion because of covenant breaches
optionD: Issue a clean report without mentioning the uncertainty
answerText: Issue an Unmodified opinion with a separate section titled 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern'
explanation: Under SA 570 (Revised), if adequate disclosure of a material uncertainty is made, the auditor expresses an unmodified opinion and includes a distinct section titled 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern'.

subject: Audit
prompt: If management refused to disclose the material uncertainty regarding the term loan recall and land sale in the notes to accounts, what would be the appropriate audit report modification?
optionA: Qualified or Adverse opinion
optionB: Emphasis of Matter paragraph only
optionC: Unmodified opinion with Other Matter paragraph
optionD: No modification required
answerText: Qualified or Adverse opinion
explanation: Per SA 570 (Revised), if adequate disclosure is not made in the financial statements, the auditor shall express a qualified opinion or an adverse opinion.

subject: Audit
prompt: Since Sunrise Textiles Ltd. is an unlisted company, is it mandatory for the auditor to communicate Key Audit Matters under SA 701?
optionA: Yes, for all companies under the Companies Act, 2013
optionB: No, unless required by law/regulation or voluntarily decided by the auditor
optionC: Yes, whenever losses exceed INR 10 crores
optionD: No, SA 701 applies exclusively to banking companies
answerText: No, unless required by law/regulation or voluntarily decided by the auditor
explanation: SA 701 applies to audits of listed entities. For unlisted entities like Sunrise Textiles Ltd., KAM communication is not mandatory unless required by law/regulation or elected by the auditor.
conceptTags: SA 701 | Key Audit Matters | Unlisted Entities

subject: Audit
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: M/s Apex & Associates, Chartered Accountants, are auditing Omega Engineering Ltd. for the financial year 2025-26. The financial statements include corresponding figures for the prior year (2024-25). The prior year's financial statements were audited by a predecessor auditor, whose report expressed a qualified opinion due to unverified work-in-progress inventory. In the current year, the matter giving rise to the prior qualification has been completely resolved. However, during the current audit, a new and material dispute regarding patent infringement arises, which remains unresolved at the signing date.

subject: Audit
prompt: Which auditing standard governs the auditor's responsibilities regarding comparative information and corresponding figures in this scenario?
optionA: SA 700
optionB: SA 710
optionC: SA 705
optionD: SA 706
answerText: SA 710
explanation: SA 710 deals with the auditor's responsibilities relating to comparative information, including corresponding figures and comparative financial statements.

subject: Audit
prompt: How should the auditor report on the prior year's qualification given that the matter has been fully resolved in the current period?
optionA: The current auditor's report generally should not refer to the previous qualification since it is resolved
optionB: The current auditor must re-issue the predecessor's qualified report
optionC: The current auditor must express an adverse opinion on the current year's figures
optionD: The current auditor must add an Emphasis of Matter regarding the old WIP
answerText: The current auditor's report generally should not refer to the previous qualification since it is resolved
explanation: Under SA 710, when the prior period matter that caused a qualification is resolved, the current period opinion does not need to refer to the previous qualification.

subject: Audit
prompt: How should the current auditor deal with the new and material patent infringement dispute that is unresolved at the signing date?
optionA: Ignore it because it relates to legal matters
optionB: Evaluate its materiality and pervasiveness and modify the current year's audit opinion accordingly (qualified or adverse)
optionC: Issue an unmodified opinion with an Other Matter paragraph
optionD: Issue a disclaimer of opinion automatically without assessment
answerText: Evaluate its materiality and pervasiveness and modify the current year's audit opinion accordingly (qualified or adverse)
explanation: A current period material misstatement or scope limitation regarding a patent dispute requires the auditor to modify the opinion on the current financial statements in accordance with SA 705.
conceptTags: SA 705 | Current Period Misstatement | Modified Opinion

subject: Audit
prompt: If the predecessor auditor's report on the prior period's financial statements was NOT reissued, what paragraph may the current auditor include in the report under SA 710?
optionA: An Other Matter paragraph stating that the prior period financial statements were audited by a predecessor auditor
optionB: An Emphasis of Matter paragraph modifying the opinion on prior balances
optionC: A Key Audit Matter paragraph detailing predecessor fees
optionD: A CARO reporting clause on predecessor competence
answerText: An Other Matter paragraph stating that the prior period financial statements were audited by a predecessor auditor
explanation: SA 710 permits the current auditor to include an Other Matter paragraph indicating that the prior period financial statements were audited by a predecessor auditor, the opinion expressed, and the date thereof.
conceptTags: SA 710 | Predecessor Auditor | Other Matter Paragraph

subject: Audit
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Delta Commercial Ltd. is a manufacturing company registered under the Companies Act, 2013. During the statutory audit for 2025-26, the auditor reviews compliance with CARO 2020 and the Companies Act, 2013. The auditor finds that the company has defaulted in repayment of dues to a financial institution for 90 days. Furthermore, the company has taken unsecured loans from three directors, the terms of which the auditor suspects may be prejudicial to the company's interest. Lastly, management has used short-term working capital borrowings amounting to INR 12 crores to fund long-term capital machinery acquisitions.

subject: Audit
prompt: Under CARO 2020, how should the auditor report on the default in repayment of dues to the financial institution?
optionA: Report under clause (ix) regarding default in repayment of loans or other borrowings to any financial institution, bank, government, or debenture holders
optionB: Report under clause (i) on Fixed Assets
optionC: Report under Section 143(3) only without CARO reference
optionD: Ignore if settled before the AGM
answerText: Report under clause (ix) regarding default in repayment of loans or other borrowings to any financial institution, bank, government, or debenture holders
explanation: Paragraph 3(ix) of CARO 2020 requires reporting on whether the company has defaulted in repayment of loans or other borrowings or in the payment of interest thereon to any lender.

subject: Audit
prompt: Regarding the unsecured loans taken from directors, which statutory inquiry under Section 143(1) of the Companies Act, 2013 is directly triggered?
optionA: Whether loans and advances made by the company are prejudicial, and whether loans taken are properly managed
optionB: Whether terms on which loans and advances have been made are prejudicial to the interests of the company or its members
optionC: Whether directors have paid tax on such loans
optionD: Whether loans exceed the paid-up capital of the company
answerText: Whether terms on which loans and advances have been made are prejudicial to the interests of the company or its members
explanation: Section 143(1)(a) requires the auditor to inquire whether terms on which loans and advances made by the company are prejudicial to the interests of the company or its members.
conceptTags: Companies Act 2013 | Section 143(1) | Loans and Advances

subject: Audit
prompt: Which specific CARO 2020 clause requires reporting when short-term funds are utilized for long-term purposes?
optionA: Clause (ix)(e) regarding funds raised on short term basis being used for long term purposes
optionB: Clause (iii) regarding loans granted to parties covered in register
optionC: Clause (vii) regarding statutory dues
optionD: Clause (xi) regarding managerial remuneration
answerText: Clause (ix)(e) regarding funds raised on short term basis being used for long term purposes
explanation: CARO 2020 paragraph 3(ix)(e) requires reporting on whether the company has taken any funds from any entity or person on account of or to meet the obligations of its subsidiaries, associates, or joint ventures, and clause (ix)(f) covers short-term funds used for long-term purposes.
conceptTags: CARO 2020 | Short-term vs Long-term Funds | Clause (ix)

subject: Audit
prompt: Where must the CARO 2020 report be presented in relation to the main independent auditor's report under the Companies Act, 2013?
optionA: As an annexure/addendum attached to the independent auditor's report
optionB: Inside the Director's Report as a separate chapter
optionC: Submitted directly to SEBI without attaching to the audit report
optionD: As part of the Notes to Accounts
answerText: As an annexure/addendum attached to the independent auditor's report
explanation: The CARO report is issued as an annexure to the independent auditor's report under the Companies Act, 2013, addressing the specific matters prescribed by the Central Government.

subject: Audit
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Aura Tech Solutions Ltd. is a software development company. During the audit for the year ended March 31, 2026, the engagement partner decided to include an Emphasis of Matter (EOM) paragraph in the auditor's report to highlight a catastrophic fire incident that occurred at the company's primary server facility after the balance sheet date but before the signing of the audit report. Management has made full and appropriate disclosure of this event in Note 24 of the financial statements. Additionally, the auditor observed that the financial statements include a supplementary unaudited schedule required by a specific industry regulator.

subject: Audit
prompt: Which auditing standard governs the inclusion of the Emphasis of Matter paragraph regarding the fire incident?
optionA: SA 700
optionB: SA 706 (Revised)
optionC: SA 560
optionD: SA 570
answerText: SA 706 (Revised)
explanation: SA 706 (Revised) deals with Emphasis of Matter paragraphs and Other Matter paragraphs in the auditor's report.
conceptTags: SA 706 | Emphasis of Matter | Server Fire Incident

subject: Audit
prompt: Is the inclusion of the EOM paragraph for the fire incident a substitute for modifying the auditor's opinion?
optionA: Yes, EOM replaces a qualified opinion when management is cooperative
optionB: No, an Emphasis of Matter paragraph is not a modification of the auditor's opinion
optionC: Yes, because the event occurred after the balance sheet date
optionD: No, but it automatically converts an unmodified opinion into a disclaimer
answerText: No, an Emphasis of Matter paragraph is not a modification of the auditor's opinion
explanation: SA 706 explicitly clarifies that an Emphasis of Matter paragraph is not a modification of the auditor's opinion; the opinion remains unmodified.

subject: Audit
prompt: How should the auditor report on the supplementary unaudited schedule required by the industry regulator?
optionA: Using an Other Matter paragraph under SA 706 to draw attention to a matter other than those presented in financial statements
optionB: By modifying the core opinion on the main financial statements
optionC: By issuing a separate audit report with a qualified opinion
optionD: By ignoring the supplementary schedule entirely
answerText: Using an Other Matter paragraph under SA 706 to draw attention to a matter other than those presented in financial statements
explanation: An Other Matter paragraph is used when the auditor needs to communicate a matter other than those presented or disclosed in the financial statements that is relevant to users' understanding, such as reporting on supplementary information.
conceptTags: SA 706 | Other Matter Paragraph | Supplementary Information

subject: Audit
prompt: Where should the Emphasis of Matter paragraph regarding Note 24 be positioned within the independent auditor's report?
optionA: Before the Auditor's Opinion section
optionB: After the Opinion and Basis for Opinion sections, and before Key Audit Matters (if applicable)
optionC: As a footnote on the Balance Sheet
optionD: In the Report on Other Legal and Regulatory Requirements
answerText: After the Opinion and Basis for Opinion sections, and before Key Audit Matters (if applicable)
explanation: SA 706 (Revised) requires the EOM paragraph to be located separately in the auditor's report, after the Opinion and Basis for Opinion sections.
conceptTags: SA 706 | Paragraph Placement | Audit Report Formatting

subject: Audit
prompt: Which of the following is the primary document governing the audit of a registered cooperative society in India?
optionA: The Companies Act, 2013
optionB: The Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002 or respective State Cooperative Societies Act
optionC: The Banking Regulation Act, 1949
optionD: The Indian Trusts Act, 1882
answerText: The Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002 or respective State Cooperative Societies Act
explanation: Cooperative societies are formed and registered under specific legislative frameworks such as the State Cooperative Societies Act or the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002, which govern their administration and audit requirements.
conceptTags: Cooperative Societies | Statutory Framework | Audit Mandate

subject: Audit
prompt: In the audit of a cooperative society, the auditor is specifically required to report on which of the following due to statutory mandates?
optionA: Personal investments of the managing committee members
optionB: Violation of the provisions of the Cooperative Societies Act, rules, and bye-laws
optionC: Market share and competitor pricing strategies
optionD: Private business transactions of ordinary members
answerText: Violation of the provisions of the Cooperative Societies Act, rules, and bye-laws
explanation: Special audit reports for cooperative societies heavily emphasize checking compliance with the governing Act, registered rules, and the society's specific bye-laws, particularly regarding loans, investments, and utilization of funds.
conceptTags: Cooperative Audit | Bye-laws Compliance | Statutory Reporting

subject: Audit
prompt: While auditing a cooperative society, an auditor notices that loans have been advanced to non-members. Under general cooperative principles, what is the appropriate audit position?
optionA: It is acceptable if authorized by a majority vote in the annual general meeting.
optionB: It is a violation unless specifically permitted by the Registrar or the Act/Bye-laws.
optionC: It is standard banking practice and requires no special comment.
optionD: It is permitted if secured by adequate immovable property.
answerText: It is a violation unless specifically permitted by the Registrar or the Act/Bye-laws.
explanation: Cooperative societies are mutual associations intended primarily to serve their members. Advancing loans to non-members is generally prohibited unless specific exemptions exist under the Act, rules, or bye-laws, or with the Registrar's sanction.
conceptTags: Cooperative Audit | Loans to Non-members | Statutory Violation

subject: Audit
prompt: Who has the statutory authority to appoint the auditor of a cooperative society in most jurisdictions in India?
optionA: The Board of Directors of the society
optionB: The Registrar of Cooperative Societies
optionC: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (C&AG)
optionD: The Reserve Bank of India
answerText: The Registrar of Cooperative Societies
explanation: In most cooperative societies, the statute vests the power of appointing the auditor directly in the Registrar of Cooperative Societies, or the audit is conducted directly by the Registrar's staff.

subject: Audit
prompt: What is the primary objective of an audit of a charitable institution or NGO?
optionA: To maximize net profit distributable to founders
optionB: To ensure that funds are applied towards the objects of the trust and comply with legal provisions
optionC: To verify compliance with the SEBI Listing Regulations
optionD: To assess the personal tax liability of the trustees
answerText: To ensure that funds are applied towards the objects of the trust and comply with legal provisions
explanation: Charitable trusts and NGOs operate for public or mutual benefit. The auditor must verify that income and donations are applied strictly in accordance with the objects specified in the trust deed or memorandum of association.
conceptTags: NGO Audit | Charitable Trust | Object Compliance

subject: Audit
prompt: When auditing anonymous donations received by a charitable trust, which audit procedure is most critical?
optionA: Confirming the identity of each donor through PAN cards
optionB: Checking internal controls over collection boxes, receipt issuance, and recording in books
optionC: Inspecting the minutes of the board meeting for personal approvals
optionD: Verifying that tax has been deducted at source on such donations
answerText: Checking internal controls over collection boxes, receipt issuance, and recording in books
explanation: Anonymous donations present a high risk of misappropriate handling. Auditors must evaluate internal controls governing physical collection, hundi boxes, and timely accounting to ensure completeness.
conceptTags: NGO Audit | Anonymous Donations | Internal Controls

subject: Audit
prompt: Under Indian tax laws applicable to trusts and NGOs, accumulation of income beyond the permissible limit requires filing which form or compliance?
optionA: Form 10 to accumulate income for specific purposes
optionB: Form 3CD for tax audit
optionC: Form 15G for non-deduction of tax
optionD: Form 26AS reconciliation
answerText: Form 10 to accumulate income for specific purposes
explanation: Under Section 11(2) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, if a trust wishes to accumulate or set apart income exceeding 15% for application to charitable or religious purposes, it must file Form 10 within the prescribed time.
conceptTags: NGO Audit | Income Tax Act | Form 10

subject: Audit
prompt: In the audit of an educational institution (like a school or college), what is the key verification step regarding tuition fee revenue?
optionA: Checking fee collection against student rolls, admission registers, and concession records
optionB: Inspecting the market value of land owned by the institution
optionC: Verifying the personal salary advances given to teaching staff
optionD: Tracing all expenditure vouchers to the university syndicate resolutions
answerText: Checking fee collection against student rolls, admission registers, and concession records
explanation: Fee income is the lifeblood of educational institutions. Auditors must reconcile fee collections with student attendance/admission rolls and verify that any fee concessions are properly authorized by competent authorities.
conceptTags: Educational Institution | Fee Revenue | Audit Procedures

subject: Audit
prompt: While auditing a university, the auditor notices that caution money collected from students has been utilized to finance day-to-day administrative expenses. How should the auditor treat this?
optionA: Accept it as normal working capital management
optionB: Qualify the report as caution money is a liability that should be kept separately or invested safely
optionC: Suggest transferring it to the general reserve fund immediately
optionD: Ignore it if the amount is less than 5% of total revenue
answerText: Qualify the report as caution money is a liability that should be kept separately or invested safely
explanation: Caution money is a refundable deposit received from students and represents a liability. Utilizing it for operational expenses without maintaining liquid funds or specific investments is improper and warrants qualification.

subject: Audit
prompt: What is the prime governing statute for the audit of a localized hospital run by a public trust?
optionA: The Companies Act, 2013 exclusively
optionB: The Clinical Establishments Act and the Trust Act / Societies Registration Act under which it is formed
optionC: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act
optionD: The Pharmacy Act, 1948
answerText: The Clinical Establishments Act and the Trust Act / Societies Registration Act under which it is formed
explanation: Hospitals operate under various legal structures—trusts, societies, corporate bodies, or government departments. Their audit is governed by the specific statute of incorporation along with applicable medical regulations.
conceptTags: Hospital Audit | Governing Statutes | Entity Types

subject: Audit
prompt: When auditing pharmaceutical inventories and surgical stores in a hospital, which specific audit risk must the auditor address?
optionA: Foreign exchange fluctuations on imported medicines
optionB: Obsolescence, expiry dates, and proper valuation of drugs and consumables
optionC: Capitalization of consumable items as fixed assets
optionD: Depreciation of medicines using the straight-line method
answerText: Obsolescence, expiry dates, and proper valuation of drugs and consumables
explanation: Hospital inventories include drugs, consumables, and surgical items that are prone to expiration and obsolescence. Auditors must verify physical stock verification and proper valuation at the lower of cost and net realizable value.
conceptTags: Hospital Audit | Inventory Valuation | Expiry Risk

subject: Audit
prompt: In a hotel audit, which of the following represents a crucial internal control area regarding room occupancy and billing?
optionA: Reconciliation of front office daily night audit reports with housekeeping reports and kitchen orders
optionB: Verification of export duty drawback claims
optionC: Checking compliance with factory labor welfare legislation
optionD: Ensuring actuarial valuation of gratuity for permanent staff
answerText: Reconciliation of front office daily night audit reports with housekeeping reports and kitchen orders
explanation: Hotels rely heavily on front office systems. The night audit reconciles room occupancy records with actual billings, restaurant KOTs (Kitchen Order Tickets), and cash collections to prevent revenue leakage.
conceptTags: Hotel Audit | Night Audit | Revenue Controls

subject: Audit
prompt: Which of the following documents is most essential for an auditor to review when verifying guest ledger balances in a hotel audit?
optionA: The guest register, bill folios, and daily summary of cash/credit card collections
optionB: The charter of incorporation
optionC: The annual general meeting minutes book
optionD: The title deeds of the hotel building
answerText: The guest register, bill folios, and daily summary of cash/credit card collections
explanation: Guest ledger balances represent amounts due from currently staying or recently departed guests. Reviewing bill folios and daily collection summaries ensures that receivables are accurately stated and collected.

subject: Audit
prompt: What is a distinguishing feature of a Self-Help Group (SHG) audit that sets it apart from a corporate audit?
optionA: Focus on informal group dynamics, micro-savings, internal lending records, and resolution books
optionB: Mandatory compliance with Ind AS and quarterly financial reporting to stock exchanges
optionC: Extensive testing of derivatives and hedging instruments
optionD: Verification of consolidated financial statements of global subsidiaries
answerText: Focus on informal group dynamics, micro-savings, internal lending records, and resolution books
explanation: SHGs are informal or semi-formal micro-finance groups. Their audits focus heavily on meeting minutes, internal savings registers, inter-loaning records, and repayment tracking among members rather than complex accounting standards.

subject: Audit
prompt: When auditing a cinema hall or multiplex, what is the primary source document for verifying box office collections?
optionA: Daily movie-wise/show-wise statement of tickets sold, counter counterfoils, and computerized ticketing system logs
optionB: Electricity consumption bills of the theater
optionC: Maintenance contracts for projection equipment
optionD: Catering vendor agreement files
answerText: Daily movie-wise/show-wise statement of tickets sold, counter counterfoils, and computerized ticketing system logs
explanation: Box office revenue in a cinema is verified using computerized ticketing system reports, physical counterfoil checks, and daily show statements reconciled with seat occupancy data.
conceptTags: Cinema Audit | Box Office | Revenue Verification

subject: Audit
prompt: In a club audit, what is the treatment of life membership fees received from members?
optionA: Credited entirely to the income and expenditure account in the year of receipt
optionB: Capitalized and treated as a liability/capital fund, amortized over a period or retained as corpus
optionC: Distributed as dividends to founding members
optionD: Treated as an advance tax liability
answerText: Capitalized and treated as a liability/capital fund, amortized over a period or retained as corpus
explanation: Life membership fees represent amounts received for lifetime services and are generally capitalized in the balance sheet under capital fund or reserves, recognizing them as income over the expected period of membership or retaining them as corpus as per bye-laws.

subject: Audit
prompt: Which of the following is a critical check when auditing a hire-purchase finance company?
optionA: Ensuring that the ownership of the asset remains with the financier until the final installment is paid
optionB: Confirming that hire charges are recognized as income entirely on the date of agreement
optionC: Checking that leased assets are depreciated in the books of the hirer only
optionD: Verifying that no interest element is included in installment amounts
answerText: Ensuring that the ownership of the asset remains with the financier until the final installment is paid
explanation: In hire-purchase transactions, legal ownership remains with the financier until the option to purchase is exercised by payment of the final installment, which dictates asset and revenue recognition principles.
conceptTags: Hire Purchase Audit | Ownership | Finance Companies

subject: Audit
prompt: What special consideration must an auditor keep in mind when auditing a local body (such as a Gram Panchayat, Municipality, or Municipal Corporation)?
optionA: Compliance with municipal budgetary sanctions, fund allocations, and statutory sanctioning powers
optionB: Maximization of shareholder dividend yields
optionC: Transfer pricing documentation requirements
optionD: Inventory turnover ratios for finished goods
answerText: Compliance with municipal budgetary sanctions, fund allocations, and statutory sanctioning powers
explanation: Local body audits focus extensively on regularity and propriety, ensuring that expenditure does not exceed budgetary allocations and that statutory approvals and sanctioning powers are strictly adhered to.
conceptTags: Local Bodies Audit | Budgetary Control | Sanctions

subject: Audit
prompt: When conducting an audit of a government department, the auditor (C&AG or person acting on its behalf) must verify 'Sanction to Expenditure'. What does this entail?
optionA: Checking whether every item of expenditure is covered by a sanction, general or special, given by competent authority
optionB: Verifying that the department made a net profit on its operational activities
optionC: Ensuring that all employees have filed their personal income tax returns
optionD: Confirming that goods were procured from the lowest bidder regardless of quality
answerText: Checking whether every item of expenditure is covered by a sanction, general or special, given by competent authority
explanation: Audit against sanction is a key pillar of government audit, ensuring that no expenditure is incurred without proper authority and competence as laid down in financial rules and delegation of financial powers.
conceptTags: Government Audit | Audit Against Sanction | C&AG

subject: Audit
prompt: What is the primary purpose of 'Propriety Audit' in government and public sector undertakings?
optionA: To check whether the expenditure is incurred with financial wisdom, public interest, and avoidance of extravagance
optionB: To verify arithmetical accuracy of accounting entries
optionC: To ensure compliance with corporate income tax filing deadlines
optionD: To calculate the exact market capitalization of the entity
answerText: To check whether the expenditure is incurred with financial wisdom, public interest, and avoidance of extravagance
explanation: Propriety audit goes beyond mere legality. It requires the auditor to examine whether public funds have been spent with due regard to public interest, economy, and freedom from wasteful expenditure.
conceptTags: Propriety Audit | Public Sector | Wasteful Expenditure

subject: Audit
prompt: In the audit of a branch of a nationalized bank, what is the primary focus regarding Non-Performing Assets (NPAs)?
optionA: Classification of advances based on RBI prudential norms regarding overdue periods and security realization
optionB: Checking whether the branch has achieved its annual deposit mobilization targets
optionC: Verifying the physical count of stationery items
optionD: Inspecting the personal loan files of bank directors
answerText: Classification of advances based on RBI prudential norms regarding overdue periods and security realization
explanation: Bank branch audits require rigorous verification of loan accounts to classify them into Standard, Sub-standard, Doubtful, or Loss categories strictly in accordance with RBI income recognition and asset classification (IRAC) norms.
conceptTags: Bank Audit | NPA Classification | RBI Norms

subject: Audit
prompt: Which of the following entities is subject to audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (C&AG) under the Constitution of India?
optionA: Only Central Government ministries and departments
optionB: Central Government, State Governments, and Government Companies as specified by law
optionC: All private limited companies registered in India
optionD: Only cooperative societies registered under Multi-State Acts
answerText: Central Government, State Governments, and Government Companies as specified by law
explanation: Under Article 149-151 of the Constitution and the CAG (DPC) Act, 1971, the C&AG audits the accounts of the Union, States, Union Territories, and government companies/corporations.
conceptTags: C&AG Audit | Constitutional Mandate | Government Entities

subject: Audit
prompt: When auditing a transport company (fleet operator), which operational expense requires special audit attention and testing for fuel leakage or misuse?
optionA: High-Speed Diesel (HSD) consumption compared with mileage logs and vehicle route sheets
optionB: Depreciation of office computers
optionC: Audit fees paid to the statutory auditor
optionD: Board meeting refreshment expenses
answerText: High-Speed Diesel (HSD) consumption compared with mileage logs and vehicle route sheets
explanation: For transport operators, fuel is a major cost component. Auditors must correlate fuel purchases and consumption with distance traveled, vehicle efficiency, and logbooks to detect pilferage or misuse.
conceptTags: Transport Company | Fuel Consumption | Operational Audit

subject: Audit
prompt: In the context of an electricity distribution company (Discom) audit, what is 'Distribution Loss' and why is it audited?
optionA: The difference between energy injected into the distribution system and energy billed to consumers, audited to detect technical losses and commercial theft
optionB: The loss incurred on the sale of copper scrap by the utility
optionC: Financial losses arising from foreign currency loans taken for power plants
optionD: Depreciation of power transformers over their useful life
answerText: The difference between energy injected into the distribution system and energy billed to consumers, audited to detect technical losses and commercial theft
explanation: Distribution loss in power utilities represents electricity lost due to technical factors and theft/meter tampering. Auditors review loss figures as they directly impact regulatory tariff determinations and operational efficiency.
conceptTags: Electricity Company | Distribution Loss | Utility Audit

subject: Audit
prompt: What is the key audit objective when examining 'Grants-in-Aid' received by an institution from the government?
optionA: Verifying that the grants are utilized strictly for the specific purpose and conditions stipulated by the sanctioning authority
optionB: Treating the grant as general business revenue without restrictions
optionC: Checking whether income tax has been paid on the grant amount
optionD: Ensuring the grant is distributed as bonus to employees
answerText: Verifying that the grants are utilized strictly for the specific purpose and conditions stipulated by the sanctioning authority
explanation: Government grants are typically tied to specific projects or conditions. Auditors must verify utilization certificates, separate accounting, and compliance with all terms of the grant order.

subject: Audit
prompt: While auditing a mutual fund, what responsibility does the auditor have regarding the Net Asset Value (NAV) computation?
optionA: Verifying that NAV is computed in accordance with SEBI Regulations and valuation policies, and checking methodology for asset valuation
optionB: Guaranteeing investors a minimum rate of return on their investments
optionC: Managing the day-to-day portfolio buy/sell decisions
optionD: Filing quarterly income tax returns on behalf of investors
answerText: Verifying that NAV is computed in accordance with SEBI Regulations and valuation policies, and checking methodology for asset valuation
explanation: Mutual fund auditors evaluate the systems and controls surrounding NAV calculation, ensuring securities are valued as per SEBI guidelines and units are correctly priced.
conceptTags: Mutual Fund Audit | NAV Calculation | SEBI Regulations

subject: Audit
prompt: In an audit of a Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC), how are credit concentration norms verified by the auditor?
optionA: Checking whether credit exposure to single borrowers and borrower groups exceeds the limits prescribed by the RBI
optionB: Verifying that the NBFC only lends to government entities
optionC: Ensuring that all borrowings are unsecured
optionD: Checking that administrative overheads do not exceed 10% of income
answerText: Checking whether credit exposure to single borrowers and borrower groups exceeds the limits prescribed by the RBI
explanation: RBI prudential norms for NBFCs prescribe concentration limits on lending and investments to single borrowers and group borrowers to mitigate credit risk. Auditors must verify compliance.
conceptTags: NBFC Audit | Credit Concentration | RBI Norms

subject: Audit
prompt: What is a primary audit concern when examining the accounts of a publisher regarding royalty payments to authors?
optionA: Ensuring royalties are calculated accurately based on sales/royalty agreements and verifying stock records of books sold versus unsold
optionB: Checking whether authors are permanent employees of the publishing house
optionC: Verifying that royalty expenses are capitalized under intangible assets
optionD: Confirming that royalty is paid in advance before manuscript printing
answerText: Ensuring royalties are calculated accurately based on sales/royalty agreements and verifying stock records of books sold versus unsold
explanation: Publishers pay royalties based on contractual terms linked to sales or editions. Auditors must reconcile royalty statements with sales registers and stock movement records to ensure correct expenses.

subject: Audit
prompt: When auditing a cooperative housing society, what is the significance of examining the 'Share Transfer Register' and 'Nomination Register'?
optionA: To ensure proper legal transfer of flat ownership, membership rights, and succession in case of a member's demise
optionB: To calculate the corporate tax liability of the society
optionC: To verify the market valuation of building construction materials
optionD: To check the electricity meter readings for each apartment
answerText: To ensure proper legal transfer of flat ownership, membership rights, and succession in case of a member's demise
explanation: In cooperative housing societies, shares are linked to flat ownership. Verifying transfer and nomination registers ensures that voting rights and property rights vest in legally valid members.
conceptTags: Cooperative Housing | Share Transfer | Nomination Register

subject: Audit
prompt: What is the auditor's primary concern when reviewing 'Capital Work-in-Progress' (CWIP) in the audit of a manufacturing enterprise undergoing expansion?
optionA: Ensuring that pre-operative expenses are properly allocated and capitalization ceases when assets are ready for intended use
optionB: Checking whether employees working on the project are paid overtime
optionC: Verifying that CWIP is depreciated at the standard rate of 15% per annum
optionD: Ensuring all project funds are kept in current accounts without interest
answerText: Checking whether employees working on the project are paid overtime
explanation: CWIP represents assets not yet ready for use and is not depreciated. The auditor must verify that capitalization stops when the asset is ready for its intended use, and pre-operative expenses are allocated properly.

subject: Audit
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Green Valley Cooperative Housing Society Ltd., registered under the State Cooperative Societies Act, has 150 members. During the financial year 2025-26, the managing committee undertook major repairs to the society's water tank costing Rs 15 lakhs without inviting competitive tenders, citing urgency. Additionally, the society advanced a temporary loan of Rs 2 lakhs from its reserve fund to a committee member for personal medical emergencies. The statutory auditor appointed by the Registrar is reviewing the accounts.

subject: Audit
prompt: How should the auditor evaluate the contract for water tank repairs given that no competitive tenders were invited?
optionA: Ignore it since managing committees have absolute discretion in emergencies.
optionB: Verify whether the bye-laws or procurement rules of the society require tenders and whether emergency powers were validly exercised and ratified.
optionC: Qualify the report solely based on the quantum of expenditure without checking bye-laws.
optionD: Treat the entire repair cost as a personal liability of the committee members.
answerText: Verify whether the bye-laws or procurement rules of the society require tenders and whether emergency powers were validly exercised and ratified.
explanation: Cooperative societies must adhere to procurement procedures laid down in their bye-laws or state rules. The auditor must examine if emergency provisions exist and if the committee acted within its delegated powers.
conceptTags: Cooperative Audit | Procurement Tenders | Bye-laws Compliance

subject: Audit
prompt: What is the audit implication of the temporary loan of Rs 2 lakhs advanced from the reserve fund to a committee member?
optionA: It is completely valid if the member repays it within 30 days with interest.
optionB: It constitutes a statutory violation as cooperative funds and reserves cannot generally be lent to committee members unless specifically authorized by the Act/Registrar.
optionC: It is acceptable as long as majority members consented informally at a tea party.
optionD: It should be reclassified as an administrative expense of the society.
answerText: It constitutes a statutory violation as cooperative funds and reserves cannot generally be lent to committee members unless specifically authorized by the Act/Registrar.
explanation: Lending society funds—especially reserve funds—to managing committee members is strictly regulated or prohibited under cooperative laws to prevent conflict of interest and misuse of mutual funds. This requires strong adverse reporting.
conceptTags: Cooperative Audit | Loans to Members | Statutory Violation

subject: Audit
prompt: Who is legally responsible for appointing the statutory auditor for Green Valley Cooperative Housing Society Ltd.?
optionA: The Managing Committee of the society
optionB: The Registrar of Cooperative Societies
optionC: The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
optionD: The National Housing Bank
answerText: The Registrar of Cooperative Societies
explanation: Under cooperative legislation, the statutory audit of cooperative societies is under the direct control of the Registrar of Cooperative Societies, who appoints the auditor from an approved panel.

subject: Audit
prompt: If the auditor discovers widespread financial irregularities, to whom must the special report under cooperative law be submitted?
optionA: Only to the Chairman of the managing committee
optionB: To the Registrar of Cooperative Societies and presented at the general body meeting as required
optionC: To the local police station directly without informing management
optionD: To the stock exchange regulators
answerText: To the Registrar of Cooperative Societies and presented at the general body meeting as required
explanation: Statutory audit reports of cooperative societies are submitted directly to the Registrar of Cooperative Societies, and significant irregularities must also be brought to the notice of the general body of members.

subject: Audit
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Hope Charitable Trust runs an educational hospital and a school. During 2025-26, the trust received Rs 50 lakhs as corpus donations with specific directions from donors that the amount be kept as permanent endowment. It also received Rs 10 lakhs in cash through hundi collection boxes without names. The trust utilized 70% of its total income for charitable objects, accumulated 15% under Section 11(2) by filing Form 10, and retained the remaining 10% as unspent surplus. The auditor is conducting the annual audit under the Income-tax Act and trust deed.

subject: Audit
prompt: How should the auditor verify the Rs 50 lakhs received as corpus donations?
optionA: Treat them as revenue income taxable at normal corporate rates.
optionB: Verify donor letters/instructions confirming corpus nature and ensure they are credited directly to the corpus fund balance sheet head, exempt under Section 11(1)(d).
optionC: Deduct 30% tax at source before recording them in books.
optionD: Transfer them immediately to the income and expenditure account.
answerText: Verify donor letters/instructions confirming corpus nature and ensure they are credited directly to the corpus fund balance sheet head, exempt under Section 11(1)(d).
explanation: Corpus donations received with specific directions that they shall form part of the corpus of the trust are exempt from income tax under Section 11(1)(d), provided they are invested or deposited in approved modes.
conceptTags: NGO Audit | Corpus Donations | Income Tax Act

subject: Audit
prompt: What audit procedures are appropriate for verifying the Rs 10 lakhs collected through anonymous hundi boxes?
optionA: Obtain PAN cards of every devotee who dropped cash into the hundi.
optionB: Verify internal controls over hundi box opening, dual custody, physical counting in the presence of authorized trustees, and proper receipt issuance.
optionC: Treat the entire hundi collection as taxable income without checking records.
optionD: Ignore the amount as it is below materiality thresholds.
answerText: Verify internal controls over hundi box opening, dual custody, physical counting in the presence of authorized trustees, and proper receipt issuance.
explanation: Anonymous donations in hundis lack direct donor identification. Auditors must rely heavily on robust internal controls governing hundi opening, counting committees, and contemporaneous documentation.
conceptTags: NGO Audit | Anonymous Donations | Internal Controls

subject: Audit
prompt: Is the accumulation of income by the trust compliant with income tax provisions governing charitable trusts?
optionA: No, trusts must spend 100% of income in the same year.
optionB: Yes, application of 70% plus accumulation of 15% (plus remaining surplus within statutory limits) along with filing Form 10 complies with Section 11 requirements.
optionC: No, Form 10 is only filed by profit-making companies.
optionD: Yes, provided the surplus is distributed among the trustees.
answerText: Yes, application of 70% plus accumulation of 15% (plus remaining surplus within statutory limits) along with filing Form 10 complies with Section 11 requirements.
explanation: Under Section 11, a trust must apply at least 85% of its income to charitable purposes. It can accumulate up to 15% unconditionally, and further amounts if Form 10 is filed specifying the purpose and period.

subject: Audit
prompt: What is the primary governing document the auditor must examine to verify the powers of the trustees of Hope Charitable Trust?
optionA: The Memorandum of Association of local commercial companies
optionB: The registered Trust Deed or Trust Indenture
optionC: The SEBI Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements
optionD: The Banking Regulation Act guidelines
answerText: The registered Trust Deed or Trust Indenture
explanation: The trust deed is the foundational legal document establishing a charitable trust, outlining the objects, powers of trustees, investment criteria, and governance rules.

subject: Audit
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Grand Palace Hotel, a luxury 5-star hotel, is undergoing its annual financial audit. The hotel operates a front office, multiple restaurants, a spa, and banquet halls. During the audit, the auditor reviews the night audit reports, guest ledger reconciliations, and inventory of food, beverages, and operating supplies (linen, cutlery). The auditor notes a significant variance between the stock of high-end liquor in the main cellar and the quantities issued to bars based on Kitchen Order Tickets (KOTs) and point-of-sale logs.

subject: Audit
prompt: What is the primary purpose of the 'night audit' function in a hotel that the auditor must test?
optionA: To verify physical security guard attendance at night
optionB: To reconcile daily room occupancies, food and beverage sales, and guest billing totals to ensure all revenues are captured accurately
optionC: To calculate annual corporate income tax provisions
optionD: To perform actuarial valuation of employee retirement benefits
answerText: To reconcile daily room occupancies, food and beverage sales, and guest billing totals to ensure all revenues are captured accurately
explanation: The night audit is a critical operational control in hotels where daily transactions across all revenue centers are audited, balanced, and posted to guest accounts before the next business day starts.
conceptTags: Hotel Audit | Night Audit | Revenue Controls

subject: Audit
prompt: How should the auditor address the significant variance in liquor stock between the cellar and bar issues?
optionA: Write off the variance as normal evaporation without further inquiry.
optionB: Investigate physical security, issue slips, breakage records, complimentary drinks policy, and potential pilferage or unrecorded sales.
optionC: Adjust the variance by capitalizing it under fixed assets.
optionD: Report it as a contingent liability in the notes to accounts.
answerText: Investigate physical security, issue slips, breakage records, complimentary drinks policy, and potential pilferage or unrecorded sales.
explanation: Unexplained variances in high-value inventory like liquor indicate potential leakage, theft, or unbilled sales. The auditor must perform detailed substantive testing and review internal controls.

subject: Audit
prompt: What audit procedure should be performed regarding 'advance deposits' received from guests for future banquet bookings?
optionA: Recognize them immediately as hotel revenue on the date of receipt.
optionB: Verify that they are recorded as current liabilities (advance from customers) and not recognized as income until the banquet event actually takes place.
optionC: Treat them as corpus donations exempt from tax.
optionD: Ignore them as they do not affect the balance sheet.
answerText: Verify that they are recorded as current liabilities (advance from customers) and not recognized as income until the banquet event actually takes place.
explanation: Advance deposits for future room or banquet bookings represent cash received for services not yet rendered. They must be accounted for as liabilities until the service is delivered.

subject: Audit
prompt: When verifying trade receivables (guest ledger and city ledger balances) in the hotel audit, what is the best corroborative audit procedure?
optionA: Sending direct confirmation requests to corporate clients and travel agents listed in the city ledger
optionB: Asking the hotel general manager to verbally guarantee all outstanding balances
optionC: Tracing hotel room keys to guest names
optionD: Checking the electricity tariff rates applied by the utility provider
answerText: Sending direct confirmation requests to corporate clients and travel agents listed in the city ledger
explanation: External confirmation of receivables (especially corporate accounts and travel agents in the city ledger) provides reliable audit evidence regarding the existence and valuation of receivables.

subject: Audit
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Sunrise Power Distribution Ltd. (Discom) is audited by joint auditors appointed under the Electricity Act, 2003 and the Companies Act, 2013. The company has massive consumer connections across urban and rural areas. During the audit, the auditors review power purchase costs, transmission and distribution (T&D) losses, consumer meter readings, and subsidy receivables from the State Government. The audit team notes that subsidy claims amounting to Rs 25 crores for free power supplied to agricultural pump sets remain unconfirmed by the state government department.

subject: Audit
prompt: What is the key audit concern regarding the unconfirmed government subsidy receivables of Rs 25 crores?
optionA: It has no impact since government dues are always recoverable.
optionB: It affects the valuation and recoverability of receivables under revenue recognition principles, requiring management representation and adequate provisioning if realization is doubtful.
optionC: It should be capitalized as part of power transmission lines.
optionD: It must be treated as a contingent asset disclosed with high certainty.
answerText: It affects the valuation and recoverability of receivables under revenue recognition principles, requiring management representation and adequate provisioning if realization is doubtful.
explanation: Unconfirmed subsidy claims from the government represent significant revenue and receivables risk. If the state government disputes or delays payment, provisioning or qualification may be necessary.
conceptTags: Discom Audit | Government Subsidy | Receivables Valuation

subject: Audit
prompt: How should the auditors verify power purchase costs, which form the largest expense item for the Discom?
optionA: Check power purchase agreements (PPAs), CERC/SERC tariff orders, energy bills from generating companies, and joint meter readings at grid substations.
optionB: Verify personal expense vouchers of plant engineers.
optionC: Inspect the share capital register of the power company.
optionD: Trace electricity bills of individual domestic consumers.
answerText: Check power purchase agreements (PPAs), CERC/SERC tariff orders, energy bills from generating companies, and joint meter readings at grid substations.
explanation: Power purchase costs are regulated by statutory tariff orders and PPAs. Auditors must reconcile grid energy input data with generator invoices and regulatory rates.
conceptTags: Discom Audit | Power Purchase Cost | Regulatory Tariffs

subject: Audit
prompt: Why is the audit of Distribution Loss critical in an electricity distribution company?
optionA: It helps calculate the exact personal income tax of the utility's directors.
optionB: High distribution losses indicate commercial inefficiencies, billing leakages, or power theft, which directly impact tariff fixation and financial viability.
optionC: It determines the depreciation rate of office furniture.
optionD: It is required solely for calculating Goods and Services Tax (GST) input tax credit.
answerText: High distribution losses indicate commercial inefficiencies, billing leakages, or power theft, which directly impact tariff fixation and financial viability.
explanation: Regulators cap allowable distribution losses in tariff orders. Excessive losses signal operational inefficiencies, meter tampering, or theft, making it a critical audit focus area.
conceptTags: Discom Audit | Distribution Loss | Operational Efficiency

subject: Audit
prompt: Which statutory framework primarily governs the electricity sector and tariff regulations in India?
optionA: The Electricity Act, 2003 and regulations issued by Central/State Electricity Regulatory Commissions
optionB: The Banking Regulation Act, 1949
optionC: The Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002
optionD: The Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016
answerText: The Electricity Act, 2003 and regulations issued by Central/State Electricity Regulatory Commissions
explanation: The Electricity Act, 2003, along with regulatory bodies like CERC and SERCs, forms the core statutory framework governing power generation, transmission, distribution, and tariff setting.
conceptTags: Discom Audit | Electricity Act 2003 | Regulatory Framework

subject: Audit
prompt: CASE SCENARIO: Apex Urban Cooperative Bank Ltd. is a scheduled cooperative bank operating across three states. The statutory auditors are conducting the annual audit for 2025-26. During the review of the loan portfolio, the auditors examine a large cash credit account of a manufacturing unit with a sanctioned limit of Rs 5 crores. The account has remained out of order for the past 120 days, with no credits to cover interest debited, and the primary stock security has been depleted without the bank's prior permission.

subject: Audit
prompt: How should the auditors classify this cash credit advance under RBI prudential norms?
optionA: Standard Asset, because the borrower promises to pay next month.
optionB: Non-Performing Asset (NPA) - Sub-standard Asset, since the account has been 'out of order' and interest/principal overdue exceeds 90 days.
optionC: Loss Asset immediately without any provisioning requirement.
optionD: Performing Asset since it is a manufacturing unit.
answerText: Non-Performing Asset (NPA) - Sub-standard Asset, since the account has been 'out of order' and interest/principal overdue exceeds 90 days.
explanation: Under RBI IRAC norms, an advance is classified as an NPA if it is 'out of order' for a continuous period of 90 days in respect of overdraft/cash credit facilities. Since it is 120 days, it must be classified as an NPA.
conceptTags: Bank Audit | NPA Classification | IRAC Norms

subject: Audit
prompt: What impact does the classification of this advance as an NPA have on the bank's income recognition?
optionA: Interest accrued and unrealized on the NPA must be reversed or not recognized as income, adhering to prudential norms.
optionB: Interest should continue to be accrued and recognized as operating income.
optionC: Interest is treated as tax-free dividend income.
optionD: Interest rate should be doubled in the books automatically.
answerText: Interest accrued and unrealized on the NPA must be reversed or not recognized as income, adhering to prudential norms.
explanation: Income from non-performing assets is not recognized on an accrual basis; rather, it is recognized only when actually realized, and any unrealized interest previously recognized must be reversed.

subject: Audit
prompt: What audit procedure is essential regarding the depleted stock security in this borrower's account?
optionA: Verify stock audit reports, inspect godowns where possible, check drawing power calculations, and report the shortfall in collateral security.
optionB: Accept the borrower's verbal assurance that replacement stock is arriving.
optionC: Increase the sanctioned limit to compensate for missing stock.
optionD: Ignore stock levels if the bank manager signed a personal guarantee.
answerText: Verify stock audit reports, inspect godowns where possible, check drawing power calculations, and report the shortfall in collateral security.
explanation: Depletion of security without bank consent affects drawing power and asset safety. Auditors must verify stock audit reports and ensure adequate provisioning for unsecured portions.
conceptTags: Bank Audit | Security Verification | Drawing Power

subject: Audit
prompt: Which statutory guidelines and regulations govern the audit and classification norms of Apex Urban Cooperative Bank Ltd.?
optionA: Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (As Applicable to Cooperative Societies) and RBI Master Circulars
optionB: SEBI ICDR Regulations exclusively
optionC: The Companies Act, 2013 alone
optionD: The Indian Partnership Act, 1932
answerText: Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (As Applicable to Cooperative Societies) and RBI Master Circulars
explanation: Cooperative banks are governed by the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (AACS) and RBI directives/master circulars in addition to the respective Cooperative Societies Act.
conceptTags: Cooperative Bank | Banking Regulation Act | RBI Master Circulars

subject: Audit
prompt: Which of the following bodies is primarily responsible for prescribing the prudential norms on income recognition, asset classification, and provisioning (IRACP norms) for commercial banks in India?
optionA: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI)
optionB: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
optionC: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
optionD: Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA)
answerText: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
explanation: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) regulates banking operations in India and issues comprehensive Master Circulars on prudential norms relating to Income Recognition, Asset Classification, and Provisioning (IRACP). Auditors must verify bank accounts strictly against these RBI guidelines. This falls under the regulatory framework of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
conceptTags: RBI Regulations | IRACP Norms | Regulatory Framework

subject: Audit
prompt: In the context of bank auditing, what is the primary purpose of the 'LFAR' (Long Form Audit Report)?
optionA: To report on the true and fair view of the financial statements to the shareholders.
optionB: To provide detailed comments and observations on specific operational, structural, and control aspects of the branch to the management and statutory central auditors.
optionC: To calculate the final tax liability of the banking company for the assessment year.
optionD: To verify the statutory liquidity ratio (SLR) maintenance on a daily basis.
answerText: To provide detailed comments and observations on specific operational, structural, and control aspects of the branch to the management and statutory central auditors.
explanation: The Long Form Audit Report (LFAR) is a questionnaire-based report prescribed by the RBI that branch auditors must submit. It focuses on internal controls, credit appraisal, NPAs, branch operations, and housekeeping, supplementing the main financial audit report.

subject: Audit
prompt: An advance is classified as a 'Sub-standard Asset' if it has remained a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) for a period not exceeding how many months?
optionA: 6 months
optionB: 12 months
optionC: 18 months
optionD: 24 months
answerText: 12 months
explanation: According to RBI IRACP norms, a sub-standard asset is one that has remained an NPA for a period less than or equal to 12 months. Assets remaining in the sub-standard category for more than 12 months are downgraded to doubtful assets.

subject: Audit
prompt: What is the general provisioning percentage required for unsecured exposures classified as 'Sub-standard' assets under RBI norms?
explanation: Under RBI IRACP norms, sub-standard assets attract a general provision of 15% of total outstanding. If the advance is backed by infrastructure security with specific relaxations or has unsecured exposures, additional provisioning rules apply, but the standard sub-standard provisioning rate is 15%.

subject: Audit
prompt: When can interest income on an advance classified as a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) be recognized in the Profit and Loss Account?
optionA: When the borrower gives a written promise to pay within 90 days.
optionB: When the interest is actually received in cash.
optionC: On an accrual basis, provided adequate provisions have been made.
optionD: When the branch manager approves the capitalization of interest.
answerText: When the interest is actually received in cash.
explanation: Income recognition on NPAs must be based on cash realization. Unrealized interest accrued on advances that are classified as NPAs must be reversed or kept in suspense account and cannot be recognized as income until actually received.

subject: Audit
prompt: In a bank audit, what does the term 'Concurrent Audit' signify?
optionA: An annual statutory audit conducted simultaneously across all branches.
